en: The First Chapter.
Homage to all the glorious Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, noble Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
That which leads the Śrāvakas seeking peace to tranquility through omniscience (*sarvajñatā*),
and which, through the knowledge of the paths (*mārgajñatā*), brings about the welfare of the world and the attainment of the purpose of the light [of the Dharma]—
the Sages declare that this entire universe is endowed with these two aspects.
Homage to that Mother of the Buddha, who possesses a multitude of Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas.

That which is difficult to obtain even in hundreds of millions of infinite eons, and which is beyond the reach of those devoid of the necessary causes— may this supreme vehicle, which serves as the eye for perceiving reality, become like the rays of the sun that is the Jina.

c: Cf. *Samādhirājasūtra*, ed. Seiren Matsunami in: *Taishō Daigaku Kenkyū Kiyō* (“Memoirs of Taishō University”) 60 (1975), verse 39c (p. 236): “May it be beneficial; the word of the Sage is like the rays of the sun of the Jinas. It is profound, not easily practiced, and difficult to obtain; yet without it there is no liberation. Therefore, it should be heard with reverence.”
c: cf. *Samādhirājasūtra*, ed. Seiren Matsunami in: *Taishō Daigaku Kenkyū Kiyō* (“Memoirs of Taisho University”) 60 (1975), p. 236, verse 41c: “And without that, there is no liberation.
Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha! Homage to the Blessed Lady!”

Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One! Homage to the Great Yakṣa General Cāṇḍavajrapāṇi! Homage to all the Blessed Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! May the outflows of all sentient beings be extinguished; may the source of their virtue arise through yogic practices; may they attain the supreme accomplishment of the Tathāgatas; and may there be the presence of happiness and mental well-being for all sentient beings.

Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Raśmicandraprātimaṇḍitavidyuttejaghoṣeṣvararāja. Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, for whom this torch of Dharma blazes.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain together with a great saṅgha of monks, numbering about five thousand.

By all those Arhats who had exhausted their outflows, were free from afflictions, had attained mastery, whose minds were well-liberated and whose wisdom was well-liberated; who were noble steeds, great elephants, who had accomplished what was to be done and performed their duties; who had laid down the burden, attained their own goal, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and whose minds were well-liberated through right knowledge.

Except for one individual—the Venerable Ānanda, who was still a trainee (*śaikṣa*) and a stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*)—there were about five hundred monks who had attained the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states, along with many laymen and laywomen headed by Yaśodharā and Mahāprajāpatī, all of whom had realized the Dharma in this very life.

And together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas—immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattvas who had all attained the gateways of dhāraṇī; who dwelt in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; whose range was signlessness; whose vows were non-conceptual; who had attained the patient acceptance of the equality of all phenomena; who possessed unimpeded vows and unimpeded eloquence; who gave inexhaustible explanations and further instructions; and who were bound to the method of the analytical knowledges.

who sported with the great superknowledges, whose superknowledges were utterly unshakable, whose words were authoritative, who were free from indolence, who had initiated heroic vigor, and who were indifferent to body and life;

They were free from deceit and guile, devoid of any thought of gaining knowledge for personal profit, and taught the Dharma without worldly motives. Having reached the ultimate limit of profound patience regarding the Dharma, they had attained great fearlessness and possessed unshrinking minds. They had completely transcended all the works of Māra, were confident in their purification of karmic obstructions, and had struck down the adversaries of karma and afflictions. They surpassed all those who propound opposing doctrines and were difficult for any Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha to fathom; they were skilled in the detailed analysis and exposition of the discernment of karma.

They had made excellent vows throughout incalculable eons; they were gateways of mindfulness, the first to speak, free from frowns, and possessed of smooth and sweet speech. They were skilled in conversing by means of singing verses, endowed with uninterrupted eloquence, capable of overwhelming infinite assemblies, possessed of the grounds of self-confidence, knowledgeable in teaching for infinite millions of eons, and skilled in providing refuge.

They were resolved upon the dharmas that are the means of liberation—like an illusion, a mirage, the moon in water, a dream, an echo, an optical illusion, a city of the Gandharvas, and a reflection—and their minds were free from despondency. They were skilled in entering into the resolve for the practice of subtle knowledge regarding the mental dispositions of all sentient beings; their minds were unimpeded toward all sentient beings, and they were endowed with supreme patience. They were skilled in the knowledge that penetrates the equality of all phenomena, which is difficult to fathom in its profound nature, and they had attained mastery over their own minds.

They had attained mastery over all phenomena; they were liberated from the obscurations of all karma, afflictions, and views; they were skilled in teaching dependent origination; they had entered the method of the inexhaustible principle of profound dependent origination; they were free from all views, latent tendencies, and active outbursts; they had abandoned all fetters; they were skilled in the knowledge that penetrates the truths; they were constantly and perpetually convinced that all phenomena are like echoes; they possessed the fearlessnesses in teaching the immeasurable methods of the Dharma; they were skilled in leading others into the noble path; and they were sustained by their resolve and application toward the array of infinite Buddha-fields.

They were those who had brought before them, at all times and continuously, the recollection of the Buddhas and the meditative absorption pertaining to the Buddha-fields of incalculable world-systems; who were skilled in approaching all Buddhas as they appeared; who were skilled in making requests of immeasurable Buddhas; who were skilled in pacifying all afflictions and the arising of various views; who were skilled in entering the knowledge that sports with the accomplishment of hundreds of thousands of samādhis; and who were endowed with qualities and praises whose excellence was inexhaustible throughout boundless eons.

They were as follows: the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Bhadrapāla; the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnakara; the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnagarbha; the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnadatta; the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Susārthavāha; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Naradatta.

and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Guhagupta; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Varuṇadeva; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Indradeva; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Bhadrapāla; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Uttaramati; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Viśeṣamati; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Varddhamānamati.

And with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Anantamati; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Amoghadarśin; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Anāvaraṇamati; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Susaṃprasthita; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Suvikrāntavikrāmin; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Anantavīrya; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Nityodyukta.

And by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Nityaprayukta; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Anikṣiptadhura; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryagarbha; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Candragarbha; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Anupamamati.

and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva [Avalokiteśvara]; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Avalokiteśvara; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mārabalapramardin; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramati; and by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnamudrāhasta.

And with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Nityotkṣiptahasta; and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇācitta; and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Mahāvyūha; and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Praharāja; and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Merukūṭa; and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Maitreya; and with these and many other hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas.

Then, at that time, the Blessed One himself prepared a lion-throne and sat down upon it. Having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him, he sat there and entered the samādhi named "King of All Samādhis," in which all samādhis are contained, included, gathered, and brought together.

Then the Blessed One, mindful and clearly comprehending, arose from that samādhi and surveyed this buddha-field with his divine eye. Having surveyed it, he emitted light from his entire body. From beneath him, from the two thousand-spoked wheels on the soles of his feet, sixty-six hundred-thousand-billion-trillion rays of light issued forth.

From the ten toes of his feet, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from his two ankles, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from the circle of his navel, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; and from his two sides, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth.

They issued forth: from the *śrīvatsa* on the heart, that mark of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*), sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from the ten fingers of the hands, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from the two arms, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; and from the two shoulders, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth.

From his neck, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from his four fangs, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from his forty teeth, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; and from his two eyes, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth.

From his two ears, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from his two nostrils, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; from the *ūrṇā* hair-tuft between his eyebrows, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth; and from the *uṣṇīṣa* on the crown of his head, sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth.

And from his mouth, sixty times sixty hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light issued forth. All those hundreds of thousands of *koṭī-niyuta* rays of light, having issued forth, pervaded this entire great trichiliocosm with a great radiance, and they also pervaded world-systems in the eastern direction equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges with that great radiance;
likewise, world-systems in the southern direction equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges [they pervaded] with that great radiance.

They radiated forth; they pervaded world systems in the western direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, with a great radiance. They pervaded world systems in the northeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, with a great radiance. They pervaded world systems in the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, with a great radiance.

In the southwestern direction, they pervaded world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā with a great radiance. In the northwestern direction, they pervaded world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā with a great radiance. In the downward direction, they pervaded world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā with a great radiance. In the upward direction, they pervaded world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā with a great radiance.
And those beings who saw that radiance, and those who were touched by that radiance, all became destined for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One again emitted light from all his pores; by that light, this trichiliocosm was suffused with a great radiance. In the eastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused with a great radiance. In the southern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused with a great radiance.

In the western direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by a great radiance; in the northern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by a great radiance.

They became clearly illuminated. In the northeastern direction, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by a great radiance. In the southeastern direction, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by a great radiance. In the southwestern direction, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by a great radiance.

In the northwestern direction, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused with a great radiance. In the downward direction, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused with a great radiance. In the upward direction, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused with a great radiance.
And all those beings who saw that radiance, and all those who were suffused by that radiance, became destined for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then, indeed, the Blessed One again caused that natural radiance of the Tathāgata to pervade the great trichiliocosm with a vast illumination. By that great illumination, world-systems in the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, were pervaded; by that great illumination, world-systems in the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, were pervaded.

In the western direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by that great radiance; in the northern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were pervaded by that great radiance.

They shone forth. In the northeastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by that great radiance. In the southeastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by that great radiance. In the southwestern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by that great radiance.

In the northwestern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused by that great radiance. In the downward direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused by that great radiance. In the upward direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused by that great radiance. And those beings who saw that radiance, and those who were touched by that radiance, all became fixed in their destiny for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

Then the Blessed One, having extended his tongue-faculty from his mouth, pervaded this entire triple-thousand great-thousand world-system with that tongue-faculty and manifested a smile. From that tongue-faculty there issued forth many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of light rays of various colors. And upon every ray, lotuses consisting of various jewels and shining with the luster of gold, each with a thousand petals, came into being.

And there were lotuses—variegated, beautiful, delightful, golden, fragrant, soft, made of *kācilindika* cloth, and pleasant to the touch. Upon those lotuses, forms of the Tathāgatas were seated, teaching the Dharma; that is to say, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the six perfections (*ṣaṭpāramitā*). They went to world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma;
that is to say, this very [teaching] connected with the six perfections.

They went to world systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and having gone there, they taught the Dharma—that is to say, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections. They went to world systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and having gone there, they taught the Dharma—that is to say, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections.

They went to world systems in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma—namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections. They went to world systems in the northeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma—namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections.

They went to world systems in the southeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma, namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections. They went to world systems in the southwestern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma, namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections.

In the northwestern direction, they went to world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma, namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections. In the downward direction, they went to world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma, namely, this very [teaching] associated with the six perfections.

They went to world systems in the upward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and having gone there as well, they taught the Dharma—namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the six perfections—and all those beings who heard that Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Then, indeed, the Blessed One, seated upon that very lion-throne, entered the Buddha-samādhi called "Lion’s Play" (siṃhavikrīḍita) and performed such a miraculous feat (ṛddhyabhisaṃskāra) that, by means of that performed feat, this great trichiliocosm world-system shook, trembled, and quaked in six ways; it stirred, trembled, and quaked; it moved, trembled, and quaked.

It shook, it shook violently, it shook intensely; it roared, it roared loudly, it roared intensely; it resounded, it resounded loudly, it resounded intensely. It rose up at the edges while sinking in the middle, and it sank at the edges while rising in the middle. It became soft, smooth, and subtle, perceiving itself as the source of benefit and happiness for all sentient beings.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, all the hells, animal births, the world of Yama, the unfavorable states, the miserable destinies, and the states of ruin within this great trichiliocosm were completely cut off. All those beings were reborn into the commonality of human beings, and all those beings were reborn into the commonality of the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, the Tuṣita, the Nirmāṇarati, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very joy, serene confidence, and gladness, recollected their former births. Having recollected them and having attained joy, serene confidence, and gladness, they approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, all the hells, all the animal realms, and all the worlds of Yama in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction were utterly destroyed; all unfavorable conditions came to an end, and all those beings were reborn among the fellowship of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very state of joy, serene faith, and gladness born within them, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, serene faith, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined in reverence, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southern direction, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were completely severed, and all unfavorable conditions vanished; and all those beings were reborn into the common lot of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very state of joy, serene confidence, and rapture born [within them], recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, serene confidence, and rapture, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined in reverence, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in world systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were utterly destroyed, and all unfavorable conditions came to an end; and all those beings were reborn into the common lot of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very state of joy, serene confidence, and gladness born [within them], recollected their former births. Having recollected them and attained joy, serene confidence, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were residing there in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined in reverence, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in world systems in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were utterly destroyed, and all unfavorable conditions came to an end; and all those beings were reborn into the common destiny of humans, asuras, and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very birth of joy, serene confidence, and gladness, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, serene confidence, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northeastern direction, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were utterly destroyed, and all states of deprivation came to an end; and all those beings were reborn into the commonality of non-humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very birth of joy, serene faith, and gladness, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, serene faith, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were residing there in their respective world-systems and Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the southeastern direction, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were completely severed, and all unfavorable conditions came to an end; and all those beings were reborn in the commonality of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very state of joy, serene confidence, and gladness born [within them], recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, serene confidence, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in as many world-systems in the southwestern direction as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were utterly severed, and all unfavorable conditions came to an end; and all those beings were reborn into the common lot of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very state of joy, faith, and gladness born within them, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, faith, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in the northwestern direction, all the hells, all the animal realms, and all the worlds of Yama in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were completely cut off, and all unfavorable conditions vanished; and all those beings were reborn among the fellowship of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very state of joy, serene confidence, and gladness born within them, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, and having attained joy, serene confidence, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined in reverence, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

In that single moment, instant, and muhūrta, in world systems in the downward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were completely cut off, and all unfavorable conditions vanished; and all those beings were reborn into the common lot of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very joy, faith, and gladness born within them, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, having attained joy, faith, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields. Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, in the worlds above as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, all the hells, all the animal realms, and all the worlds of Yama were completely severed; all unfavorable conditions came to an end, and all those beings were reborn among the fellowship of humans and gods.

Then those humans and those gods, through that very joy, serene confidence, and gladness born within them, recollected their former births. Having recollected them, and having attained joy, serene confidence, and gladness, they approached the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were residing in their respective Buddha-fields.
Having approached and bowed at their feet, with palms joined in reverence, they paid homage to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

Then, at that very moment, all those beings in this triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system who were born blind saw forms with their eyes; the deaf heard sounds with their ears; the insane regained their mindfulness; those with distracted minds attained a state of non-distraction; the naked received robes; and the poor obtained wealth.

Those who were hungry obtained food; those who were thirsty obtained drink. Those afflicted by disease became free from disease. Those with deficient bodies or impaired faculties became possessed of complete bodies and faculties. Those with exhausted bodies became free from exhaustion. Those whose bodily, vocal, and mental actions and livelihoods were unceasingly unwholesome became free from such unwholesome bodily, vocal, and mental actions and livelihoods. And all sentient beings came to possess a mind of equanimity toward all other sentient beings.

They were as follows: all beings possessed minds of equanimity toward their mothers, fathers, brothers, sisters, friends, kinsmen, and companions; they were endowed with the paths of wholesome action. They were celibate, pure, free from the stench of impurity, and devoid of all unwholesome thoughts. At that time, all beings were endowed with every form of happiness—just like the bliss of a monk who has attained the third dhyāna.

And at that very time, all sentient beings were endowed with such wisdom that they understood thus: "Excellent is giving; excellent is the Dharma; excellent is self-restraint; excellent is truth; excellent is heedfulness; excellent is loving-kindness; excellent is compassion; excellent is non-violence toward all living beings."

Then the Blessed One, seated upon that very lion-throne, remained surpassing this great trichiliocosm world-system—including Sumeru and the Cakravāḍa mountains, the abodes of the gods, Indra, the moon, and the rays of the sun; including the hosts of devas and dānavas, Brahmā, and the Śuddhāvāsa heavens—shining, gleaming, glowing, and radiating with splendor, complexion, majesty, and glory.

Just as, for example, a powerful sun in the utterly pure expanse of the sky, or the orb of the moon on the night of the full moon, so too did the Blessed One stand, having surpassed this great trichiliocosm world-system; he shone, gleamed, blazed, and radiated with light, complexion, splendor, and majesty.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, he stands, shines, blazes, and radiates with splendor, color, brilliance, and majesty.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he stands resplendent, shines, glows, and radiates with light, color, brilliance, and majesty.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he stands, beautiful, radiant, glowing, and resplendent with light, color, brilliance, and glory.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, he stands, beautiful, radiant, glowing, and resplendent with light, complexion, majesty, and glory.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the northeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he stands, beautiful, radiant, glowing, and resplendent with light, color, brilliance, and glory.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the southeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, he stands resplendent, shines, blazes, and radiates with light, color, brilliance, and glory.
In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the south-western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he stands, shines, blazes, and radiates with light, color, splendor, and glory.

In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the northwestern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he stands, shines, glows, and blazes with radiance, color, splendor, and majesty.

Thus, having surpassed world-systems in the downward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, he stands, beautiful, radiant, glowing, and resplendent with light, complexion, splendor, and majesty.
In this way, having surpassed world-systems in the upward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges,
he stands, shines, glows, and radiates with light, color, splendor, and majesty.
Just as Sumeru, the king of mountains, stands surpassing all other black mountains, shining, gleaming, blazing, and radiating with its luster, color, brilliance, and splendor; so too does he stand.
It is just as if the orb of the moon, having surpassed all the forms of the stars, remains beautiful, radiant, glowing, and resplendent with its light, color, brilliance, and majesty.
Just as, for example, the orb of the sun, having surpassed all other lights, stands out, shines, blazes, and radiates with its brilliance, color, splendor, and majesty.

In the very same way, the Blessed One, having surpassed the world with its gods, its Indras, and its Brahmās, including the Śuddhāvāsa deities, stands resplendent, shines, blazes, and radiates with light, complexion, majesty, and glory.
Then the Blessed One once again manifested within this triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system a physical body exactly like his own natural form.

Then, as many as there were devas belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host, the Ābhāsvara, the Brahmakāyika, the Paranirmitavaśavartin, the Nirmāṇarati, the Tuṣita, the Yāma, the Trāyastriṃśa, and the Cāturmahārājakāyika hosts in this triple-thousand great thousandfold world system—all of them beheld the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, seated upon the lion throne.
They were satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; taking divine flowers, divine garlands, and divine...

Taking divine perfumes, divine ointments, divine powders, divine garments, divine blue lotuses, white water lilies, white lotuses, red lotuses, and fragrant flowers; divine saffron and tamāla leaves; divine substances, divine ornaments, divine parasols, divine banners, and divine flags, they approached the Blessed One and, having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One.

And all those flowers, garlands, ointments, powders, and so forth, as well as the fragrant garments, ornaments, parasols, banners, and flags, by the very power of the Blessed One’s empowerment, immediately became a great pavilion of flowers and other materials for all beings, situated in the air above the Blessed One, equal in size to the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system. And from that pavilion, divine flowers, flower-patterned cloths, and flower-garlands hung down, dangled down, and were suspended far below.

And by those flower-garlands and silk streamers, this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world-system was made resplendent. And by that golden-colored radiance of the Blessed One’s majesty, it was exceedingly beautified, shone, blazed, and gleamed. Just as this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world-system was so illuminated, even so world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction were pervaded by that radiance of the Blessed One’s majesty.

In the southern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the radiance of that Blessed One’s power. In the western direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the radiance of that Blessed One’s power. In the northern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the radiance of that Blessed One’s power.

In the northeastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were suffused by the radiance of that Blessed One’s majestic power. In the southeastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were suffused by the radiance of that Blessed One’s majestic power. In the southwestern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were suffused by the radiance of that Blessed One’s majestic power.

In the northwestern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the radiance of that Blessed One’s power. In the downward direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the radiance of that Blessed One’s power. In the upward direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the radiance of that Blessed One’s power.

There, the humans of Jambudvīpa, upon seeing that body of the Tathāgata which was so pleasing to behold, thought: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. And just as it was for the humans of Jambudvīpa, so too did the humans of Godānīya, upon seeing that body of the Tathāgata which was so pleasing to behold, think: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the humans of Pūrvavideha saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. As for the humans of Uttarakuru, they too beheld that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold.

Upon seeing their own forms, it occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm saw that most enchanting form of the Tathāgata, it occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Yāma gods saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the Tuṣita gods saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Nirmāṇarati gods saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the gods of the Paranirmitavaśavartin heaven saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the gods of the Brahmakāyika heaven saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the gods of the Brahmā-purohita realm saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the gods of the Brahma-pārṣadya realm saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the gods of the Mahābrahmā realm saw that most enchanting manifestation of the Tathāgata’s physical form, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Ābhā gods saw that most enchanting manifestation of the Tathāgata’s physical form, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Parīttābhā gods saw that most enchanting manifestation of the Tathāgata’s [physical form]...

Upon seeing their own bodies, it occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. Upon seeing the body of the Tathāgata—which is a sight that never satiates—the gods of Immeasurable Light (Apramāṇābha) thought: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. Upon seeing the body of the Tathāgata—which is a sight that never satiates—the gods of Radiant Purity (Ābhāsvara) thought: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the Ābhā devas saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Parīttaśubha devas saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the gods of the Apramāṇaśubha realm saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the gods of the Śubhakṛtsna realm saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the Bṛhatphala devas saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Parīttabṛhatphala devas saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the gods of the Apramāṇa-bṛhat heavens saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the gods of the Bṛhat-phala heavens saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the Avṛha gods beheld that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Atapa gods beheld that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold...

Upon seeing their own forms, it occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. Upon seeing the Tathāgata’s body, which is so pleasing to behold that one never tires of looking at it, it occurred to the Sudṛśa devas: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

When the Sudarśana gods saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma. When the Akaniṣṭha gods saw that body of the Tathāgata, so pleasing to behold, this thought occurred to them: "The Tathāgata is seated before us, teaching the Dharma."

Thus, in a thousandfold world system, all humans and all gods, upon seeing that body of the Tathāgata which is so pleasing to behold, thought: "The Tathāgata is sitting right before us, teaching the Dharma. In a two-thousandfold world system, all humans and all gods, upon seeing that body of the Tathāgata which is so pleasing to behold, thought: "The Tathāgata is sitting right before us, teaching the Dharma."
Thus, in this trichiliocosm, all humans and all gods, upon seeing that body of the Tathāgata—so pleasing to behold—thought: "The Tathāgata is seated right before us, teaching the Dharma."

Then the Blessed One, seated upon that very lion-throne, again emitted a radiance by which this great trichiliocosm was once more illuminated. In the eastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated; in the southern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated; in the western direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated; and in the northern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated.

The world-systems were illuminated. In the northeastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated. In the southeastern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated. In the southwestern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated. In the northwestern direction, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated.

In the direction below, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were illuminated; in the direction above, world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were illuminated. By that radiance, all the sentient beings in this great trichiliocosm beheld, in the eastern direction, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and surrounded by their retinues of Bodhisattvas.

And there, in the eastern direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, the sentient beings also saw this trichiliocosm—the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—along with the community of monks and his retinue of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the southern direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, those beings also saw this great trichiliocosm, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the western direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, those beings also saw this great trichiliocosm, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas. And there, in the northern direction, in [world systems] as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges...

The beings in those world-systems also saw this great trichiliocosm, as well as the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by the assembly of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the northeastern direction, those beings who dwell in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges also saw this great trichiliocosm, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the southeastern direction, those beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges also saw this great trichiliocosm, and the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the southwestern direction, those beings in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges also saw this great trichiliocosm, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the northwestern direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, those beings also saw this great trichiliocosm, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with his assembly of śrāvakas and his retinue of bodhisattvas.

And there, in the direction below, those beings who dwell in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges likewise saw this great trichiliocosm and the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha.

They saw him together with the community of monks and surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas. Furthermore, those beings in the worlds above, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, also saw this great trichiliocosm, as well as the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of monks and surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas.

Then, having crossed world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system at the very end called Ratnāvatī. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratnākara resides, stays, and maintains himself; he thoroughly proclaims this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Samantaraśmi, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the Tathāgata’s body—which was lovely to behold—approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened Buddha Ratnākara. Having approached, he addressed this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened Buddha:

"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance in the world of this great radiance, this great earthquake of the earth, and the manifestation of such a body of the Tathāgata?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnākara, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaraśmi: "Noble son, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the western direction, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself; he fully reveals the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. This is his such-like majestic power."
Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantaraśmi addressed that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnākara, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, in this way:

“Blessed One, I would go to that great world-system to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon that Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and all those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are for the most part youthful, who have attained the realization of dhāraṇīs and analytical knowledges, and who have acquired mastery over all meditative concentrations and attainments. The Tathāgata Ratnākara said:
Go, son of good family, to that great world-system whenever you deem it the right time.

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnākara gave to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaraśmi a thousand lotuses made of various jewels, shining like gold and each having a thousand petals. "O son of good family, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni, and remain there in that buddha-field dwelling with full awareness."
For what reason? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been born in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not harm them there.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantaraśmi, having taken from that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened Buddha Ratnākara, those thousand-petaled lotuses shining like gold, vanished together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and those appearing in the forms of boys and girls—from that buddha-field and proceeded toward as many Blessed Buddhas as there were in the eastern direction.

Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshiping all those who stand, abide, and remain—by means of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags, with great bodhisattva offerings and great bodhisattva majesty—he approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantaraśmi stood to one side and addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"Lord, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnākara inquires after the Lord’s freedom from affliction, freedom from ailment, ease of movement, strength, and dwelling in comfort. And these thousand-petaled lotuses, shining like gold, have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnākara as an offering to the Lord."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, took those lotuses and cast them toward the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the eastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.

Then all those world-systems were suffused with those lotuses, and upon those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas sat and taught the Dharma. That is to say, they taught beginning with these very six perfections; and all those beings who heard that teaching of the Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Those bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls—honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, each with their own roots of merit. To the south, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system which is the very last of all, named Sarvaśokāpagata (Free from All Sorrow).
There dwells, remains, and maintains his life a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Aśokaśrī; he thoroughly reveals this very Prajñāpāramitā to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vigataśoka, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the Tathāgata’s body which was lovely to behold, approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī, as follows:

“Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake, and for the manifestation of such a body of a Tathāgata? When this was said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vigataśoka:

"Noble son, to the north, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself. He is fully revealing the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Such is his majestic power."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vigataśoka addressed these words to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī:

“Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni, and all those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, most of whom are youthful, who have attained the realization of the dhāraṇīs and analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), and who have acquired mastery over all meditative concentrations and attainments. The Blessed One, the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī, said: “Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system, whenever you deem it the right time.”

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī, gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels and shining like gold, each with a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vigataśoka. "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni. And, noble son, you should dwell there in that Buddha-field with full awareness."
For what reason? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been born in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not cause them harm there.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vigataśoka, having taken those thousand-petaled lotuses shining like gold from the presence of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī, vanished from that buddha-field together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and those in the form of boys and girls—and proceeded toward as many Blessed Buddhas as there were in the southern direction.

Abiding, remaining, and persisting, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, garments, ornaments, umbrellas, banners, and flags—with great bodhisattva reverence and great bodhisattva majesty—he approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha Śākyamuni. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side; and while standing to one side, he...

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vigataśoka addressed the Blessed One: "Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, ease of movement, strength, and well-being.
And these thousand-petaled lotuses, radiant as gold, have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī, as an act of worship for the Blessed One."

Then the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, having taken those lotuses, cast them toward the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the worlds of the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.

Then all those world-systems were suffused with those lotuses, and upon those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas sat and taught the Dharma. That is to say, they taught starting from these very six perfections; and those beings by whom that teaching of the Dharma was heard all became destined for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Those bodhisattvas as well—both householders and renunciants, and boys and girls—honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, by means of their respective roots of merit.

In the western direction, beyond as many world-systems as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system which is the very last of all, named Upaśāntā. Therein dwells, stays, and maintains himself a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratnārcis. He thoroughly proclaims this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva named Cāritramati, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the Tathāgata’s body—which was so beautiful to behold—approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis, saying:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition for this?"

"For the appearance of a great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake of the earth, and for the manifestation of such a body of a Tathāgata. When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnārcis, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, spoke thus to that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cāritramati:

"Noble son, having passed beyond world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself. He is thoroughly proclaiming the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power."

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Cāritramati said this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis: "Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."

And to all those bodhisattva mahāsattvas—who were for the most part youths, who had attained the realization of *dhāraṇīs* and the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvids*), and who had acquired mastery over all meditative concentrations and attainments—the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnārcis, said: "Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system, whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis gave to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cāritramati a thousand lotuses made of various jewels, shining like gold and each having a thousand petals. "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni. And, noble son, you should remain there in that Buddha-field, conducting yourself with full awareness."
For what reason? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been reborn in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not cause them harm there.

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Cāritramati, having taken from that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis, those thousand-petaled lotuses with the luster of gold, vanished from that buddha-field together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls—and proceeded toward as many Blessed Buddhas as there are in the western direction.

They remain, endure, and subsist; honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping them all with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, ornaments, parasols, banners, and flags—with great bodhisattva hospitality and great bodhisattva majesty—[he dwells].

He approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One; having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cāritramati addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"Lord, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis, inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, strength, and well-being. And these golden-hued, thousand-petaled lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnārcis, as an act of worship for the Blessed One."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, took those lotuses and cast them toward the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the western direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

Then all those world-systems were filled with those lotuses, and upon those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas sat and taught the Dharma. That is to say, they taught starting from these very six perfections. And those beings who heard that teaching of the Dharma all became fixed in their destiny for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; they too were bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls, honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, each with their own roots of merit.

To the north, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system which is the very last of all, named Jāyā. Therein dwells, remains, and maintains himself a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Jāyendra, who fully reveals this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Jayadatta, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the body of the Tathāgata which was so pleasing to behold, approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jāyendra. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jāyendra, saying: "Blessed One, what is the cause?"

What is the cause for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, and for this great earthquake, and for the manifestation of such a body of the Tathāgata, so that we may pay homage to it, revere it, and attend upon it?

When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha Jayendra, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta: "Noble son, beyond world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself; he thoroughly proclaims the Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. Such is his majestic power."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta [approached] that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Jāyendra.

He said this to the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One: "Lord, I would go to that Sahā world-system to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One, and also those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, all of whom are for the most part youthful, have attained the mastery of dhāraṇīs and analytical knowledges, and have acquired sovereignty over all meditative concentrations and attainments. The Blessed One—
The Tathāgata Jāyenadra said: "Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jāyendra gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels and shining like gold, each with a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta. "O son of good family, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. And, O son of good family, you must dwell there in that Buddha-field with full awareness. Why is that? Because those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have been born in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not cause them to be offended."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta, having taken from the presence of that Blessed One Jāyendra, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, those thousand-petaled lotuses shining like gold, vanished from that buddha-field together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and in the form of boys and girls—and proceeded toward as many Buddha-Blessed Ones as there were residing in the northern direction.

Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshiping them all—sustaining and maintaining them with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags; with great bodhisattva honor and great bodhisattva majesty—he approached the place where the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha was staying. Having approached, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta...

He said this to the Blessed One: "Lord, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jāyendra inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from ailment, freedom from distress, ease of movement, strength, and well-being. And these thousand-petaled lotuses, shining like gold, have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jāyendra, as an offering to the Blessed One."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, took those lotuses and cast them toward the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones in the northern direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
Then all those world-systems became filled with those lotuses, and upon those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas were seated, teaching the Dharma.

Furthermore, concerning these very six perfections, all those beings by whom that teaching of the Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Those bodhisattvas as well—both householders and renunciants, both girls and boys—honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, with their own respective roots of merit.

In the northeastern direction, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system which is the furthest of all, named Samādhyalaṅkṛta. There dwells, remains, and maintains himself a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One named Samādhihastyuttaraśrī. He thoroughly proclaims this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vijayavikrāmī, having seen that radiance, that great earthquake, and the body of the Tathāgata—whose appearance was never-tiring to behold—approached where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, was.

He approached the Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha; having approached, he said this to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake, and for the manifestation of such a body of a Tathāgata?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijayavikrāmin: "Noble son, in the southwestern direction, beyond as many world-systems as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains his life."
He thoroughly elucidates the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijayavikrāmin said this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī: "Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni."

And to those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who were for the most part youthful, who had attained the realization of dhāraṇīs and the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), and who had acquired mastery over all meditative concentrations and attainments, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata named Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, said: "Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system, whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels and shining like gold, each with a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijayavikrāmin, saying: "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni, while dwelling in full awareness."

And, noble son, let there be no [such] in that buddha-field. For what reason? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been born in that world-system are difficult to approach; lest you be harmed there.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijayavikrāmin, having taken those thousand-petaled lotuses with a golden luster from the presence of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and appearing in the forms of boys and girls—vanished from that Buddha-field and proceeded toward the northeastern direction.

Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshiping all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones—who remain, stay, and maintain themselves—he approached the place where the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha was, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, garments, banners, and flags, by means of the great majesty of a Bodhisattva and the great power of a Bodhisattva.

Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijayavikrāmī said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, strength, and well-being."
And these golden-hued, thousand-petaled lotuses were offered by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, as an act of worship for the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, took those lotuses and cast them toward the northeastern direction, to the world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā where the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas reside.

Then, by means of those lotuses, all world-systems became suffused; and upon those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas were seated, teaching the Dharma—namely, beginning with these very six perfections. And all those beings who heard that teaching of the Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

And those bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls—honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, each with their own roots of merit.

In the southeastern direction, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system which is the very last of all, named Bodhimaṇḍālaṅkārasurucirā. Therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Padmottaraśrī. He thoroughly reveals this very Perfection of Wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Padmahasta, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the Tathāgata’s body—which was lovely to behold—approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottaraśrī. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottaraśrī, as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake, and for the manifestation of such a body of the Tathāgata?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One Padmottaraśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmahasta: "Noble son, in the northwestern direction, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself. He thoroughly proclaims the Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmahasta said this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottaraśrī: "Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni."

And to all those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who were for the most part youthful (*kumārabhūta*), who had attained the mastery of the *dhāraṇīs* and analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and who had acquired sovereignty over all meditative concentrations and attainments, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī, said: "Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system, whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottaraśrī gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels and shining like gold, each with a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmahasta, saying: "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni. And, noble son, you should remain there in that Buddha-field, reflecting with full awareness."
For what reason? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been reborn in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not let them be harmed there.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmahasta, having taken from that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottaraśrī, those thousand-petaled lotuses radiant as gold, together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas, [departed].

Together with householders and renunciants, as well as those in the form of boys and girls, he disappeared from that buddha-field and, while honoring, revering, respecting, and worshiping all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the eastern direction with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags—with great bodhisattva honor and great bodhisattva majesty—he approached the Blessed One.

The Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, approached him. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmahasta addressed the Blessed One as follows:

The Blessed One Padmottaraśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, strength, and dwelling in comfort. And these thousand-petaled lotuses, radiant as gold, have been sent by that Blessed One Padmottaraśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, for the purpose of making an offering to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, took those lotuses and cast them toward the southeastern direction, to the world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones reside.

Then all the world-systems became filled with those lotuses, and upon those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas were seated, teaching the Dharma—namely, beginning with these very six perfections. And all those beings by whom that teaching of the Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Those bodhisattva mahāsattvas—both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls—honored and revered the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, by means of their respective roots of merit.

They honored it, they revered it, they worshipped it. To the south-west, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system which is the very last of all, named Vigatarājasambhava. There a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī resides, stays, and maintains himself. He thoroughly proclaims this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sūryapratibhāsa, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the Tathāgata’s body—which was of a form so beautiful as to be never-tiring to behold—approached the place where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī, was staying.

Having approached that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī, he said this to him: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance in the world of this great radiance, this great earthquake, and the manifestation of such a body of a Tathāgata?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryapratibhāsa: "Noble son, in the northeastern direction, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system called Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself."
