He fully reveals the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryapratibhāsa said this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī: "Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."

And to all those bodhisattva mahāsattvas—who were for the most part youthful, who had attained the realization of dhāraṇīs and the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvids), and who had acquired mastery over all meditative concentrations and attainments—the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī, said: "Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system, whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels and shining like gold, each with a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryapratibhāsa, saying: "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni."

And, noble son, one should dwell with clear comprehension in that buddha-field. Why is that? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been reborn in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not let them come to grief there.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryapratibhāsa, having taken from the presence of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī, those thousand-petaled lotuses shining like gold, vanished from that buddha-field together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and in the forms of boys and girls—as far as...

In the southwestern direction, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, reside, remain, and maintain themselves; honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping them all with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags—with great bodhisattva honor and great bodhisattva majesty—he approached the place where the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One was.

Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryapratibhāsa stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryapratibhāsa addressed the Blessed One: "The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Blessed One Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī [inquires after] the Blessed One’s freedom from illness..."

He inquires after [the Blessed One’s] freedom from ailment, ease of movement, strength, and dwelling in comfort. And these golden-hued, thousand-petaled lotuses, sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One Sūryamaṇḍalapratibhāsottamaśrī, have been dispatched as an act of worship for the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, took those lotuses and cast them toward the tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly enlightened ones in the southwestern direction, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

Then, all world-systems were filled with those lotuses, and upon those lotuses, forms of the Tathāgata sat and taught the Dharma, namely, beginning with these very six perfections. And all those beings who heard that teaching of the Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Those bodhisattvas as well—both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls—honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, each with their own roots of merit.

To the northwest, beyond as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges, there is a world system which is the very last of all, named Vaśībhūta. Therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ekachattra; he thoroughly proclaims this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnottama, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the Tathāgata’s body which was lovely to behold, approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekachattra. Having approached, he [approached] that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Ekachattra...

He said this to the Samyaksambuddha: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake, and for the manifestation of such a body of the Tathāgata?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekacchattra, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnottama: "Noble son, in the southwestern direction, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself."
He fully reveals the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnottama said this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekachattra: "Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."

And to all those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—most of whom were youthful princes (*kumārabhūta*), who had attained the mastery of the *dhāraṇīs* and analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and who had acquired sovereignty over all meditative concentrations and attainments—the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ekachattra, said: "Go, noble son, to that great world-system, whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekachattra gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnottama, saying: "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni. And, noble son, you should dwell there in that Buddha-field with full awareness.
Why is that? Because [that field] is difficult to approach."
Do not disregard those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been reborn in that world-system.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnottama, having taken from that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekachattra, those thousand-petaled lotuses radiant with gold, vanished from that buddha-field together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and those appearing in the forms of boys and girls—and proceeded toward as many Blessed Buddhas as there were in the northwestern direction.

They remain, endure, and persist. Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshiping them all with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags—with great bodhisattva honor and great bodhisattva majesty—he approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha Śākyamuni. Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnottama addressed the Blessed One: "Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekachattra inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, physical vigor, strength, and whether he dwells in comfort.
And these thousand-petaled lotuses, shining like gold, have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ekachattra, as an act of worship for the Blessed One."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, took those lotuses and cast them toward the northwestern direction, to those world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā where the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones reside.
Thereupon, all those world-systems were filled with those lotuses, and within those lotuses, forms of Tathāgatas sat and taught the Dharma; that is to say, this very same sixfold perfection.

Beginning from that point, all those beings who heard that teaching of the Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Those bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls—honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksambuddha, each with their own roots of merit.

In the direction below, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system which is the very last of all, named Padmā. Therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Padmaśrī. He thoroughly proclaims this very Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Padmottara, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and the body of the Tathāgata which was so pleasing to behold, approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī, as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for the manifestation of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake, and for the appearance of such a body of the Tathāgata?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmottara: "Noble son, above in the direction of the zenith, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, remains, and maintains himself. He thoroughly proclaims the Perfection of Wisdom to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmottara said this to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī: "Blessed One, I would go to that Sahā world-system in order to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."

And to those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, who were for the most part youthful, who had attained the production of dhāraṇīs and analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), and who had acquired mastery over all meditative concentrations and attainments, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Padmaśrī, said: "Go, noble son, to that Sahā world-system, whenever you deem it the right time."

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī gave a thousand lotuses made of various jewels and shining like gold, each with a thousand petals, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmottara, saying: "Noble son, scatter these lotuses over that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni. And, noble son, you should dwell there in that Buddha-field with full awareness."
For what reason? Because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been reborn in that world-system are difficult to approach; do not cause harm there.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmottara, having taken from that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī, those thousand-petaled lotuses shining like gold, vanished from that buddha-field together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—both householders and renunciants, and those appearing in the forms of boys and girls—and proceeded as far as the Blessed Buddhas who reside in the downward direction.

They maintain and sustain them all, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping them with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, garments, ornaments, umbrellas, banners, and flags—with great Bodhisattva hospitality and great Bodhisattva majesty—wherever the Blessed One Śākyamuni is.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to present [this perfection], and who—by means of a single flower, a single garland, a single fragrance, a single ointment, a single powder, a single cloth, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, or a single flag—wishes to honor, revere, respect, and worship it, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to provide a single meal to all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their retinues of bodhisattvas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, in as many world-systems in the northeastern direction as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā; and who wishes to honor, revere, respect, and worship them with a single flower, a single garland, a single ointment, a single powder, a single cloth, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, and a single flag, should train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

A bodhisattva who wishes to provide for all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their retinues of bodhisattvas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, in as many world systems in the southeastern direction as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, by means of a single alms-offering; and who wishes to honor, revere, respect, and worship them with a single flower, a single garland, a single ointment, a single powder, a single cloth, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, and a single pennant—[should practice this samādhi].

A mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom if he desires to provide for all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their retinues of bodhisattvas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, in as many world-systems in the southwestern direction as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, by means of a single alms-offering; and if he desires to honor, revere, respect, and worship them with a single flower, a single garland, a single ointment, a single powder, a single cloth, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, and a single flag.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to honor and worship [the Buddhas] should train in the perfection of wisdom. This applies to as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their retinues of bodhisattvas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, as there are in world-systems in the northwestern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—should they wish to provide for all of them with a single alms-offering, a single flower, a single garland, a single ointment, a single powder, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, or a single flag.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to honor, revere, respect, and worship [the Buddhas] should train in the perfection of wisdom. As many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are in the world-systems of the lower direction—numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—together with their retinues of bodhisattvas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, all of them [should be served] with a single offering of alms-food.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to present [this teaching], and who wishes to honor, revere, respect, and worship it with a single flower, a single garland, a single fragrance, a single ointment, a single powder, a single cloth, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, or a single flag, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

To one who desires to provide for all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their retinues of bodhisattvas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, in as many world-systems in the direction above as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā—desiring to serve them all with a single offering of alms-food, and desiring to honor, revere, respect, and worship them with a single flower, a single garland, a single fragrance, a single unguent, a single powder, a single cloth, a single ornament, a single parasol, a single banner, and a single flag.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, one who wishes to establish all those beings in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the eastern direction within the aggregate of ethical discipline, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation [should train in the perfection of wisdom].

by one desiring to establish [beings] in the fruit of stream-entry, by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of once-returning, by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of non-returning, by one desiring to establish them in arhatship, by one desiring to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by one desiring to establish them in omniscience, and by one desiring to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path;
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings] in omniscience, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whoever wishes to establish all those beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southern direction within the aggregate of ethical discipline, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, and within the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of once-returning;

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish others in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to establish all those beings in world-systems in the western direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, in the aggregate of ethical discipline; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of concentration; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of wisdom; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of liberation; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; who wishes to establish them in the fruit of stream-entry; who wishes to establish them in the fruit of once-returning; [and so forth].

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish others in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to establish all those beings in the worlds of the northern direction—as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—in the aggregate of ethical discipline, in the aggregate of concentration, in the aggregate of wisdom, in the aggregate of liberation, and in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; one who wishes to establish them in the fruit of stream-entry and in the fruit of once-returning.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish others in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to establish all those beings in the worlds of the northeast—numbering as many as the sands of the river Ganges—in the aggregate of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*), in the aggregate of concentration (*samādhiskandha*), in the aggregate of wisdom (*prajñāskandha*), in the aggregate of liberation (*vimuktiskandha*), in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha*), and in the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) and the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*).

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings] in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to establish all those beings in the worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the southeastern direction in the aggregate of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*), in the aggregate of concentration (*samādhiskandha*), in the aggregate of wisdom (*prajñāskandha*), in the aggregate of liberation (*vimuktiskandha*), in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha*), and in the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) and the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*).

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings] in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whoever wishes to establish all those beings in the worlds of the south-western direction—numbering as many as the sands of the river Ganges—in the aggregate of ethical discipline, in the aggregate of meditative concentration, in the aggregate of wisdom, in the aggregate of liberation, in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, in the fruit of stream-entry, and in the fruit of once-returning;

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings] in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, [should practice] in the perfection of wisdom.

One should train [in this way]: desiring to establish all those beings in the world systems of the northwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, in the aggregate of ethical discipline; desiring to establish them in the aggregate of concentration; desiring to establish them in the aggregate of wisdom; desiring to establish them in the aggregate of liberation; desiring to establish them in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; desiring to establish them in the fruit of stream-entry; [desiring to establish them] in the fruit of once-returning...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish others in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whoever wishes to establish all those beings in the world systems of the lower direction—as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—in the aggregate of ethical discipline; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of concentration; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of wisdom; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of liberation; who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; who wishes to establish them in the fruit of stream-entry; and who wishes to establish them in the fruit of once-returning.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish others in the fruit of non-returning, who wishes to establish them in arhatship, who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, who wishes to establish them in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, must train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who desires to establish all those beings in the world systems in the upward direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, in the aggregate of ethical discipline.

by one who wishes to establish [beings] in the aggregate of concentration; by one who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of wisdom; by one who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of liberation; by one who wishes to establish them in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; by one who wishes to establish them in the fruit of stream-entry; by one who wishes to establish them in the fruit of once-returning; by one who wishes to establish them in the fruit of non-returning; by one who wishes to establish them in arhatship; by one who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish others in omniscience, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, who wishes to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects, and who wishes to establish them in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to lead all sentient beings, however many there may be in the world systems of the ten directions, to final nirvāṇa by means of both the vehicle of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and the Great Vehicle, should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should train in this way even while giving a gift.

When one gives a gift in such a manner, it becomes of great fruit; by giving a gift in such a manner, one is reborn among the kṣatriya families of great virtue; by giving a gift in such a manner, one is reborn among the brahmin families of great virtue; by giving a gift in such a manner, relying upon that very gift, one is reborn among the gods of the Four Great Kings; by giving a gift in such a manner, relying upon that very gift, one is reborn among the Trāyastriṃśa gods.
Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one is reborn among the Yāma gods; having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one is reborn among the Tuṣita gods.

One is reborn among the gods. Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one is reborn among the Nirmāṇarati gods. Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one is reborn among the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods. Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one attains the first dhyāna. Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one attains the second dhyāna.

Having given such a gift, relying upon that very gift, he enters the third dhyāna. Having given such a gift, relying upon that very gift, he enters the fourth dhyāna. Having given such a gift, relying upon that very gift, he enters the attainment of the sphere of infinite space. Having given such a gift, relying upon that very gift, he enters the attainment of the sphere of infinite consciousness.

Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one enters the meditative attainment of the sphere of nothingness (*ākiñcanyāyatana-samāpatti*). Having given such a gift, by relying on that very gift, one enters the meditative attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana-samāpatti*). Having given such a gift, the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) arise. Having given such a gift, the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) arise. Having given such a gift, the five faculties (*indriya*) arise.

Having given such a gift, the five powers arise; having given such a gift, the seven factors of enlightenment arise; having given such a gift, the noble eightfold path arises; having given such a gift, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—arise; having given such a gift, the fruit of stream-entry is attained; having given such a gift, the fruit of once-returning is attained.

By giving such a gift, the fruit of non-returning is attained; by giving such a gift, arhatship is attained; by giving such a gift, the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha is attained; by giving such a gift, unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is attained. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom understands thus through skill in means.

Giving is given; it fulfills the perfection of generosity. Giving is given; it fulfills the perfection of ethical discipline. Thus giving is given; it fulfills the perfection of patience. Thus giving is given; it fulfills the perfection of vigor. Thus giving is given; it fulfills the perfection of meditative concentration. Thus giving is given; it fulfills the perfection of wisdom.

Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while giving gifts, fulfill the perfection of generosity? Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while guarding ethical discipline, fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline? Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while cultivating patience, fulfill the perfection of patience?"

“Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by exerting vigor, fulfill the perfection of vigor? Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by entering into meditative concentration, fulfill the perfection of concentration? Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by cultivating wisdom, fulfill the perfection of wisdom? The Blessed One said:

Śāradvatīputra, through the yoga of non-apprehension and by means of the complete purity of the three spheres regarding the gift, the giver, and the recipient, the perfection of generosity is fulfilled. By taking into account the state of transgression, non-transgression, and the commission of offenses, the perfection of ethical discipline is fulfilled. By taking into account the state of being unshakable, the perfection of patience is fulfilled. By taking into account the non-exhaustion of vigor in body and mind, the perfection of vigor is fulfilled.

By means of non-distraction and non-confusion, the perfection of meditative concentration is fulfilled; by means of the yoga of the non-apprehension of the wisdom of all phenomena, the perfection of wisdom [is fulfilled].

It becomes fulfilled. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to know and attain all the qualities of a Buddha belonging to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present, should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of phenomena that are both with outflows and without outflows should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of phenomena that are wholesome and unwholesome should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of mundane and supramundane phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of phenomena that are both with form and without form should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of phenomena that are either predicted or not predicted should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of phenomena that are either fixed or unfixed should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of those dharmas that lead to liberation and those that do not lead to liberation should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva who wishes to reach the further shore of those dharmas conducive to decline and those conducive to distinction should [train in the perfection of wisdom].

A mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of those dharmas conducive to the parts [of enlightenment] and those conducive to distinction should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of the dharmas of ordinary persons and the dharmas of the noble ones should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of the dharmas of those in training and the dharmas of those beyond training should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of the dharmas of the śrāvakas and the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of the qualities of a bodhisattva and the qualities of a buddha should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the further shore of all phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to realize the suchness of all phenomena—past, future, and present—should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reach the limit of non-arising of all phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to penetrate the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) of all phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to be a forerunner among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [who wishes to be a forerunner] among all buddhas...

One who wishes to be an attendant to the Blessed Ones should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to be an ultimate attendant to all the Blessed Buddhas should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to have a great retinue should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to obtain the retinues of the bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to purify the sacrificial offerings of all donors should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to have a mind that has grasped generosity should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to separate the mind from immorality should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon a mind of ill-will should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes not to give rise to a mind of indolence should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes not to give rise to a distracted mind should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes not to give rise to a mind of faulty wisdom should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings in the basis of meritorious action consisting of giving should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings in the basis of meritorious action consisting of ethical discipline should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings in the basis of meritorious action consisting of cultivation (bhāvanāmaya-puṇyakriyāvastu) should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings in the basis of meritorious action associated with the modes of deportment (airyāpatha-sahagata-puṇyakriyāvastu) should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings in the bases of meritorious action associated with all medicinal herbs should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to bring the five eyes to completion in every aspect should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to accomplish the supreme eye of the self should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to accomplish the divine eye should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to accomplish the eye of wisdom should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to bring about the eye of dharma should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to bring about the Buddha-eye should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to behold with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems of the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and [who wishes to hear] whatever Dharma those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim—should train in the perfection of wisdom.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to hear all that with the divine ear; who wishes to know the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, by means of their own mind;

who wishes to recollect the bodhisattva conduct associated with the former lives of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and who wishes to behold the various kinds of miraculous transformations of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones—such a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

By one who desires to behold with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems of the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; by one who desires to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; by one who desires to know with his own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and by one who desires to recollect the conduct of a Bodhisattva associated with their former lives, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to behold the manifold kinds of miraculous transformations performed by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Desiring to behold with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems of the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; desiring to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; desiring to know with one's own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and desiring to recollect the bodhisattva conduct associated with their former lives, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to behold the manifold miraculous transformations of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; who wishes to see with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems of the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; and who wishes to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim—must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to hear [this], who wishes to know with his own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; who wishes to recollect the bodhisattva conduct associated with their former lives; and who wishes to behold the manifold miraculous transformations of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones—such a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Desiring to see with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in the world-systems in the northeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; desiring to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; desiring to know with one's own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and [desiring to know] the conduct of a Bodhisattva associated with their former lives—those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to recollect those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and who wishes to behold their manifold miraculous transformations of supernatural power, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Desiring to see with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems of the southeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; desiring to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; desiring to know with his own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and [desiring to know] the conduct of a Bodhisattva associated with their former lives—those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to recollect those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and who wishes to behold their manifold miraculous transformations of supernatural power, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Desiring to see with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the worlds of the south-western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; desiring to hear with the divine ear all that Dharma those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are preaching; desiring to know with one’s own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and [desiring to know] the former lives associated with those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to recollect the conduct of the bodhisattvas and who wishes to behold the manifold miraculous transformations of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Desiring to see with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the worlds of the northwest—worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—and desiring to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; and desiring to know with one’s own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and [desiring to know] the conduct of Bodhisattvas associated with their former lives, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones...
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to recollect those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and who wishes to behold their manifold displays of supernatural power, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

By one who desires to behold with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems in the direction below as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; by one who desires to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; by one who desires to know with his own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and by one who desires to recollect the bodhisattva conduct associated with their former lives—those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems in the direction below as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.
And by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to behold the manifold miraculous transformations of the supernatural power of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, one must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Desiring to behold with the divine eye all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems of the upper direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; desiring to hear with the divine ear all the Dharma that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim; desiring to know with one’s own mind the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and desiring to recollect the bodhisattva conduct associated with their former lives—those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems of the upper direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges... [he should train].

And by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to behold the manifold miraculous transformations of the supernatural powers (*ṛddhi-vikurvita*) of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, [one should train] in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

One must train [in this]. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, having heard all that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, preach—the Dharma they preach throughout all the world-systems in the ten directions—desires to retain it all through the power of an uninterrupted faculty of mindfulness, and desires not to let anything perish during the interval until he has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, [should train] in the perfection of wisdom.

One must train. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to see and wishes to bring to fulfillment the buddha-fields and the purification of the buddha-fields of the Blessed Buddhas of the past, future, and present, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, whatever has been spoken by the Tathāgatas—whether it be discourses (*sūtra*), verses (*geya*), prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), stanzas (*gāthā*), inspired utterances (*udāna*), introductory narratives (*nidāna*), legends (*ityuktaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), extensive teachings (*vaipulya*), or marvelous accounts (*adbhutadharma*)—all of which have not been heard by the disciples: a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to hear all that, who desires to take it up, who desires to retain it, who desires to recite it, who desires to master it, who desires to practice in accordance with suchness (*tathatā*), and who desires to reveal it in detail to others [should apply this method].

One should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—by one who desires to hear it all, who desires to take it up, who desires to retain it, who desires to recite it, who desires to master it, who desires to proclaim it extensively to others, and who desires to practice in accordance with suchness.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the southern direction—all that—desiring to hear it, desiring to take it up, desiring to retain it, desiring to recite it, desiring to master it, desiring to reveal it extensively to others, and desiring to practice therein for the sake of suchness, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in world-systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to hear all that, to take it up, to retain it, to recite it, to master it, to proclaim it in detail to others, and to practice in accordance with suchness therein, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Blessed Buddhas in the northern direction—a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who desires to hear all that, to take it up, to retain it, to recite it, to master it, to reveal it extensively to others, and to practice for the sake of suchness therein, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Blessed Buddhas in the northeastern direction—a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who desires to hear all that, who desires to take it up, who desires to retain it, who desires to recite it, who desires to master it, who desires to reveal it extensively to others, and who desires to practice in accordance with suchness therein, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Blessed Buddhas in the southeastern direction—a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who desires to hear all that, to take it up, to retain it, to recite it, to master it, to proclaim it in detail to others, and to practice in accordance with suchness therein, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the southwestern direction— all that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to hear it, who desires to take it up, who desires to retain it, who desires to recite it, who desires to master it, who desires to reveal it extensively to others, and who desires to practice in accordance with suchness therein, must train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Blessed Buddhas in the northwestern direction—all that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to hear it, to take it up, to retain it, to recite it, to master it, to proclaim it extensively to others, and to practice in accordance with suchness therein, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Blessed Buddhas in the direction below—all that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to hear it, who desires to take it up, who desires to retain it, who desires to recite it, who desires to master it, who desires to reveal it extensively to others, and who desires to practice for the sake of suchness therein, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by all the Blessed Buddhas in the direction above—all that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to hear it, who wishes to take it up, who wishes to retain it, who wishes to recite it, who wishes to master it, who wishes to proclaim it in detail to others, and who wishes to practice accordingly for the sake of suchness, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those world systems in the eastern direction—as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with misery and pervaded by calamity, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those worlds in the southern direction— worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā— which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with misery and pervaded by calamity, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those world-systems in the western direction—as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with calamity and pervaded by misfortune, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those world systems in the northern direction—world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with misfortune and pervaded by calamity, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great miraculous power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those world-systems in the northeastern direction—world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with misfortune and pervaded by evil, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those worlds in the southeastern direction—worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with calamity and pervaded by misfortune, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great miraculous power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those worlds in the southwestern direction— worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā— which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with calamities and pervaded by misfortune, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great influence, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those worlds in the northwestern direction—worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with calamity and pervaded by evil, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those world-systems in the direction below—numbering as many as the sands of the river Ganges—which are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with calamity and pervaded by misfortune, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessing such great miraculous power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light, must train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those world-systems in the direction above—world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges that are shrouded in blinding darkness, filled with misfortune and pervaded by calamity, where even these two, the sun and the moon, though possessed of such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great authority, do not shine, do not glow, and do not radiate light—must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those beings in as many world-systems as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the eastern direction—wherein beings do not hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, or the sound of the Saṅgha—to hear the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, [should practice this].

One should train in the perfection of wisdom. Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the southern direction, comparable in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," or the sound of "Saṅgha"—a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those sentient beings in those world systems to hear the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the western direction, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, or the sound of the Saṅgha—in those world systems, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those sentient beings to hear the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, or the sound of the Saṅgha—in those world systems, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those sentient beings to hear the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the northeastern direction, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, wherein sentient beings do not hear the sound of "Buddha," nor the sound of "Dharma," nor the sound of "Saṅgha"—a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those sentient beings in those world systems to hear the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the southeastern direction, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," or the sound of "Saṅgha"—if one wishes to cause all those sentient beings in those world systems to hear the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings] in right view should train in the perfection of wisdom. Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the southwestern direction, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, or the sound of the Saṅgha—a bodhisattva who wishes to cause all those sentient beings in those world systems to hear the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha [should train in the perfection of wisdom] for the sake of right view.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings in the truth] must train in the perfection of wisdom. Śāradvatīputra, as many world-systems as there are in the northwestern direction, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, or the sound of the Saṅgha—a bodhisattva who wishes to make all those sentient beings in those world-systems hear the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. Śāradvatīputra, as many world systems as there are in the direction below, equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges, wherein sentient beings do not hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," or the sound of "Saṅgha"—a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to cause all those sentient beings in those world systems to hear the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who desires to establish them in right view, [should train in the perfection of wisdom].

One should train in the perfection of wisdom. Śāradvatīputra, as many world-systems as there are in the direction above, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, where sentient beings do not hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," or the sound of "Saṅgha"—a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those sentient beings in those world-systems to hear the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish them in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, those beings who are blind in the world systems of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall by my power see forms with their eyes, and those who are deaf shall hear with their ears.

"Those who are insane shall hear [these] words and regain their mindfulness; those who are naked shall obtain robes; those who are hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink; the sick shall be liberated from diseases; and those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall go according to their desire—by my supernatural power (ṛddhi) and by my majesty (anubhāva). For this reason, that bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."

Śāradvatīputra, those beings who are blind in the world systems of the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall by my power see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; those who are naked shall obtain robes; those who are hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink; the sick shall be liberated from their diseases; and those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall go wherever they desire.

"By my crushing power, by my majesty"—thus should that bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom. Śāradvatīputra, those beings who are blind in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the western direction shall, through my majesty, see forms with their eyes; the deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; the insane shall regain their mindfulness; the naked shall obtain robes; and the hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink.

"The sick shall recover from their diseases, those who have fallen into bondage or imprisonment shall be liberated, and they shall go wherever they desire through my supernatural power and my majesty"—thinking thus, that bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, by my power, those beings who are blind in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the northern direction shall see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; and those who are naked shall obtain robes; likewise those who are hungry and thirsty [shall obtain food and drink].

"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'By my supernatural power and by my majesty, those who are sick shall obtain food and drink, they shall be liberated from diseases, and those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall be able to go wherever they desire.'"

Śāradvatīputra, by my power, those beings who are blind in the worlds of the northeast—numbering as many as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—shall see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; those who are naked shall obtain robes; those who are hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink; and those who are ill shall be liberated from their diseases. Those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall be able to go wherever they desire.

"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'By my power, by my majesty. Śāradvatīputra, those beings who are blind in the world systems of the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall—by my majesty—see forms with their eyes; the deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; the insane shall regain their mindfulness; the naked shall obtain robes; and the hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink."

"A sick person shall recover and be liberated from diseases; those who have fallen into bondage or imprisonment shall be able to go wherever they desire through my supernatural power and my majesty"—thinking thus, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, by my power, those beings who are blind in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the southwestern direction shall see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; those who are naked shall obtain robes; those who are hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink; and those who are ill shall be liberated from their diseases, while those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall go wherever they desire.
"By my supernatural power and by my majesty they will come to be," thus [should it be thought] by a bodhisattva mahāsattva regarding the perfection of wisdom.

One should train thus: "O Śāradvatīputra, by my power, those beings who are blind in the world-systems of the northwestern direction—numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—shall see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; those who are naked shall obtain robes; those who are hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink; and those who are sick or imprisoned in bonds and confinement shall be liberated from their diseases and fetters."

"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'By my supernatural power and by my majesty, they shall be able to go wherever they desire. Śāradvatīputra, those beings who are blind in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the direction below shall, through my majesty, see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; and those who are naked shall obtain robes; and those who are hungry and thirsty..."

"A sick person shall obtain food and drink and be liberated from diseases; those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall go according to their desire through my supernatural power and my majesty"—thus should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, by my power, those beings who are blind in world-systems in the direction above, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, shall see forms with their eyes; those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness; those who are naked shall obtain robes; those who are hungry and thirsty shall obtain food and drink; the sick shall be liberated from their diseases; and those who have fallen into bondage or confinement shall be able to go wherever they desire.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom [with the thought]: "May I crush them; may it be through my power. Why is this? Because those who are there...

In all ten directions, in each direction in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, may those beings who have fallen into the states of no-leisure or the miserable destinies—whether they be denizens of hell, animals, or inhabitants of the realm of Yama—through my power, pass away from there and obtain a human body; and may I, desiring to establish all those beings in ethical discipline (*śīla*), desiring to establish them in meditative concentration (*samādhi*), desiring to establish them in wisdom (*prajñā*), [and] in liberation (*vimukti*)...

by one desiring to establish [beings] in the vision and knowledge of liberation; by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of stream-entry, by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of once-returning, by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of non-returning, by one desiring to establish them in arhatship, by one desiring to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by one desiring to establish them in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), by one desiring to establish them in the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and by one desiring to establish them in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish [beings] therein, and who wishes to establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train in the deportment of a Tathāgata, and who wishes to train in the purity of the conduct and behavior of a Tathāgata—the complete purity of the Tathāgata’s bodily, vocal, and mental actions preceded by wisdom—should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:

"How might I, having looked upon the gaze of the Great Naga, teach the unimpaired Dharma to sentient beings? How might I leap from here with the leap of a lion? How might I stride with the unfailing stride? How might I [cover] the great earth by a mere four finger-breadths?"

"May I travel without touching the ground with my feet. How may I proceed by placing my soles upon thousand-petaled lotuses, without harming the living beings who dwell supported beneath my soles? How may I travel adorning the great earth with my two thousand-spoked wheels on the soles of my feet? How may I cause the great earth to revolve and traverse it in the measure of a single wheel?"

Why should I not wander over the entire earth without being stained by the dust of the earth? Why should I not travel one *yojana*, or two, or three, or four, or five, or ten, or twenty, or thirty, or a hundred *yojanas*, or a thousand *yojanas*, or a hundred thousand *yojanas*, or ten million *yojanas*, or a hundred million *yojanas*, or a billion *yojanas*, or ten billion *yojanas*, or even up to immeasurable or incalculable [distances]?

While wandering and strolling through Buddha-fields that are inconceivable, incomparable, infinite, boundless, ineffable, inexpressible, or even inexpressibly inexpressible, one should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "There is no fruit of the body in my mind. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, should investigate in this way: "Why is it that [the fruit] is not in my two soles? (Note: *kramatalayor* = "of the two soles").

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May I emit hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of light from my two thousand-spoked wheels, pacifying all the sufferings of the unfortunate states and the lower realms, and bringing happiness to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate thus: "How may I [be honored] by the gods of the Four Great Kings' assembly?"

[He was surrounded] by the Trāyastriṃśas, Yāmas, Tuṣitas, Nirmāṇaratis, Paranirmitavaśavartins, Brahmakāyikas, Brahmapurohitas, Brahmapārṣadyas, Mahābrahmans, Ābhās, Parīttābhās, Apramāṇābhās, Ābhāsvaras, Śubhas, Parīttaśubhas, Apramāṇaśubhas, Śubhakṛtsnas, Vṛhas, Parīttavṛhas, Apramāṇavṛhas, Bṛhatphalas, Avṛhas, Atapas, Sudṛśas, Sudarśanas, and Akaniṣṭhas.

Surrounded and honored by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devas, thinking, "I am approaching the seat of awakening," or "I shall approach it," one should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:

Why is it that as I sit at the foot of the Bodhi tree, the gods of the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, the Mahābrahman gods, the Parīttābha gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Vṛha gods, and the Vṛhatphala gods [are present]?

"The gods of the Avṛha heaven, the gods of the Atapa heaven, the gods of the Sudṛśa heaven, the gods of the Sudarśana heaven, the gods of the Akaniṣṭha heaven—[thinking] 'May they make it difficult to traverse,' one should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:

'How might I, seated upon the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), having struck the great earth with my hand adorned with the marks [of a great man], [subdue] Namuci, the black kinsman, along with his retinue?'"

Thinking, "I shall be victorious," one should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way: "How may the ground where I walk, stand, sit, or lie down, once I have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, become composed of diamond? For that purpose, he should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate as follows: "On the very day that I go forth from home, on that same day may I defeat the Kinsman of Darkness together with his assembly, realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, and having realized it, on that very same day may I set in motion the wheel of Dharma."

And as he proceeds, may the stainless, dust-free, and pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena arise for immeasurable and incalculable beings; may the minds of immeasurable and incalculable beings be liberated from the outflows of non-expedient means; and may immeasurable and incalculable beings become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—for this reason, he should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way: "How may it be that when I have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment, I shall have an immeasurable and incalculable saṅgha of śrāvakas; and by a single teaching of the Dharma, there shall be immeasurable and incalculable arhats seated upon a single seat, as well as bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive in their progress toward unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment?"

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May the community of bodhisattvas be immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite; may my lifespan be immeasurable, and may my radiance be truly immeasurable. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should generate this thought: "How may it be that when I have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, even the word 'passion,' 'hatred,' or 'delusion' shall not exist in that buddha-field? Thus one should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should generate this thought: "When I have realized unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, may all sentient beings in that buddha-field be endowed with such wisdom that they would know: 'Excellent is giving! Excellent is self-control! Excellent is the holy life! Excellent is non-violence toward all living beings!'"

One should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should generate this thought: "How may it be that even the sound of the disappearance of my true dharma after I have passed into parinirvāṇa does not occur? Thus should one train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should generate this thought: [as before].

Thinking, "How might sentient beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges become destined for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment merely by hearing my name? one should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Śāradvatīputra, at the time when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, produces these qualities, at that time the four great kings become joyful and think: "We shall here set down four bowls, those which were set down by former great kings for former Tathāgatas."
The gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven become joyful; the Yāma gods become joyful; the Tuṣita gods become joyful; the Nirmāṇarati gods become joyful.

The gods who exercise power over the creations of others become joyful, thinking: "We too shall perform the work of attending upon and serving him. Thus, the hosts of asuras will diminish, while the divine hosts will increase; the gods of the Brahma-realm become joyful, the gods who are ministers of Brahmā become joyful, the gods who are the retinue of Brahmā become joyful, and the gods of Mahābrahmā become joyful.

The gods of Limited Light become joyful; the gods of Immeasurable Light become joyful; the gods of Radiant Purity become joyful; the gods of Limited Beauty become joyful; the gods of Immeasurable Beauty become joyful; the gods of Pervasive Beauty become joyful; the gods of Vastness become joyful; the gods of Limited Vastness become joyful; the gods of Immeasurable Vastness become joyful.

The Bṛhatphala gods become joyful; the Avṛha gods become joyful; the Atapa gods become joyful; the Sudṛśa gods become joyful; the Sudarśana gods become joyful; and the Akaniṣṭha gods [think], "We shall entreat this one who has attained perfect awakening to turn the wheel of Dharma. Śāradvatīputra, at whatever time a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, increases [in virtue].

At that time, those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, being delighted by the six perfections, will think: "We shall become the mother and father, brothers, sisters, wives, sons, daughters, friends, ministers, kinsmen, and companions of this Great Being, rejoicing together with him."
