It is neither appropriate nor inappropriate to say that the fruit of the once-returner exists or does not exist; it is neither appropriate nor inappropriate to say that arhatship exists or does not exist; it is neither appropriate nor inappropriate to say that the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha exists or does not exist; it is neither appropriate nor inappropriate to say that the knowledge of the aspects of the path exists or does not exist; it is neither appropriate nor inappropriate to say that the knowledge of all aspects exists or does not exist.
Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in this way is said to be engaged in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of generosity; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of ethical discipline; he does not [practice the perfection of wisdom] for the sake of the perfection of patience.

He practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the perfection of wisdom; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of vigor; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of meditation; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the perfection of wisdom itself; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of internal emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of external emptiness.

He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of internal-external emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of great emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of ultimate emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of conditioned emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of unconditioned emptiness.

He does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of absolute emptiness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of non-dispersal; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of all phenomena; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of specific characteristics.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of non-apprehension; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of non-existence; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the stage of non-retrogression; and one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of maturing sentient beings.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of purifying a buddha-field; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the foundations of mindfulness; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the right efforts; nor for the sake of the bases of psychic power.

One practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the [five] faculties; one practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the [five] powers; one practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the [seven] factors of enlightenment; one practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the noble eightfold path; one practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the noble truths; one practices the perfection of wisdom not for the sake of the meditative absorptions.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the immeasurables; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the formless attainments; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eight liberations; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the nine successive meditative attainments; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of emptiness; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the signless.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the wishless; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the superknowledges; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the concentrations; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the gateways of mnemonic formulas; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the ten powers of a Tathāgata; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four grounds of self-confidence.

One does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the four analytical knowledges; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of great loving-kindness; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of great compassion; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of suchness; one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the realm of phenomena;
one does not practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the limit of reality.

For what reason? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom does not perceive the disintegration, differentiation, or distinction of any dharma whatsoever. Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in this manner is to be called "engaged in the perfection of wisdom."

He does not course in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the divine eye; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the divine ear; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of knowledge of others' minds; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of recollection of past lives; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of supernormal powers; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows.

For what reason? Because, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, he does not even perceive the perfection of wisdom itself, let alone the bodhisattva; how much less could he apprehend all aspects or all superknowledges? Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in this way is to be called "engaged in the perfection of wisdom."

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it does not occur to him: "Abiding in the bases of miraculous power, I shall honor, revere, respect, and worship all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā."

It does not occur to him: "Abiding in the bases of psychic power, I shall honor, revere, respect, and worship all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges. It does not occur to him: "Abiding in the bases of psychic power, I shall honor, revere, respect, and worship all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in world-systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges."

It does not occur to him: "Abiding in the bases of psychic power, I shall honor, revere, respect, and worship all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems of the upward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges. "I shall recollect their former abodes; with the divine eye, I shall see all of them—those passing away, those being reborn, and those already reborn; I shall bring immeasurable and incalculable beings to final nirvāṇa. In this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is to be called "engaged in the perfection of wisdom."

In this way, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom, those who seek flaws or search for an opportunity to harm him find no such opportunity. Furthermore, whatever mundane or supramundane tasks there may be, they are all rendered effortless; and whatever mundane afflictions he may have, they are all utterly destroyed without effort or conceptualization.

And those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems of the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking: "May he not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.

Moreover, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in the world systems of the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking: "May he not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha."

And those who are the four great kings, the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, the Mahābrahmans, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Parīttābha gods, the Apramāṇābha gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Vṛha gods, the Parīttavṛha gods, the Apramāṇavṛha gods, the Vṛhatphala gods, the Avṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods—they too.

They protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects there may be, they all cease to exist for him entirely in this very life. For what reason? Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*).

And those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems in the northeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva so that he may not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.

And those who are the four great kings, the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, the Mahābrahmaṇas, the Ābhā gods, the Parīttābhā gods, the Apramāṇābhā gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Vṛha gods, the Parīttavṛha gods, the Apramāṇavṛha gods, the Vṛhatphala gods, the Avṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods—they [all came].

They also protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects there may be, they all cease to exist for him entirely in this very life. For what reason? Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*).

And those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems of the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, lest he fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.

And those who are the four great kings; the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods; the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmapārṣadya gods, as well as the Mahābrahmans; the Ābhā, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, and Ābhāsvara gods; the Śubha, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna gods; the Vṛha, Parīttavṛha, Apramāṇavṛha, and Vṛhatphala gods; the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods—they too [were present].

They protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects there may be, they all cease to exist for him entirely in this very life. Why is that? It is because the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*). And as for those [beings] in the southwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges...
In all world-systems, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, also protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva so that he may not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.

And those who are the four great kings; the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods; the gods of the Brahma-realm, the Brahmapurohitas, the Brahmapārṣadyas, and the Mahābrahmans; the Ābhāsvara gods—namely, the Ābhāsvaras, the Parīttābhas, the Apramāṇābhas, and the Ābhāsvaras; the Śubha gods—namely, the Śubhas, the Parīttaśubhas, the Apramāṇaśubhas, and the Śubhakṛtsnas; the Bṛhat gods—namely, the Bṛhats, the Parīttabṛhats, the Apramāṇabṛhats, and the Bṛhatphalas; and the Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods.

They also protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects there may be, they all cease to exist for him entirely in this very life. For what reason? Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*).

Moreover, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems of the northwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, lest he fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.

And those who are the four great kings; the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods; the gods of the Brahma-realm, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, and the Mahābrahmans; the Ābhā gods, the Parīttābhā gods, the Apramāṇābhā gods, and the Ābhāsvara gods; the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, and the Śubhakṛtsna gods; the Vṛha gods, the Parīttavṛha gods, the Apramāṇavṛha gods, and the Vṛhatphala gods; the Avṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods—they [all came].

They also protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever bodily defects there may be, they all completely and entirely cease for him in this very life.

This is why it is so: for the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*). Furthermore, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world systems of the lower direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May he not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha."

And those who are the four great kings; the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods; the gods of Brahmā’s retinue, the Brahmapurohitas, the Brahmapārṣadyas, and the Mahābrahmans; the Ābhāsvara gods, the Parīttābhas, the Apramāṇābhas, and the Ābhāsvaras; the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubhas, the Apramāṇaśubhas, and the Śubhakṛtsnas; the Vṛha gods, the Parīttavṛhas, the Apramāṇavṛhas, and the Vṛhatphalas; the Avṛhas, the Atapas, the Sudṛśas, the Sudarśanas, and the Akaniṣṭha gods—they [all came].

They also protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva, thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects there may be, they all cease to exist for him entirely in this very life. Why is that? Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*).

Moreover, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are in the worlds of the upper direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they too protect that bodhisattva mahāsattva so that he may not fall into the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha.

And those who are the four great kings, the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, the Mahābrahmans, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Parīttābha gods, the Apramāṇābha gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Vṛha gods, the Parīttavṛha gods, the Apramāṇavṛha gods, the Vṛhatphala gods, the Avṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods— they too [approached] that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

They protect [him], thinking, "May no one whatsoever create an obstacle for this bodhisattva mahāsattva. Furthermore, whatever physical defects there may be, they all cease to exist for him entirely in this very life. For what reason? Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva pervades all sentient beings with loving-kindness (*maitrī*). Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in this manner should be said to be "engaged in the perfection of wisdom" (*prajñāpāramitā-yukta*)."

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the gateways of dhāraṇīs, the gateways of the samādhis, and the gateways of the analytical knowledges of eloquence appear without difficulty. In all places of rebirth, he pleases the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas, and he is never separated from those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, until he awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it does not occur to him: "There is any dharma that is conjoined with or disjoined from other dharmas; or that is equal to or unequal to them. Why is that? Because he does not perceive any such dharma that would be conjoined or disjoined, or that would be equal or unequal.

In this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom should be said to be "engaged. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in the perfection of wisdom, it does not occur to him: "Might I fully awaken to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), or might I not fully awaken to it? Why is that? Because indeed, one has not fully awakened to the realm of phenomena, one does not fully awaken to it, and one will not fully awaken to it.
In this way indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom should be said to be "engaged.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom does not perceive anything whatsoever as being separate from the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). In this way indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom should be said to be "engaged."

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not make a distinction between the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) and phenomena (dharmas). In this way indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom is to be called "engaged" (yukta).

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it does not occur to him: "I shall penetrate the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). For he does not perceive any phenomenon by which any phenomenon might be penetrated. Thus, he does not apply himself to the thought that the realm of phenomena is empty, nor does he apply himself to the thought that it is not empty.
In this way indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom is to be called "engaged."

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not conjoin form with emptiness, nor does he conjoin emptiness with form. He does not conjoin feeling with emptiness, nor does he conjoin emptiness with feeling. He does not conjoin perception with emptiness, nor does he conjoin emptiness with perception. He does not conjoin volitional formations with emptiness, nor does he conjoin emptiness with volitional formations.

One does not join consciousness with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with consciousness. One does not join the eye with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with the eye. One does not join the ear with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with the ear. One does not join the nose with emptiness...

He does not join emptiness with the nose, nor does he join the tongue with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the tongue; he does not join the body with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the body; he does not join the mind with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the mind; he does not join form with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with form; he does not join sound with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with sound.

One does not associate odor with emptiness, nor does one associate emptiness with odor. One does not associate taste with emptiness, nor does one associate emptiness with taste. One does not associate tangibles with emptiness, nor does one associate emptiness with tangibles. One does not associate mental phenomena with emptiness, nor does one associate emptiness with mental phenomena. One does not associate the eye-element with emptiness, nor does one associate emptiness with the eye-element.

He does not join the form-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the form-element. He does not join the eye-consciousness-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the eye-consciousness-element. He does not join the ear-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the ear-element. He does not join the sound-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the sound-element.

He does not join the ear-consciousness element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the ear-consciousness element. He does not join the nose element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the nose element. He does not join the odor element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the odor element. He does not join the nose-consciousness element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the nose-consciousness element.

He does not join the tongue-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the tongue-element; he does not join the taste-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the taste-element; [he does not join] the tongue-consciousness-element...

One joins [them] with emptiness, yet one does not join emptiness with the tongue-consciousness element; one does not join the body element with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with the body element; one does not join the tangible-object element with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with the tangible-object element; one does not join the body-consciousness element with emptiness, nor does one join emptiness with the body-consciousness element.

He does not join the mind-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the mind-element. He does not join the phenomena-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the phenomena-element. He does not join the form-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the form-element. He does not join the eye-consciousness-element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the eye-consciousness-element.

He does not join the mind-consciousness element with emptiness, nor does he join emptiness with the mind-consciousness element. Why is that? For this, Śāradvatīputra, is the supreme yoga, namely, the yoga of emptiness. Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in emptiness, he does not fall into the level of the śrāvakas or the level of the pratyekabuddhas; rather, he purifies the buddha-field and brings sentient beings to maturity.

And he quickly awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Śāradvatīputra, whatever yogas there may be, the yoga of the perfection of wisdom is declared among them to be the foremost, the eldest, the best, the most excellent, the most preeminent, and the most sublime. Why is that? Because this yoga is unsurpassed; namely, the yoga of the perfection of wisdom, the yoga of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in this way is to be called "one who has received a prophecy."

And having drawn near to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who applies himself in this way, Śāradvatīputra, acts for the benefit of immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings.

He practices; yet it does not occur to him: "I am engaged in or dissociated from the perfection of wisdom"; "the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will grant me a prophecy"; "I have become near to receiving a prophecy"; "I shall purify a Buddha-field"; "I shall bring sentient beings to maturity"; "having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I shall turn the wheel of Dharma. For what reason? Because, in such a way...

He distinguishes the dharmadhātu; he does not perceive any dharma whatsoever as other than the dharmadhātu—whether it be one who would course in the perfection of wisdom, or one who would be prophesied by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, or one who would fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is that? Because when a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom, the notion of a "being" (sattva-saṃjñā) does not arise, nor does the notion of a "self" (ātma-saṃjñā) arise.

The notion of a living soul does not arise; the notion of a creature does not arise; the notion of a nourisher does not arise; the notion of a person does not arise; the notion of an individual does not arise; the notion of a human being does not arise; the notion of a descendant of Manu does not arise; the notion of an agent does not arise; the notion of an experiencer does not arise; the notion of a knower does not arise; the notion of a seer does not arise.

For what reason? Because, in this way, a sentient being is absolutely neither produced nor ceased; for there is no production or cessation of a sentient being. And how could that which has neither production nor cessation [be perceived]? How indeed?

He will course in the perfection of wisdom. Coursing in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom by way of the non-arising of sentient beings; he courses in the perfection of wisdom by way of the emptiness of sentient beings; he courses in the perfection of wisdom by way of the non-apprehension of sentient beings; he courses in the perfection of wisdom by way of the solitude of sentient beings; he courses in the perfection of wisdom by way of the nature of sentient beings; he courses in the perfection of wisdom by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of sentient beings. This, Śāradvatīputra, is the supreme [practice] of the bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Yoga is indeed the yoga of the perfection of wisdom; Śāradvatīputra, this is the yoga of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, which stands surpassing all other yogas.

And here, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing this yoga brings forth the ten powers of a Tathāgata; he brings forth the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Here, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing this yoga does not give rise to a mind of stinginess.

He does not give rise to a mind of immorality, a mind of malice, a mind of laziness, a mind of distraction, or a mind of faulty wisdom. When this had been said, the venerable Śāradvatīputra addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, from where has that bodhisattva mahāsattva who dwells in this yoga of the perfection of wisdom passed away to be reborn here? Or, having passed away from here, where will he be reborn?"

The Blessed One said: "Śāradvatīputra, it should be known that whichever bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells by means of this yoga of the perfection of wisdom has passed away from other buddha-fields and been reborn here. Or, it should be known that he has passed away from the Tuṣita host of gods or from among humans and been reborn here. In this regard, Śāradvatīputra, as for this bodhisattva mahāsattva who has passed away from other buddha-fields and been reborn here..."

He quickly enters this yoga, namely, the yoga of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Even after he has passed away from that birth, these profound dharmas become manifest to him, and subsequently he enters the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. In whichever Buddha-fields the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas reside, stay, and maintain themselves, there he is reborn; and he pleases those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

In this regard, Śāradvatīputra, it should be understood that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has descended from the Tuṣita host of gods and been reborn here. Indeed, being bound by only one more birth, his six perfections remain undiminished; all the gateways of dhāraṇīs and the gateways of samādhis are contained therein. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, there is the bodhisattva mahāsattva who, having passed away from among humans, is reborn into the very same class of humanity.

With the exception of an irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattva, that bodhisattva mahāsattva possesses auspicious faculties; yet he does not quickly enter into this yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Having passed away from one buddhafield, he will migrate to another buddhafield where Buddhas, Blessed Ones, currently reside, stay, and maintain themselves.
He shall never be separated from the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, until he has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, being unskilled in means, enter the first dhyāna; they enter the second dhyāna; they enter the third dhyāna; they enter the fourth dhyāna; and they practice the six perfections. By virtue of their attainment of dhyāna, they are reborn among the long-lived gods. If they subsequently obtain a human birth, they please the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, yet their faculties become dull and not sharp.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who enter into the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) and course in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), yet being unskilled in means (anupāyakauśala), they relinquish those meditative absorptions and are reborn once again in the desire realm (kāmadhātu). For these bodhisattva mahāsattvas as well, Śāradvatīputra, the faculties (indriya) become sluggish; it is not so for others.

They are sharp. Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who enter the first dhyāna; they enter the second dhyāna; they enter the third dhyāna; they enter the fourth dhyāna; they enter loving-kindness; they enter compassion; they enter sympathetic joy; they enter equanimity; they enter the sphere of infinite space; and they enter the sphere of infinite consciousness.

They enter the sphere of nothingness; they enter the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; they enter the four foundations of mindfulness; they enter the four right efforts; they enter the four bases of psychic power; they enter the five faculties; they enter the five powers; they enter the seven factors of enlightenment; they enter the noble eightfold path; they enter great compassion.

Being possessed of great compassion, through their skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*), they do not take rebirth by the power of meditative absorption (*dhyāna*), nor by the power of the divine abodes (*brāhmavihāra*), nor by the power of the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*). Rather, they are reborn wherever the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, reside, stay, and maintain themselves. Furthermore, never being separated from the yoga of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they shall realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (*anuttarā samyaksambodhi*) right here in this Fortunate Aeon (*bhadrakalpa*).

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, who enter the first dhyāna; they enter the second dhyāna; they enter the third dhyāna; they enter the fourth dhyāna; they enter loving-kindness (maitrī); they enter great compassion (mahākaruṇā); they enter sympathetic joy (muditā); they enter equanimity (upekṣā); they enter the sphere of infinite space (ākāśānantyāyatana); and they enter the sphere of infinite consciousness (vijñānānantyāyatana).

They enter the sphere of nothingness; they enter the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. And by means of skillful means, through the power of their meditations, concentrations, and attainments, they take birth. They are born again here in this desire realm—born into great kṣatriya families, born into great brahmin families, and born into great householder families—for the sake of maturing sentient beings, and not out of a longing for further existence.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, who enter the first dhyāna; they enter the second dhyāna; they enter the third dhyāna; they enter the fourth dhyāna. They enter loving-kindness; they enter compassion; they enter sympathetic joy; they enter equanimity. They enter the sphere of infinite space; they enter the sphere of infinite consciousness.

They enter the sphere of nothingness; they enter the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. By means of skillful means, and not by means of the power of meditative absorptions, concentrations, and attainments, they are reborn in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings; they are reborn in the company of the gods of the Thirty-three; they are reborn in the company of the Yāma gods; they are reborn in the company of the Tuṣita gods.

They are reborn in the assembly of the Nirmāṇarati gods; they are reborn in the assembly of the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods. Abiding there, they bring sentient beings to maturity, purify a buddha-field, and please the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones. Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, enter the first dhyāna through skillful means.
They enter the second dhyāna; they enter the third dhyāna; they enter the fourth dhyāna; they enter loving-kindness; they enter compassion.

They attain sympathetic joy; they attain equanimity; they attain the sphere of infinite space; they attain the sphere of infinite consciousness; they attain the sphere of nothingness; they attain the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Having passed away from here, they are reborn in the Brahma-world, where they become Brahmās, Great Brahmās.

Those who are masters, living for a thousand years—the foremost, excellent, most eminent, and most supreme among those beings—remaining there, travel from buddha-field to buddha-field. Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, turn the wheel of Dharma, they entreat those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas bound to only one more birth who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through skill in means enter the first dhyāna; they enter the second dhyāna; they enter the third dhyāna; they enter the fourth dhyāna; they enter loving-kindness; they enter compassion; they enter sympathetic joy; and they enter equanimity.

They enter the meditative attainment of the sphere of infinite space; they enter the meditative attainment of the sphere of infinite consciousness; they enter the meditative attainment of the sphere of nothingness; they enter the meditative attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. They cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness; they cultivate the four right efforts; they cultivate the five faculties; they cultivate the seven factors of awakening; they cultivate the noble eightfold path.

They enter into the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, yet they are not reborn under their influence. Having pleased the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who have appeared before them, and having practiced the holy life there, they are reborn in the company of the Tuṣita gods. There, they...

Having remained for the duration of their lifespan with unimpaired faculties, mindful and clearly comprehending, surrounded and honored by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of deities, they manifest rebirth here, and having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they turn the wheel of Dharma in various buddha-fields.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having attained the six supernormal knowledges, are reborn in the desire realm and are not reborn in the formless realm; they travel from buddhafield to buddhafield, honoring, revering, respecting, and making offerings to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the six superknowledges; sporting with those superknowledges, they travel from buddhafield to buddhafield, to those buddhafields where even the sound of the vehicle of the hearers or the vehicle of the solitary buddhas is not heard, except for the vehicle of the buddhas.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the six superknowledges; sporting with those superknowledges, they travel from buddhafield to buddhafield, to those buddhafields where the lifespan of sentient beings is not predetermined.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having attained the six higher knowledges, travel to world systems where the sound of "Buddha" is not heard, nor the sound of "Dharma," nor the sound of "Saṅgha. Having gone there, they proclaim the praise of the Buddha and proclaim the praise of the Dharma and the Saṅgha. Those beings, their minds having become serene through that sound of "Buddha" and the sound of "Saṅgha," are reborn wherever the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, reside.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, from the first production of the thought of awakening, have attained the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the five superknowledges, and the four applications of mindfulness.

Those who have attained the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, are never reborn in the desire realm, nor are they reborn in the form realm, nor are they reborn in the formless realm; yet, even there, they act for the benefit of sentient beings.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the six perfections, enter the bodhisattva’s certainty by the very first production of the thought of awakening, or they attain the stage of non-retrogression.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, who, by the very first production of the thought of awakening, fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Having fully awakened, they turn the wheel of the true Dharma and, having accomplished the welfare of immeasurable and incalculable beings, pass into final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder. For those who have passed into final nirvāṇa, the true Dharma remains for an eon or for the remainder of an eon.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, by the very first production of the thought of awakening, enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas, they travel from buddhafield to buddhafield in order to behold the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to bring sentient beings to maturity, and to purify the buddhafields.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, are attainers of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; they sport in manifold ways with those dhyānas, immeasurables, and formless attainments.

That is to say: they enter the first dhyāna; then, emerging from the first dhyāna, they enter the attainment of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*); emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the second dhyāna; emerging from the second dhyāna, they enter the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the third dhyāna; and emerging from the third dhyāna, they enter the attainment of cessation.

Emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the fourth dhyāna; emerging from the fourth dhyāna, they enter the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the sphere of infinite space; emerging from the sphere of infinite space, they enter the attainment of cessation; emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the sphere of infinite consciousness.

Emerging from the sphere of infinite consciousness, they enter the attainment of cessation. Emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the sphere of nothingness. Emerging from the sphere of nothingness, they enter the attainment of cessation. Emerging from the attainment of cessation, they enter the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Emerging from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, they enter the attainment of cessation.

In this way, Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva mahāsattvas practicing in the perfection of wisdom, being endowed with skillful means, enter into these meditative concentrations, immeasurables, and meditative absorptions and attainments after having clearly distinguished them.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the four foundations of mindfulness, who have attained the four right efforts, who have attained the four bases of psychic power, who have attained the five faculties, who have attained the five powers, who have attained the seven factors of enlightenment, who have attained the noble eightfold path, who have attained the four noble truths, who have attained the meditative concentrations, and who have attained the four immeasurables.

They are attainers of the four formless attainments; attainers of the eight liberations; attainers of the nine successive meditative absorptions; attainers of the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; attainers of the superknowledges; attainers of the concentrations; attainers of the gateways to the dhāraṇīs; attainers of the ten powers of a Tathāgata; attainers of the four grounds of self-confidence; attainers of the four analytical knowledges; [attainers] of the eighteen...

They are attainers of the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) and attainers of the three gateways to liberation (vimokṣamukha), yet they do not realize the fruit of stream-entry; they do not realize the fruit of once-returning; they do not realize the fruit of non-returning; they do not realize arhatship; and they do not realize the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.

Practicing the perfection of wisdom and embraced by skillful means, they demonstrate the noble eightfold path to sentient beings, by which those beings attain the fruit of stream-entry, attain the fruit of once-returning, attain the fruit of non-returning, attain arhatship, and attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha.

Śāradvatīputra, that which is the knowledge of the attainment of the fruits by Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas is the *kṣānti* (receptive patience) of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva. Śāradvatīputra, those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who dwell in this manner through this very *prajñāpāramitā* should be known as irreversible (*avaivarttika*). Śāradvatīputra, there are Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who, being well-established in the six *pāramitās*, purify the Tuṣita heaven. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas should be known as belonging to the Fortunate Aeon (*bhadrakalpika*).

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, are attainers of the four dhyānas, attainers of the four immeasurables, attainers of the four formless attainments, and [attainers] of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.

They are possessors of the six superknowledges (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*), possessors of the ten powers of a Tathāgata (*daśa-tathāgata-bala*), possessors of the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*), possessors of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and possessors of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*aṣṭādaśāveṇika-buddhadharma*). They practice here for the sake of realization regarding the four truths, yet they do not penetrate those truths. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas should be known as being bound by only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*).

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, practicing the six perfections, travel from world-system to world-system; there they incite sentient beings toward awakening and purify buddha-fields. Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment after immeasurable and incalculable eons.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the six perfections, are constantly and diligently devoted to the sake of sentient beings; they never utter speech associated with what is unbeneficial, nor do they perform actions of body, speech, or mind associated with what is unbeneficial.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the six perfections and devoted therein to the sake of sentient beings, travel from buddha-field to buddha-field while cutting off the three paths of the lower realms for sentient beings.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the six perfections and placing the perfection of generosity foremost, provide every means of happiness for all sentient beings: food to those seeking food, drink to those seeking drink, vehicles to those seeking vehicles, flowers to those seeking flowers, perfumes to those seeking perfumes, garlands to those seeking garlands, ointments to those seeking ointments, and beds and seats to those seeking beds and seats.

They provide clothing to those who need clothing, ornaments to those who need ornaments, means of livelihood to those who need a livelihood, and shelter to those who need shelter; they supply appropriate requisites for life.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections and placing the perfection of ethical discipline at the forefront, establish sentient beings in the restraint of body, speech, and mind. Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections and placing the perfection of patience at the forefront, establish sentient beings in freedom from anger and malice.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections and placing the perfection of vigor at the forefront, establish sentient beings in the application of all wholesome dharmas.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections and placing the perfection of meditative concentration at the forefront, establish sentient beings in tranquility, one-pointedness, and seclusion from sensual desires.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the six perfections and placing the perfection of wisdom at the forefront, manifest a physical body exactly like the form of a Tathāgata, and teach the Dharma to beings in the hells, beings born in the animal realm, and beings in the world of Yama, so that they may completely transcend all miserable states of existence.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the six perfections, manifest a physical body exactly like the form of a Buddha, and having approached buddha-fields in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings.

They attend upon the Tathāgatas and listen to the Dharma; they behold the assembly of Bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields. Having taken up those emanated [qualities] in those Buddha-fields, they bring forth even more sublime and distinguished Buddha-fields, and Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas bound to one more birth are established in those Buddha-fields.

Having approached as many Buddha-fields in the southern direction as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings; they attend upon the Tathāgatas and listen to the Dharma; and they behold the assembly of Bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of those Buddha-fields.

Having taken those emanated [lands] in those buddha-fields, they bring about even more magnificent and more distinguished buddha-fields; and bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being born only once more are produced in those buddha-fields. Having approached buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the western direction, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings and attend upon the Tathāgatas.

They hear the Dharma and behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields. Taking up those emanated [fields] therein, they bring about even more sublime and distinguished buddha-fields; and bodhisattva mahāsattvas bound by only one more birth are established in those buddha-fields.

Having approached Buddha-fields in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings; they attend upon the Tathāgatas, listen to the Dharma, and behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of those Buddha-fields.

Having taken those emanated [Buddha-fields] in those Buddha-fields, they bring about even more magnificent and more distinguished Buddha-fields; and Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being bound to only one more birth are produced in those Buddha-fields. Having approached as many Buddha-fields in the northeastern direction as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings and to the Tathāgatas.

They attend upon them, hear the Dharma, and behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields. Having taken up those emanated [qualities] in those buddha-fields, they bring about even more exalted and more distinguished buddha-fields. And bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being "born with only one more birth" (ekajātipratilabdha) are perfected in those buddha-fields.

Having approached Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the southeastern direction, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings, attend upon the Tathāgatas, and listen to the Dharma. They behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of those Buddha-fields. Taking up emanated [forms] in those Buddha-fields, they bring forth even more sublime and distinguished Buddha-fields.

And bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being born only once more are reborn in those buddha-fields. Having approached buddha-fields in the southwestern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings; they attend upon the Tathāgatas, listen to the Dharma, and behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields.

Having taken those emanated [lands] in those buddha-fields, they bring about even more magnificent and more distinguished buddha-fields. And bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being born only once more are produced in those buddha-fields. Having approached buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the northwestern direction, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings, attend upon the Tathāgatas, and listen to the Dharma.

They behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields. Taking up emanated [forms] in those buddha-fields, they bring about even more sublime and distinguished buddha-fields. Bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being born only once more are produced there in those buddha-fields. Having approached buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the downward direction, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings.
They attend upon the Tathāgatas, listen to the Dharma, and behold the assembly of Bodhisattvas as well as the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields.

They behold them; having taken up those emanated [lands] in those Buddha-fields, they bring forth even more magnificent and more distinguished Buddha-fields. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being born only once more are produced in those Buddha-fields. Having approached Buddha-fields in the upward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings, attend upon the Tathāgatas, and listen to the Dharma.

They behold the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields. Taking up those emanated [qualities] within those buddha-fields, they bring about even more sublime and distinguished buddha-fields; and bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have attained the state of being born only once more are produced in those buddha-fields.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the six perfections, become endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, yet they remain possessed of faculties that are refined but not yet completely purified. Through those various purified physical forms, they generate joy and serene confidence in many people, and they become beloved by many people.

And those beings become pleasing because of that very root of merit from their mental clarity; they gradually attain final nirvana through the three vehicles. In this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should train in the purity of body, should train in the purity of speech, and should train in the purity of mind.
Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas [established] in the six perfections.
Practicing, they acquire refined faculties; with those refined faculties, they exalt themselves but do not disparage others.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, from the first production of the thought of awakening, abide in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, and never fall into poverty; they do not fall into the miserable states or the lower realms, until they reach the stage of non-retrogression.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, from the first production of the thought of awakening, never abandon the ten paths of wholesome action until they reach the stage of non-retrogression.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, become universal monarchs (cakravartin). They establish sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action and gather them through generosity and pleasant speech.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, established in the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline, assume many universal monarchies and exercise the rule of many hundreds of thousands of universal monarchies. Remaining therein, they please many hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshipping those Blessed Buddhas with all necessaries and every form of worship.
Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections, themselves bring forth the illumination of the eightfold dharma for sentient beings who hold wrong views.

And by that illumination of the Dharma, they are never separated from it until they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. This, Śāradvatīputra, is the arising of Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, with respect to the Buddha-dharmas. Therefore, Śāradvatīputra, a Bodhisattva, Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not allow any opportunity for faulty actions of body, speech, or mind.

When this had been said, the venerable Śāradvatīputra addressed the Blessed One as follows: “Blessed One, what is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s faulty bodily action, faulty vocal action, or faulty mental action? The Blessed One replied: “Śāradvatīputra, it is when it occurs to the bodhisattva mahāsattva: ‘This is the body by which I would initiate bodily activity; this is the speech by which I would initiate vocal activity.’”

"This is the mind by which I might initiate mental activity. Śāradvatīputra, this is the initiation of faulty actions of body, speech, and mind for a bodhisattva mahāsattva. For, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not perceive a body; he does not perceive speech; he does not perceive a mind.

“Śāradvatīputra, it should not be understood in this way: that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, would give rise to a mind of stinginess with whatever body, speech, or mind; or would give rise to a mind of immorality, a mind of malice, a mind of laziness, a mind of distraction, or a mind of faulty wisdom—it is impossible for such a thing to occur. Furthermore, it is impossible that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, would give rise to physical corruption, verbal corruption, or mental corruption.”

For what reason? Because, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six perfections, he purifies the corruption of body, he purifies the corruption of speech, and he purifies the corruption of mind. This is the irreproachable bodily action, the irreproachable vocal action, and the irreproachable mental action of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. [Śāradvatīputra] asked: "But how, Blessed One, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify the corruption of body, purify the corruption of speech, and purify the corruption of mind?"

The Blessed One said: "Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive the body, does not perceive speech, and does not perceive the mind—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies the corruption of body, purifies the corruption of speech, and purifies the corruption of mind."

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, from the first production of the thought of awakening (prathamacittotpāda) onward, a bodhisattva mahāsattva undertakes and abides in the ten paths of wholesome action (daśakuśalakarmapatha). He does not give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or the mind of a pratyekabuddha. And toward all sentient beings, his mind of great compassion (mahākaruṇācitta) is constantly and continuously present.
In this way, I declare that the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s corruption of body, corruption of speech, and corruption of mind are completely purified.

“Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom and purifying the bodhisattva path, practice the perfection of generosity; they practice the perfection of ethical discipline; they practice the perfection of patience; they practice the perfection of vigor; they practice the perfection of meditative concentration. [Śāradvatīputra] asked: “Blessed One, what is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s path to awakening? The Blessed One replied:

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not apprehend the body; he does not apprehend speech; he does not apprehend the mind; he does not apprehend the perfection of generosity; he does not apprehend the perfection of ethical discipline; he does not apprehend the perfection of patience; he does not apprehend the perfection of vigor; he does not apprehend the perfection of meditative concentration; he does not apprehend the perfection of wisdom; and he does not apprehend the vehicle of the śrāvakas.

One does not apprehend the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, nor does one apprehend the vehicle of the Samyaksambuddhas. Śāradvatīputra, this is the path to enlightenment for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; that is to say, it is the state of neither taking up nor casting away all phenomena due to their non-apprehension. Śāradvatīputra, by means of this path, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas proceed while practicing the six perfections; they cannot be crushed by anyone.

He asked: "Blessed One, practicing in what manner do bodhisattva mahāsattvas become invincible? The Blessed One replied: "When bodhisattva mahāsattvas, practicing in the six perfections, do not conceive of form, do not conceive of feeling, do not conceive of perception, do not conceive of mental formations, and do not conceive of consciousness; when they do not conceive of the eye and forms, do not conceive of the ear and sounds, and do not conceive of the nose and odors."

They do not conceive of tastes of the tongue; they do not conceive of touches of the body; they do not conceive of mental objects. They do not conceive of the earth element; they do not conceive of the water element; they do not conceive of the fire element; they do not conceive of the wind element; they do not conceive of the space element; they do not conceive of the consciousness element. They do not conceive of the eye element; they do not conceive of the form element; they do not conceive of the eye-consciousness element.

They do not conceive of the ear-element; they do not conceive of the sound-element; they do not conceive of the ear-consciousness-element. They do not conceive of the nose-element; they do not conceive of the odor-element; they do not conceive of the nose-consciousness-element. They do not conceive of the tongue-element; they do not conceive of the taste-element; they do not conceive of the tongue-consciousness-element. They do not conceive of the body-element; they do not conceive of the tangible-object-element; they do not conceive of the body-consciousness-element. They do not conceive of the mind-element...

They do not conceive of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); they do not conceive of the realm of mental consciousness (*manovijñānadhātu*). They do not conceive of dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*). They do not conceive of generosity (*dāna*); they do not conceive of ethical discipline (*śīla*); they do not conceive of patience (*kṣānti*); they do not conceive of vigor (*vīrya*); they do not conceive of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*); they do not conceive of wisdom (*prajñā*). They do not conceive of internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*); they do not conceive of external emptiness (*bahirdhāśūnyatā*); they do not conceive of internal and external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*).

They do not conceive of the emptiness of emptiness; they do not conceive of great emptiness; they do not conceive of the emptiness of the ultimate truth; they do not conceive of the emptiness of the conditioned; they do not conceive of the emptiness of the unconditioned; they do not conceive of absolute emptiness; they do not conceive of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they do not conceive of the emptiness of non-dispersal; they do not conceive of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not conceive of the emptiness of all phenomena; they do not conceive of the emptiness of specific characteristics; they do not conceive of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

They do not conceive of the emptiness of non-existence; they do not conceive of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not conceive of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. They do not conceive of the four foundations of mindfulness; they do not conceive of the four right efforts; they do not conceive of the four bases of psychic power; they do not conceive of the five faculties; they do not conceive of the seven factors of enlightenment; they do not conceive of the noble eightfold path; they do not conceive of the four noble truths.

They do not conceive of the four dhyānas; they do not conceive of the four immeasurables; they do not conceive of the four formless attainments; they do not conceive of the eight liberations; they do not conceive of the nine successive meditative attainments; they do not conceive of emptiness; they do not conceive of the signless; they do not conceive of the wishless; they do not conceive of the superknowledges; they do not conceive of the gateways of dhāraṇī; they do not conceive of the ten powers of a Tathāgata.

They do not conceive of the four grounds of self-confidence; they do not conceive of the four analytical knowledges; they do not conceive of great loving-kindness; they do not conceive of great compassion; they do not conceive of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they do not conceive of the fruit of stream-entry; they do not conceive of the fruit of once-returning; they do not conceive of the fruit of non-returning; they do not conceive of arhatship; they do not conceive of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; they do not conceive of the knowledge of the aspects of the path.

They do not conceive of omniscience; they do not conceive of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; they do not conceive of saṃsāra; they do not conceive of nirvāṇa. In this way, Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva mahāsattvas increase by means of the six perfections and are not overcome by anything.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, abiding in the six perfections, fulfill the knowledge of omniscience; endowed with which knowledge they are never reborn in the lower realms, do not experience human poverty, and do not encounter such [conditions].

They take up a physical existence by means of which they become objects of reproach for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the omniscient knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, endowed with which knowledge bodhisattva mahāsattvas are never reborn in the lower realms, nor do they experience human poverty?"
They do not assume such a physical form by which they would become subject to reproach in the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

The Blessed One said: "Śāradvatīputra, endowed with such wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in the eastern direction, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; he hears the Dharma and beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields."

Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; and he hears the Dharma, and beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields.

Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in world systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; he hears the Dharma, and he beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields.

Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in world systems in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; he hears the Dharma and beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields. Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva [beholds], in world systems in the northeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā...

He beholds Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; he hears the Dharma; and he beholds the assembly of Bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields. A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who is not yet fully endowed with such wisdom beholds, in the southeastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and hears the Dharma.

And he beholds the assemblies of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields. Endowed with that wisdom, the bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the southwestern direction, Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; he hears their Dharma and beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the buddha-fields.

Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in world systems in the northwestern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; he hears the Dharma, and he beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields.

Endowed with which knowledge a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in the world-systems of the lower direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; he hears the Dharma and beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields.

Endowed with which gnosis a bodhisattva mahāsattva beholds, in world systems in the direction above as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; he hears the Dharma and beholds the assembly of bodhisattvas and the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields. Endowed with which gnosis a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not even give rise to the notion of a "Buddha."
He does not give rise to the notion of a Saṃgha; he does not give rise to the notion of a Śrāvaka; he does not give rise to the notion of a Pratyekabuddha; nor...

He gives rise to the perception of a bodhisattva, but he does not give rise to the perception of a Buddha; he does not give rise to the perception of a self, nor does he give rise to the perception of another. Endowed with that knowledge, the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of giving, yet he does not apprehend a perfection of giving. He practices the perfection of ethical discipline, yet he does not practice the perfection of patience, nor does he apprehend a perfection of patience.

He practices the perfection of vigor, yet does not apprehend the perfection of vigor; he practices the perfection of meditation, yet does not apprehend the perfection of meditation; he practices the perfection of wisdom, yet does not apprehend the perfection of wisdom. He cultivates internal emptiness, yet does not apprehend internal emptiness; he cultivates external emptiness, yet does not apprehend external emptiness.

He cultivates internal-external emptiness, yet he does not apprehend internal-external emptiness; he cultivates the emptiness of emptiness, yet he does not apprehend the emptiness of emptiness; he cultivates great emptiness, yet he does not apprehend great emptiness; he cultivates the emptiness of the ultimate truth, yet he does not apprehend the emptiness of the ultimate truth; he cultivates the emptiness of the conditioned, yet he does not apprehend the emptiness of the conditioned.

He cultivates the emptiness of the unconditioned, yet he does not perceive the emptiness of the unconditioned; he cultivates absolute emptiness, yet he does not perceive absolute emptiness; he cultivates the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, yet he does not perceive the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; he cultivates the emptiness of non-dispersal, yet he does not perceive the emptiness of non-dispersal; he cultivates the emptiness of intrinsic nature, yet he does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

He cultivates the emptiness of all phenomena, yet does not apprehend the emptiness of all phenomena; he cultivates the emptiness of specific characteristics, yet does not apprehend the emptiness of specific characteristics; he cultivates the emptiness of non-apprehension, yet does not apprehend the emptiness of non-apprehension; he cultivates the emptiness of non-existence, yet does not apprehend the emptiness of non-existence.

He cultivates the emptiness of intrinsic nature, yet he does not apprehend the emptiness of intrinsic nature; he cultivates the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, yet he does not apprehend the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. He cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, yet he does not apprehend the foundations of mindfulness; he cultivates the four right efforts, yet he does not apprehend the right efforts; he cultivates the four bases of psychic power, yet he does not apprehend the bases of psychic power.

He cultivates the five faculties, yet does not apprehend the faculties; he cultivates the five powers, yet does not apprehend the powers; he cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment, yet does not apprehend the factors of enlightenment; he cultivates the noble eightfold path, yet does not apprehend the noble eightfold path; he cultivates the noble truths, yet does not apprehend the noble truths; he cultivates the meditative absorptions, yet does not apprehend the meditative absorptions.

He cultivates the immeasurables, yet he does not perceive the immeasurables; he cultivates the formless attainments, yet he does not perceive the formless attainments; he cultivates the eight liberations, yet he does not perceive the eight liberations; he cultivates the nine successive meditative attainments, yet he does not perceive the nine successive meditative attainments.

He cultivates the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and yet he does not apprehend the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. He cultivates the superknowledges and yet does not apprehend the superknowledges. He cultivates the meditative concentrations and yet does not apprehend the meditative concentrations. He cultivates the gateways to the dhāraṇīs and yet does not apprehend the gateways to the dhāraṇīs. He cultivates the ten powers of a Tathāgata and yet does not apprehend the powers of a Tathāgata.

He cultivates the four grounds of self-confidence, yet he does not apprehend the grounds of self-confidence; he cultivates the four analytical knowledges, yet he does not apprehend the analytical knowledges; he cultivates great loving-kindness, yet he does not apprehend great loving-kindness; he cultivates great compassion, yet he does not...

He perceives great compassion; he cultivates the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, yet he does not perceive the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. He cultivates the fruit of stream-entry, yet he does not perceive the fruit of stream-entry. He cultivates the fruit of once-returning, yet he does not perceive the fruit of once-returning. He cultivates the fruit of non-returning, yet he does not perceive the fruit of non-returning. He cultivates arhatship, yet he does not perceive arhatship.

He cultivates the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, yet he does not apprehend the awakening of a pratyekabuddha; he cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), yet he does not apprehend the knowledge of the aspects of the path; he cultivates the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), yet he does not apprehend the knowledge of all aspects. This is the wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Endowed with this wisdom, the bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills all the qualities of a buddha, yet he does not perceive any qualities of a buddha as real entities.

Śāradvatīputra, there are bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, attain and purify the five eyes. And what are these five eyes? Namely: the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the dharma eye, and the buddha eye.

He asked: "Blessed One, what is the purification of the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One replied: "Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees for a hundred yojanas with his fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees for two hundred yojanas with his fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees for three hundred yojanas with his fleshly eye."

Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees four hundred yojanas with the fleshly eye. Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees five hundred yojanas with the fleshly eye. Śāradvatīputra, there is...

There is, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees six hundred yojanas with the fleshly eye. There is, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees seven hundred yojanas with the fleshly eye. There is, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees eight hundred yojanas with the fleshly eye. There is, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees nine hundred yojanas with the fleshly eye.

Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees a thousand yojanas with the fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees a thousand yojanas with the fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees Jambudvīpa with the fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees two continents with the fleshly eye.

“Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees a thousandfold world system with the fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees a two-thousandfold world system with the fleshly eye; Śāradvatīputra, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who sees a three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the fleshly eye.
This, Śāradvatīputra, is the purification of the fleshly eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.”

He asked: "Blessed One, what is the purification of the divine eye of a bodhisattva mahāsattva?
