Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling (*vedanā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand perception (*saṃjñā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom."

"Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand consciousness (*vijñāna*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva who wishes to fully understand the eye (*cakṣus*),"

A Mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the ear should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the nose should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the tongue should train in the perfection of wisdom.

“Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the body should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the mind should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand form should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

“Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand sound should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand odor should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand taste should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

“Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand contact (*sparśa*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand phenomena (*dharma*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

"Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand eye-consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand ear-consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand nose-consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom."

One must train. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand tongue-consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand body-consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand mind-consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom.

“O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand eye-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand ear-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand nose-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

"Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand tongue-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand body-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand mind-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom."

“Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling born of eye-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling born of ear-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling born of nose-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling born of tongue-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling born of body-contact should train in the perfection of wisdom. [A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling] born of mind-contact...

“Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand ignorance should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand formative factors should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

"Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand consciousness should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand name-and-form should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand the six sense bases should train in the perfection of wisdom."

“O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand contact (*sparśa*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand feeling (*vedanā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand craving (*tṛṣṇā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.”

“Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand clinging (*upādāna*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand existence (*bhava*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand birth (*jāti*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.”
O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully understand aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, depression, and despair should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon attachment should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon aversion should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon delusion should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the view of a self-identity should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon doubt should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the clinging to rules and observances should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon sensual desire and ill will should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon sensual desire should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon attachment to the formless realm should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the fetters should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the underlying tendencies should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the outbursts of passion should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the four nutriments should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the four attachments should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the four floods should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the four knots should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the four types of grasping should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the four misfortunes should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon the ten unwholesome paths of action should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the ten paths of wholesome action should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four meditative concentrations should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four immeasurables should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four formless attainments should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the five superknowledges should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the perfection of generosity should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the perfection of patience should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the perfection of vigor should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the perfection of meditation should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the perfection of wisdom should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill internal emptiness should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill external emptiness should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill internal-external emptiness should train in the perfection of wisdom; [and] a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of emptiness...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill [the perfections] should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill great emptiness should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill ultimate emptiness should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of non-existence should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of intrinsic nature should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence should train in the perfection of wisdom;
and a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four right efforts should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four bases of miraculous power should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the five faculties should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the five powers should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the noble eightfold path should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four noble truths should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the eight liberations should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the ten powers of a Tathāgata should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four grounds of self-confidence should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the four analytical knowledges should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill great loving-kindness should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill great compassion should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the meditative absorption of the seven factors of enlightenment should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Wherein one enters the cessation associated with the first dhyāna; having emerged from cessation, one enters the second dhyāna; having emerged from the second dhyāna, one enters cessation; having emerged from cessation, one enters the third dhyāna; having emerged from the third dhyāna, one enters cessation; having emerged from cessation, one enters the fourth dhyāna; and having emerged from the fourth dhyāna, one enters cessation.

Emerging from cessation, he enters the concentration of loving-kindness (*maitrī-samādhi*). Emerging from the concentration of loving-kindness, he enters cessation. Emerging from cessation, he enters the concentration of compassion (*karuṇā-samādhi*). Emerging from the concentration of compassion, he enters cessation. Emerging from cessation, he enters the concentration of sympathetic joy (*muditā-samādhi*). Emerging from the concentration of sympathetic joy, he enters cessation. Emerging from cessation, he enters the concentration of equanimity (*upekṣā-samādhi*).
Emerging from the meditative absorption of equanimity, one enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from cessation, one enters the sphere of infinite space; from the sphere of infinite space...

Emerging from cessation, one enters the attainment of nothingness; emerging from the attainment of nothingness, one enters cessation; emerging from cessation, one enters the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness; emerging from the attainment of infinite consciousness, one enters cessation; emerging from cessation, one enters the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
Emerging from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters the attainment of cessation; emerging from cessation, one enters the lion’s yawn samādhi (*siṃhavijṛmbhita-samādhi*).

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter meditative attainments should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the lion’s sport samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to obtain all the gateways of dhāraṇīs and the gateways of samādhis should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain the Śūraṅgama samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain the Ratnamudrā samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom; a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain the Candraprabha samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration known as the Moon-Flag Banner should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration that encompasses the seal of all phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the Avalokita-seal concentration should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration fixed in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration of the fixed banner and crest (*niyatadhvajaketu*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva who wishes to enter the diamond-like concentration (*vajropamasamādhi*) [should train in the perfection of wisdom].

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train in the perfection of wisdom should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the meditative absorption that is the gateway for entering all dharmas should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the King of Meditative Absorptions (samādhirāja) should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the Royal Seal (rājamudrā) meditative absorption should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the *balavyūha* samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the *samudgata* samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the *sarvadharmmaniruktiniyatapraveśa* samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the samādhi of the perfuming of the knowledge of all dharmas should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the samādhi of the survey of the ten directions should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the samādhi of the seal of the gateway to all dhāraṇīs should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration called "Non-forgetfulness of all phenomena" (*sarvadharmāsaṃpramoṣa*) should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration called "The Seal of the Mode of the Convergence of All Phenomena" (*sarvadharmasamavaśaraṇākāramudrā*) should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration abiding in the station of space should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration of the triple-circle purity should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration of unfailing supernormal knowledge should train in the perfection of wisdom. [Likewise,] one who wishes to enter the concentration that has reached the vessel...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain the Dhvajāgrakeyūra samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain the Sarvakleśanirdahana samādhi should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration that dispels the power of the four māras should train in the perfection of wisdom. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to enter the concentration that is unattached, liberated, and unstained like space should train in the perfection of wisdom. Indeed, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain these and other gateways to concentration should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the aspirations of all sentient beings should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the roots of virtue—by means of which roots of virtue, being fulfilled, he does not fall into the miserable states, is not reborn into lowly families, and does not abide on the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha—should train in the perfection of wisdom.
And so that a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not fall from the summit, he should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the venerable Subhūti: "Venerable Subhūti, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva fall from the summit? When this was said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the venerable Śāradvatīputra: "Venerable..."

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the six perfections without skill in means, and relying on the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness without skill in means, he neither falls onto the level of a śrāvaka nor falls onto the level of a pratyekabuddha, yet he does not enter the fixed course of a bodhisattva. This is called the "stagnation" of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. He said:

"For what reason, venerable Subhūti, is this called the 'craving' (*āma*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? Subhūti replied: "Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is called the 'craving' of a bodhisattva mahāsattva because of craving for phenomena (*dharmatṛṣṇā*). [Śāradvatīputra] asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what is craving for phenomena? Subhūti replied:

In this regard, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives that "form is empty. He adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives that "feeling is empty. He adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives that "perception is empty. He adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives that "volitional formations are empty. He adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives that "consciousness is empty."
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this is called the immature, conforming craving for phenomena of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives form as impermanent; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives feeling as impermanent; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives perception as impermanent; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives mental formations as impermanent.

One adheres to, persists in, and perceives that "consciousness is impermanent. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this is called the "conformable craving for phenomena" (anulomikī dharmatṛṣṇā) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; it is the "unripe" [stage].

Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives form as suffering; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives feeling as suffering; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives perception as suffering; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives mental formations as suffering.
One adheres to, persists in, and perceives that "consciousness is suffering. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this is called the immature bodhisattva mahāsattva’s conformable craving for phenomena.

Furthermore, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives form as being selfless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives feeling as being selfless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives perception as being selfless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives mental formations as being selfless.
One adheres to, relies upon, and perceives that "consciousness is non-self. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, this is called the immature bodhisattva mahāsattva’s conformative craving for phenomena.

Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives form as signless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives feeling as signless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives perception as signless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives mental formations as signless.
He adheres to, relies upon, and perceives consciousness as being signless (*animitta*). This, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is called the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s compliant thirst for the Dharma.
Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva [practices] in the perfection of wisdom...

Practicing, he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives form as being wishless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives feeling as being wishless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives perception as being wishless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives mental formations as being wishless; he adheres to, dwells upon, and perceives consciousness as being wishless.
This, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is called the immature, conforming craving for phenomena of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

"This form is to be abandoned; by this means form is to be abandoned. This feeling is to be abandoned; by this means feeling is to be abandoned. This perception is to be abandoned; by this means perception is to be abandoned. These formations are to be abandoned; by this means formations are to be abandoned. This consciousness is to be abandoned; by this means consciousness is to be abandoned. "This suffering is to be fully understood; by this means suffering is to be fully understood."

"This is origination; it is to be abandoned. By this means, origination is to be abandoned. This is cessation; it is to be realized. By this means, cessation is to be realized. This is the path; it is to be cultivated. By this means, the path is to be cultivated. "This is affliction; this is purification. "These phenomena are to be practiced; these phenomena are not to be practiced. "In this, the bodhisattva mahāsattva should practice; in this, he should not practice."

"This is the path of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is not the path. "This is the training of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is not the training. "This is the perfection of generosity of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is not the perfection of generosity. "This is the perfection of ethical discipline of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is not the perfection of ethical discipline. "This is the perfection of patience of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this is not the perfection of patience."

"This is the perfection of vigor of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, yet it is not the perfection of vigor; this is the perfection of meditation of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, yet it is not the perfection of meditation;

this is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, yet it is not the perfection of wisdom; this is the skill in means of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, yet this is not skill in means"—this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s entry into the state of certainty (*nyāma*).

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, becomes attached to, adheres to, or perceives these phenomena in such a way, this is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s conformable craving for phenomena (*anulomikī dharmatṛṣṇā*); it is his 'unripened' state. Śāradvatīputra asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s *nyāma*? Subhūti replied:

In this regard, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom perceives internal emptiness within internal-external emptiness; he does not perceive internal emptiness within external emptiness; he does not perceive internal-external emptiness within external emptiness; nor does he perceive external emptiness within internal emptiness.

He does not perceive the emptiness of emptiness within the internal-external emptiness; he does not perceive the internal-external emptiness within the emptiness of emptiness. He does not perceive the great emptiness within the emptiness of emptiness; he does not perceive the ultimate emptiness within the great emptiness; he does not perceive the great emptiness within the ultimate emptiness; he does not perceive the conditioned emptiness within the ultimate emptiness.

One does not perceive ultimate emptiness within conditioned emptiness; one does not perceive unconditioned emptiness within conditioned emptiness; one does not perceive conditioned emptiness within unconditioned emptiness; one does not perceive the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end within unconditioned emptiness; one does not perceive unconditioned emptiness within the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; one does not perceive the emptiness of non-dispersal within the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end;
and one does not perceive the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end within the emptiness of non-dispersal.

He does not perceive ultimate emptiness within the emptiness of non-dispersal; he does not perceive natural emptiness within ultimate emptiness; he does not perceive ultimate emptiness within natural emptiness; he does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena within natural emptiness; he does not perceive natural emptiness within the emptiness of all phenomena; he does not perceive the emptiness of specific characteristics within the emptiness of all phenomena.

In the emptiness of self-characteristic, one does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena; in the emptiness of self-characteristic, one does not perceive the emptiness of non-apprehension; in the emptiness of non-apprehension, one does not perceive the emptiness of self-characteristic; in the emptiness of non-apprehension, one does not perceive the emptiness of non-existence; in the emptiness of non-existence, one does not perceive the emptiness of non-apprehension; in the emptiness of non-existence, one does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

In the emptiness of intrinsic nature, one does not perceive the emptiness of non-existence; in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, one does not perceive the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena.

In this way indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom enters the bodhisattva’s path of certainty. Furthermore, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should train as follows: while training, form is to be known, yet one must not conceive of it; feeling is to be known, and by that...

Feeling is to be known, but one should not conceive of it as feeling. Perception is to be known, but one should not conceive of it as perception. Volitional formations are to be known, but one should not conceive of them as volitional formations. Consciousness is to be known, but one should not conceive of it as consciousness. The eye is to be known, but one should not conceive of it as the eye. The ear is to be known, but one should not conceive of it as the ear. The nose is to be known, but one should not conceive of it as the nose.

The tongue is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that tongue; the body is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that body; the mind is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that mind; form is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that form; sound is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that sound; odor is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that odor; taste is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that taste.

Contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that contact. Phenomena are to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of those phenomena. Eye-consciousness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that nose-consciousness.

Tongue-consciousness is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that tongue-consciousness; body-consciousness is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that body-consciousness; mind-consciousness is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that mind-consciousness.

Eye-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that eye-contact. Ear-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that ear-contact. Nose-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that nose-contact. Tongue-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that tongue-contact. Body-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that body-contact. Mind-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that mind-contact.

Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that feeling conditioned by eye-contact. Feeling conditioned by ear-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that feeling conditioned by ear-contact. Feeling conditioned by nose-contact is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that feeling conditioned by nose-contact. Feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is to be known.

One should not conceive of that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; one should know the feeling conditioned by body-contact, yet one should not conceive of that feeling conditioned by body-contact; one should know the feeling conditioned by mind-contact, yet one should not conceive of that feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

The earth element is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that earth element. The water element is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that water element. The fire element is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that fire element. The wind element is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that wind element. The space element is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that space element. The consciousness element is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that consciousness element.

Ignorance is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that ignorance. Formative forces are to be known, and one should not conceive by means of those formative forces. Consciousness is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that consciousness. Name-and-form is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that name-and-form. The six sense bases are to be known, and one should not conceive by means of those six sense bases. Contact is to be known, and one should not conceive by means of that contact.

Feeling is to be known, and one should not conceive of oneself by means of that feeling. Craving is to be known, and one should not conceive of oneself by means of that craving. Grasping is to be known, and one should not conceive of oneself by means of that grasping. Becoming is to be known, and one should not conceive of oneself by means of that becoming. Birth is to be known, and one should not conceive of oneself by means of that birth. Old age and death are to be known, and one should not conceive of oneself by means of that old age and death.

The perfection of generosity should be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that perfection of generosity. The perfection of ethical discipline should be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that perfection of ethical discipline. The perfection of patience should be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that perfection of patience. The perfection of vigor should be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that perfection of vigor. The perfection of meditative concentration should be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that perfection of meditative concentration.
The perfection of wisdom should be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that perfection of wisdom.

Internal emptiness is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment to that internal emptiness. External emptiness is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment to that external emptiness. Internal-and-external emptiness is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment to that internal-and-external emptiness. The emptiness of emptiness is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment to that emptiness of emptiness. Great emptiness is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment to that great emptiness.

Ultimate emptiness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that ultimate emptiness. Conditioned emptiness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that conditioned emptiness. Unconditioned emptiness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that unconditioned emptiness. Absolute emptiness is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that absolute emptiness. Emptiness without beginning or end is to be known, yet one should not conceive by means of that emptiness without beginning or end.

The emptiness of non-dispersal is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment even to that emptiness of non-dispersal. The emptiness of non-apprehension is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment even to that emptiness of non-apprehension. The emptiness of non-existence is to be known, yet one should not form a conceptual attachment even to that emptiness of non-existence. The emptiness of intrinsic nature is to be known, and likewise, one should not [form a conceptual attachment] even to that emptiness of intrinsic nature.

One should contemplate; one should know the emptiness of specific characteristics, yet one should not contemplate by means of that emptiness of specific characteristics. One should know the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, yet one should not contemplate by means of that emptiness of the nature of non-existence.

The meditative absorptions (dhyāna) are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those meditative absorptions. The immeasurables (apramāṇa) are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those immeasurables. The formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those formless attainments. The supernormal knowledges (abhijñā) are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those supernormal knowledges. The five eyes (pañcacakṣus) are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those five eyes.

The foundations of mindfulness are to be known, yet one should not conceive of them by means of those foundations of mindfulness. The right efforts are to be known, yet one should not conceive of them by means of those right efforts. The bases of psychic power are to be known, yet one should not conceive of them by means of those bases of psychic power. The faculties are to be known, yet one should not conceive of them by means of those faculties. The powers are to be known, yet one should not conceive of them by means of those powers. The factors of enlightenment are to be known, yet one should not conceive of them by means of those factors of enlightenment.

The noble eightfold path is to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of that noble eightfold path. The noble truths are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those noble truths. The eight liberations are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those eight liberations. The nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling.

The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. The meditative concentrations are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those meditative concentrations. The gateways to the dhāraṇīs are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those gateways to the dhāraṇīs. The ten powers of a Tathāgata are to be known, yet one should not conceive of oneself by means of those ten powers of a Tathāgata.

The four grounds of self-confidence (vaiśāradya) are to be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of those grounds of self-confidence. The four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are to be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of those analytical knowledges. Great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī) is to be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that great loving-kindness. Great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is to be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of that great compassion. The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are to be known, yet one should not be conceited on account of those eighteen unique qualities.

"In this way, indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not conceive even that thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*); he should not conceive it as a mind equal to the unequaled; he should not conceive it as a sublime mind. Why is that? Because that mind is no-mind; the nature of the mind is luminosity. He asked: "Venerable Subhūti, what is the luminous nature of the mind? Subhūti replied:

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, when the mind is neither conjoined nor disjoined with passion, neither conjoined nor disjoined with the fetters, neither conjoined nor disjoined with the products of views, neither conjoined nor disjoined with the mind of a śrāvaka, and neither conjoined nor disjoined with the mind of a pratyekabuddha—this, venerable Śāradvatīputra, is the intrinsic luminosity of the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. He said:

"But, venerable Subhūti, does that mind which is 'no-mind' exist? Subhūti said: "But, venerable Śāradvatīputra, as for this state of no-mind, does existence exist therein? Or rather, neither existence nor non-existence is found, nor is it apprehended. He replied: "Certainly not, venerable Subhūti. Subhūti said: "If, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither existence nor non-existence exists nor is apprehended therein—"

"Is this question of yours appropriate, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, when you ask: 'Does that mind exist which is non-mind? He replied: 'And what, Venerable Subhūti, is this state of non-mind? Subhūti said: 'Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the state of non-mind is unchanging and undifferentiated; it is the suchness (*tathatā*) of all phenomena. This is called the inconceivable state of non-mind. He asked:"
Furthermore, venerable Subhūti, just as the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual, so too is form unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is feeling unchanging and non-conceptual;
so too is perception unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are mental formations unchanging and non-conceptual; and so too is consciousness unchanging and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual, so too is the eye unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the ear is unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the nose is unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tongue is unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the body is unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the mind-faculty is unchanging and non-conceptual; and likewise, the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, form is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, sound is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, odor is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, taste is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, tangibility is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, mental phenomena are also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the mind is also unchanging and non-conceptual; and likewise, the eye-element is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the form-element (*rūpadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the eye-consciousness-element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual. Likewise, the ear-element (*śrotradhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the sound-element (*śabdadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the ear-consciousness-element (*śrotravijñānadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual. Likewise, the nose-element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the odor-element (*gandhadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the nose-consciousness element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tongue element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the taste element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tongue-consciousness element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the body element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tangible object element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; and likewise, the body-consciousness element is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the mind-element (manodhātu) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the phenomena-element (dharmadhātu) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the mind-consciousness-element (manovijñānadhātu) is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual, so too is ignorance unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the formative forces are also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, consciousness is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, name-and-form is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the six sense bases are also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, contact is also unchanging and non-conceptual; and likewise, feeling is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, craving is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, grasping is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, becoming is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, birth is also without modification and without conceptualization; and likewise, aging and death are also without modification and without conceptualization.

Just as the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual, so too is the perfection of generosity unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the perfection of ethical discipline unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the perfection of patience unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the perfection of vigor unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the perfection of meditative concentration unchanging and non-conceptual; and so too is the perfection of wisdom unchanging and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual, so too is internal emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is external emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is internal-and-external emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the emptiness of emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is great emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the emptiness of the ultimate unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the emptiness of the conditioned unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, absolute emptiness is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, beginningless and endless emptiness is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, non-dispersal emptiness is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, natural emptiness is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the emptiness of all phenomena is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the emptiness of specific characteristics is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

Likewise, the emptiness of non-apprehension is also without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, the emptiness of non-existence is also without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is also without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is also without modification and without conceptual construction.

Just as the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual, so too are the applications of mindfulness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the right efforts unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the bases of psychic power unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the faculties unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the meditative absorptions unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the factors of enlightenment unchanging and non-conceptual; and so too is the noble eightfold path unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the noble truths are unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the meditative absorptions are unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the immeasurables are unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the formless attainments are also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the eight liberations are also unchanging and non-conceptual; and in the same way, the nine successive meditative attainments are also unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unchanging and non-conceptual. Likewise, the superknowledges are also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the meditative concentrations are also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the ten powers of a Tathāgata are unchanging and non-conceptual; and likewise, the grounds of self-confidence are unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; and in the same way, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are also unchanging and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is no-mind, unchanging, and non-conceptual, so too is the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*) unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the fruit of the non-returner is also changeless and non-conceptual; likewise, arhatship is also changeless and non-conceptual; likewise, solitary enlightenment is also changeless and non-conceptual; likewise, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is also changeless and non-conceptual; and likewise, the knowledge of all aspects is also changeless and non-conceptual.

Subhūti said: "It is so, venerable Śāradvatīputra. Just as the mind is non-mind, unchanging, and non-conceptual, even so the eye is unchanging and non-conceptual; even so the ear is unchanging and non-conceptual; even so the nose is unchanging and non-conceptual; even so the tongue is unchanging and non-conceptual; even so the body is unchanging and non-conceptual; even so the mind is unchanging and non-conceptual."

Just as the mind is non-mind, unchanging, and non-conceptual, so too is form unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is sound unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is odor unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is taste unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is tangibility unchanging and non-conceptual; and so too are phenomena unchanging and non-conceptual.
Just as the mind is non-mind, unchanging, and non-conceptual, so too is the eye-element unchanging.

It is free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the form element (*rūpadhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the eye-consciousness element (*cakṣurvijñānadhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the ear element (*śrotradhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the sound element (*śabdadhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the ear-consciousness element (*śrotravijñānadhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the nose element (*ghrāṇadhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction. In the same way, the odor element (*gandhadhātu*) is also unchanging and free from conceptual construction.

In the same way, the nose-consciousness element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tongue element is unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the taste element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tongue-consciousness element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the body element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the tangible-object element is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the body-consciousness element is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the mind-element (*manodhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the phenomena-element (*dharmadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the mind-consciousness-element (*manovijñānadhātu*) is also unchanging and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is non-mind, without modification and without conceptualization, so too is ignorance without modification and without conceptualization; so too are the formative forces without modification and without conceptualization; so too is consciousness without modification and without conceptualization; so too is name-and-form without modification and without conceptualization; so too are the six sense bases without modification and without conceptualization; so too is contact without modification and without conceptualization; and so too is feeling without modification and without conceptualization.

In the same way, craving (*tṛṣṇā*) is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, grasping (*upādāna*) is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, existence (*bhava*) is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, birth (*jāti*) is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, aging and death (*jarāmaraṇa*) are also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) is also without modification and without conceptualization; likewise, the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) is also...

It is without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, the perfection of vigor is also without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, the perfection of meditation is also without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, the perfection of wisdom is also without modification and without conceptual construction.

Just as the mind is no-mind, unchanging, and non-conceptual, so too is internal emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is external emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is internal-external emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is the emptiness of emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too is great emptiness unchanging and non-conceptual; and so too is the emptiness of the ultimate truth unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the emptiness of the conditioned is also without change and without conceptualization; in the same way, the emptiness of the unconditioned is also without change and without conceptualization; in the same way, absolute emptiness is also without change and without conceptualization; in the same way, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is also without change and without conceptualization; in the same way, the emptiness of non-dispersal is also without change and without conceptualization; in the same way, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is also without change and without conceptualization; in the same way, the emptiness of all phenomena is also without change and without conceptualization.

In the same way, the emptiness of specific characteristics is also changeless and non-conceptual; in the same way, the emptiness of non-apprehension is also changeless and non-conceptual; in the same way, the emptiness of non-existence is also changeless and non-conceptual; in the same way, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is also changeless and non-conceptual; and in the same way, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is also changeless and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is non-mind, unchanging, and non-conceptual, so too are the applications of mindfulness unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the right efforts unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the bases of psychic power unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the faculties unchanging and non-conceptual; so too are the factors of enlightenment unchanging and non-conceptual; and so too is the noble eightfold path unchanging and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the noble truths are unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the meditative absorptions are also unchanging and non-conceptual; likewise, the immeasurables [are unchanging and non-conceptual].

They are indeed changeless and non-conceptual. Likewise, the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*) are also changeless and non-conceptual. Likewise, the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*) are also changeless and non-conceptual. Likewise, the serial attainments of meditative dwelling (*anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*) are also changeless and non-conceptual. Likewise, the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (*śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) are also changeless and non-conceptual. Likewise, the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) are also changeless and non-conceptual. Likewise, the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) are also changeless and non-conceptual.

In the same way, the gateways of dhāraṇī are also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, great loving-kindness is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, great compassion is also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the ten powers of a Tathāgata are also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the four grounds of self-confidence are also unchanging and non-conceptual; in the same way, the four analytical insights are also unchanging and non-conceptual;
and in the same way, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are also unchanging and non-conceptual.

Just as the mind is non-mind, changeless, and non-conceptual, so too is the fruit of stream-entry changeless and non-conceptual; so too is the fruit of once-returning changeless and non-conceptual; so too is the fruit of non-returning changeless and non-conceptual; so too is arhatship changeless and non-conceptual; so too is solitary enlightenment changeless and non-conceptual; and so too is the knowledge of the aspects of the path changeless and non-conceptual.

In the same way, omniscience in all its aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is also without modification and without conceptual construction; likewise, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is also without modification and without conceptual construction.

Then the Venerable Śāradvatīputra gave his approval to the Venerable Subhūti: "Excellent, excellent, Venerable Subhūti! Just as you are indeed the Lord’s legitimate son, born from his mouth, born of the Dharma, fashioned by the Dharma, an heir to the Dharma, and not an heir to material things; one who has direct vision regarding the Dharmas and is a bodily witness—this instruction is indeed worthy of you, who have been designated by the Lord as the foremost among the disciples dwelling in the forest. Thus it is, Venerable Subhūti."

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom. From this, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is to be examined as one who is irreversible; and it should be known that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is not separated from the perfection of wisdom.

Even one who wishes to train in the stage of the śrāvakas, O Venerable Subhūti, that bodhisattva mahāsattva should with diligence hear, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this very perfection of wisdom.

"Venerable Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train even on the level of a pratyekabuddha must hear, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this very perfection of wisdom.

Venerable Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train even on the level of a bodhisattva must hear, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this very perfection of wisdom."

Furthermore, O Venerable Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train even in the stage of a Buddha must hear, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and attend to this very perfection of wisdom in a systematic manner. Why is that? Because herein, in this perfection of wisdom, the three vehicles are taught in detail, wherein bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas must constantly and continuously train.
The third chapter in the Prajñāpāramitā in One Hundred Thousand Lines.
Now begins the fourth chapter.

Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, since I do not find and do not apprehend a bodhisattva or the perfection of wisdom, not finding and not apprehending either the bodhisattva mahāsattva or the perfection of wisdom, which bodhisattva mahāsattva shall I instruct and admonish in which perfection of wisdom?"

"O Blessed One, this indeed would be my remorse: that while not perceiving the coming or going of all dharmas, I should perform a coming or going by means of a mere name—namely, 'Bodhisattva' or 'Perfection of Wisdom. Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.
Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained."

“Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I see the arising and passing away of form. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor see the arising and passing away of form, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation is neither established nor sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

"Blessed One, I do not apprehend, nor do I perceive, the arising and the passing away of feeling. Blessed One, since I do not apprehend and do not perceive the arising and the passing away of feeling, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding feeling and perception, I do not perceive nor do I observe their arising or their passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of perception, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation of "perception" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of conditioned phenomena, for what [phenomenon] shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One...

Even that designation "formations" (saṃskāra) is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I discern the arising and passing away of consciousness.

Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing this exhaustion of consciousness, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, the designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I fully behold the arising and passing away of the eye. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor fully behold the arising and passing away of the eye, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, O Blessed One, even that name ‘eye’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, this name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of the ear. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of the ear, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "ear" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not apprehend, nor do I perceive, the arising and passing away of the nose. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive the arising and passing away of the nose, for whom shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"?
Furthermore, indeed, the name "nose" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, the name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising and passing away of the tongue. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising and passing away of the tongue, for what [entity] shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, O Blessed One, even that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I discern, the arising or the passing away of the body.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe this disintegration of the body, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the mind. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the mind, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
Why is that? Because that designation does not exist; thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

“Blessed One, I do not apprehend and do not perceive the arising and passing away of form. Blessed One, since I do not apprehend and do not perceive the arising and passing away of form, for what reason shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘form’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.
Thus, that designation is not established, nor is it...”

It is not fixed, nor is it established. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I fully behold, the arising or the passing away of sound. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or fully behold the arising or the passing away of sound, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation is not fixed, not established, and not firmly grounded. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of odor. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of odor, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "odor" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of taste. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of taste, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of contact (*sparśa*). Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving nor observing the arising and passing away of contact, [I do not perceive a self].

"Whose name shall I give as 'Bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name 'contact' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I see the coming or going of phenomena. Therefore, Blessed One, regarding phenomena..."

Not perceiving and not observing either coming or going, for whom shall I establish the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I fully behold, the arising and passing away of visual consciousness. Blessed One, since I do not perceive or fully behold the arising and passing away of visual consciousness, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation 'visual consciousness' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of auditory consciousness. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising or the passing away of auditory consciousness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "auditory consciousness" is not established, not fixed, and not supported. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not supported. Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of olfactory consciousness.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the cessation of this olfactory consciousness, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "olfactory consciousness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
"Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of tongue-consciousness. Therefore, Blessed One, regarding the arising of tongue-consciousness—"

Not perceiving and not observing its passing away, for whom shall I designate the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "tongue-consciousness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I clearly see, the arising and passing away of body-consciousness. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive or clearly see the arising and passing away of body-consciousness, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation 'body-consciousness' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that designation is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I fully observe, the arising and passing away of mental consciousness. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or fully observe the arising and passing away of mental consciousness, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "mental consciousness" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising and passing away of eye-contact. Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising and passing away of eye-contact, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘eye-contact’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, such is the arising and passing away of ear-contact.

I do not apprehend it, nor do I perceive it. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive the cessation of this ear-contact, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "ear-contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of olfactory contact. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of olfactory contact, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "nose-contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising and passing away of tongue-contact.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not apprehend and do not perceive the cessation of this tongue-contact, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "tongue-contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not apprehend, nor do I perceive, the arising and passing away of body-contact. Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive the arising and passing away of body-contact, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘body-contact’ is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”
Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive the arising or the passing away of mental contact.

I do not perceive it. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not apprehend nor perceive this cessation of mental contact (*manaḥsaṃsparśa*), for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "mental contact" is not established, not fixed, and not grounded. Why is that? Because that name does not exist; thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not grounded.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising and the passing away of feeling born of eye-contact. Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe the arising and the passing away of feeling born of eye-contact, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘feeling born of eye-contact’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of sensation born of auditory contact. Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising or the passing away of sensation born of auditory contact, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "feeling born of ear-contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of feeling born of nose-contact.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of feeling born of nose-contact, of what shall I make the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation "feeling born of nose-contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because it does not exist.

[It is] of the name. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not apprehend nor perceive the arising and passing away of sensation born of tongue-contact. O Blessed One, since I do not apprehend nor perceive the arising and passing away of sensation born of tongue-contact, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "feeling born of tongue-contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of feeling born of body-contact.

Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of sensation born of bodily contact, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, O Blessed One, even that designation "sensation born of bodily contact" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.
