“Blessed One, I do not apprehend, nor do I perceive, the arising and passing away of feeling born of mental contact. Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive the arising and passing away of feeling born of mental contact, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation ‘feeling born of mental contact’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the earth element.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of the earth element, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation "earth element" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. In this way, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, regarding the water element, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the water element, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘water element’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of the fire element (*tejodhātu*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of the fire element, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "fire element" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the element of wind, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the element of wind, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "wind element" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the space element, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, Blessed One, as for that space element—

Not perceiving and not observing either coming or going, for whom shall I establish the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "space-element" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. In the same way, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the consciousness element (*vijñānadhātu*). Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the consciousness element, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘consciousness element’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of ignorance. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of ignorance, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "ignorance" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I discern, the arising and passing away of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*). Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive or discern the arising and passing away of conditioned phenomena, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "formations" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising and passing away of consciousness.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing this exhaustion of consciousness, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "consciousness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*). Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of name-and-form, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation 'name-and-form' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of the six sense bases, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "six sense bases" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding contact (*sparśa*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or passing away of contact, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising and passing away of feeling. Blessed One, since I do not perceive the arising and passing away of feeling...

"Observing thus, for whom shall I make the designation 'Bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation 'feeling' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of craving."

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of craving, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "craving" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of grasping (*upādāna*). Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of grasping, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation 'grasping' is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding birth, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Since I, O Blessed One, do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of birth, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "birth" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Bhagavat, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of old age and death. Therefore, O Bhagavat, regarding the arising of old age and death—

Not perceiving and not observing its passing away, for whom shall I make the designation "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation "old age and death" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I see, the arising or the passing away of the cessation of ignorance. Blessed One, since I do not perceive or see the arising or the passing away of the cessation of ignorance, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name 'cessation of ignorance' does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that name does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the cessation of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra-nirodha*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the cessation of conditioned phenomena, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "cessation of formations" does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that name is non-existent. Thus, that name does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Blessed One, regarding the cessation of consciousness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe the cessation or the passing away of consciousness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "cessation of consciousness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, nor...

It is not fixed, nor is it established. O Blessed One, regarding the cessation of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), I do not perceive, nor do I fully discern, its coming or its going. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or discern the coming or going of the cessation of name-and-form, for what should I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "cessation of name-and-form" is not fixed, not established, and not established [as a reality].

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the cessation of the six sense bases, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the cessation of the six sense bases, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "cessation of the six sense-bases" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the cessation of contact, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the exhaustion of this cessation of contact, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "cessation of contact" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of the cessation of feeling. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising or the passing away of the cessation of feeling, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name ‘cessation of feeling’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the cessation of craving, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the cessation of craving, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "cessation of craving" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the cessation of clinging, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the cessation and the passing away of this grasping, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "cessation of grasping" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I discern, the arising or the passing away of the cessation of existence. Therefore, Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor discern the arising or the passing away of the cessation of existence, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name 'cessation of existence' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist."

Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the cessation of birth, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the cessation of birth, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "cessation of birth" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
Why is that?

Because that name lacks a causal basis, that name is thus neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the cessation of old age and death, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the cessation of old age and death, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "cessation of old age and death" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of passion. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe its arising or its passing away, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘passion’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and the passing away of hatred. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and the passing away of hatred, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "hatred" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of delusion (*moha*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of delusion, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?
Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "delusion" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not situated, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, regarding these views, I do not perceive nor do I observe their arising or their passing away. O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of these views, for what [entity] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘view’ is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of a self. Since I, O Blessed One, do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of a self, for whom shall I establish the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name of a self is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of a "sentient being. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of a sentient being, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name of a "sentient being" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or the going of a "living soul."

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or passing away of this "living being" (jīva), for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "living being" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because it does not exist.

Of that name: thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of a "being. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of a being, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "being" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. All that name is neither established, nor situated, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or going of a "person" (poṣa). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the coming or going of a person, for whom shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "nourisher" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not apprehend nor do I perceive the income or the expenditure of a person.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not find and do not perceive the passing away of this person, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name of the person is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I clearly see, the coming or the going of a person (*pudgala*). Blessed One, since I do not perceive or clearly see the coming or the going of a person, for whom shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘person’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.
Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

"Blessed One, I do not apprehend and do not perceive the coming or the going of a person. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not apprehend and do not perceive the coming or the going of a person, for whom shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation 'person' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.
Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained."

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I clearly discern, the coming or the going of a ‘man. Blessed One, since I do not perceive or clearly discern the coming or the going of a man, for whom shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘man’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the acquisition or the loss of an agent. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the acquisition or the loss of an agent, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Moreover, O Blessed One, even that name of an agent is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of a feeler. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of a feeler, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "experiencer" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of one who knows. Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of one who knows, for whom shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation ‘one who knows’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the seer, I do not perceive nor do I fully observe either its coming or its going. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor fully observe the coming or the going of the seer, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name of the seer is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, regarding the perfection of generosity, I do not apprehend nor perceive its acquisition or its expenditure. Blessed One, since I do not apprehend nor perceive the acquisition or the expenditure of the perfection of generosity, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation 'perfection of generosity' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of the perfection of ethical discipline, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "perfection of ethical discipline" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established.

It is neither fixed nor established. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arrival or departure of the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arrival or departure of the perfection of patience, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "perfection of patience" is not fixed, not established, and not established by any foundation.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not apprehend, nor do I perceive, the coming or going of the perfection of vigor. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive the coming or going of the perfection of vigor, for whom shall I designate the name "Bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "perfection of vigor" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of the perfection of meditation.

Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing either the acquisition or the loss of the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*), for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, O Blessed One, even that name "perfection of meditation" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.

“O Bhagavat, I do not apprehend nor do I perceive the coming or the going of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). O Bhagavat, since I do not apprehend nor perceive the coming or the going of the perfection of wisdom, for what shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, even that name ‘perfection of wisdom’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

“O Blessed One, regarding internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or going. Since I, O Blessed One, do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of internal emptiness, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘internal emptiness’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding external emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming into being or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming into being or the passing away of external emptiness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "external emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding internal-external emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of internal-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*), for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "internal-external emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.
Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, [I do not perceive] the arising and passing away of the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatāśūnyatā*).

I do not apprehend it, nor do I perceive it. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of emptiness, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "emptiness of emptiness" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding great emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of great emptiness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "great emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding ultimate emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of ultimate emptiness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "ultimate emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of the honored, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of conditioned emptiness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Moreover, O Blessed One, even that name "conditioned emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus...

That name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, within absolute emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe any arising or passing away. Thus, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe any arising or passing away within absolute emptiness, for what shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that which is called "extreme emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding beginningless and endless emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the coming or going of the emptiness that is without beginning or end, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "emptiness without beginning or end" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I see, the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*). Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive or see the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of non-dispersal, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘emptiness of non-dispersal’ does not abide, does not persist, and is not established.”

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, within the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), I do not perceive nor do I observe either its coming or its going. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or the going of intrinsic emptiness, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?
Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "emptiness of intrinsic nature" [is likewise non-existent].

It is not established, not fixed, and not presided over. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not presided over. O Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing either the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of all phenomena, whose name shall I designate as "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "emptiness of all phenomena" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or the going of the emptiness of specific characteristics, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘emptiness of specific characteristics’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of non-apprehension, I do not apprehend nor do I perceive its arising or its passing away. Blessed One, since I do not apprehend nor perceive the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of non-apprehension, for what shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘emptiness of non-apprehension’ does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because it is non-existent.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of non-existence, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of non-existence, for what [phenomenon] would there be a name?

"I shall become a bodhisattva. However, Blessed One, even that designation "emptiness of non-existence" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of intrinsic nature, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of intrinsic emptiness, whose name shall I designate as "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "intrinsic emptiness" does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name does not abide, does not persist, and is not established.

“Blessed One, regarding the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, for what shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name ‘emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*). Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the applications of mindfulness, for what shall I apply the name 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name 'application of mindfulness' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained."

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*), I do not perceive nor do I observe their coming or their going. Therefore, O Blessed One, concerning the right efforts—

Not perceiving and not observing either gain or loss, for whom shall I establish the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "Right Exertion" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*). Since I, O Blessed One, do not perceive or observe the arising or the passing away of the bases of psychic power, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘bases of psychic power’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of the sense faculties. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of the sense faculties, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation "sense faculty" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of the powers. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of the powers, for whom shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that which is called "power" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*). Thus, Blessed One, not perceiving the arising or the passing away of the factors of enlightenment, I...

"Observing thus, for whom shall I bestow the name 'Bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name of the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga) is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. In this way, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained."

"Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or the going of the noble eightfold path. Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the coming or the going of the noble eightfold path, for what should I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name 'noble eightfold path' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained."

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the gate of liberation that is emptiness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the gate of liberation that is emptiness, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "the gate of liberation of emptiness" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the gate of liberation of wishlessness, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.
Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the exhaustion of this gateway to liberation through aspiration, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "the gate of liberation through aspiration" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Furthermore, Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of even the four dhyānas.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising or the passing away of the four dhyānas, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "dhyāna" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, through loving-kindness (*maitrī*), I do not apprehend nor perceive its arrival or departure. Since, O Blessed One, I do not apprehend nor perceive the arrival or departure of loving-kindness, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘loving-kindness’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of compassion. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of compassion, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "compassion" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or going of sympathetic joy (*muditā*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the coming or going of sympathetic joy, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Moreover—

Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "joy" (muditā) is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding equanimity (upekṣā), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of equanimity, for what shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "equanimity" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising and passing away of the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*). O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe their arising and passing away, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘formless attainment’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, through the recollection of the Buddha, I do not perceive nor do I observe any arising or passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe any arising or passing away of the recollection of the Buddha, for what shall I designate the name "bodhisattva"?

Thus it is said. Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "recollection of the Buddha" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. In this way, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the recollection of the Dharma, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.
Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of the recollection of the Dharma, for what shall I bestow the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "recollection of the Dharma" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist; thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the recollection of the Saṅgha, I do not apprehend nor perceive its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing either the gain or the loss of the recollection of the Saṅgha, whose name shall I designate as "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "recollection of the Saṅgha" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, regarding the recollection of ethical discipline (*śīlānusmṛti*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going. Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or the going of the recollection of ethical discipline, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name ‘recollection of ethical discipline’ does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the recollection of generosity (*tyāgānusmṛti*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its income or its expenditure. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the income or expenditure of the recollection of generosity, for what shall I establish the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "recollection of generosity" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, regarding this mindfulness directed to the body, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising or the passing away of this mindfulness directed to the body, [I abide].

"Whose name shall I give as 'Bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name 'Recollection of the Body' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained."

“O Blessed One, through the recollection of agitation, I do not apprehend nor do I perceive any coming or going. O Blessed One, since I do not apprehend or perceive any coming or going through the recollection of agitation, for whom shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name ‘recollection of agitation’ is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Because of the recollection of discourse, O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe any coming or going. Since I, O Blessed One, do not perceive nor observe any coming or going of the recollection of discourse, for whom shall I establish the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "recollection of discourse" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, through the recollection of death (*maraṇānusmṛti*), I do not perceive nor do I observe any coming or going. Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe any coming or going of the recollection of death, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "recollection of death" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, with my fleshly eye, I do not perceive nor do I see its coming or its passing away. Therefore, Blessed One, I—

Not perceiving and not observing the gain and loss of the fleshly eye, for whom shall I establish the designation "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation "fleshly eye" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, with my divine eye, I do not perceive nor do I see the arising or the passing away [of beings]. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor see the arising or the passing away of the divine eye, for whom shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘divine eye’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, with the eye of wisdom, I do not perceive nor do I see either the arising or the passing away [of anything]. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor see the arising or the passing away of anything with the eye of wisdom, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "eye of wisdom" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, with the Dharma-eye, I do not perceive nor do I behold the arising or the passing away [of anything]. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor behold the arising or the passing away of the Dharma-eye, for whom shall I apply the name "Bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that which is called the "Dharma-eye" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the Buddha-eye, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going. Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving the coming or the going of the Buddha-eye, I—

Observing thus, for whom shall I bestow the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "Buddha-eye" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. In this way, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.

"Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of the six superknowledges (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*). Therefore, Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the six superknowledges, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the name 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name 'the six superknowledges' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the ten powers of a Tathāgata. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "the ten powers of a Tathāgata" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the four grounds of self-confidence, I do not perceive nor do I observe their coming or their going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing the arising or the passing away of the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*), for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "ground of self-confidence" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.
Blessed One, I do not perceive the arising or the passing away of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*).

“I do not perceive it. Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not apprehend and do not perceive the arising and passing away of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), for what shall I designate the name ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name ‘analytical knowledge’ is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising or the passing away of great compassion, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "great compassion" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*). Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, for whom shall I designate the name "Bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, regarding the five aggregates of clinging which are like a dream, I do not perceive nor do I observe their arising or their passing away. O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of these five aggregates of clinging which are like a dream, for what shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘aggregates of clinging’ does not abide, does not persist, and is not established.
Why is that?”

Because that name does not exist as a cause, that name is thus neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the five aggregates of clinging, which are like an illusion. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the five aggregates of clinging, which are like an illusion, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "the five aggregates of clinging" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the five aggregates of clinging as being like an echo, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, their arising or their passing away.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of clinging, which are like an echo, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation of the aggregates of clinging does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the five aggregates of clinging which are like a reflection, I do not perceive nor do I observe their arising or their passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the five aggregates of clinging which are like a reflection, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "the five aggregates of clinging" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, I regard the five aggregates of clinging as being like a reflection.

I do not perceive nor do I observe either the arising or the passing away [of these]. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of clinging which are like a reflection, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name of the aggregates of clinging is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.

Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the five aggregates of clinging which are like a mirage, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, their arising or their passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the arising or the passing away of the five aggregates of clinging which are like a mirage, for what shall I apply the name "Bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "the five aggregates of clinging" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Blessed One, regarding the five aggregates of clinging which are like the moon in water, I do not perceive nor do I observe their arising or their passing away.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of clinging, which are like the moon reflected in water, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation of the aggregates of clinging does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist.

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of these five aggregates of clinging, which are like signs and metaphors. This, O Blessed One, is what I [say].

Not perceiving and not observing the arising and passing away of these five appropriated aggregates which are like a mirage, for whom shall I apply the designation "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation for the appropriated aggregates does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation does not abide, does not persist, and is not established.

“O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I see the coming or going of that which is secluded. O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor see the coming or going of that which is secluded, for what shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, even that name ‘secluded’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.
Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.”

"Blessed One, regarding that which is peaceful, I do not apprehend nor perceive its coming or its going. Blessed One, since I neither apprehend nor perceive the coming or the going of that which is peaceful, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name 'peaceful' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding non-arising, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming into being or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming into being or the passing away of non-arising, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name "non-arising" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not situated, and not sustained.

"Blessed One, regarding that which is without cessation, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of that which is without cessation, for what shall I apply the designation 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that designation 'non-cessation' is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist."

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding this non-manifestation, I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of this non-manifestation, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name of non-manifestation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding that which is unconditioned (*anabhisaṃskāra*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of that which is unconditioned, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "non-conditioning" (anabhisaṃskāra) does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Blessed One, regarding this non-affliction (asaṃkleśa), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe the arising and passing away of this non-affliction, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name "non-affliction" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. As for purification, Blessed One, I [do not perceive its] arising...

I do not perceive nor do I observe its passing away. Therefore, Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the passing away of this purification, for what shall I apply the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "purification" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.
Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of the *dharmadhātu*. Therefore, Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the coming or going of the *dharmadhātu*, for what shall I apply the name ‘bodhisattva’? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name ‘*dharmadhātu*’ is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist.”

Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the coming or going of the Tathāgata. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of the Tathāgata, for whom shall I designate the name "Bodhisattva"? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name of the Tathāgata is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not situated, and not sustained. O Blessed One, regarding the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or going. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive nor observe the coming or going of the limit of reality, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that which is called the "limit of reality" (bhūtakoṭi) is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
Blessed One, regarding the stability of phenomena (dharmasthititā), I do not perceive nor do I observe any coming or going.

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not observing either the arising or the passing away of the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), whose name shall I designate as "bodhisattva"? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name "stability of phenomena" is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained.

"Blessed One, regarding the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmmaniyāmatā*), I do not perceive nor do I observe any coming or going. Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe any coming or going in the fixed nature of phenomena, for what shall I apply the name 'bodhisattva'? Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name 'fixed nature of phenomena' is not established, not situated, and not sustained."

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not situated, and not sustained. O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of wholesome and unwholesome states. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of wholesome and unwholesome dharmas, for whom shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that which is designated as "wholesome" or "unwholesome" does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the arising or the passing away of worldly or supramundane phenomena.

Therefore, Blessed One, since I do not perceive and do not observe the arising or the passing away of worldly and transcendent phenomena, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"? Moreover, Blessed One, even that name—worldly or transcendent—is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not...

It is neither stationary, nor fixed, nor established. O Blessed One, I do not perceive, nor do I clearly see, the arising and passing away of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or clearly see the arising and passing away of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that designation "conditioned" or "unconditioned" is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that designation does not exist. Thus, that designation is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of conditioned phenomena (*sāśrava-dharma*). Since I, O Blessed One, do not perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of conditioned phenomena, for what [phenomenon] shall I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that name of conditioned phenomena does not abide, does not persist, and is not established.”

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or going of past, future, and present phenomena. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I do not perceive or observe the coming or going of past, future, and present phenomena, for what shall I apply the name "bodhisattva"?

Furthermore, Blessed One, even that name of past, future, and present phenomena does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Why is that? Because that name is non-existent. Thus, that name does not abide, does not persist, and is not established. Blessed One, regarding what is neither past, nor future, nor present, I do not perceive nor do I observe its coming or its going. Why is it called "that"? Because the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) is indeed neither past nor future.

Not the present. Blessed One, I do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of the unconditioned. And what is the unconditioned? That which has neither arising, nor duration, nor cessation. Blessed One, I also do not perceive nor do I observe the arising or the passing away of even the Blessed One.

“O Blessed One, in the eastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive nor do I behold the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas.

O Blessed One, in the southern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive nor do I behold the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas.”

"Blessed One, in the western direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas.

Blessed One, in the northern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive, nor do I observe, the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas."

"Blessed One, in the northeastern direction, across world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive nor do I behold the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas.

Blessed One, in the southeastern direction, across world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive nor do I behold the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas."

"Blessed One, in the southwestern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive nor do I behold the income and expenditure of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas. Blessed One, in the northwestern direction, in [world-systems] as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā..."

In the world-systems, I do not perceive nor do I see the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas. O Blessed One, in the world-systems in the downward direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, I do not perceive nor do I see the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas.

"Blessed One, in the direction above, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, I do not perceive and do not see the coming or the going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and their Bodhisattvas."

Therefore, Blessed One, not perceiving and not seeing the coming or going of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas, which Bodhisattva shall I advise and instruct in which Perfection of Wisdom? And which Perfection of Wisdom shall I teach?

Moreover, Blessed One, even that name of the Tathāgata is not established, not fixed, and not sustained; even that name of the Saṅgha is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. Why is that? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.

“O Blessed One, regarding the suchness of all phenomena (*sarvadharmatathatā*), I do not perceive nor do I observe either its arising or its passing away. Therefore, O Blessed One, since I neither perceive nor observe the arising or the passing away of the suchness of all phenomena, for what should I apply the designation ‘bodhisattva’? Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation ‘the suchness of all phenomena’ does not abide, does not persist, and is not established.”
For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained.
Furthermore, O Blessed One, even that designation of a phenomenon through the convention of names—namely, "bodhisattva"—is likewise.

It cannot be described by anyone in terms of form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; nor in terms of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; nor in terms of visible forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects; nor in terms of eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, or mind-consciousness.

Whether by eye-contact, or ear-contact, or nose-contact, or tongue-contact, or body-contact, or mind-contact; or by feeling conditioned by eye-contact, or feeling conditioned by ear-contact, or feeling conditioned by nose-contact, or feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, or feeling conditioned by body-contact, or feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

Neither by the earth element, nor the water element, nor the fire element, nor the wind element, nor the space element, nor the consciousness element; nor by ignorance, nor by volitional formations, nor by consciousness, nor by name-and-form, nor by the six sense bases, nor by contact, nor by feeling, nor by craving, nor by clinging, nor by existence, nor by birth, nor by aging and death.

Whether by the perfection of generosity, or the perfection of ethical discipline, or the perfection of patience, or the perfection of vigor, or the perfection of meditative concentration, or the perfection of wisdom; or by internal emptiness, or external emptiness, or internal and external emptiness; or by the emptiness of emptiness, or the emptiness of the ultimate.

Whether by means of the emptiness of the unconditioned, or the ultimate emptiness, or the emptiness of non-dispersal, or the emptiness of intrinsic nature, or the emptiness of all phenomena, or the emptiness of specific characteristics, or the emptiness of non-apprehension, or the emptiness of non-existence, or the emptiness of self-nature, or the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence; or by means of the applications of mindfulness, or the right efforts, or the bases of psychic power, or the faculties, or the powers, or the factors of enlightenment, or the noble eightfold path.

Or by means of the noble truths, or the meditative concentrations, or the immeasurables, or the formless attainments, or the specific qualities of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, or the powers of a Tathāgata, or the grounds of self-confidence, or the analytical knowledges, or great loving-kindness, or great compassion, or the unique attributes of a Buddha—whatever constitutes the designation of phenomena (*dharmaprajñapti*). Nevertheless, Blessed One, it is as if the name "seven" must be uttered by someone.

It may be called "illusion" by someone; it may be called "echo," "appearance," "mirage," or "moon in water" by someone; it may be called "Tathāgata" by someone. Just as, Blessed One, it may be called "space" by someone, or "earth" by someone, or "water" by someone.
It may be designated by someone as "fire"; it may be designated by someone as "wind"; it may be designated by someone as "suchness"; it may be designated by someone as "non-falsity."

The name "non-other suchness" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "suchness of phenomena" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "dharma-realm" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "stability of phenomena" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "limit of reality" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "perfection of generosity" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "perfection of ethical discipline" cannot be expressed by anyone; the name "perfection of patience" cannot be expressed by anyone.

The name "perfection of vigor" is not to be expressed by anyone; the name "perfection of meditation" is not to be expressed by anyone; the name "perfection of wisdom" is not to be expressed by anyone;

the name "ethical discipline" is not to be expressed by anyone; the name "concentration" is not to be expressed by anyone; the name "wisdom" is not to be expressed by anyone; the name "liberation" is not to be expressed by anyone; the name "knowledge and vision of liberation" is not to be expressed by anyone.

It is not to be designated by anyone as "stream-enterer"; a stream-enterer is not to be designated by anyone. It is not to be designated by anyone as "the dharmas of a stream-enterer. It is not to be designated by anyone as "once-returner"; it is not to be designated by anyone as "the dharmas of a once-returner. It is not to be designated by anyone as "non-returner"; it is not to be designated by anyone as "the dharmas of a non-returner."

The name "Arhat" is not to be spoken by anyone; the name "qualities of an Arhat" is not to be spoken by anyone. The name "Pratyekabuddha" is not to be spoken by anyone; the name "qualities of a Pratyekabuddha" is not to be spoken by anyone. The name "Bodhisattva" is not to be spoken by anyone; the name "qualities of a Bodhisattva" is not to be spoken by anyone. The name "Samyaksambuddha" is not to be spoken by anyone.

Whether it be wholesome or unwholesome, blameworthy or blameless, permanent or impermanent, pleasant or painful, self or non-self, peaceful or unpeaceful, secluded or unsecluded, existent or non-existent.

"Lord, it is for this very reason that I speak thus. It would indeed be a cause for regret for me if, while not perceiving and not observing the coming and going of all dharmas, I were to assign a name—such as 'Bodhisattva' or 'Perfection of Wisdom. Moreover, Lord, even that name is neither established, nor fixed, nor sustained."

For what reason? Because that name does not exist. Thus, that name is not established, not fixed, and not sustained. If, when this perfection of wisdom is being spoken and taught through these aspects, these marks, and these signs, the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not sink, does not become despondent, does not feel regret, and his mind does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear.
It should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is certainly irreversible on the bodhisattva stage, abiding by way of non-abiding.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in form; he should not abide in feeling; he should not abide in perception; he should not abide in mental formations; he should not abide in consciousness. He should not abide in the eye; he should not abide in the ear; he should not abide in the nose; he should not abide in the tongue.

He should not abide in the body; he should not abide in the mind; he should not abide in forms; he should not abide in sounds; he should not abide in odors; he should not abide in tastes; he should not abide in tangibles; he should not abide in mental phenomena (*dharmas*); he should not abide in eye-consciousness; he should not abide in ear-consciousness; he should not abide in nose-consciousness.
