He should not abide in tongue-consciousness; he should not abide in body-consciousness; he should not abide in mind-consciousness. He should not abide in eye-contact; he should not abide in ear-contact; he should not abide in nose-contact; he should not abide in tongue-contact; he should not abide in body-contact; he should not abide in mind-contact.

He should not abide in the feeling born of eye-contact; he should not abide in the feeling born of ear-contact; he should not abide in the feeling born of nose-contact; he should not abide in the feeling born of tongue-contact; he should not abide in the feeling born of body-contact; he should not abide in the feeling born of mind-contact; he should not abide in the earth element.

He should not abide in the water element; he should not abide in the fire element; he should not abide in the wind element; he should not abide in the space element; he should not abide in the consciousness element.

Therefore, one should not abide in ignorance; one should not abide in volitional formations; one should not abide in consciousness; one should not abide in name-and-form; one should not abide in the six sense bases; one should not abide in contact; one should not abide in feeling; one should not abide in craving; one should not abide in clinging; one should not abide in birth; one should not abide in aging and death.

For what reason? Because, Blessed One, form is empty of form. That which is the emptiness of form is not that form, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from form; form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is form. Feeling is empty of feeling. That which is the emptiness of feeling is not that feeling, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from feeling; feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling. Perception is empty of perception. That which is the emptiness of perception is not that perception.

And emptiness is not other than perception; perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is perception. Volitional formations are empty of volitional formations. That which is the emptiness of volitional formations is not those volitional formations, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from volitional formations; volitional formations themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is volitional formations. Consciousness is empty of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of consciousness is that consciousness; nor is emptiness elsewhere than from consciousness; consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is consciousness.

In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in form; he should not abide in feeling; he should not abide in perception; he should not abide in mental formations; he should not abide in consciousness.

For in this way, Blessed One, the eye is empty of the eye; and that which is the emptiness of the eye is neither the eye, nor is emptiness elsewhere than the eye. The eye itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the eye. The ear is empty of the ear; and that which is the emptiness of the ear is neither the ear, nor is emptiness elsewhere than the ear. The ear itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the ear. The nose is empty of the nose; and that which is...

The emptiness of the nose is not that nose; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the nose. The nose itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the nose. The tongue is empty of the tongue; that which is the emptiness of the tongue is not the tongue, nor is emptiness elsewhere than the tongue. The tongue itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the tongue. The body is empty of the body; that which is the emptiness of the body is not the body, nor is emptiness elsewhere than the body. The body itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the body.

The mind is empty of mind; that which is the emptiness of mind is not the mind. Nor is emptiness elsewhere than the mind; the mind itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the mind. Form is empty of form; that which is the emptiness of form is not form. Nor is emptiness elsewhere than form; form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is form. Sound is empty of sound; that which is the emptiness of sound is not sound. Nor is emptiness elsewhere than sound.

Sound is emptiness, and emptiness is sound. Odor is empty of odor; that which is the emptiness of odor is not odor, nor is there emptiness apart from odor—odor itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is odor. Taste is empty of taste; that which is the emptiness of taste is not taste, nor is there emptiness apart from taste—taste itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is taste. Tangible object is empty of tangible object; that which is the emptiness of tangible object is not tangible object.

Nor is emptiness other than contact; contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is contact. Phenomena are empty of phenomena. That which is the emptiness of phenomena is not those phenomena. Nor is emptiness other than phenomena; phenomena themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is phenomena.

Eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness; that which is the emptiness of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from eye-consciousness. Eye-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness is empty of ear-consciousness; that which is the emptiness of ear-consciousness is not that ear-consciousness, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from ear-consciousness.
Ear-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ear-consciousness.

Olfactory consciousness is empty of olfactory consciousness. That which is the emptiness of olfactory consciousness is not that olfactory consciousness, nor is emptiness elsewhere than olfactory consciousness; olfactory consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is olfactory consciousness. Gustatory consciousness is empty of gustatory consciousness. And that which is the emptiness of gustatory consciousness is not that gustatory consciousness.

Nor is emptiness other than tongue-consciousness; tongue-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is tongue-consciousness. Body-consciousness is empty of body-consciousness. That which is the emptiness of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness. Nor is emptiness other than body-consciousness; emptiness itself is body-consciousness. Mind-consciousness is empty of mind-consciousness. That which is the emptiness of mind-consciousness is not that mind-consciousness. Nor is emptiness other than mind-consciousness; mind-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is mind-consciousness.

Eye-contact is empty of eye-contact. That which is the emptiness of eye-contact is not eye-contact; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in eye-contact. Eye-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is eye-contact. Ear-contact is empty of ear-contact. That which is the emptiness of ear-contact is not ear-contact; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in ear-contact.

Auditory contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is auditory contact. Olfactory contact is empty of olfactory contact; that which is the emptiness of olfactory contact is not that olfactory contact, nor is emptiness elsewhere than olfactory contact. Auditory contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is auditory contact. Gustatory contact is empty of gustatory contact; that which is the emptiness of gustatory contact is not that gustatory contact.

And emptiness is not elsewhere than tongue-contact; tongue-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is tongue-contact. Body-contact is empty of body-contact; and that which is the emptiness of body-contact—

That body-contact is not [inherently existent]; moreover, emptiness is not apart from body-contact. Body-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is body-contact. Mental contact is empty of mental contact; that which is the emptiness of mental contact is not that mental contact. Nor is emptiness apart from mental contact. Mental contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is mental contact.

Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by eye-contact. That which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from feeling conditioned by eye-contact. Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is itself emptiness; emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by eye-contact.

Feeling conditioned by auditory contact is empty of feeling conditioned by auditory contact. Nor is emptiness other than feeling conditioned by auditory contact; feeling conditioned by auditory contact is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself feeling conditioned by auditory contact. Feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is empty of feeling conditioned by olfactory contact.

That which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by nose-contact is not that feeling conditioned by nose-contact, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from feeling conditioned by nose-contact; feeling conditioned by nose-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by nose-contact. Feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.

That which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; nor is emptiness other than the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact. The feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is itself emptiness, and emptiness itself is the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact. Feeling conditioned by body-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by body-contact.

That which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by bodily contact is not that feeling conditioned by bodily contact; nor is emptiness other than the feeling conditioned by bodily contact. Feeling conditioned by bodily contact is itself emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by bodily contact. [The same applies to] feeling conditioned by mental contact.

Feeling conditioned by mental contact is empty. That which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not that feeling conditioned by mental contact; nor is emptiness apart from feeling conditioned by mental contact. Feeling conditioned by mental contact is itself emptiness; emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by mental contact.

The earth element is empty of the earth element. That which is the emptiness of the earth element is not the earth element; nor is there emptiness apart from the earth element. The earth element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the earth element. The water element is empty of the water element. That which is the emptiness of the water element is not the water element; nor is there emptiness apart from the water element. The water element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the water element. The fire element is empty of the fire element.

That which is the emptiness of the fire element is not that fire element; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the fire element. The fire element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the fire element. The air element is empty of the air element; that which is the emptiness of the air element is not that air element; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the air element. The air element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the air element. The space element is empty of the space element.

That which is the emptiness of the space-element is not that space-element; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the space-element. The space-element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the space-element. The consciousness-element is empty of the consciousness-element; that which is the emptiness of the consciousness-element is not that consciousness-element; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the consciousness-element. The consciousness-element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the consciousness-element. Ignorance, Blessed One, is empty of ignorance.

That which is the emptiness of ignorance is not ignorance; nor is emptiness other than ignorance. Ignorance itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ignorance. Formations are empty of formations; that which is the emptiness of formations is not those formations, nor is emptiness other than formations. Formations themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is formations. Consciousness is empty of consciousness; that which is the emptiness of consciousness is not that consciousness, nor is emptiness other than consciousness. Consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is consciousness.

Name-and-form is empty of name-and-form; that which is the emptiness of name-and-form is not that name-and-form, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from name-and-form. Name-and-form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is name-and-form. The six sense bases are empty of the six sense bases; that which is the emptiness of the six sense bases is not those six sense bases, nor is emptiness elsewhere than from the six sense bases. The six sense bases themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the six sense bases. Contact is empty of contact.

That which is the emptiness of contact is not that contact; nor is emptiness elsewhere than from contact. Contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is contact. Feeling is empty of feeling; that which is the emptiness of feeling is not that feeling; nor is emptiness elsewhere than from feeling. Feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling. Craving is empty of craving; that which is the emptiness of craving is not that craving; nor is emptiness elsewhere than from craving.

Craving itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is craving. Grasping is empty of grasping; that which is the emptiness of grasping is not grasping, nor is emptiness elsewhere than grasping. Grasping itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is grasping. Existence is empty of existence; that which is the emptiness of existence is not existence, nor is emptiness elsewhere than existence. Existence itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is existence. Birth is empty of birth; that which is the emptiness of birth is not birth.

And emptiness is not elsewhere than birth; birth itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is birth. Old age and death are empty of old age and death. That which is the emptiness of old age and death is not old age and death. And emptiness is not elsewhere than old age and death; old age and death themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is old age and death.

In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in ignorance; he should not abide in volitional formations; he should not abide in consciousness; he should not abide in name-and-form; he should not abide in the six sense bases; he should not abide in contact; he should not abide in feeling; he should not abide in craving; he should not abide in grasping; he should not abide in aging and death.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of giving. Why is that? Because the perfection of giving is empty of the perfection of giving. That which is the emptiness of the perfection of giving is not the perfection of giving; nor is there emptiness apart from the perfection of giving. The perfection of giving itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of giving.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of ethical discipline. Why is that? Because the perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline. That which is the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline; nor is there emptiness apart from the perfection of ethical discipline. The perfection of ethical discipline itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of ethical discipline.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of patience. Why is that? Because the perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience. That which is the emptiness of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience; nor is there emptiness apart from the perfection of patience. The perfection of patience itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of patience.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of vigor. Why is that? Because the perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor; and that which is...

The emptiness of the perfection of vigor is not that perfection of vigor; nor is emptiness other than the perfection of vigor. The perfection of vigor itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of vigor. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of meditative concentration. Why is that? Because the perfection of meditative concentration is empty of the perfection of meditative concentration.

That which is the emptiness of the perfection of meditation is not that perfection of meditation; nor is emptiness apart from the perfection of meditation. The perfection of meditation itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of meditation. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom.

That which is the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom is not the perfection of wisdom; nor is emptiness apart from the perfection of wisdom. The perfection of wisdom itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of wisdom. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the six perfections.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four foundations of mindfulness. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the foundations of mindfulness are empty of the foundations of mindfulness. And that which is the emptiness of the foundations of mindfulness, Blessed One, is not those foundations of mindfulness; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in the foundations of mindfulness.

The foundations of mindfulness are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the foundations of mindfulness. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the foundations of mindfulness. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom [should not abide] in the right efforts.

One should not abide therein. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, the right efforts are empty of the right efforts. That which is the emptiness of the right efforts is not those right efforts; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the right efforts. The right efforts themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the right efforts. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the right efforts.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the bases of psychic power are empty of the bases of psychic power. That which is the emptiness of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power; nor is emptiness apart from the bases of psychic power. The bases of psychic power themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the bases of psychic power.

"In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*). Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the faculties (*indriya*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the faculties are empty of faculties; and that which is the emptiness of the faculties, Blessed One, is not those faculties."

Nor is emptiness other than the sense faculties; the sense faculties themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the sense faculties. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the sense faculties. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the five powers.

For what reason? Because, Blessed One, the powers are empty of powers. And that which is the emptiness of the powers, Blessed One, is not those powers; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in the powers. The powers themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the powers. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the powers.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the seven factors of enlightenment. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment. That which is the emptiness of the factors of enlightenment, Blessed One, is not those factors of enlightenment; nor is emptiness apart from the factors of enlightenment. The factors of enlightenment themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the factors of enlightenment.

In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the seven factors of enlightenment. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the noble eightfold path. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the path is empty of a path.

And as for that emptiness of the path, O Blessed One, it is not the path, nor is emptiness elsewhere than the path; the path itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the path. By this method, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not stand upon the path. Furthermore, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not stand upon the four noble truths. Why is that? Because:

"Blessed One, the noble truths are empty of the noble truths. And that which is the emptiness of the noble truths, Blessed One, is not those noble truths, nor is emptiness apart from the noble truths; the noble truths themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the noble truths. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the noble truths."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the meditative concentrations are empty of meditative concentrations. That which is the emptiness of the meditative concentrations is not those meditative concentrations; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in the meditative concentrations. The meditative concentrations themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the meditative concentrations. It is by this method, Blessed One, [that one should understand].

A bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*). Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the immeasurables are empty of measures; and that which is the emptiness of the immeasurables, Blessed One, is not those immeasurables themselves.

Nor is emptiness other than the immeasurables; the immeasurables themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the immeasurables. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the immeasurables. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four formless attainments. Why is that? Because:

"Blessed One, the formless attainments are empty of formless attainments. And that which is the emptiness of the formless attainments, Blessed One, is not those formless attainments. Nor is emptiness elsewhere than the formless attainments; the formless attainments themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the formless attainments. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the formless attainments."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the eight liberations. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the liberations are empty of liberations. And that which is the emptiness of the liberations, Blessed One, is not those liberations; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the liberations. The liberations themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the liberations.

"In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the liberations. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the successive attainments of meditative dwelling..."

They are empty of the attainments of the successive dwellings (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*). And, Blessed One, that which is the emptiness of the attainments of the successive dwellings is not those attainments of the successive dwellings; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the attainments of the successive dwellings. The attainments of the successive dwellings themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the attainments of the successive dwellings.

In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the successive meditative attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*). Furthermore, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is that? Because:

"Blessed One, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. And that which is the emptiness of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—that is not those gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness."

And emptiness is not found apart from the doors of liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the doors of liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Therefore, Blessed One, by this method, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the doors of liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the ten powers of a Tathāgata. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the powers of a Tathāgata. And that which is the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata, Blessed One, is not those powers of a Tathāgata; nor is emptiness apart from the powers of a Tathāgata. The powers of a Tathāgata are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the powers of a Tathāgata.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the powers of a Tathāgata. Furthermore, Blessed One, by a bodhisattva mahāsattva...

One practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four grounds of self-confidence. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the grounds of self-confidence are empty of the grounds of self-confidence. That which is the emptiness of the grounds of self-confidence, Blessed One, is not those grounds of self-confidence; nor is emptiness apart from the grounds of self-confidence. The grounds of self-confidence are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the grounds of self-confidence.
By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the grounds of self-confidence.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the analytical knowledges are empty of analytical knowledges. That which is the emptiness of the analytical knowledges is not those analytical knowledges; nor is emptiness elsewhere than the analytical knowledges—the analytical knowledges themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the analytical knowledges.

In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*). Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, great compassion is empty of great compassion; and that which is the emptiness of great compassion is not [itself] great compassion.

And emptiness does not exist apart from great compassion; great compassion itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is great compassion. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in great compassion. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Why is that? Because:

"Blessed One, the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha. And that emptiness of the unique qualities of a Buddha, Blessed One, is not those unique qualities of a Buddha; nor is emptiness other than the unique qualities of a Buddha. The unique qualities of a Buddha are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the unique qualities of a Buddha. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) should not dwell upon the unique qualities of a Buddha."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in syllables; he should not abide in single utterances; he should not abide in distinct utterances. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, syllables are empty of syllables. That which is the emptiness of syllables is not those syllables. Nor is emptiness apart from syllables; syllables themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is syllables.

By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in syllables. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the superknowledges (*abhijñā*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the superknowledges are empty of superknowledges; and that which is the emptiness of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges.

Nor is emptiness apart from the superknowledges; the superknowledges themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the superknowledges. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in the superknowledges. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell in any of the gateways to meditative concentration. Why is that? Because:

"Blessed One, all gateways to concentration are empty by means of the gateways to concentration. That which is the emptiness of the gateways to concentration is not those gateways to concentration; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in the gateways to concentration. The gateways to concentration themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the gateways to concentration. Blessed One, by this method, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom [should train] in all gateways to concentration."

One should not abide [therein]. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in all the gateways of the dhāraṇīs. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are empty of the gateways of the dhāraṇīs. That which is the emptiness of the gateways of the dhāraṇīs is not those gateways of the dhāraṇīs; nor is emptiness apart from the gateways of the dhāraṇīs. The gateways of the dhāraṇīs are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the gateways of the dhāraṇīs.
In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the gateways of dhāraṇī.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is impermanent. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the impermanence of form is empty of the impermanence of form. That which is the emptiness of the impermanence of form is not that impermanence of form; nor is emptiness other than the impermanence of form. The very impermanence of form is emptiness; emptiness itself is the impermanence of form.

In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the impermanence of form. Furthermore, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "feeling is impermanent. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, the impermanence of feeling is empty of the impermanence of feeling; and that which is the emptiness of the impermanence of feeling is not that impermanence of feeling.

Nor is emptiness other than the impermanence of feeling; the impermanence of feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the impermanence of feeling. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the impermanence of feeling. Therefore, in the perfection of wisdom...

One practicing [the path] should not abide in the notion that "perception is permanent. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the permanence of perception is empty of the permanence of perception. That which is the emptiness of the permanence of perception is not that permanence of perception; nor is emptiness other than the permanence of perception. The permanence of perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the permanence of perception.

In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that "perception is impermanent. While practicing the perfection of wisdom, he should not abide in the thought that "formative forces are impermanent. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, the impermanence of formative forces is empty of the impermanence of formative forces; and that which is the emptiness of the impermanence of formative forces is not itself the impermanence of formative forces.

The very impermanence of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) is emptiness; emptiness itself is the impermanence of conditioned phenomena. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) should not dwell on the thought that "conditioned phenomena are impermanent. While practicing the perfection of wisdom, he should not dwell on the thought that "consciousness (*vijñāna*) is impermanent. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the impermanence of consciousness is empty of the impermanence of consciousness.

And as for that emptiness of the impermanence of consciousness, O Blessed One, it is not [separate from] the impermanence of consciousness; nor is emptiness elsewhere than in the impermanence of consciousness. The very impermanence of consciousness is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the impermanence of consciousness. By this method, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "consciousness is impermanent."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "form is suffering. Why is that? Because the state of suffering of form is empty of the state of suffering of form. That which is the emptiness of the state of suffering of form is not itself the state of suffering of form; nor is emptiness other than the state of suffering of form. It is the very state of suffering of form [that is emptiness].

Emptiness is indeed emptiness; it is the very nature of form that is suffering. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the suffering of form. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "feeling is suffering. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the suffering of feeling is empty of the suffering of feeling.

That which is the emptiness of the suffering of feeling is not that suffering of feeling; nor is emptiness apart from the suffering of feeling. The suffering of feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the suffering of feeling. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the suffering of feeling.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "perception is suffering. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the suffering of perception is empty of the suffering of perception. That which is the emptiness of the suffering of perception is not itself the suffering of perception; nor is emptiness other than the suffering of perception. The suffering of perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the suffering of perception.

In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the suffering of perception. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell upon the thought that "formative forces are suffering. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the suffering of formative forces is empty of the suffering of formative forces.

That which is the emptiness of the suffering of conditioned formations is not itself the suffering of conditioned formations; nor is emptiness other than the suffering of conditioned formations. The suffering of conditioned formations is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the suffering of conditioned formations. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the suffering of conditioned formations. Furthermore, Blessed One, by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom...

One practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that consciousness is suffering. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the suffering-nature of consciousness is empty of the suffering-nature of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of the suffering-nature of consciousness is not itself the suffering-nature of consciousness; nor is emptiness other than the suffering-nature of consciousness. The suffering-nature of consciousness is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the suffering-nature of consciousness.
By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the suffering-nature of consciousness.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is selfless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the selflessness of form is empty of the selflessness of form. That which is the emptiness of the selflessness of form is not that selflessness of form; nor is emptiness other than the selflessness of form. The selflessness of form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the selflessness of form.

In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that "form is selfless. Furthermore, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that "feeling is selfless. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, the selflessness of feeling is empty of the selflessness of feeling; and that which is the emptiness of the selflessness of feeling is not itself the selflessness of feeling.

Nor is emptiness other than the selflessness of feeling; the very selflessness of feeling is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the selflessness of feeling. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "feeling is selfless. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "perception is selfless. Why is that? Because:
Blessed One, the nature of perception is empty of the nature of perception; and that which is the emptiness of the nature of perception is not [that nature].

The nature of perception is emptiness; nor is emptiness other than the nature of perception. The nature of perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the nature of perception. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that "perception is the self. Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that "formative forces are non-self."

For what reason? Because, Blessed One, the selflessness of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) is empty by virtue of the selflessness of conditioned phenomena. That which is the emptiness of the selflessness of conditioned phenomena is not that selflessness of conditioned phenomena; nor is emptiness other than the selflessness of conditioned phenomena. The selflessness of conditioned phenomena itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the selflessness of conditioned phenomena. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) should not dwell on the thought that "conditioned phenomena are without self."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "consciousness is non-self. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the non-selfhood of consciousness is empty of the non-selfhood of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of the non-selfhood of consciousness is not that non-selfhood of consciousness; nor is emptiness other than the non-selfhood of consciousness. The non-selfhood of consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the non-selfhood of consciousness.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that consciousness is selfless.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that "form is peaceful. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the peacefulness of form is empty of the peacefulness of form. That which is the emptiness of the peacefulness of form is not the peacefulness of form; nor is emptiness other than the peacefulness of form. The peacefulness of form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the peacefulness of form. It is by this method, Blessed One, [that one should understand].
A bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that form is peaceful.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "feeling is peaceful. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the peacefulness of feeling is empty of the peacefulness of feeling. That which is the emptiness of the peacefulness of feeling is not that peacefulness of feeling; nor is emptiness other than the peacefulness of feeling. The peacefulness of feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the peacefulness of feeling.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "feeling is peaceful."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that “perception is peaceful. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the peacefulness of perception is empty of the peacefulness of perception. That which is the emptiness of the peacefulness of perception is not that peacefulness of perception; nor is emptiness other than the peacefulness of perception. The peacefulness of perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the peacefulness of perception.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "perception is peaceful."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "conditioned phenomena are peaceful. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the peacefulness of conditioned phenomena is empty of the peacefulness of conditioned phenomena. That which is the emptiness of the peacefulness of conditioned phenomena is not itself the peacefulness of conditioned phenomena; nor is emptiness other than the peacefulness of conditioned phenomena. The peacefulness of conditioned phenomena is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the peacefulness of conditioned phenomena.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "formative forces are peaceful."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "consciousness is peaceful. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the peacefulness of consciousness is empty of the peacefulness of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of the peacefulness of consciousness is not that peacefulness of consciousness; nor is emptiness other than the peacefulness of consciousness. The peacefulness of consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the peacefulness of consciousness.
In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that "consciousness is peaceful."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is empty. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the emptiness of form is empty of the emptiness of form. That which is the emptiness of form is not the emptiness of form; nor is there emptiness apart from the emptiness of form. The very emptiness of form is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of form.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is empty."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "feeling is empty. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the emptiness of feeling is empty of the emptiness of feeling. That which is the emptiness of feeling is not the emptiness of feeling; nor is there emptiness apart from the emptiness of feeling. The very emptiness of feeling is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of feeling.
By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "feeling is empty.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "perception is empty. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the emptiness of perception is empty of the emptiness of perception; and that which is the emptiness of perception is not [perception].

The emptiness of perception; nor is emptiness other than the emptiness of perception. The emptiness of perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of perception. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "perception is empty."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "formations are empty. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the emptiness of formations is empty of the emptiness of formations. That which is the emptiness of formations is not [inherently] the emptiness of formations; nor is there emptiness apart from the emptiness of formations. The emptiness of formations is itself emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of formations.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "formative forces are empty."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "consciousness is empty. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the emptiness of consciousness is empty of the emptiness of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of the emptiness of consciousness is not the emptiness of consciousness. Nor is there emptiness apart from the emptiness of consciousness; the emptiness of consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of consciousness.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "consciousness is empty."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "form is signless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the signlessness of form is empty of the signlessness of form. That which is the emptiness of the signlessness of form is not the signlessness of form; nor is emptiness other than the signlessness of form. The signlessness of form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the signlessness of form.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that form is signless.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that "feeling has a sign. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the state of having a sign in feeling is empty of the state of having a sign in feeling. That which is the emptiness of the state of having a sign in feeling is not that state of having a sign in feeling. Nor is emptiness other than the state of having a sign in feeling; the state of having a sign in feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the state of having a sign in feeling.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that "this is the sign of feeling."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that "this is a sign. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the state of being a sign is empty of the state of being a sign. That which is the emptiness of the state of being a sign is not that state of being a sign; nor is emptiness other than the state of being a sign. The state of being a sign is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the state of being a sign.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the notion that "this is a sign."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "conditioned phenomena are signless. Why is that? Because the signlessness of conditioned phenomena is empty of the signlessness of conditioned phenomena. That which is the emptiness of the signlessness of conditioned phenomena is not itself the signlessness of conditioned phenomena; nor is emptiness other than the signlessness of conditioned phenomena. The signlessness of conditioned phenomena is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the signlessness of conditioned phenomena. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva...
A mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that conditioned phenomena are signless.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "consciousness is signless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the signlessness of consciousness is empty of the signlessness of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of the signlessness of consciousness is not itself the signlessness of consciousness; nor is there emptiness apart from the signlessness of consciousness. The signlessness of consciousness is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself the signlessness of consciousness.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that consciousness is signless.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is wishless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the wishlessness of form is empty of the wishlessness of form. That which is the emptiness of the wishlessness of form is not that wishlessness of form; nor is there emptiness apart from the wishlessness of form. The wishlessness of form itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is the wishlessness of form.

In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "form is wishless. Furthermore, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "[it] is wishless. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, the wishlessness of feeling is empty of the wishlessness of feeling.

That which is the emptiness of the wishlessness of feeling is not that wishlessness of feeling; nor is emptiness other than the wishlessness of feeling. The wishlessness of feeling itself is emptiness;

emptiness itself is the wishlessness of feeling. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell [with the thought], "this is the wishlessness of feeling."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "perception is wishless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, perception as wishless is empty by virtue of its being wishless. That which is the emptiness of perception as wishless is not that perception as wishless; nor is emptiness other than perception as wishless. Perception as wishless itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is perception as wishless.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "perception is wishless."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "formations are wishless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the wishlessness of formations is empty of the wishlessness of formations. That which is the emptiness of the wishlessness of formations is not that wishlessness of formations; nor is emptiness other than the wishlessness of formations. The wishlessness of formations itself is emptiness.

Emptiness itself is the wishlessness of conditioned phenomena. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "conditioned phenomena are wishless."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "consciousness is wishless. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the wishlessness of consciousness is empty of the wishlessness of consciousness. And that which is the emptiness of the wishlessness of consciousness is not that wishlessness of consciousness; nor is emptiness other than the wishlessness of consciousness. It is simply the wishlessness of consciousness itself.

Emptiness; emptiness itself is the wishlessness of consciousness. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "consciousness is wishless."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is secluded. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the seclusion of form is empty of the seclusion of form. That which is the emptiness of the seclusion of form is not that seclusion of form; nor is emptiness other than the seclusion of form. The seclusion of form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the seclusion of form.
In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "form is secluded."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "feeling is secluded. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the seclusion of feeling is empty of the seclusion of feeling. That which is the emptiness of the seclusion of feeling is not the seclusion of feeling; nor is there emptiness apart from the seclusion of feeling. The seclusion of feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the seclusion of feeling.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that feeling is secluded.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "perception is secluded. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the seclusion of perception is empty of the seclusion of perception. That which is the emptiness of the seclusion of perception is not the seclusion of perception, nor is emptiness other than the seclusion of perception; the seclusion of perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the seclusion of perception. By this...
"Blessed One, by way of this method, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that 'perception is secluded'."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "formations are secluded. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the seclusion of formations is empty of the seclusion of formations. That which is the emptiness of the seclusion of formations is not that seclusion of formations; nor is emptiness other than the seclusion of formations. The seclusion of formations itself is emptiness.

Emptiness itself is the state of being secluded from conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*). By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the thought that "conditioned phenomena are secluded."

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not dwell on the thought that "consciousness is secluded. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the seclusion of consciousness is empty of the seclusion of consciousness. That which is the emptiness of the seclusion of consciousness is not that seclusion of consciousness; nor is emptiness other than the seclusion of consciousness. The seclusion of consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the seclusion of consciousness.
In this manner, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the notion that consciousness is secluded.

Furthermore, O Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in suchness. Why is that? Because, O Blessed One, suchness is empty of suchness. That which is the emptiness of suchness is not suchness; nor is emptiness other than suchness. Suchness itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is suchness.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in suchness.

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the nature of phenomena (dharmatā). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the nature of phenomena is empty of the nature of phenomena. That which is the emptiness of the nature of phenomena is not that nature of phenomena; nor is emptiness other than the nature of phenomena—emptiness itself is the nature of phenomena.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide even in the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the realm of phenomena is empty of the realm of phenomena. That which is the emptiness of the realm of phenomena is not the realm of phenomena; nor is emptiness other than the realm of phenomena. The realm of phenomena itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the realm of phenomena.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmmaniyāmatā*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the fixed nature of phenomena is empty of the fixed nature of phenomena. That which is the emptiness of the fixed nature of phenomena is not the fixed nature of phenomena; nor is emptiness other than the fixed nature of phenomena. The fixed nature of phenomena itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the fixed nature of phenomena.
In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmmaniyāmatā*).

Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the limit of reality is empty of the limit of reality; and that which is the emptiness of the limit of reality is not [the limit of reality].

It is the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Emptiness is not other than the limit of reality; the limit of reality itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the limit of reality. By this method, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should not abide in the limit of reality.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in form, he courses in the conditioning of form and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in feeling...

If he courses in the formative activity of feeling, he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, through lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in perception, he courses in the formative activity of perception and does not course in the perfection of wisdom.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells in formative forces with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine" due to a lack of skill in means, he courses in the construction of formative forces and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells in consciousness with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine" due to a lack of skill in means...

If one courses in the mental formation of consciousness, one does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in mental formation does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Failing to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into all-aspect-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skillful means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," dwells in the eye; [from] the eye...

He courses in mental construction; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, through lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in the ear, he courses in the mental construction of the ear; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in the nose, he courses in the formative activity of the nose and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in the tongue...

He courses in the mental formation of the tongue, but he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skillful means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," dwells in the body, he courses in the mental formation of the body, but he does not course in the perfection of wisdom.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine" due to a lack of skill in means, he courses in the mental formation of that mind and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in mental formation does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he apply himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Failing to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-aspect omniscience.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in form, he courses in the conditioned formation of form and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine"...

If he abides in sound with a mind [characterized by] "I" and "mine," he courses in the formative activity of sound and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, through lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by "I" and "mine," abides in odor, he courses in the formative activity of odor and does not course in the perfection of wisdom.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in taste, he practices the conditioning of taste and does not practice the perfection of wisdom. If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," abides in contact, he practices the conditioning of contact.

He does not course in the perfection of wisdom.
