Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, one does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the ten powers of a Tathāgata, he courses in the conditioned construction of those powers of a Tathāgata; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioned construction does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the four grounds of self-confidence, he is practicing the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) regarding those grounds of self-confidence; he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva who practices in formative activity [does not fulfill the perfection of wisdom].

The Mahāsattva grasps the perfection of wisdom, yet does not enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom; failing to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-aspect-knowledge.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the perfection of wisdom, dwells in the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) with a mind characterized by "I-making" and "mine-making" due to a lack of skill in means, he practices in the fabrication of the analytical knowledges; he does not practice in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in fabrication does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*). Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skillful means (*anupāyakauśala*) and with a mind characterized by "I-making" and "mine-making," should abide in great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), he practices the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) of great compassion; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-aspect-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*). Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by "I-making" and "mine-making," abides in the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), he courses in the conditioned formation of those eighteen unique qualities of a buddha; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioned formation does not grasp the perfection of wisdom.
He does not enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom; failing to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by "I-making" and "mine-making," should abide in the fruit of stream-entry, he courses in the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) of the fruit of stream-entry; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, one does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the fruit of a once-returner, he courses in the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) of the fruit of a once-returner; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the fruit of a non-returner, he courses in the formative activity of the fruit of a non-returner; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skillful means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in arhatship, he courses in the conditioned formation (*abhisaṃskāra*) of arhatship; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioned formation does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," comes to abide in solitary awakening (pratyekabodhi), he courses in the conditioned formation of solitary awakening; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioned formation does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Without fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, one does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells in the knowledge of the aspects of the path with a mind characterized by "I-making" and "mine-making" due to a lack of skill in means, he practices in the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) of the knowledge of the aspects of the path; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he apply himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, one does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the knowledge of all aspects, he courses in the conditioned activity of the knowledge of all aspects; he does not truly course [in it].

In the *prajñāpāramitā*. For what reason? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioned activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) does not grasp the *prajñāpāramitā*, nor does he enter into the yoga of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Without fulfilling the *prajñāpāramitā*, he does not go forth to all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, dwells in suchness with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine" due to a lack of skill in means, he practices the conditioning of suchness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in conditioning does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-aspect omniscience.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in suchness, he is practicing the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) of suchness; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in non-dual suchness, he courses in the conditioning of non-dual suchness; he does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioning does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, does not enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom, and failing to fulfill the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), he practices the conditioned formation of the true nature of phenomena; he does not practice the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices conditioned formation does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Without fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), he is practicing the conditioned activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) of the realm of phenomena; he is not practicing in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices in conditioned activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*), he is practicing the formative activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) regarding the stability of phenomena; he is not practicing the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices formative activity does not grasp the perfection of wisdom, nor does he apply himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.

Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to the knowledge of all aspects. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skill in means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide in the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), he courses in the conditioned activity of the fixed nature of phenomena; he does not truly course [in the perfection of wisdom].

In the *Prajñāpāramitā*: For what reason? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioned activity (*abhisaṃskāra*) does not grasp the *prajñāpāramitā*, nor does he enter into the yoga of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Without fulfilling the *prajñāpāramitā*, he does not go forth to all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the perfection of wisdom, through a lack of skillful means and with a mind characterized by the notions of "I" and "mine," should abide at the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), he courses in the conditioning of the limit of reality and does not course in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in conditioning does not grasp the perfection of wisdom; he does not enter into the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
Not fulfilling the perfection of wisdom, he does not go forth to all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

For what reason? Because, Blessed One, form is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of form is not form, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Feeling is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of feeling is not feeling, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Perception is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of perception is not perception, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Volitional formations are ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of volitional formations is not those volitional formations, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. Consciousness is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of consciousness is not that consciousness, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. The eye is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of the eye is not that eye, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The ear is ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the ear is not the ear, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. The nose is ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the nose is not the nose, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. The tongue is ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the tongue is not the tongue, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The body is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of the body is not the body, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. The mind is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of the mind is not the mind, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Form is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of form is not form, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Sound is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of sound is not sound, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Odor is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of odor is not that odor, because of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Taste is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of taste is not that taste, because of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Touch is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of touch is not that touch, because of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Phenomena are ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of phenomena is not those phenomena, because of their emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Eye-consciousness is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of eye-consciousness is not eye-consciousness, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Knowledge is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of knowledge is not knowledge, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Ear-consciousness is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of ear-consciousness is not ear-consciousness, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Olfactory consciousness is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of olfactory consciousness is not that olfactory consciousness, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Gustatory consciousness is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of gustatory consciousness is not that gustatory consciousness, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Tactile consciousness is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of tactile consciousness is not that tactile consciousness, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Mental consciousness is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of mental consciousness is not that mental consciousness, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Visual contact is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of visual contact is not that [visual contact].

Visual contact is empty by nature; auditory contact is ungraspable, and that which is the non-grasping of auditory contact is not auditory contact, because it is empty by nature. Olfactory contact is ungraspable, and that which is the non-grasping of olfactory contact is not olfactory contact, because it is empty by nature.

Tongue-contact is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of tongue-contact is not tongue-contact, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Body-contact is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of body-contact is not body-contact, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Mind-contact is ungraspable; that which is the non-grasping of mind-contact is not mind-contact, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

It is not grasped by the feeling conditioned by eye-contact; and that which is the non-grasping of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is not grasped by the feeling conditioned by ear-contact; and that which is the non-grasping of the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not that feeling conditioned by ear-contact, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is not grasped by the feeling conditioned by nose-contact.

And that which is the non-appropriation of feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is not that feeling conditioned by olfactory contact, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is not appropriated as feeling conditioned by gustatory contact. And that which is the non-appropriation of feeling conditioned by gustatory contact is not that feeling conditioned by gustatory contact, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is not appropriated as feeling conditioned by tactile contact.

And that which is the non-appropriation of feeling conditioned by bodily contact is not that feeling conditioned by bodily contact, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. Feeling conditioned by mental contact is not appropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not that feeling conditioned by mental contact, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The earth element is unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the earth element is not the earth element, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. The water element is unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the water element is not the water element, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. The fire element is unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the fire element is not the fire element, by virtue of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The wind element is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of the wind element is not the wind element, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. The space element is ungraspable; and that which is the non-grasping of the space element is not the space element, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The consciousness-element is ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the consciousness-element is not the consciousness-element, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Ignorance is grasped; and that which is the non-grasping of ignorance is not ignorance, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Formative forces are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of formative forces is not those formative forces, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Consciousness is ungrasped.

That which is the non-appropriation of consciousness is not that consciousness, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature; name-and-form is unappropriated. That which is the non-appropriation of name-and-form is not that name-and-form, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature; the six sense bases are unappropriated. That which is the non-appropriation of the six sense bases is not those six sense bases, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Contact is ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of contact is not contact, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Feeling is ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of feeling is not feeling, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Craving is ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of craving is not craving, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Grasping is ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of grasping is not grasping, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Existence is ungrasped.

That which is the non-appropriation of existence is not existence, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Birth is unappropriated; that which is the non-appropriation of birth is not birth, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Old age and death are unappropriated; that which is the non-appropriation of old age and death is not old age and death, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

It is embraced by the perfection of generosity; yet that which is the non-appropriation of the perfection of generosity is not the perfection of generosity, based on its emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the perfection of ethical discipline; yet that which is the non-appropriation of the perfection of ethical discipline is not the perfection of ethical discipline, based on its emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the perfection of patience; yet that which is the non-appropriation of the perfection of patience is not the perfection of patience, based on its emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the perfection of vigor.

That which is the non-appropriation of the perfection of vigor is not that perfection of vigor, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; it is embraced by the perfection of meditative concentration. That which is the non-appropriation of the perfection of meditative concentration is not that perfection of meditative concentration, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; it is embraced by the perfection of wisdom. And that which is the non-appropriation within the perfection of wisdom is not that perfection of wisdom, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

It is embraced by internal emptiness; yet that which is the non-appropriation of internal emptiness is not [itself] internal emptiness, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by external emptiness; yet that which is the non-appropriation of external emptiness is not [itself] external emptiness, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by internal-and-external emptiness.

That which is the non-appropriation of internal-and-external emptiness is not that internal-and-external emptiness, by reason of its being empty of intrinsic nature; and that which is the non-appropriation of the emptiness of emptiness is not that emptiness of emptiness, by reason of its being empty of intrinsic nature.

By way of dependence: it is embraced by great emptiness; yet that which is the non-appropriation of great emptiness is not "great emptiness," by way of dependence on natural emptiness. It is embraced by ultimate emptiness; yet that which is the non-appropriation of ultimate emptiness is not "ultimate emptiness," by way of dependence on natural emptiness. It is embraced by conditioned emptiness; yet that which is the non-appropriation of conditioned emptiness is not "conditioned emptiness," by way of dependence on natural emptiness.

Embraced by the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), that which is the non-embrace of the emptiness of the unconditioned is not that emptiness of the unconditioned, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*). Embraced by the ultimate emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), that which is the non-embrace of the ultimate emptiness is not that ultimate emptiness, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Embraced by the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), that which is the non-embrace of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is not that emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

Emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) is embraced by that which is the non-appropriation of emptiness of non-dispersal; yet, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), that non-appropriation of emptiness of non-dispersal is not itself emptiness of non-dispersal. It is embraced by the emptiness of intrinsic nature; yet, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, that non-appropriation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not itself the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*); yet, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, that non-appropriation of the emptiness of all phenomena is not itself the emptiness of all phenomena.

It is embraced by the emptiness of specific characteristics; yet that which is the non-appropriation of the emptiness of specific characteristics is not itself the emptiness of specific characteristics, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the emptiness of the unapprehendable; yet that which is the non-appropriation of the emptiness of the unapprehendable is not itself the emptiness of the unapprehendable, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the emptiness of non-existence; yet that which is the non-appropriation of the emptiness of non-existence is not itself the emptiness of non-existence, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is embraced by the emptiness of self-nature.

That which is the non-appropriation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not that emptiness of intrinsic nature, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; it is embraced by the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. And that which is the non-appropriation of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not that emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The applications of mindfulness are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the applications of mindfulness is not those applications of mindfulness, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The right efforts are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the right efforts is not those right efforts, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The bases of psychic power are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the bases of psychic power is not those bases of psychic power, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The faculties are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the faculties does not, by virtue of their being empty of intrinsic nature, constitute those very faculties. The powers are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the powers does not, by virtue of their being empty of intrinsic nature, constitute those very powers. The factors of enlightenment are ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the factors of enlightenment does not, by virtue of their being empty of intrinsic nature, constitute those very factors of enlightenment.

The Noble Eightfold Path is ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of the Noble Eightfold Path is not the Noble Eightfold Path, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*). The Noble Truths are ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of the Noble Truths is not those Noble Truths, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. The meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) are ungrasped; that which is the non-grasping of the meditative absorptions is not those meditative absorptions, by reason of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. The immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) are ungrasped.

And that which is the non-appropriation of the immeasurables is not those immeasurables, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature; the formless attainments are unappropriated. And that which is the non-appropriation of the formless attainments is not those formless attainments, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature; the eight liberations are unappropriated.

And that which is the non-appropriation of the liberations is not those liberations, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The nine successive meditative attainments are unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the nine successive meditative attainments is not those nine successive meditative attainments, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unappropriated.

And that which is the non-appropriation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is not those gateways to liberation, because they are empty by nature. The superknowledges are unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the superknowledges is not those superknowledges, because they are empty by nature. The meditative concentrations are unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the meditative concentrations is not those meditative concentrations, because they are empty by nature. The gateways of the dhāraṇīs are unappropriated.

And that which is the non-appropriation of the gateways of dhāraṇī is not those gateways of dhāraṇī, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The ten powers of a Tathāgata are unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the powers of a Tathāgata is not those powers of a Tathāgata, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The grounds of self-confidence are unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the grounds of self-confidence is not those grounds of self-confidence, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. The four analytical knowledges are unappropriated.

And that which is the non-appropriation of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) is not those analytical knowledges, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature. Great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of great compassion is not that great compassion, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the unique qualities of a Buddha is not those unique qualities of a Buddha, by reason of their emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The fruit of stream-entry is ungrasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the fruit of stream-entry is not the fruit of stream-entry.

Based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmi-phala*) is not grasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the fruit of once-returning is, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, not that fruit of once-returning. The fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmi-phala*) is not grasped; and that which is the non-grasping of the fruit of non-returning is, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, not that fruit of non-returning. Arhatship (*arhattva*) is not grasped; and that which is the non-grasping of arhatship is, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, not that arhatship.

Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is not grasped; and that which is the non-grasping of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is not that pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is grasped by the knowledge of the aspects of the path; and that which is the non-grasping of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not that knowledge of the aspects of the path, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is grasped by the knowledge of all aspects; and that which is the non-grasping of the knowledge of all aspects is not that knowledge of all aspects, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. It is grasped by suchness.

That which is the non-appropriation of suchness is not that suchness, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature; it is not appropriated by non-falsity. The stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*) is unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the stability of phenomena is not that stability of phenomena, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. And that which is the non-appropriation of the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmmaniyāmatā*) is not that fixed order of phenomena, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛtiśūnyatā*). The limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is unappropriated; wherein there is no appropriation of the limit of reality, that is not the limit of reality, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature. That perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is also unappropriated; and that which is the non-appropriation of the perfection of wisdom is not that perfection of wisdom, by reason of its emptiness of intrinsic nature.

In this way, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should thoroughly investigate all phenomena as being empty by nature; they should be investigated in such a manner that there is no mental activity regarding any phenomenon whatsoever.

This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s samādhi-maṇḍala named "Non-appropriation of All Dharmas," which is vast, preeminent, immeasurable, fixed, unassailable, and uncommon to all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Abiding in this samādhi-maṇḍala, the bodhisattva mahāsattva will emerge into omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That omniscience, too, is non-appropriated, based upon internal emptiness and external emptiness.

Based on internal-external emptiness; based on the emptiness of emptiness; based on great emptiness; based on ultimate emptiness; based on conditioned emptiness; based on unconditioned emptiness; based on absolute emptiness; based on the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; based on the emptiness of non-dispersal; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based on the emptiness of all phenomena; and based on the emptiness of specific characteristics.

By relying on the emptiness of non-apprehension; by relying on the emptiness of non-existence; by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by relying on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

For what reason? Because it cannot be described in terms of signs (*nimitta*). This is because a sign arises from affliction (*kleśa*). What is a sign? In this regard, concerning the knowledge of the omniscient one (*sarvajñajñāna*), what is faith? Thus, it should be embraced through signlessness within signlessness. Furthermore, the wandering mendicant Śreṇika, having gained resolute belief in this knowledge of the omniscient one, is a follower by faith who has entered [the path] by means of partial knowledge.

Having descended, he did not grasp at form; he did not grasp at feeling; he did not grasp at perception; he did not grasp at mental formations; he did not grasp at consciousness. He did not perceive that knowledge through the realization of attainment externally; he did not perceive that knowledge through the realization of attainment both internally and externally; nor did he perceive that knowledge through the realization of attainment elsewhere. He did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry internally; he did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry externally; he did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry both internally and externally; nor did he perceive that knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry as something other than that. He did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of once-returning internally.

He did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of once-returning externally; he did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of once-returning both internally and externally; nor did he perceive that knowledge of the fruit of once-returning anywhere else. He did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of non-returning internally; he did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of non-returning externally.

He did not perceive that knowledge of the fruit of non-returning as being either internal or external; nor did he perceive that knowledge of the fruit of non-returning as being anywhere else. He did not perceive that knowledge of arhatship as being internal; he did not perceive that knowledge of arhatship as being external; he did not perceive that knowledge of arhatship as being both internal and external; nor did he perceive that knowledge of arhatship as being anywhere else.

He did not perceive that knowledge regarding individual enlightenment within; he did not perceive that knowledge regarding individual enlightenment without; he did not perceive that knowledge regarding individual enlightenment both within and without; nor did he perceive it anywhere else apart from individual enlightenment.

He perceived that knowledge. He did not perceive that knowledge of the knowledge of the aspects of the path internally; he did not perceive that knowledge of the knowledge of the aspects of the path externally; he did not perceive that knowledge of the knowledge of the aspects of the path both internally and externally; nor did he perceive that knowledge anywhere other than the knowledge of the aspects of the path.

He did not perceive that knowledge of all-aspect within all-aspect-knowledge; he did not perceive that knowledge of all-aspect outside all-aspect-knowledge; he did not perceive that knowledge of all-aspect both within and outside all-aspect-knowledge; nor did he perceive that knowledge of all-aspect elsewhere than all-aspect-knowledge, by virtue of the emptiness of the internal and external.

He did not perceive that knowledge as being within suchness; he did not perceive that knowledge as being outside suchness; he did not perceive that knowledge as being both within and outside suchness; nor did he perceive that knowledge as being elsewhere than suchness. He did not perceive that knowledge as being within non-falsity; he did not perceive that knowledge as being outside falsity.

He did not perceive that knowledge as being within or without the non-falsity; nor did he perceive that knowledge as being elsewhere than the non-falsity. He did not perceive that knowledge as being internally other than the suchness; he did not perceive that knowledge as being externally other than the suchness; he did not perceive that knowledge as being both internally and externally other than the suchness.

Nor did he perceive that knowledge as being other than suchness (*tathatā*), nor as non-other than it. He did not perceive that knowledge within the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), nor did he perceive that knowledge outside the nature of phenomena, nor did he perceive that knowledge both within and outside the nature of phenomena, nor did he perceive that knowledge as being other than the nature of phenomena. He did not perceive that knowledge within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), nor did he perceive it outside the realm of phenomena.

He did not perceive that knowledge; he did not perceive that knowledge within the internal realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), nor did he perceive that knowledge elsewhere than in the realm of phenomena. He did not perceive that knowledge within the stability of phenomena internally, nor did he perceive that knowledge outside the stability of phenomena, nor did he perceive that knowledge both inside and outside the stability of phenomena.

Nor did he perceive that knowledge as being elsewhere than in the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*). He did not perceive that knowledge within the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmmaniyāmatā*) internally; he did not perceive that knowledge externally in the fixed order of phenomena; he did not perceive that knowledge both internally and externally in the fixed order of phenomena. He did not perceive that knowledge within the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) internally.

He did not perceive that knowledge as being outside the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); he did not perceive that knowledge as being both inside and outside the limit of reality; nor did he perceive that knowledge as being elsewhere than the limit of reality, by virtue of internal and external emptiness.

In this sequence, the wandering mendicant Śreṇika was inclined toward faith; having become thus inclined, he followed by way of faith and entered into the knowledge of the omniscient one, taking the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā) as his authority on the basis of the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena. Being thus inclined, he did not grasp any phenomenon whatsoever, on the basis of mental attention directed toward the signless.

Nor has he apprehended any dharma whatsoever that he might grasp or resolve upon, by virtue of the non-grasping and non-rejection of all dharmas. He does not even conceive of nirvāṇa, by virtue of the non-inclination toward all dharmas. This also, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by virtue of going from the hither shore to the further shore: in that he does not grasp form, does not grasp feeling, does not grasp perception, [and does not grasp] mental formations...

He does not grasp at consciousness, because all phenomena are non-grasped. He does not grasp at the eye; he does not grasp at the ear; he does not grasp at the nose; he does not grasp at the tongue; he does not grasp at the body; he does not grasp at the mind, because all phenomena are non-grasped. He does not grasp at form; he does not grasp at sound; he does not grasp at odor.

He does not grasp at taste; he does not grasp at touch; he does not grasp at all phenomena (*dharmas*); he does not grasp at phenomena, because all phenomena are non-grasped. He does not grasp at eye-consciousness; he does not grasp at ear-consciousness; he does not grasp at nose-consciousness; he does not grasp at tongue-consciousness; he does not grasp at body-consciousness; he does not grasp at mind-consciousness.

Because all phenomena are not grasped, one does not grasp visual contact; one does not grasp auditory contact; one does not grasp olfactory contact; one does not grasp gustatory contact; one does not grasp tactile contact; one does not grasp mental contact. Because all phenomena are not grasped, one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by visual contact.

He does not grasp at feeling conditioned by auditory contact; he does not grasp at feeling conditioned by olfactory contact; he does not grasp at feeling conditioned by gustatory contact; he does not grasp at feeling conditioned by tactile contact; he does not grasp at feeling conditioned by mental contact, because of the non-grasping of all phenomena.
He does not grasp at the earth element; he does not grasp at the water element.

He does not grasp the fire element; he does not grasp the wind element; he does not grasp the space element; he does not grasp the consciousness element, because all phenomena are non-grasped. He does not grasp ignorance; he does not grasp formative forces; he does not grasp consciousness; he does not grasp name-and-form; he does not grasp the six sense bases; he does not grasp contact; he does not grasp feeling.

He does not grasp at craving; he does not grasp at clinging; he does not grasp at existence; he does not grasp at birth; he does not grasp at old age and death, because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. He does not grasp at the perfection of generosity; he does not grasp at the perfection of ethical discipline; he does not grasp at the perfection of patience; he does not grasp at the perfection of vigor; he does not grasp at the perfection of meditation.

One does not grasp at the perfection of wisdom, because all phenomena are non-grasped. One does not grasp at internal emptiness; one does not grasp at external emptiness; one does not grasp at internal-and-external emptiness; one does not grasp at the emptiness of emptiness; one does not grasp at great emptiness; one does not grasp at the emptiness of the ultimate; one does not grasp at the emptiness of the conditioned; one does not grasp at the emptiness of the unconditioned.

He does not grasp at absolute emptiness; he does not grasp at the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; he does not grasp at the emptiness of non-dispersal; he does not grasp at the emptiness of intrinsic nature; he does not grasp at the emptiness of all phenomena; he does not grasp at the emptiness of specific characteristics;

he does not grasp at the emptiness of non-apprehension; he does not grasp at the emptiness of non-existence; he does not grasp at the emptiness of self-nature; and he does not grasp at the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence. This is because all phenomena are beyond grasping.

He does not grasp at the foundations of mindfulness, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the right efforts, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the bases of psychic power, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the faculties, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the powers, because all phenomena are ungraspable.

He does not grasp at the factors of enlightenment, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the noble eightfold path, because all phenomena are ungraspable. The noble truths are not grasped, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the meditative absorptions, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the immeasurables, because all phenomena are ungraspable.

He does not grasp at the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), because of the non-grasping of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-aparigṛhītatā*). He does not grasp at the eight liberations (*aṣṭa-vimokṣa*), because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. He does not grasp at the nine successive meditative attainments (*navānupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*), because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. The gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (*śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*) are not grasped, because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. He does not grasp at the superknowledges (*abhijñā*).

Based on the fact that all phenomena are not grasped, one does not grasp at meditative absorptions (*samādhi*). Based on the fact that all phenomena are not grasped, one does not grasp at the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*). [One likewise does not grasp at] the ten powers of a Tathāgata, based on the fact that all phenomena are not grasped.

He does not grasp at them, because all dharmas are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*), because all dharmas are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the three types of analytical knowledge (*pratisaṃvid*), because all dharmas are ungraspable. He does not grasp at great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), because all dharmas are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), because all dharmas are ungraspable.

He does not grasp at the fruit of stream-entry, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the fruit of once-returning, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the fruit of non-returning, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at arhatship, because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at solitary enlightenment, because all phenomena are ungraspable.

One does not grasp at the knowledge of the aspects of the path, because all phenomena are ungraspable. One does not grasp at the knowledge of all aspects, because all phenomena are ungraspable. One does not grasp at suchness, because all phenomena are ungraspable. One does not grasp at non-falsity, because all phenomena are ungraspable. One does not grasp at non-otherness, because all phenomena are ungraspable.

He does not grasp at the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the fixed order of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*), because all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp at the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), because all phenomena are ungraspable.

He attains final nirvāṇa midway through his life, with his vows unfulfilled, and with the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path unfulfilled.

With the four noble truths unfulfilled, with the four meditative absorptions (dhyānas) unfulfilled, with the four immeasurables (apramāṇas) unfulfilled, with the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpattis) unfulfilled, with the eight liberations (vimokṣas) unfulfilled, with the nine successive meditative attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpattis) unfulfilled, with the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness unfulfilled, with the superknowledges (abhijñās) unfulfilled, and with the meditative concentrations (samādhis) unfulfilled.

With the gateways of dhāraṇī being incomplete, with the ten powers of a Tathāgata being incomplete, with the four grounds of self-confidence being incomplete, with the four analytical knowledges being incomplete, with great compassion being incomplete, and with the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha being incomplete.

For what reason? Because those vows are non-vows; those foundations of mindfulness are non-foundations of mindfulness; the right efforts are non-right efforts; the bases of psychic power are non-bases of psychic power; the faculties are non-faculties; the powers are non-powers; the factors of enlightenment are non-factors of enlightenment; the noble eightfold path is the non-noble eightfold path; the noble truths are non-noble truths; the meditations are non-meditations; and the immeasurables are non-immeasurables.

The formless attainments are non-formless attainments; the eight liberations are non-liberations; the nine successive dwellings in attainment are non-successive dwellings in attainment; the gateways to liberation through emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are the gateways to liberation through non-emptiness, non-signlessness, and non-wishlessness; the superknowledges are non-superknowledges; the concentrations are non-concentrations; the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are non-gateways to the dhāraṇīs; and the powers of a Tathāgata are non-powers of a Tathāgata.

The grounds of self-confidence and the lack of self-confidence; the analytical knowledges and the lack of analytical knowledges; great compassion and the absence of great compassion; the unique qualities of a Buddha and the non-unique qualities of a Buddha.

This, O Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva: that it does not grasp at form; it does not grasp at feeling; it does not grasp at perception; it does not grasp at mental formations; it does not grasp at consciousness—on account of the non-grasping of all phenomena. It does not grasp at the eye; it does not grasp at the ear; it does not grasp at the nose; it does not grasp at the tongue; it does not grasp at the body.

He does not grasp the mind, based on the fact that all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp form; he does not grasp sound; he does not grasp odor; he does not grasp taste; he does not grasp tangibles; he does not grasp mental objects, based on the fact that all phenomena are ungraspable. He does not grasp eye-consciousness; he does not grasp ear-consciousness; he does not grasp nose-consciousness.

He does not grasp at tongue-consciousness; he does not grasp at body-consciousness; he does not grasp at mind-consciousness, because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. He does not grasp at eye-contact; he does not grasp at ear-contact; he does not grasp at nose-contact; he does not grasp at tongue-contact; he does not grasp at body-contact; he does not grasp at mind-contact.

Based on the fact that all phenomena are ungraspable, one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by eye-contact; one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by ear-contact; one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by nose-contact; one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by body-contact; and one does not grasp the feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

Based on the fact that all phenomena are not grasped, one does not grasp the earth element; one does not grasp the water element; one does not grasp the fire element; one does not grasp the wind element; one does not grasp the space element.

He does not grasp the element of consciousness, because all phenomena are non-grasping. He does not grasp ignorance; he does not grasp formative forces; he does not grasp consciousness; he does not grasp name-and-form; he does not grasp the six sense bases; he does not grasp contact; he does not grasp craving; he does not grasp clinging; he does not grasp existence; he does not grasp birth; he does not grasp aging and death, because all phenomena are non-grasping.

He does not grasp at the perfection of generosity; he does not grasp at the perfection of ethical discipline; he does not grasp at the perfection of vigor; he does not grasp at the perfection of meditative concentration; he does not grasp at the perfection of wisdom—this being based on the non-grasping of all phenomena.

He does not grasp at internal emptiness; he does not grasp at external emptiness; he does not grasp at internal-external emptiness; he does not grasp at the emptiness of emptiness; he does not grasp at great emptiness; he does not grasp at ultimate emptiness; he does not grasp at conditioned emptiness; he does not grasp at unconditioned emptiness; he does not grasp at absolute emptiness; he does not grasp at the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.

He does not grasp at the emptiness of non-dispersal; he does not grasp at the emptiness of intrinsic nature; he does not grasp at the emptiness of all phenomena; he does not grasp at the emptiness of specific characteristics; he does not grasp at the emptiness of non-apprehension; he does not grasp at the emptiness of non-existence; he does not grasp at the emptiness of self-nature. Because all phenomena are ungraspable, he grasps at the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence. On account of this ungraspability of all phenomena, he does not grasp at the foundations of mindfulness; he does not grasp at the right efforts.

He does not grasp at the bases of psychic power; he does not grasp at the faculties; he does not grasp at the powers; he does not grasp at the factors of enlightenment; he does not grasp at the noble eightfold path; he does not grasp at the meditative absorptions; he does not grasp at the immeasurables; he does not grasp at the formless attainments; he does not grasp at the eight liberations; he does not grasp at the nine successive meditative attainments.

One does not grasp at the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; one does not grasp at the superknowledges; one does not grasp at the meditative concentrations; one does not grasp at the gateways to the dhāraṇīs, because of the non-grasping of all phenomena.

One does not grasp at the ten powers of a Tathāgata; one does not grasp at the four grounds of self-confidence; one does not grasp at the four analytical knowledges; one does not grasp at great compassion; one does not grasp at the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—this is because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. One does not grasp at the fruit of stream-entry; one does not grasp at the fruit of once-returning; one does not grasp at the fruit of non-returning.

One does not grasp at arhatship; one does not grasp at pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; one does not grasp at the knowledge of the aspects of the path; one does not grasp at the knowledge of all aspects. This is because of the non-grasping of all phenomena. One does not grasp at suchness; one does not grasp at non-falsity; one does not grasp at non-otherness; one does not grasp at the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*). Yet, one grasps at the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) and does not grasp at the fixed course of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*).
He does not grasp at the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), because all phenomena are non-grasped.
Furthermore, Blessed One, by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom...

One should practice in this way and investigate thus: "What is this perfection of wisdom? To whom does this perfection of wisdom belong? What is this perfection of wisdom? By what means is this perfection of wisdom [known]? If, however, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the perfection of wisdom, reflects in this manner: "Is that which is neither existent nor apprehended the perfection of wisdom?"—then he practices in the perfection of wisdom.

Then, indeed, the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the venerable Subhūti: "Venerable Subhūti, which phenomena do not exist and are not apprehended? Subhūti replied: "Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of meditation does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of vigor does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of patience does not exist and is not apprehended."

The perfection of ethical discipline does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of generosity does not exist and is not apprehended. This is by virtue of internal emptiness, by virtue of external emptiness, by virtue of internal and external emptiness, by virtue of the emptiness of emptiness, by virtue of great emptiness, by virtue of the emptiness of the ultimate, by virtue of the emptiness of the conditioned, by virtue of the emptiness of the unconditioned, and by virtue of absolute emptiness.

Based on the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; based on the emptiness of non-dispersal; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based on the emptiness of all phenomena; based on the emptiness of specific characteristics; based on the emptiness of non-apprehension; based on the emptiness of non-existence; based on the emptiness of self-nature; and based on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence—O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form does not exist and is not apprehended.

Perception does not exist and is not apprehended; mental formations do not exist and are not apprehended; consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended—this is by way of internal emptiness, by way of the emptiness of emptiness, and by way of the emptiness of the ultimate.

Based on the emptiness of the conditioned; based on the emptiness of the unconditioned; based on absolute emptiness; based on the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; based on the emptiness of non-dispersal; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based on the emptiness of the non-apprehendable; based on the emptiness of non-existence; based on the emptiness of self-nature; and based on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the eye does not exist and is not apprehended; the ear does not exist and is not apprehended; the nose does not exist and is not apprehended; the tongue does not exist and is not apprehended; the body does not exist and is not apprehended; the mind does not exist and is not apprehended. This is by virtue of internal emptiness, by virtue of external emptiness, and by virtue of internal-external emptiness.

By means of the emptiness of emptiness; by means of great emptiness; by means of the emptiness of the ultimate truth; by means of the emptiness of the conditioned; by means of the emptiness of the unconditioned; by means of absolute emptiness; by means of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; by means of the emptiness of non-dispersal; by means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by means of the emptiness of all phenomena; by means of the emptiness of specific characteristics; and by means of the emptiness of non-apprehension.
Based on the emptiness of non-existence; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, form does not exist and is not apprehended; sound does not exist and is not apprehended; odor does not exist and is not apprehended; taste does not exist and is not apprehended; tangibility does not exist and is not apprehended; mental phenomena do not exist and are not apprehended. This is by way of internal emptiness, by way of external emptiness, and by way of internal-external emptiness.
By way of the emptiness of emptiness; by way of great emptiness; by way of the emptiness of the ultimate truth; and by way of the emptiness of the conditioned.

Based on dependent origination; based on the emptiness of the unconditioned; based on absolute emptiness; based on the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; based on the emptiness of non-dispersal; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based on the emptiness of all phenomena; based on the emptiness of specific characteristics; based on the emptiness of non-apprehension; based on the emptiness of non-existence; based on the emptiness of self-nature; based on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, eye-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; ear-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; nose-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; tongue-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; body-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; mind-consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended. This is by virtue of internal emptiness and by virtue of external emptiness.

By way of internal-external emptiness; by way of the emptiness of emptiness; by way of great emptiness; by way of the emptiness of the ultimate; by way of the emptiness of the conditioned; by way of the emptiness of the unconditioned; by way of absolute emptiness; by way of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; by way of the emptiness of non-dispersal; by way of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by way of the emptiness of all phenomena; and by way of the emptiness of specific characteristics.

By relying on the emptiness of non-apprehension; by relying on the emptiness of non-existence; by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and by relying on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, visual contact does not exist and is not apprehended; auditory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; olfactory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; gustatory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; tactile contact does not exist and is not apprehended; mental contact does not exist and is not apprehended. This is by way of internal emptiness, by way of external emptiness, and by way of internal-external emptiness.

Based upon [the emptiness of] emptiness; based upon the emptiness of the great; based upon the emptiness of the ultimate truth; based upon the emptiness of the conditioned; based upon the emptiness of the unconditioned; based upon absolute emptiness; based upon the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; based upon the emptiness of non-dispersal; based upon the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based upon the emptiness of all phenomena; based upon the emptiness of specific characteristics; based upon the emptiness of non-apprehension.

Based on the emptiness of non-existence, based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and based on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, feeling conditioned by visual contact does not exist and is not apprehended; feeling conditioned by auditory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; feeling conditioned by olfactory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; feeling conditioned by gustatory contact does not exist and is not apprehended; feeling conditioned by tactile contact does not exist and is not apprehended.

Feeling conditioned by mental contact does not exist and is not apprehended, by virtue of internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate truth, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, and the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.

By relying on the emptiness of non-dispersal; by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by relying on the emptiness of all phenomena; by relying on the emptiness of specific characteristics; by relying on the emptiness of non-apprehension; by relying on the emptiness of non-existence; by relying on the emptiness of self-nature; and by relying on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence—O Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the earth element does not exist and is not apprehended; the water element does not exist and is not apprehended; the fire element does not exist and is not apprehended.

The wind element does not exist and is not apprehended; the space element does not exist and is not apprehended; the consciousness element does not exist and is not apprehended. This is by virtue of internal emptiness, by virtue of external emptiness, by virtue of internal and external emptiness, by virtue of the emptiness of emptiness, by virtue of great emptiness, by virtue of ultimate emptiness, by virtue of conditioned emptiness, and by virtue of unconditioned emptiness.

Based on absolute emptiness; based on the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; based on the emptiness of non-dispersal; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; based on the emptiness of all phenomena; based on the emptiness of specific characteristics; based on the emptiness of non-apprehensibility; based on the emptiness of non-existence; based on the emptiness of self-nature; and based on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

Ignorance, venerable Śāradvatīputra, does not exist and is not apprehended; volitional formations do not exist and are not apprehended; consciousness does not exist and is not apprehended; the six sense bases do not exist and are not apprehended; contact does not exist and is not apprehended; feeling does not exist and is not apprehended; craving does not exist and is not apprehended; grasping does not exist and is not apprehended.

Existence does not exist and is not apprehended; birth does not exist and is not apprehended; old age and death do not exist and are not apprehended. This is by virtue of internal emptiness, by virtue of external emptiness, by virtue of internal and external emptiness, by virtue of the emptiness of emptiness, by virtue of great emptiness, by virtue of the emptiness of the ultimate truth, by virtue of the emptiness of the conditioned, and by virtue of the emptiness of the unconditioned.

By relying on absolute emptiness; by relying on the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; by relying on the emptiness of non-dispersal; by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by relying on the emptiness of all phenomena; by relying on the emptiness of specific characteristics;

by relying on the emptiness of non-apprehension; by relying on the emptiness of non-existence; by relying on the emptiness of self-nature; and by relying on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of generosity does not exist and is not apprehended; Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of ethical discipline does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of patience does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of vigor does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of meditative concentration does not exist and is not apprehended; the perfection of wisdom does not exist and is not apprehended—this is based on internal emptiness.

By way of external emptiness; by way of internal-external emptiness; by way of the emptiness of emptiness; by way of great emptiness; by way of ultimate emptiness; by way of conditioned emptiness; by way of unconditioned emptiness; by way of absolute emptiness; by way of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; by way of the emptiness of non-dispersal; by way of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and by way of the emptiness of all phenomena.

Based on the emptiness of specific characteristics; based on the emptiness of non-apprehension; based on the emptiness of non-existence; based on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and based on the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the foundations of mindfulness do not exist and are not apprehended; the right efforts do not exist and are not apprehended; the bases of psychic power do not exist and are not apprehended; the faculties do not exist and are not apprehended; the powers do not exist and are not apprehended; the factors of enlightenment do not exist and are not apprehended; the noble eightfold path does not exist and is not apprehended.

In this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom becomes habituated to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). To the extent that he becomes habituated to the knowledge of all aspects, to that same extent he attains purity of body, purity of speech, purity of mind, and purity of the marks [of a great man]. To the extent that he attains purity of body, purity of speech, and purity of mind...

In such a manner, that bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to a mind accompanied by passion; he does not give rise to a mind accompanied by hatred, delusion, pride, deceit and guile, envy and stinginess, greed, or wrong views. Having given rise to a mind free from passion, and giving rise to a mind unaccompanied by hatred, delusion, deceit, guile, envy, stinginess, or greed, he is never again born within a mother’s womb.

He is constantly and perpetually born through spontaneous apparition (*upapāduka*), and he is never reborn in the miserable realms (*apāya*). Except for the sake of maturing sentient beings, he travels from one Buddha-field to another Buddha-field. While maturing sentient beings, he is never separated from the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, until he has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

Therefore, then, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to obtain these benefits and advantages should practice this perfection of wisdom without laying down the burden. For in this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom becomes self-luminous regarding the knowledge of all aspects.

If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom without skill in means practices thinking that the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is permanent or impermanent, he practices in signs. If, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom without skill in means...
If he practices the applications of mindfulness as being secluded or as being unsecluded, he courses in a sign.

Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, courses in the right efforts as being permanent or as being impermanent, he courses in a sign. Blessed One, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom without skillful means, courses in the right efforts as being pleasant or as being painful, he courses in a sign.
