Then, through the power of the Buddha, the Venerable Subhūti spoke again as follows: "Venerable Śāradvatīputra, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas have been predicted for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by those former Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones. Furthermore, there are currently Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who abide, remain, and maintain themselves in world-systems throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges."

Those Tathāgatas, the perfectly awakened ones, also grant a prophecy to that bodhisattva who dwells in these samādhis; yet he does not perceive even the samādhi, nor does he conceive pride because of that samādhi, thinking: "I am concentrated," "I shall enter into concentration," "I am entering," or "I have entered. In all respects, no such conceptual constructions exist or arise for that bodhisattva mahāsattva.

He asked: "Furthermore, Venerable Subhūti, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, established in these samādhis, receive a prophecy from the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas? Subhūti replied: "Certainly not, Venerable Śāradvatīputra. Why is that? Because, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, the perfection of wisdom is not one thing, the samādhi another, and the bodhisattva another."

The perfection of wisdom itself is the samādhi; the samādhi itself is the bodhisattva; the bodhisattva himself is the samādhi. He said: "Venerable Subhūti, the samādhi is not one thing and the bodhisattva another, nor is the bodhisattva one thing and the samādhi another. The samādhi is the bodhisattva, and the bodhisattva is the samādhi, by virtue of the equality of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-samatā*). Therefore, is it possible to demonstrate this samādhi? Subhūti replied: "Certainly not, venerable Śāradvatīputra."

He asked: "But, venerable Subhūti, does that son of good family perceive that samādhi? Subhūti replied: "He does not perceive it, venerable Śāradvatīputra. He asked: "In what way does he not perceive it? Subhūti replied: "Insofar as he does not conceptualize it. He asked: "Why, venerable Subhūti, does he not cognize and not perceive it? Subhūti replied: "Because that samādhi of that bodhisattva is non-existent; therefore, he does not cognize and does not perceive it."

Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the venerable Subhūti: "Excellent, excellent, Subhūti! Well-spoken are these words, for you have been designated by me as the foremost among my disciples who dwell in the state of non-contention."

This is the instruction for that which has been pointed out: thus should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom; he should train in the perfection of meditation; he should train in the perfection of vigor; he should train in the perfection of patience; he should train in the perfection of ethical discipline; he should train in the perfection of generosity; he should train in the applications of mindfulness; he should train in the right efforts; he should train in the bases of miraculous power.

One should train in the faculties; one should train in the powers; one should train in the factors of enlightenment; one should train in the noble eightfold path; one should train in the noble truths; one should train in the meditative absorptions; one should train in the immeasurables; one should train in the formless attainments; one should train in the liberations; one should train in the serial attainments; one should train in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and one should train in the superknowledges.

One should train in the meditative concentrations; one should train in the gateways of mnemonic formulas; one should train in the powers of a Tathāgata; one should train in the grounds of self-confidence; one should train in the analytical knowledges; one should train in great loving-kindness; one should train in great compassion; and one should train in the unique qualities of a Buddha.

Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in this way trains in the perfection of wisdom by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of meditative concentration by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of vigor by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of patience by means of non-apprehension."

He trains in the perfection of ethical discipline by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of generosity by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the applications of mindfulness by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the right efforts by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the bases of miraculous power by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the faculties by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the powers by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the factors of enlightenment by way of non-apprehension.

One trains in the noble eightfold path by means of non-apprehension; one trains in the noble truths by means of non-apprehension; one trains in the meditative concentrations by means of non-apprehension; one trains in the immeasurables by means of non-apprehension; one trains in the formless attainments by means of non-apprehension; one trains in the serial attainments by means of non-apprehension; and one trains in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—by means of non-apprehension.

He trains in the superknowledges by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the gateways of mnemonic formulas by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the powers of a Tathāgata by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the grounds of self-confidence by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the analytical knowledges by way of non-apprehension; he trains in great loving-kindness by way of non-apprehension; he trains in great compassion by way of non-apprehension; he trains in the unique qualities of a Buddha by way of non-apprehension.

The Blessed One said: "Śāradvatīputra, training in this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the perfection of wisdom by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of vigor by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of patience by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of ethical discipline by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the perfection of generosity by means of non-apprehension; and he trains in the applications of mindfulness by means of non-apprehension."

He trains in the right efforts by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the bases of psychic power by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the faculties by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the powers by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

He trains in the factors of enlightenment by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the noble eightfold path by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the noble truths by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the meditative concentrations by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the immeasurables by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the formless attainments by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; he trains in the liberations by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; and he trains in the successive meditative attainments by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

He trains in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the superknowledges by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the meditative concentrations by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the gateways of the dhāraṇīs by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the powers of a Tathāgata by means of non-apprehension; he trains in the grounds of self-confidence by means of non-apprehension; and he trains in the analytical knowledges by means of non-apprehension.

One trains in great loving-kindness by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; one trains in great compassion by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; one trains in the unique qualities of a Buddha by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra asked: "Why, Blessed One, is it not apprehended? The Blessed One replied: "Śāradvatīputra, one does not apprehend a self; one does not apprehend a living being; one does not apprehend a creature; one does not apprehend a nourisher; one does not apprehend a person; one does not apprehend an individual; one does not apprehend a human; one does not apprehend a youth; one does not apprehend an agent; one does not apprehend a knower; one does not apprehend a seer—by virtue of their absolute purity."

One does not apprehend form, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend feeling, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend perception, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend mental formations, by virtue of their absolute purity; one does not apprehend consciousness, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the eye, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the ear, by virtue of its absolute purity; [one does not apprehend] the nose...

One does not apprehend [it], based on its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the tongue, based on its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the body, based on its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the mind, based on its absolute purity; one does not apprehend form, based on its absolute purity; one does not apprehend sound, based on its absolute purity; one does not apprehend odor, based on its absolute purity.

One does not perceive taste, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not perceive contact, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not perceive mental phenomena, by reason of their absolute purity.

One does not apprehend the eye-element, the form-element, or the eye-consciousness-element, by reason of their absolute purity. One does not apprehend the ear-element, the sound-element, or the ear-consciousness-element, by reason of their absolute purity. One does not apprehend the nose-element, the odor-element, or the nose-consciousness-element. One does not apprehend the tongue-element, the taste-element, or the tongue-consciousness-element, by reason of their absolute purity.

One does not apprehend the body-element, the touch-element, or the body-consciousness-element, by virtue of their absolute purity; one does not apprehend the mind-element, the phenomena-element, or the mind-consciousness-element, by virtue of their absolute purity; one does not apprehend the earth-element, the water-element, the fire-element, the wind-element, the space-element, or the consciousness-element, by virtue of their absolute purity.

One does not apprehend ignorance, based on its ultimate purity; one does not apprehend formative forces, based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend consciousness, based on its ultimate purity; one does not apprehend name-and-form, based on its ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the six sense bases, based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend contact, based on its ultimate purity; one does not apprehend feeling, based on its ultimate purity.

One does not apprehend craving, on account of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend grasping, on account of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend becoming, on account of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend birth, on account of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend aging and death, on account of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend suffering, on account of its absolute purity.

One does not apprehend origination, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend cessation, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the path, by virtue of its absolute purity. One does not apprehend the element of form, by virtue of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the element of formlessness or the formless realm, by virtue of its absolute purity. One does not apprehend the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, or the perfection of wisdom, by virtue of their absolute purity.

One does not apprehend the applications of mindfulness, based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the right efforts, based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the bases of psychic power, based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the faculties, the powers, or the factors of enlightenment, based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the noble eightfold path, based on its ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the noble truths, based on their ultimate purity.

One does not apprehend the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) and the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the liberations (*vimokṣa*), based on their ultimate purity; one does not apprehend the serial attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), based on their ultimate purity; and one does not apprehend the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (*śūnyatānimittāpraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*), based on their ultimate purity.

One does not apprehend the superknowledges, based on their absolute purity; one does not apprehend the meditative concentrations, based on their absolute purity; one does not apprehend the gateways of mnemonic formulas, based on their absolute purity.

On account of ultimate purity, one does not apprehend the powers of a Tathāgata; on account of ultimate purity, one does not apprehend the grounds of self-confidence; on account of ultimate purity, one does not apprehend the analytical knowledges; on account of ultimate purity, one does not apprehend great loving-kindness; on account of ultimate purity, one does not apprehend great compassion; and on account of ultimate purity, one does not apprehend the unique qualities of a Buddha.

One does not apprehend the fruit of stream-entry, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the fruit of once-returning, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the fruit of non-returning, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend arhatship, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend the state of a pratyekabuddha, by reason of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend a bodhisattva, by reason of its absolute purity.
One does not apprehend awakening on account of its absolute purity; one does not apprehend a Buddha on account of his absolute purity.

He asked: "Lord, what is this purity? The Blessed One replied: "It is the non-arising, the non-cessation, the absence of affliction, the absence of purification, the non-manifestation, the non-apprehension, and the lack of volitional formation of all phenomena—this is called the purity of these. Thus, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in any phenomenon whatsoever.
For what reason? Śāradvatīputra, these phenomena do not exist in the way that foolish ordinary people are attached to them.

He asked: "Blessed One, how do these phenomena exist? The Blessed One said: "They exist in the very manner that they do not exist; because they exist in such a way, it is called 'ignorance' (avidyā)."

He asked: "But why, Blessed One, is it said that 'ignorance' (avidyā) does not exist? The Blessed One replied: "Form (rūpa) does not exist by way of internal emptiness (adhyātma-śūnyatā), by way of external emptiness (bahirdhā-śūnyatā), by way of internal-and-external emptiness (adhyātmabahirdhā-śūnyatā), and by way of the emptiness of emptiness (śūnyatā-śūnyatā)."

By relying on the emptiness of non-dispersal; by relying on the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by relying on the emptiness of all phenomena; by relying on the emptiness of specific characteristics; by relying on the emptiness of non-apprehension; by relying on the emptiness of non-existence; by relying on the emptiness of self-nature; and by relying on the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

In this regard, foolish ordinary people, through their attachment, are obsessed with craving; by them, ignorance is imagined. Being obsessed with ignorance, they are attached to both of the two extremes—namely, annihilationism and eternalism—and because of that, they do not know and do not see those phenomena which do not exist.

Having conceptualized those, they are attached to name-and-form; they are attached to the perfection of generosity; they are attached to the perfection of ethical discipline; they are attached to the perfection of patience; they are attached to the perfection of vigor; they are attached to the perfection of meditative concentration; and they are attached to the perfection of wisdom.

They are attached to internal emptiness; they are attached to external emptiness; they are attached to internal and external emptiness; they are attached to the emptiness of emptiness; they are attached to great emptiness; they are attached to ultimate emptiness; they are attached to conditioned emptiness; they are attached to unconditioned emptiness; they are attached to absolute emptiness; they are attached to the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.

They are attached to the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are attached to the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are attached to the emptiness of all phenomena; they are attached to the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are attached to the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are attached to the emptiness of non-existence; they are attached to the emptiness of self-nature; and they are attached to the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

They are attached to the foundations of mindfulness; they are attached to the right efforts; they are attached to the bases of psychic power; they are attached to the faculties; they are attached to the powers; they are attached to the factors of enlightenment; they are attached to the noble eightfold path; they are attached to the noble truths; they are attached to the meditative absorptions; they are attached to the immeasurables; they are attached to the formless attainments; they are attached to the liberations.

They are attached to the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling; they are attached to the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they are attached to the superknowledges; they are attached to the concentrations; they are attached to the gateways of the dhāraṇīs; they are attached to the powers of a Tathāgata; they are attached to the grounds of self-confidence; they are attached to the analytical knowledges; they are attached to great loving-kindness; they are attached to great compassion; and they are attached to the unique qualities of a Buddha.
Being thus attached, they conceptualize phenomena that do not exist; they neither know nor see. What is it that they neither know nor see?

They do not know and do not see form; they do not know and do not see feeling; they do not know and do not see perception; they do not know and do not see mental formations; they do not know and do not see consciousness. They do not know and do not see the eye; they do not know and do not see the ear; they do not know and do not see the nose; they do not know and do not see the tongue; they do not know and do not see the body; they do not know and do not see the mind.

They do not know and do not see form; they do not know and do not see sound; they do not know and do not see odor; they do not know and do not see taste; they do not know and do not see tangibles; they do not know and do not see mental phenomena.

They do not know and do not see eye-consciousness; they do not know and do not see ear-consciousness; they do not know and do not see nose-consciousness; they do not know and do not see tongue-consciousness; they do not know and do not see body-consciousness; they do not know and do not see mind-consciousness.

They do not know and do not see eye-contact; they do not know and do not see ear-contact; they do not know and do not see nose-contact; they do not know and do not see tongue-contact; they do not know and do not see body-contact; they do not know and do not see mind-contact.

They do not know and do not see feeling conditioned by eye-contact; they do not know and do not see feeling conditioned by ear-contact; they do not know and do not see feeling conditioned by nose-contact; they do not know and do not see feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; they do not know and do not see feeling conditioned by body-contact; they do not know and do not see feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

They do not know and do not see the perfection of generosity; they do not know and do not see the perfection of ethical discipline; they do not know and do not see the perfection of patience; they do not know and do not see the perfection of vigor; they do not know and do not see the perfection of meditative concentration; they do not know and do not see the perfection of wisdom.

They do not know and do not see internal emptiness; they do not know and do not see external emptiness; they do not know and do not see internal-external emptiness; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of emptiness; they do not know and do not see great emptiness; they do not know and do not see ultimate emptiness; they do not know and do not see conditioned emptiness; they do not know and do not see unconditioned emptiness.

They do not know and do not see extreme emptiness; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of non-dispersal; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of all phenomena; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of specific characteristics; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of non-apprehension; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of non-existence.
They do not know and do not see the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not know and do not see the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
they do not know and do not see the applications of mindfulness; they do not [know and do not see] the right efforts.

They do not know and do not see; they do not know and do not see the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*); they do not know and do not see the five faculties (*pañcendriya*); they do not know and do not see the five powers (*pañcabala*); they do not know and do not see the seven factors of awakening (*saptabodhyaṅga*); they do not know and do not see the noble eightfold path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*); they do not know and do not see the noble truths (*āryasatya*); they do not know and do not see the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*); they do not know and do not see the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*).

They do not know and do not see the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*). They do not know and do not see the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*). They do not know and do not see the nine successive meditative attainments (*anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*). They do not know and do not see the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (*śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*). They do not know and do not see the superknowledges (*abhijñā*). They do not know and do not see the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*). They do not know and do not see the gateways of the mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*). They do not know and do not see the powers of a Tathāgata (*tathāgatabala*).

They do not know and do not see the four grounds of self-confidence; they do not know and do not see the four analytical insights; they do not know and do not see great loving-kindness; they do not know and do not see great compassion; they do not know and do not see the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They are reckoned as fools; they do not go forth. From what do they not go forth? They do not go forth from the realm of desire; they do not go forth from the realm of form; they do not go forth from the formless realm; they do not go forth from the realm of the śrāvakas; they do not go forth from the stage of the pratyekabuddhas.

They do not have faith. Why do they not have faith? They do not have faith that form is empty of form; they do not have faith that feeling is empty of feeling; they do not have faith that perception is empty of perception; they do not have faith that mental formations are empty of mental formations; they do not have faith that consciousness is empty of consciousness.

They do not believe that "the eye is empty of the eye"; likewise, they do not believe that "the ear is empty. They do not believe that "the nose is empty of the nose"; they do not believe that "the tongue is empty of the tongue"; they do not believe that "the body is empty of the body"; they do not believe that "the mind is empty of the mind. They do not believe that "form is empty of form"; they do not believe that "sound is empty of sound."

They do not believe that odor is empty of odor; they do not believe that taste is empty of taste; they do not believe that tangibility is empty of tangibility; they do not believe that phenomena are empty of phenomena; they do not believe that eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness; they do not believe that ear-consciousness is empty of ear-consciousness.

They do not believe that olfactory consciousness is empty of olfactory consciousness; they do not believe that gustatory consciousness is empty of gustatory consciousness; they do not believe that tactile consciousness is empty of tactile consciousness; they do not believe that mental consciousness is empty of mental consciousness.

They do not have faith that eye-contact is empty of eye-contact; they do not have faith that ear-contact is empty of ear-contact; they do not have faith that nose-contact is empty of nose-contact; they do not have faith that tongue-contact is empty of tongue-contact; they do not have faith that body-contact is empty of body-contact;
they do not have faith that mind-contact is empty of mind-contact.

They do not believe that feeling conditioned by eye-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by eye-contact; they do not believe that feeling conditioned by ear-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by ear-contact; they do not believe that feeling conditioned by nose-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by nose-contact; [they do not believe that] feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.

They do not have faith that [it] is empty; they do not have faith that feeling conditioned by bodily contact is empty of feeling conditioned by bodily contact; they do not have faith that feeling conditioned by mental contact is empty of feeling conditioned by mental contact.

They do not believe that the perfection of generosity is empty of the perfection of generosity; they do not believe that the perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline; they do not believe that the perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience; they do not believe that the perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor; they do not believe that the perfection of meditation is empty of the perfection of meditation; they do not believe that the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom.

They do not believe that internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness; they do not believe that external emptiness is empty of external emptiness; they do not believe that internal-and-external emptiness is empty of internal-and-external emptiness; they do not believe that the emptiness of emptiness is empty of the emptiness of emptiness; they do not believe that great emptiness is empty of great emptiness.

They do not believe that the emptiness of the ultimate is empty of the emptiness of the ultimate; they do not believe that the emptiness of the conditioned is empty of the emptiness of the conditioned; they do not believe that the emptiness of the unconditioned is empty of the emptiness of the unconditioned; they do not believe that absolute emptiness is empty of absolute emptiness; they do not believe that the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is empty of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.

They do not believe that the emptiness of non-dispersal is empty of the emptiness of non-dispersal; they do not believe that the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not believe that the emptiness of all phenomena is empty of the emptiness of all phenomena; they do not believe that the emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of the emptiness of specific characteristics; they do not [believe] that the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

They have faith; they do not have faith that the emptiness of non-existence is empty of the emptiness of non-existence; they do not have faith that the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not have faith that the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They do not have faith that the four foundations of mindfulness are empty of the foundations of mindfulness; they do not have faith that the four right efforts are empty of the right efforts; they do not have faith that the bases of psychic power are empty of the bases of psychic power; they do not have faith that the faculties are empty of the faculties; they do not have faith that the powers are empty of the powers; they do not have faith that the factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment.

They do not believe that the noble eightfold path is empty of the noble eightfold path; they do not believe that the noble truths are empty of the noble truths; they do not believe that the meditative absorptions are empty of the meditative absorptions; they do not believe that the immeasurables are empty of the immeasurables; they do not believe that the formless attainments are empty of the formless attainments; and they do not believe that the eight liberations are empty of the eight liberations.

They do not believe that the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are empty of the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling; they do not believe that the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they do not believe that the superknowledges are empty of the superknowledges; they do not believe that the meditative concentrations are empty of the meditative concentrations; and they do not believe that the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are empty of the gateways to the dhāraṇīs.

They do not believe that the powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the powers of a Tathāgata; they do not believe that the grounds of self-confidence are empty of the grounds of self-confidence; they do not believe that the analytical knowledges are empty of the analytical knowledges; they do not believe that great loving-kindness is empty of great loving-kindness; they do not believe that great compassion is empty of great compassion; they do not believe that the unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha.

They do not believe that the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the fruit of stream-entry; they do not believe that the fruit of once-returning is empty of the fruit of once-returning; they do not believe that the fruit of non-returning is empty of the fruit of non-returning; they do not believe that arhatship is empty of arhatship; they do not believe that individual enlightenment is empty of individual enlightenment; they do not believe that the knowledge of the aspects of the path is empty of the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
They do not have faith that "all-aspect omniscience is empty of all-aspect omniscience";

thus they do not take their stand. Why do they not take their stand? They do not take their stand in the perfection of generosity; they do not take their stand in the perfection of ethical discipline; they do not take their stand in the perfection of patience; they do not take their stand in the perfection of vigor; they do not take their stand in the perfection of meditative concentration; they do not take their stand in the perfection of wisdom.

They do not abide in internal emptiness; they do not abide in external emptiness; they do not abide in internal and external emptiness; they do not abide in the emptiness of emptiness; they do not abide in great emptiness; they do not abide in the emptiness of the ultimate truth; they do not abide in the emptiness of the conditioned; they do not abide in the emptiness of the unconditioned.

They do not abide in absolute emptiness; they do not abide in the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end; they do not abide in the emptiness of non-dispersal; they do not abide in the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not abide in the emptiness of all phenomena; they do not abide in the emptiness of specific characteristics; they do not abide in the emptiness of non-apprehension.
They do not abide in the emptiness of non-existence; they do not abide in the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they do not abide in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

They do not abide in the stage of non-retrogression; they do not abide in the applications of mindfulness; they do not abide in the right efforts; they do not abide in the bases of miraculous power; they do not abide in the faculties; they do not abide in the powers; they do not abide in the factors of enlightenment; they do not abide in the noble eightfold path; they do not abide in the noble truths; they do not abide in the meditative absorptions.

They do not abide in the immeasurables; they do not abide in the formless attainments; they do not abide in the eight liberations; they do not abide in the nine successive meditative attainments; they do not abide in the superknowledges; they do not abide in the concentrations; they do not abide in the gateways of mnemonic formulas; they do not abide in the powers of a Tathāgata; they do not abide in the grounds of self-confidence.
They do not abide in the analytical knowledges; they do not abide in great loving-kindness; they do not abide in great compassion; they do not abide in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

They are attached. To what are they attached? They are attached to form (*rūpa*); they are attached to feeling (*vedanā*); they are attached to perception (*saṃjñā*); they are attached to mental formations (*saṃskāra*); they are attached to consciousness (*vijñāna*). They are attached to the eye; they are attached to the ear; they are attached to the nose; they are attached to the tongue; they are attached to the body; they are attached to the mind. They are attached to visible forms; they are attached to sounds.

They are attached to odors; they are attached to tastes; they are attached to tangibles; they are attached to mental phenomena. They are attached to the eye-element; they are attached to the ear-element; they are attached to the nose-element; they are attached to the tongue-element; they are attached to the body-element; they are attached to the mind-element.

They are attached to the eye-consciousness element; they are attached to the ear-consciousness element; they are attached to the nose-consciousness element; they are attached to the tongue-consciousness element; they are attached to the body-consciousness element; they are attached to the mind-consciousness element. They are attached to the elements of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); they are attached to consciousness; they are attached to passion; they are attached to hatred; they are attached to delusion; they are attached to the fabrication of views.

They are attached to ignorance; they are attached to volitional formations; they are attached to consciousness; they are attached to name-and-form; they are attached to the six sense bases; they are attached to contact; they are attached to feeling; they are attached to craving; they are attached to grasping; they are attached to existence; they are attached to birth; they are attached to old age and death.

They were attached to the perfection of generosity; they were attached to the perfection of ethical discipline; they were attached to the perfection of patience; they were attached to the perfection of vigor; they were attached to the perfection of meditative concentration; and they were attached to the perfection of wisdom.

They are attached to internal emptiness; they are attached to external emptiness; they are attached to internal and external emptiness; they are attached to the emptiness of emptiness; they are attached to great emptiness; they are attached to ultimate emptiness; they are attached to conditioned emptiness; they are attached to unconditioned emptiness; they are attached to absolute emptiness; they are attached to the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.

They are attached to the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are attached to the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are attached to the emptiness of all phenomena; they are attached to the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are attached to the emptiness of non-apprehension;
they are attached to the emptiness of non-existence; they are attached to the emptiness of self-nature; and they are attached to the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

They are attached to the foundations of mindfulness; they are attached to the right efforts; they are attached to the bases of psychic power; they are attached to the faculties; they are attached to the powers; they are attached to the factors of enlightenment; they are attached to the noble eightfold path; they are attached to the noble truths; they are attached to the meditative absorptions; they are attached to the immeasurables; they are attached to the formless attainments; and they are attached to the eight liberations.

They were attached to the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling; they were attached to the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they were attached to the superknowledges; they were attached to the meditative concentrations; they were attached to the powers of a Tathāgata; they were attached to the grounds of self-confidence; they were attached to the analytical knowledges; they were attached to great benevolence; they were attached to great compassion; and they were attached to the unique qualities of a Buddha.

They are attached to the fruit of stream-entry; they are attached to the fruit of once-returning; they are attached to the fruit of non-returning; they are attached to arhatship; they are attached to pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; they are attached to the knowledge of the aspects of the path; they are attached to unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment.

For that reason, they are called "fools. He said: "Blessed One, training in this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the perfection of wisdom and goes forth toward omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). The Blessed One said: "In this regard, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through a lack of skill in means (*anupāyakauśalya*), conceptualizes and becomes attached to the perfection of wisdom; he conceptualizes and becomes attached to the perfection of meditative concentration; he conceptualizes and becomes attached to the perfection of vigor; he conceptualizes and becomes attached to the perfection of patience."

He conceptualizes and adheres to the perfection of ethical discipline; he conceptualizes and adheres to the perfection of generosity; he conceptualizes and adheres to internal emptiness; he conceptualizes and adheres to external emptiness; he conceptualizes and adheres to internal and external emptiness; he conceptualizes and adheres to the emptiness of emptiness; he conceptualizes and adheres to great emptiness; he conceptualizes and adheres to the emptiness of the ultimate.

Having conceptualized conditioned emptiness, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized unconditioned emptiness, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized absolute emptiness, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized emptiness without beginning or end, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized non-dispersal emptiness, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized natural emptiness, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized the emptiness of all phenomena, one becomes attached to it; and having conceptualized the emptiness of specific characteristics, one becomes attached to it.

Having conceptualized the emptiness of non-apprehension, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized the emptiness of non-existence, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized the emptiness of intrinsic nature, one becomes attached to it; having conceptualized the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, one becomes attached to it.

Having conceptualized the foundations of mindfulness, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the right efforts, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the bases of psychic power, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the faculties, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the powers, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the factors of enlightenment, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the noble eightfold path, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the noble truths, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the meditative absorptions, one becomes attached to them.

Having conceptualized the immeasurables, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the formless attainments, one becomes attached to them; having conceptualized the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one becomes attached to them; [and likewise] the supernormal powers.

Having conceptualized, one becomes attached; having conceptualized the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*), one becomes attached; having conceptualized the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*), one becomes attached; having conceptualized the powers of a Tathāgata (*tathāgatabala*), one becomes attached; having conceptualized the grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*), one becomes attached; having conceptualized the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), one becomes attached; having conceptualized great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), one becomes attached; having conceptualized great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), one becomes attached; and having conceptualized the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*), one becomes attached.

Having conceptualized omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he becomes attached to it; having conceptualized the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), he becomes attached to it; having conceptualized the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he becomes attached to it. Śāradvatīputra, by this method, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) and does not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. He asked: "But how, Blessed One, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom, such that by training in it, he emerges into the perfection of wisdom? The Blessed One said:

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not perceive that perfection of wisdom and does not even observe it—indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-perception.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, does not apprehend nor perceive that perfection of meditative concentration—it is by training in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience through the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of vigor, does not apprehend nor perceive that perfection of vigor—thus indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom [trains] in omniscience.

He sets out by way of non-apprehension. Indeed, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of patience, neither apprehends nor perceives that perfection of patience—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by way of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of ethical discipline does not apprehend nor perceive that perfection of ethical discipline—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of generosity neither perceives nor observes that perfection of generosity, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-perception.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in internal emptiness, does not apprehend nor perceive that internal emptiness—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the emptiness of the external, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of the external—thus indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in internal-external emptiness, does not apprehend nor perceive that internal-external emptiness—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension. When, indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva...

Practicing in the emptiness of emptiness, he neither apprehends nor perceives that emptiness of emptiness; in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in great emptiness, does not apprehend that great emptiness and does not perceive it—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for all-knowledge by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of the ultimate meaning, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of the ultimate meaning—in this way, indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of the conditioned, neither perceives nor fully beholds that emptiness of the conditioned—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-perception.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the emptiness of the unconditioned, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of the unconditioned—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in absolute emptiness, does not apprehend nor perceive that absolute emptiness, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of that which is without beginning or end, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra...

A bodhisattva mahāsattva, training in the perfection of wisdom, goes forth toward omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension. Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of non-dispersal, neither apprehends nor perceives that emptiness of non-dispersal—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom goes forth toward omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither perceives nor fully beholds that emptiness of intrinsic nature—in this way, indeed, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-perception.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of all dharmas, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of all dharmas—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the emptiness of specific characteristics, neither apprehends nor perceives that emptiness of specific characteristics—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of non-apprehension, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of non-apprehension—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for all-knowledge by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of non-existence, does not apprehend nor perceive that emptiness of non-existence—it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, neither perceives nor fully beholds that emptiness of intrinsic nature—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-perception.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, neither perceives nor fully beholds that emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-perception.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the applications of mindfulness, does not apprehend nor perceive those applications of mindfulness—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the right efforts, does not apprehend nor perceive those right efforts—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the bases of miraculous power does not apprehend those bases of miraculous power and does not perceive them, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Then, Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the faculties, he does not apprehend those faculties, nor does he perceive them. In this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension. When, Śāradvatīputra—

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the powers, he does not apprehend those powers nor does he perceive them; in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom goes forth toward all-aspect omniscience by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the factors of enlightenment, does not apprehend nor perceive those factors of enlightenment—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the noble eightfold path, does not apprehend nor perceive that noble eightfold path—thus indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the noble truths, does not apprehend nor perceive those noble truths, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the meditative concentrations does not apprehend nor perceive those meditative concentrations, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the immeasurables, does not apprehend nor perceive those immeasurables, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing in the formless attainments, does not apprehend those formless attainments and does not perceive them, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva [practices] in the perfection of wisdom.

Training in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), he sets out by means of the yoga of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the liberations (*vimokṣa*), does not apprehend nor perceive those liberations, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) sets out for omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the successive attainments of meditative dwelling, does not apprehend nor perceive those successive attainments of meditative dwelling—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—does not apprehend nor perceive those gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the superknowledges, does not apprehend nor perceive those superknowledges—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the samādhis, does not apprehend nor perceive those samādhis—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), does not apprehend nor perceive those meditative concentrations, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) sets out for the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) by means of the yoga of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva...

The Mahāsattva, while practicing the immeasurables, does not apprehend nor perceive those immeasurables; in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward omniscience by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), does not apprehend nor perceive those analytical knowledges, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) by means of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing great loving-kindness, does not apprehend that great loving-kindness and does not perceive it—thus indeed, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom goes forth toward all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing great compassion does not apprehend nor perceive that great compassion, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom proceeds toward all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the unique qualities of a buddha, does not apprehend nor perceive those unique qualities of a buddha—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the knowledge of all aspects, does not apprehend nor perceive that knowledge of all aspects—in this way, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of non-apprehension.
When, Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the knowledge of the aspects of the path, does not apprehend nor perceive that knowledge of the aspects of the path...
Śāradvatīputra, it is in this way that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, training in the perfection of wisdom, sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

Śāradvatīputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, does not apprehend nor perceive that perfection of wisdom, it is in this way, Śāradvatīputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, training in the perfection of wisdom, sets out for the knowledge of all aspects by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.

He asked: "By means of the non-apprehension of what? The Blessed One replied: "By means of the non-apprehension of internal emptiness; by means of the non-apprehension of external emptiness; by means of the non-apprehension of internal-and-external emptiness; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of emptiness; by means of the non-apprehension of great emptiness; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the ultimate; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the conditioned."

By means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the unconditioned; by means of the non-apprehension of absolute emptiness; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-dispersal; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of all phenomena; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of specific characteristics; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

By means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-existence; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. This is the fifth chapter of the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*.

Now begins the sixth chapter. Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Does this illusory person, having trained in the perfection of wisdom, emerge into the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—Blessed One, how should one explain it to such a questioner? Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Does this illusory person, having trained in the perfection of meditative concentration, emerge into the knowledge of all aspects?'"

"O Blessed One, when one asks, 'Will he attain all-aspect omniscience (sarvākārajñatā)?'—how should it be explained to him? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask, 'Will this illusory person (māyāpuruṣa), having trained in the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā), emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?'—O Blessed One, when such a question is asked, how should it be explained?"

Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the perfection of patience, set out for all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, how should one explain it to that person who asks thus? Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the perfection of ethical discipline, set out for all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—[how should one explain it?]

O Blessed One, when he asks thus, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the perfection of generosity, set out for all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?"—O Blessed One, when he asks thus, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus...

"Blessed One, when this illusory person is asked: 'Having trained in internal emptiness, will he emerge into the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—to him who asks thus,"

How, Blessed One, should one explain it to someone who asks this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in external emptiness, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience? Blessed One, how should one explain it to such a person who asks this? Blessed One, how should one explain it to someone who asks this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in internal-external emptiness, emerge into all-aspect omniscience?"

"‘He will attain all-aspect omniscience’—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: ‘Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of emptiness, set forth toward all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?’—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained?"

Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the great emptiness, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, how should one answer that person who asks in such a way? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the ultimate emptiness, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—[how should one answer?]

O Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of the conditioned, set forth toward all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?"—O Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained?

"Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of the unconditioned, set out for the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—Blessed One, how should one explain it to that person who asks in this way? Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of the ultimate, set out for the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—Blessed One, to him who asks in this way..."

How, Blessed One, should one explain it to such a person? If someone were to ask, "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, how should one explain it to one who asks thus? If someone were to ask, "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of non-dispersal, emerge into all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, how should one explain it to one who asks thus?

"He will attain all-aspect omniscience. O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained?

Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of all phenomena, emerge into omniscience? Will he attain omniscience?"—Blessed One, how should one explain it to such a person who asks thus? Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics, emerge into omniscience? Will he attain omniscience?"—[how should one explain it?]

"Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of non-apprehension, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?'—Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained?"

Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of non-existence, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, how should one instruct such a person who asks thus? Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, [how should one instruct] him who asks thus?

To one who asks in this way, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, set forth toward omniscience and attain omniscience? [how would you respond?]

O Blessed One, when he asks thus, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the applications of mindfulness, set forth toward all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?"—O Blessed One, when he asks thus, how should it be explained?

"Blessed One, if someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the right efforts, set out for omniscience and attain omniscience?'—Blessed One, how should one explain it to such a person who asks thus? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the bases of psychic power, set out for omniscience and attain omniscience?'—"

Blessed One, when someone asks this, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the sense-faculties, emerge into all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—Blessed One, when someone asks this, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the factors of enlightenment, emerge into all-aspect omniscience?"—[how should it be explained?]

"He will attain all-aspect omniscience"—O Blessed One, how should this be explained to one who asks thus? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the Noble Eightfold Path, set out for all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?"—O Blessed One, how should this be explained to one who asks thus?
Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the noble truths, set out for the knowledge of all aspects and attain the knowledge of all aspects? to him—

O Blessed One, when one asks in this way, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), set forth toward all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*)? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience?"—O Blessed One, when one asks in this way, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), set forth toward all-aspect omniscience?"—[how should it be explained?]

"‘He will attain all-aspect omniscience’—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: ‘Will this illusory person, having trained in the formless attainments, set forth toward all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?’—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained?"

"Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the eight liberations, set out for the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—Blessed One, how should one answer such a questioner? Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the nine successive meditative attainments, set out for the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'"

Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, set out for the knowledge of all aspects and attain the knowledge of all aspects?"—Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained?

"Blessed One, if someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the superknowledges, set forth toward all-aspect omniscience? Will he attain all-aspect omniscience? Blessed One, how should one answer such a questioner? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the meditative concentrations, set forth toward all-aspect omniscience?'"

"‘He will attain all-aspect omniscience’—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained? O Blessed One, if someone were to ask: ‘Will this illusory person, having trained in the gateways of dhāraṇī, emerge into all-aspect omniscience and attain all-aspect omniscience?’—O Blessed One, when one asks this, how should it be explained?"

Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the powers of a Tathāgata, set out for omniscience? Will he attain omniscience? Blessed One, how should one explain it to such a person who asks thus? Blessed One, if someone were to ask this: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*), set out for omniscience? Will he attain omniscience?"

Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: "Will this illusory person, having trained in the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), emerge into the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?"—Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained?

"Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), set forth toward the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—Blessed One, how should one explain it to such a questioner? Blessed One, if someone were to ask thus: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), set forth toward the knowledge of all aspects? Will he attain the knowledge of all aspects?'—[how should one explain it?]"

"Blessed One, when he asks this, how should it be explained? Blessed One, if someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, set forth toward omniscience and attain omniscience?'—when this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable Subhūti: 'In that case, Subhūti, I shall question you on this very point. Answer as it seems right to you.'"

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is form one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is feeling one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. "What do you think, Subhūti? Is perception one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are volitional formations one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti, is consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is the eye one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is the ear one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is the nose one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One."

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the tongue one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the body one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the mind one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is form one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One."

"Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is sound one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is odor one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is taste one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is tactile sensation one thing and illusion another?"
He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are phenomena one thing and illusion another? He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is visual consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is auditory consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is olfactory consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is tongue-consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is body-consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is mind-consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is eye-contact one thing and illusion another?"

He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is auditory contact one thing and illusion another? He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is olfactory contact one thing and illusion another? He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is gustatory contact one thing and illusion another? He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

“What do you think, Subhūti? Is body-contact one thing and illusion another? He replied, “No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, “What do you think, Subhūti? Is mind-contact one thing and illusion another? He replied, “No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, “What do you think, Subhūti? Is feeling conditioned by eye-contact one thing and illusion another? He replied, “No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is the sensation conditioned by ear-contact one thing, and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the sensation conditioned by nose-contact one thing, and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact one thing, and illusion another?"

“Māyā? [Subhūti] said, “Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, “What do you think, Subhūti? Is the feeling conditioned by body-contact one thing, and illusion another? [Subhūti] said, “Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, “What do you think, Subhūti? Is the feeling conditioned by mind-contact one thing, and illusion another? [Subhūti] said, “Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, “What do you think, Subhūti? Is the earth element one thing, and illusion another? [Subhūti] said, “Certainly not, Blessed One.”

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is the water element one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is the fire element one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One.
