The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is the wind element one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, is the space element one thing and illusion another?"

He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the element of consciousness (vijñānadhātu) one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is ignorance (avidyā) one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the formative forces (saṃskāra) one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti, is consciousness one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is name-and-form one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is the six sense-bases one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is contact one thing and illusion another? He replied:
"Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is feeling one thing and illusion another? He replied: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is craving one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is grasping one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is existence one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is birth one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One."

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is aging-and-death one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the perfection of generosity one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the perfection of ethical discipline one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is the perfection of patience one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the perfection of vigor one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the perfection of meditation one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the perfection of wisdom one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One."

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is internal emptiness one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is external emptiness one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is internal-and-external emptiness one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of emptiness one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed."

“Blessed One,” [Subhūti replied]. The Blessed One said: “What do you think, Subhūti? Is the great emptiness one thing and illusion another? He said: “No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: “What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of the ultimate truth one thing and illusion another? He said: “No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: “What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of the conditioned one thing and illusion another? He said: “No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of the unconditioned one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of the ultimate one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of non-dispersal one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One."

"Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of intrinsic nature one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of all phenomena one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of specific characteristics one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: [and so forth].

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of non-apprehension one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of non-existence one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of intrinsic nature one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One."

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, are the applications of mindfulness one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, are the right efforts one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, are the bases of psychic power one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti, are the faculties one thing and illusion another? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: [and so forth].

"What do you think, Subhūti, are the powers one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, are the factors of enlightenment one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, is the eightfold path one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti, are the noble truths one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One."

"Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) one thing and illusion another? He replied: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the immeasurables (apramāṇa) one thing and illusion another? He replied: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) one thing and illusion another? He replied: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Are the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—other than illusion? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the superknowledges other than illusion? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the meditative concentrations other than illusion? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:
"What do you think, Subhūti, are the gateways of the dhāraṇīs one thing and illusion another? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think?"

"Subhūti, are the powers of a Tathāgata one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the grounds of self-confidence one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the analytical knowledges one thing and illusion another? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is great loving-kindness one thing and illusion another? He replied:

"Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is great compassion one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is awakening one thing and illusion another? He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One."

“Blessed One, form is not one thing and illusion another; form itself is illusion, and illusion itself is form. Blessed One, feeling is not one thing and illusion another; feeling itself is illusion, and illusion itself is feeling. Blessed One, perception is not one thing and illusion another; perception itself is illusion, and illusion itself, Blessed One, is perception. Blessed One, volitional formations are not one thing and illusion another; volitional formations themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is volitional formations. Blessed One, consciousness is not one thing and illusion another.”

Consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is consciousness. Blessed One, the eye is not one thing and illusion another; the eye itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the eye. Blessed One, the ear is not one thing and illusion another; the ear itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the ear. Blessed One, the nose is not one thing and illusion another; the nose itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the nose. Blessed One, the tongue is not one thing and illusion another; the tongue itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the tongue.

“O Blessed One, the body is not one thing and illusion another; the body itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the body. O Blessed One, the mind is not one thing and illusion another; the mind itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the mind.
O Blessed One, form is not one thing and illusion another; form itself is illusion, and illusion itself is form.”

“O Blessed One, sound is not one thing and illusion another; sound itself is illusion, and illusion itself is sound. O Blessed One, smell is not one thing and illusion another; smell itself is illusion, and illusion itself is smell. O Blessed One, taste is not one thing and illusion another; taste itself is illusion, and illusion itself is taste. O Blessed One, touch is not one thing and illusion another; touch itself is illusion, and illusion itself is touch. O Blessed One, phenomena are not one thing and illusion another; phenomena themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is phenomena.”

"No, Blessed One, visual consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; visual consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is visual consciousness. No, Blessed One, auditory consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; auditory consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is auditory consciousness. No, Blessed One, olfactory consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; olfactory consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is olfactory consciousness. No, Blessed One, gustatory consciousness is not one thing and illusion another."

Tongue-consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is tongue-consciousness. Blessed One, body-consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; body-consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is body-consciousness. Blessed One, mind-consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; mind-consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is mind-consciousness. Blessed One, eye-contact is not one thing and illusion another; eye-contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is eye-contact.

"No, Blessed One, auditory contact is not one thing and illusion another; auditory contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is auditory contact. No, Blessed One, olfactory contact is not one thing and illusion another; olfactory contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is olfactory contact. No, Blessed One, gustatory contact is not one thing and illusion another; gustatory contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is gustatory contact. No, Blessed One, tactile contact is not one thing and illusion another."

Body-contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is body-contact. Blessed One, mental contact is not one thing and illusion another; mental contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is mental contact. Blessed One, the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not one thing and illusion another; the feeling conditioned by eye-contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the feeling conditioned by eye-contact.

"No, Blessed One, the sensation conditioned by ear-contact is not one thing and illusion another; the sensation conditioned by ear-contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the sensation conditioned by ear-contact. No, Blessed One, the sensation conditioned by nose-contact is not one thing and illusion another; the sensation conditioned by nose-contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the sensation conditioned by nose-contact. No, Blessed One, the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is not one thing and illusion another."

The sensation conditioned by tongue-contact is itself illusion, and illusion itself is the sensation conditioned by tongue-contact. Blessed One, the sensation conditioned by body-contact is not one thing and illusion another; the sensation conditioned by body-contact is itself illusion, and illusion itself is the sensation conditioned by body-contact. Blessed One, the sensation conditioned by mind-contact is not one thing and illusion another; the sensation conditioned by mind-contact is itself illusion, and illusion itself is the sensation conditioned by mind-contact.

“Blessed One, the earth element is not one thing and illusion another; the earth element itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the earth element. Blessed One, the water element is not one thing and illusion another; the water element itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the water element. Blessed One, the fire element is not one thing and illusion another; the fire element itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the fire element. Blessed One, the wind element is not one thing and illusion another; the wind element itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the wind element.”

“Blessed One, the element of space is not one thing and illusion another; the element of space itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the element of space. Blessed One, the element of consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; the element of consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the element of consciousness. Blessed One, ignorance is not one thing and illusion another; ignorance itself is illusion, and illusion itself is ignorance. Blessed One, the formative forces are not one thing and illusion another; the formative forces themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is the formative forces.”

“O Blessed One, consciousness is not one thing and illusion another; consciousness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is consciousness. O Blessed One, name-and-form is not one thing and illusion another; name-and-form itself is illusion, and illusion itself is name-and-form. O Blessed One, the six sense bases are not one thing and illusion another; the six sense bases themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is the six sense bases.”

“O Blessed One, contact is not one thing and illusion another; contact itself is illusion, and illusion itself is contact. O Blessed One, feeling is not one thing and illusion another; feeling itself is illusion, and illusion itself is feeling. O Blessed One, craving is not one thing and illusion another; craving itself is illusion, and illusion itself is craving. O Blessed One, grasping is not one thing and illusion another; grasping itself is illusion, and illusion itself is grasping. O Blessed One, becoming is not one thing and illusion another; becoming itself is illusion, and illusion itself is becoming.”

“O Blessed One, birth is not one thing and illusion another; birth itself is illusion, and illusion itself is birth. O Blessed One, old age and death are not one thing and illusion another; old age and death themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is old age and death.”

“Blessed One, the perfection of generosity is not one thing and illusion another; the perfection of generosity itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the perfection of generosity. Blessed One, the perfection of ethical discipline is not one thing and illusion another; the perfection of ethical discipline itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the perfection of ethical discipline. Blessed One, the perfection of patience is not one thing and illusion another; the perfection of patience itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the perfection of patience. Blessed One, the perfection of vigor is not one thing and illusion another.”

The perfection of vigor is indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the perfection of vigor. Blessed One, the perfection of meditation is not one thing and illusion another; the perfection of meditation is indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the perfection of meditation. Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is not one thing and illusion another; the perfection of wisdom is indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the perfection of wisdom.

“Blessed One, internal emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; internal emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is internal emptiness. Blessed One, external emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; external emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is external emptiness. Blessed One, internal-and-external emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; internal-and-external emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is internal-and-external emptiness. Blessed One, the emptiness of emptiness is not one thing and illusion another.”

The emptiness of emptiness is itself illusion, and illusion is itself the emptiness of emptiness. Blessed One, the great emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; the great emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the great emptiness. Blessed One, the emptiness of the ultimate truth is not one thing and illusion another; the emptiness of the ultimate truth itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the emptiness of the ultimate truth. Blessed One, the emptiness of the conditioned is not one thing and illusion another; the emptiness of the conditioned itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the emptiness of the conditioned.

“Blessed One, unconditioned emptiness is not one thing and illusion another. Unconditioned emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is unconditioned emptiness. Blessed One, absolute emptiness is not one thing and illusion another. Absolute emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is absolute emptiness. Blessed One, emptiness without beginning or end is not one thing and illusion another. Emptiness without beginning or end itself is illusion, and illusion itself is emptiness without beginning or end. Blessed One, emptiness of non-dispersal is not one thing and illusion another.”

Non-dispersal emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is non-dispersal emptiness. Blessed One, intrinsic nature emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; intrinsic nature emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is intrinsic nature emptiness. Blessed One, the emptiness of all phenomena is not one thing and illusion another; the emptiness of all phenomena itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the emptiness of all phenomena. Blessed One, the emptiness of specific characteristics is not one thing and illusion another; the emptiness of specific characteristics itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the emptiness of specific characteristics.

“Blessed One, non-apprehension emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; non-apprehension emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is non-apprehension emptiness. Blessed One, non-existence emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; non-existence emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is non-existence emptiness. Blessed One, intrinsic nature emptiness is not one thing and illusion another; intrinsic nature emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is intrinsic nature emptiness. Blessed One, non-existence-of-intrinsic-nature emptiness is not one thing and illusion another;
non-existence-of-intrinsic-nature emptiness itself is illusion, and illusion itself is non-existence-of-intrinsic-nature emptiness.”

“O Blessed One, the applications of mindfulness are not one thing and illusion another; the applications of mindfulness are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the applications of mindfulness. O Blessed One, the right efforts are not something other [than illusion].”

Illusion is one thing, and the right efforts are another; the right efforts are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the right efforts. Blessed One, the bases of psychic power are not one thing and illusion another; the bases of psychic power are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the bases of psychic power. Blessed One, the faculties are not one thing and illusion another; the faculties are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the faculties. Blessed One, the powers are not one thing and illusion another; the powers are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the powers. Blessed One, the factors of enlightenment are not one thing and illusion another.

The factors of enlightenment are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the factors of enlightenment. Blessed One, the noble eightfold path is not one thing and illusion another; the noble eightfold path itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the eightfold path. Blessed One, the noble truths are not one thing and illusion another; the noble truths themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is the noble truths. Blessed One, the meditative absorptions are not one thing and illusion another; the meditative absorptions themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is the meditative absorptions. Blessed One, the immeasurables are not one thing and illusion another.

The immeasurables are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the immeasurables. Blessed One, the formless attainments are not one thing and illusion another; the formless attainments are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the formless attainments. Blessed One, the liberations are not one thing and illusion another; the liberations are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the liberations. Blessed One, the nine successive meditative attainments are not one thing and illusion another.

The nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are indeed illusion, and illusion is indeed the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling. Blessed One, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not one thing and illusion another; the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are themselves illusion, and illusion is itself the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Blessed One, the supernormal powers are not one thing and illusion another; the supernormal powers are themselves illusion, and illusion is itself the supernormal powers.

"Blessed One, meditative absorptions are not one thing and illusion another; meditative absorptions are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is meditative absorption. Blessed One, the gateways of mnemonic formulas are not one thing and illusion another; the gateways of mnemonic formulas are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the gateways of mnemonic formulas. Blessed One, the powers of a Tathāgata are not one thing and illusion another."

The powers of a Tathāgata are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the powers of a Tathāgata. Blessed One, the grounds of self-confidence are not one thing and illusion another; the grounds of self-confidence are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the grounds of self-confidence. Blessed One, the analytical knowledges are not one thing and illusion another; the analytical knowledges are themselves illusion, and illusion itself is the analytical knowledges. Blessed One, great loving-kindness is not one thing and illusion another; great loving-kindness is itself illusion, and illusion itself is great loving-kindness.

“O Blessed One, great compassion is not one thing and illusion another; great compassion itself is illusion, and illusion itself is great compassion. O Blessed One, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not one thing and illusion another; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha themselves are illusion, and illusion itself is the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. O Blessed One, the fruit of stream-entry is not one thing and illusion another; the fruit of stream-entry itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the fruit of stream-entry.”

"O Blessed One, the fruit of once-returning is not one thing and illusion another; the fruit of once-returning itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the fruit of once-returning. O Blessed One, the fruit of non-returning is not one thing and illusion another; the fruit of non-returning itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the fruit of non-returning. O Blessed One, arhatship is not one thing and illusion another; arhatship itself is illusion, and illusion itself is arhatship. O Blessed One, solitary awakening is not one thing and illusion another."

Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment itself is illusion, and illusion itself is pratyekabuddha-enlightenment. Blessed One, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not one thing and illusion another; the knowledge of the aspects of the path itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the knowledge of the aspects of the path. Blessed One, the knowledge of all aspects is not one thing and illusion another; the knowledge of all aspects itself is illusion, and illusion itself is the knowledge of all aspects.

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is there indeed arising or cessation of an illusion? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is there indeed affliction or purification of an illusion? He replied, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Will that which has neither arising nor cessation nor purification train in the perfection of wisdom, in omniscience?"

"He will go forth; he will attain all-aspect-knowledge. Subhūti said, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Is this designation, appellation, conceptualization, and conventional expression—namely, 'bodhisattva'—found within the five aggregates of clinging? Subhūti said, "No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Is the arising or the cessation, or the defilement or the purification of the five aggregates of clinging perceived as being merely by way of designation, convention, conceptualization, and linguistic usage? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Regarding one for whom there is no perception, no designation, no conceptualization, no conventional expression, no name, no designation by name, no body, no bodily action, no speech, no verbal action, no mind, no mental action, no arising, no cessation, no affliction, and no purification—would such a person, having trained in the perfection of wisdom, set out for the knowledge of all aspects and attain the knowledge of all aspects? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One."

The Blessed One said: "It is indeed thus, Subhūti, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having trained in the perfection of wisdom, will set out for all-aspect omniscience; he will attain all-aspect omniscience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension. Subhūti said: "As I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva training in the perfection of wisdom should train like an illusory person."

He becomes [established] in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, all these should be known as illusory persons; that is to say, the five aggregates.

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Do these five aggregates, having trained in the perfection of wisdom, emerge into the knowledge of all aspects? He replied: "Certainly not, Blessed One. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the five aggregates have non-existence as their intrinsic nature, and that non-existent intrinsic nature is not apprehended. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti?"

"The five aggregates are like a dream; having trained in the perfection of wisdom, they emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. Subhūti said, "No indeed, Blessed One. Why is that? Because, Blessed One, the five aggregates have non-existence as their intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*), and that non-existent intrinsic nature is not apprehended. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the five aggregates like an illusion; having trained in the perfection of wisdom, do they emerge into the knowledge of all aspects?"

He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. "For what reason? "Because, Blessed One, the five aggregates have non-existence as their intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāva*), and that non-existent intrinsic nature is not apprehended. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the five aggregates, which are like an echo, trained in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) and thereby emerge into the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)? He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One."

For what reason? Because, Blessed One, echoes have the nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva*), and that nature of non-existence is not apprehended. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the five aggregates like a reflection; having trained in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), do they emerge into the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)? He replied: "Certainly not, Blessed One. "For what reason? Because, Blessed One, a reflection has the nature of non-existence, and that nature of non-existence is not apprehended."

The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the five aggregates, which are like the moon reflected in water, able to set out for the knowledge of all aspects after training in the perfection of wisdom? He replied: "No indeed, Blessed One. "For what reason? Because, Blessed One, the moon in the water has the nature of non-existence, and that which has the nature of non-existence is not apprehended. The Blessed One said:

"What do you think, Subhūti? Are the five aggregates, which are like a mirage, led forth into all-aspect omniscience after training in the perfection of wisdom? He replied, "Certainly not, Blessed One. "For what reason? Because, Blessed One, a mirage has non-existence as its intrinsic nature, and that which has non-existence as its intrinsic nature is not apprehended. The Blessed One said, "What do you think, Subhūti? Are the five aggregates, which are like a magical creation, led forth into all-aspect omniscience after training in the perfection of wisdom?"

He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, that which is created has non-existence as its intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāva*), and that non-existent intrinsic nature is not apprehended. The Blessed One said: "What do you think, Subhūti? Is form like a dream? Are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness like a dream? Are those six sense faculties and those five aggregates of clinging like a dream?"

And they are not apprehended through internal emptiness; they are not apprehended through external emptiness; they are not apprehended through internal and external emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of emptiness; they are not apprehended through great emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the ultimate; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the conditioned; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the unconditioned; they are not apprehended through absolute emptiness.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of all phenomena; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-existence; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of self-nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

Subhūti, form is like an illusion; feeling is like an illusion; perception is like an illusion; mental formations are like an illusions; consciousness is like an illusion. And that which is consciousness is the six sense faculties; it is the five aggregates of clinging. These are not apprehended through internal emptiness; they are not apprehended through external emptiness; they are not apprehended through internal-and-external emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of emptiness; they are not apprehended through great emptiness.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of the ultimate; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the conditioned; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the unconditioned; they are not apprehended through absolute emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-dispersal.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of all phenomena; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-existence; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of self-nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

Subhūti, form is like an echo; feeling is like an echo; perception is like an echo; mental formations are like an echo; consciousness is like an echo. Those six sense faculties and those five aggregates of clinging are not apprehended through internal emptiness; they are not apprehended through external emptiness; they are not apprehended through internal-and-external emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of emptiness.

They are not apprehended through great emptiness; they are not apprehended through ultimate emptiness; they are not apprehended through conditioned emptiness; they are not apprehended through unconditioned emptiness; they are not apprehended through absolute emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are not apprehended through natural emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of all phenomena; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of specific characteristics.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-existence; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Subhūti, form is like a reflection; feeling is like a reflection; perception is like a reflection; mental formations are like a reflection; consciousness is like a reflection. And that which is consciousness is the six sense faculties and those five aggregates of clinging. These are not apprehended through internal emptiness; they are not apprehended through external emptiness; they are not apprehended through internal-and-external emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of emptiness.
They are not apprehended through the emptiness of the great; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the ultimate; [they are not apprehended] through the emptiness of the conditioned.

They are not apprehended; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of the unconditioned; they are not apprehended by way of absolute emptiness; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of all phenomena; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of non-existence.
They are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Subhūti, form is like the moon in water; feeling is like the moon in water; perception is like the moon in water; mental formations are like the moon in water; consciousness is like the moon in water. And that which is consciousness is the six sense faculties and those five aggregates of clinging. These are not apprehended through internal emptiness; they are not apprehended through external emptiness; they are not apprehended through internal-and-external emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of emptiness.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of the great; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the ultimate; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the conditioned; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the unconditioned; they are not apprehended through absolute emptiness; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of all phenomena; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of specific characteristics.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-existence; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Subhūti, form is like a mirage; feeling is like a mirage; perception is like a mirage; mental formations are like a mirage; consciousness is like a mirage. And that which is consciousness is the six sense faculties; those are the five aggregates of clinging. These are not apprehended through internal emptiness, they are not apprehended through external emptiness, nor are they apprehended through internal-and-external emptiness.

They are not apprehended. They are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of emptiness; they are not apprehended by way of great emptiness; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of the ultimate; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of the conditioned; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of the unconditioned; they are not apprehended by way of absolute emptiness; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of non-dispersal; they are not apprehended by way of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

They are not apprehended through the emptiness of all phenomena; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of specific characteristics; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-apprehension; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of non-existence; they are not apprehended through the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and they are not apprehended through the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

He said: "Blessed One, would it not be the case that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the vehicle, upon hearing this teaching, might be startled and fall into terror? The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the vehicle were not skilled in means regarding the perfection of wisdom, and were not in the hands of a spiritual friend, he would indeed be startled and fall into terror. He said:

"What, Blessed One, is the skill in means (*upāyakauśala*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), practicing in which, upon hearing this teaching, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not tremble and does not fall into fear?"

The Blessed One said: "In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, contemplates that form is impermanent, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates that feeling is impermanent, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates that perception is impermanent, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates that mental formations are impermanent, yet he does not apprehend them."

He contemplates that consciousness is impermanent, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the perfection of wisdom...

Practicing with a mind associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), he contemplates that form (*rūpa*) is suffering, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that feeling (*vedanā*) is suffering, perception (*saṃjñā*) is suffering, mental formations (*saṃskārāḥ*) are suffering, and consciousness (*vijñāna*) is suffering, yet he does not apprehend them. This is the skill in means (*upāyakauśala*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is selfless, yet he does not apprehend that [form]. He contemplates that feeling is selfless, perception is selfless, mental formations are selfless, and consciousness is selfless, yet he does not apprehend those [consciousnesses]. This, Subhūti, is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is peaceful, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that feeling is peaceful, perception is peaceful, formations are peaceful, and consciousness is peaceful, yet he does not apprehend them. This, Subhūti, is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he contemplates that form is empty, feeling is empty, perception is empty, mental formations are empty, and consciousness is empty; yet he does not apprehend that [emptiness]. This, Subhūti, is the skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva...

While practicing the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is signless, feeling is signless, perception is signless, formations are signless, and consciousness is signless; yet he does not apprehend that [signlessness]. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is wishless, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that feeling is wishless, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that perception is wishless, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that mental formations are wishless, yet he does not apprehend them.

He contemplates that consciousness is wishless, yet he does not apprehend it. This is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, contemplates that form is unconditioned, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that feeling is unconditioned.

And he does not apprehend that; he contemplates that "perception is without volitional formation," and he does not apprehend that. He contemplates that "volitional formations are without volitional formation," and he does not apprehend that. He contemplates that "consciousness is without volitional formation," and he does not apprehend that. This is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is secluded, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that feeling is secluded, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates that perception is secluded, yet he does not apprehend it; [he contemplates that] formations are secluded...

He contemplates them and yet does not apprehend them; he contemplates that consciousness is secluded and yet does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates form through the aspect of impermanence, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling through the aspect of impermanence, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception through the aspect of impermanence, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates formations through the aspect of impermanence, yet he does not apprehend them.
He contemplates consciousness through its aspect of impermanence, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates form as having the aspect of suffering, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling as having the aspect of suffering, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception as having the aspect of suffering, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates mental formations as having the aspect of suffering, yet he does not apprehend them.
He contemplates consciousness through the aspect of suffering, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mind associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates form as being selfless, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling as being selfless, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception as being selfless, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates mental formations as being selfless, yet he does not apprehend them;
[he contemplates] consciousness as being selfless...
He contemplates it and yet does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates form as peaceful, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling as peaceful, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception as peaceful, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates formations as peaceful, yet he does not apprehend them.
He contemplates consciousness through its aspect of tranquility, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates form as empty in its aspect and does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling as empty in its aspect and does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception as empty in its aspect and does not apprehend it; he contemplates formations as empty in their aspect and does not apprehend them.
He contemplates consciousness by way of its empty aspect, yet he does not apprehend it; this is the skillful means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates form as signless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates feeling in the manner of being signless, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates perception in the manner of being signless, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates volitional formations in the manner of being signless, yet he does not apprehend them.
He examines consciousness by way of its signless aspect, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates form as being wishless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates feeling in the aspect of being wishless, yet he does not apprehend it. He contemplates perception in the aspect of being wishless, yet he does not apprehend it.

He contemplates the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) by way of the aspect of wishlessness, yet he does not apprehend them; he contemplates consciousness (*vijñāna*) by way of the aspect of wishlessness, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates form through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects in the mode of non-conditioning, and yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling in the mode of non-conditioning, and yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception in the mode of non-conditioning, and yet he does not apprehend it.

He contemplates the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) by way of their lack of formative activity, yet he does not apprehend them; he contemplates consciousness (*vijñāna*) by way of its lack of formative activity, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates form as being secluded in its nature, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates feeling as being secluded in its nature, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates perception as being secluded in its nature, yet he does not apprehend it; he contemplates volitional formations as being secluded in their nature, yet he does not apprehend them.
He examines consciousness by way of its isolated aspect, yet he does not apprehend it. Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Subhūti, as that bodhisattva mahāsattva reflects in this way, it occurs to him: "I shall teach the Dharma to all sentient beings that form is impermanent, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that form is suffering, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that form is selfless, and that by way of non-apprehension."

I shall teach the Dharma that "form is peaceful," and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that "form is empty," and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that "form is signless," and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that "form is wishless," and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that "form is unconditioned," and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that "form is secluded," and that by way of non-apprehension.

I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is impermanent, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is suffering, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is selfless, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is peace, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is empty, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension.

I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is signless, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is wishless, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is unconditioned, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that feeling is secluded, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension.

I shall teach the Dharma that perception is impermanent, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is suffering, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is non-self, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is peace.

And that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is empty, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is signless, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is wishless, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that perception is unconditioned, and that by way of non-apprehension;
I shall teach the Dharma that perception is secluded, and that by way of non-apprehension.

I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are impermanent, and that through the application of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are suffering, and that through the application of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are selfless, and that through the application of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are peaceful, and that through the application of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are empty, and that through the application of non-apprehension.

I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are signless, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are wishless, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are unconditioned, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that conditioned phenomena are secluded, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension.

"I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is impermanent, and that through the method of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is suffering, and that through the method of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is selfless, and that through the method of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is peaceful, and that through the method of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is empty, and that through the method of non-apprehension."

"I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is signless, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is wishless, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is unconditioned, and that by way of non-apprehension; I shall teach the Dharma that consciousness is secluded, and that by way of non-apprehension."
Subhūti, this is the perfection of giving of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of which a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not attend to form as impermanent by means of mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and that too by way of non-apprehension. He does not attend to form as impermanent by means of mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and that too by way of non-apprehension.

When one does not attend to form with mental orientations associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of peace, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to form with mental orientations associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of emptiness, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to form with mental orientations associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of signlessness, and that through the yoga of non-apprehension.

When one does not attend to form through mental engagements associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of the aspect of wishlessness and by means of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to form through mental engagements associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of the aspect of non-conditioning and by means of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to form through mental engagements associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of the aspect of solitude and by means of non-apprehension.

When one attends to feeling in the aspect of impermanence by means of mental orientations associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one attends to feeling in the aspect of suffering by means of mental orientations associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension.

When one attends to sensation with the aspect of non-self through mental engagements associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one attends to sensation with the aspect of peace through mental engagements associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one attends to sensation with the aspect of emptiness through mental engagements associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension.

When one attends to sensation with the aspect of signlessness through the application of non-apprehension, and not by means of mental engagements associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; and when one attends to sensation with the aspect of wishlessness through the application of non-apprehension, and not by means of mental engagements associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

When one attends to feeling with mental orientations associated neither with the Disciples nor the Solitary Buddhas, in the manner of non-conditioning, and by way of non-apprehension; and when one attends to feeling with mental orientations associated neither with the Disciples nor the Solitary Buddhas, in the manner of solitude, and by way of non-apprehension.

When one attends to perception with the aspect of impermanence, not by means of mental engagements associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one attends to perception with the aspect of suffering, not by means of mental engagements associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one attends to perception with the aspect of selflessness, not by means of mental engagements associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension.

When one does not attend to perception through mental orientations associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of peace, and that by means of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to perception through mental orientations associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of emptiness, and that by means of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to perception through mental orientations associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of signlessness, and that by means of non-apprehension.

When one attends to perception with mental orientations associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, attending to it by way of the aspect of wishlessness and through the yoga of non-apprehension; when one attends to perception with mental orientations associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, attending to it by way of the aspect of lack of volitional formation and through the yoga of non-apprehension; when one attends to perception with mental orientations associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, attending to it by way of the aspect of solitude and through the yoga of non-apprehension.

When one contemplates conditioned phenomena in the aspect of impermanence through mental engagements associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, and does so by way of non-apprehension; when one contemplates conditioned phenomena in the aspect of suffering through mental engagements associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, and does so by way of non-apprehension.

When one attends to conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) in the aspect of non-self through mental engagements associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yoga*); when one attends to conditioned phenomena in the aspect of peace through mental engagements associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas, and that by way of non-apprehension; and when one attends to conditioned phenomena in the aspect of emptiness through mental engagements associated neither with Śrāvakas nor Pratyekabuddhas.

And that is by way of non-apprehension: when one does not attend to conditioned phenomena through mental orientations associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas by way of the signless aspect, that is by way of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to conditioned phenomena through mental orientations associated with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas by way of the wishless aspect, that is by way of non-apprehension.

When one attends to conditioned phenomena through mental orientations associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, doing so in the manner of non-conditioning and by way of non-apprehension; and when one attends to conditioned phenomena through mental orientations associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, doing so in the manner of solitude and by way of non-apprehension.

When one does not attend to consciousness with mental orientations associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of impermanence, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to consciousness with mental orientations associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of suffering, and that by way of non-apprehension; when one does not attend to consciousness with mental orientations associated with the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but attends to it by way of its aspect of selflessness...

He attends to it by way of non-apprehension. That which he does not attend to consciousness through mental orientations associated with the Disciples or Pratyekabuddhas in the aspect of peace, he attends to that by way of non-apprehension. That which he does not attend to consciousness through mental orientations associated with the Disciples or Pratyekabuddhas in the aspect of emptiness, he attends to that by way of non-apprehension.

When one attends to consciousness by way of the aspect of signlessness (*animitta*) through mental engagements associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, and does so by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*); and when one attends to consciousness by way of the aspect of wishlessness (*apraṇihita*) through mental engagements associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, and does so by means of non-apprehension.

When one attends to consciousness through mental orientations associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, doing so in the mode of non-conditioning and by way of non-perception; and when one attends to consciousness through mental orientations associated with neither the Śrāvakas nor the Pratyekabuddhas, doing so in the mode of solitude and by way of non-apprehension—this, Subhūti, is the unrelaxed perfection of ethical discipline of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, by which a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not tremble, is not terrified, and does not fall into terror.

Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom contemplates those phenomena through the aspect of impermanence, the aspect of suffering, the aspect of non-self, the aspect of emptiness, the aspect of signlessness, the aspect of wishlessness, the aspect of lack of formative activity, and the aspect of solitude—this patient acceptance and proclamation is the perfection of patience of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, by which the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not startled, not terrified, and does not fall into terror.

Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom contemplates form as impermanent through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and that by way of non-apprehension; he contemplates form as suffering through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and that by way of non-apprehension; [he contemplates it] through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects.

He contemplates that form is non-self by way of non-apprehension; he contemplates that form is peaceful by means of mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and that too by way of non-apprehension; he contemplates that form is empty by means of mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and that too by way of non-apprehension.

With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he contemplates that form is signless (*animitta*), and that by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is wishless (*apraṇihita*), and that by way of non-apprehension. With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that form is unconditioned (*anabhisaṃskāra*), and that by way of non-apprehension.

With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he contemplates that form is secluded, and that by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he contemplates that feeling is impermanent, feeling is suffering, feeling is non-self, feeling is peaceful, feeling is empty, feeling is signless, feeling is wishless, feeling is unconditioned, and feeling is secluded, and that by way of non-apprehension.

With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he contemplates that perception (*saṃjñā*) is impermanent, perception is suffering, perception is non-self, perception is peaceful, perception is empty, perception is signless, perception is wishless, perception is unconditioned, and perception is secluded; and he does so by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*).

With mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he contemplates that conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are impermanent, that conditioned phenomena are suffering, that conditioned phenomena are selfless, that conditioned phenomena are peaceful, that conditioned phenomena are empty, that conditioned phenomena are signless, that conditioned phenomena are wishless, that conditioned phenomena are unconditioned, and that conditioned phenomena are secluded.

And that is by way of non-apprehension. Through mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), one contemplates consciousness as impermanent, consciousness as suffering, consciousness as selfless, consciousness as peaceful, consciousness as empty, consciousness as signless, consciousness as wishless, consciousness as unconditioned, and consciousness as secluded; and that is by way of non-apprehension.

The non-abandonment of those mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and the non-laying-down of the burden—this is the perfection of vigor of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of which the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear.

Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom examines form as impermanent through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and that by way of non-apprehension. He does not allow any opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of phenomena which act as obstacles to awakening.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates form as suffering through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates form as selfless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to awakening.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that form is peaceful through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines form as empty through mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates form as signless by means of mental applications associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so through the yoga of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental applications associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates form as being wishless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that create obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates form as being without volitional construction through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects— and that by means of non-apprehension— he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates form as secluded by means of mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so through the yoga of non-apprehension, he allows no room for mental attentions associated with the disciples or solitary buddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates feeling as impermanent with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates feeling as suffering through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates feeling as selfless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates feeling as peaceful through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that create obstacles to awakening.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, examines with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects that "perception is impermanent," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma that act as obstacles to enlightenment—then [he is said to be coursing in the perfection of wisdom].

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that "perception is suffering" with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension; he does not allow any opportunity for mental attentions associated with the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects that "this is the nature of perception," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that "perception is peaceful" with mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to his progress as a bodhisattva.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that perception is empty by means of mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so through the yoga of non-apprehension; and when he allows no occasion for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma that create obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines perception as being signless through mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that create obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects that "perception is wishless," doing so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), forming perceptions through non-conceptualization by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*), he does not allow any opportunity for mental attentions associated with the disciples (*śrāvaka*) or solitary buddhas (*pratyekabuddha*), nor for other unwholesome roots (*akuśalamūla*) that act as obstacles to enlightenment.
