When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects that perception is secluded—and does so by way of non-apprehension—he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to awakening.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that conditioned phenomena are impermanent with mental orientations associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension;
and when he allows no opportunity for mental orientations associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of perception, contemplates that conditioned phenomena are suffering through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects—and that by way of non-apprehension—he does not allow any opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to awakening.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines conditioned phenomena as being selfless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension, he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines conditioned phenomena as being peaceful through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that "formations are empty" by means of mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, and does so through the yoga of non-apprehension; and when he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma which act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, examines conditioned phenomena as being signless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects—and that by way of non-apprehension—he does not allow any opportunity for mental engagements associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that all conditioned phenomena are wishless through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects—and this by way of non-apprehension—he allows no opportunity for mental engagements associated with the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma that act as obstacles to awakening.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines conditioned phenomena with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects, thinking "conditioned phenomena are unconditioned," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he allows no occasion for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots of dharma that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, contemplates that all conditioned phenomena are secluded by means of mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects—and this by way of non-apprehension—he does not allow any opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, examines consciousness as "permanent" with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), and does so by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*),
he allows no opportunity for mental attentions associated with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor for other unwholesome roots that act as obstacles to enlightenment.

He contemplates that the consciousness associated with the mental orientations (*manasikāra*) of the *śrāvakas* and *pratyekabuddhas* is suffering, and he does so by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). Furthermore, he allows no opportunity for those mental orientations associated with the *śrāvakas* and *pratyekabuddhas*, nor for other unwholesome roots (*akuśalamūla*) which act as obstacles to enlightenment. Subhūti, this is the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*) of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, by means of which the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not startled, not terrified, and does not fall into terror.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he contemplates with mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects as follows: "Form is not empty by way of the emptiness of form; form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is form. Feeling is not empty by way of the emptiness of feeling; feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling. Perception is not empty by way of the emptiness of perception; perception itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is perception."

It is not by means of the emptiness of formations that formations are empty; rather, formations themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is formations. It is not by means of the emptiness of consciousness that consciousness is empty; rather, consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is consciousness.

The eye is not empty by means of the emptiness of the eye; the eye itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the eye. The ear is not empty by means of the emptiness of the ear; the ear itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the ear. The nose is not empty by means of the emptiness of the nose; the nose itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the nose. The tongue is not empty by means of the emptiness of the tongue; the tongue itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the tongue.

The body is not empty because of the emptiness of the body; the body itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the body. The mind is not empty because of the emptiness of the mind; the mind itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the mind.

Form is not empty because of the emptiness of form; form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is form. Sound is not empty because of the emptiness of sound; sound itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is sound. Scent is not empty because of the emptiness of scent; scent itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is scent. Taste is not empty because of the emptiness of taste; taste itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is taste.

Contact is not empty because of the emptiness of contact; contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is contact. Phenomena are not empty because of the emptiness of phenomena; phenomena themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is phenomena.

Eye-consciousness is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of eye-consciousness; rather, eye-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of ear-consciousness; rather, ear-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of nose-consciousness; rather, nose-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is nose-consciousness.

It is not by means of the emptiness of tongue-consciousness that tongue-consciousness is empty; rather, tongue-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is tongue-consciousness. It is not by means of the emptiness of body-consciousness that body-consciousness is empty; rather, body-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is body-consciousness. It is not by means of the emptiness of mind-consciousness that mind-consciousness is empty; rather, mind-consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is mind-consciousness.

Eye-contact is not empty because of the emptiness of eye-contact; rather, eye-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is eye-contact. Ear-contact is not empty because of the emptiness of ear-contact; rather, ear-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ear-contact. Nose-contact is not empty because of the emptiness of nose-contact; rather, nose-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is nose-contact.

It is not by means of the emptiness of tongue-contact that tongue-contact is empty; rather, tongue-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is tongue-contact. It is not by means of the emptiness of body-contact that body-contact is empty; rather, body-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is body-contact.
It is not by means of the emptiness of mind-contact that mind-contact is empty; rather, mind-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is mind-contact.

Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by eye-contact; rather, feeling conditioned by eye-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by eye-contact. Feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by ear-contact; rather, feeling conditioned by ear-contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by ear-contact.

Feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by olfactory contact; rather, feeling conditioned by olfactory contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by olfactory contact. Feeling conditioned by gustatory contact is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by gustatory contact; rather, feeling conditioned by gustatory contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by gustatory contact.

Feeling conditioned by bodily contact is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by bodily contact; rather, feeling conditioned by bodily contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by bodily contact. Feeling conditioned by mental contact is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact; rather, feeling conditioned by mental contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by mental contact.

The earth element is not empty by means of the emptiness of the earth element; rather, the earth element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the earth element. The water element is not empty by means of the emptiness of the water element; rather, the water element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the water element. The fire element is not empty by means of the emptiness of the fire element; rather, the fire element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the fire element. The wind element is not empty by means of the emptiness of the wind element; rather, the wind element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the wind element.

The space element is not empty because of the emptiness of the space element; rather, the space element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the space element. The consciousness element is not empty because of the emptiness of the consciousness element; rather, the consciousness element itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the consciousness element.

It is not by means of the emptiness of ignorance that ignorance is empty; ignorance itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ignorance. It is not by means of the emptiness of formative forces that formative forces are empty; formative forces themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is formative forces. It is not by means of the emptiness of consciousness that consciousness is empty; consciousness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is consciousness. It is not by means of the emptiness of name-and-form that name-and-form is empty; name-and-form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is name-and-form.

The six sense bases are not empty because of the emptiness of the six sense bases; the six sense bases themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the six sense bases. Contact is not empty because of the emptiness of contact; contact itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is contact. Craving is not empty because of the emptiness of craving; craving itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is craving. Grasping is not empty because of the emptiness of grasping; grasping itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is grasping.

Feeling is not empty because of the emptiness of feeling; feeling itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is feeling. Existence is not empty because of the emptiness of existence; existence itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is existence. Birth is not empty because of the emptiness of birth; birth itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is birth. Old age and death are not empty because of the emptiness of old age and death; old age and death themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is old age and death.

The perfection of generosity is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of generosity; rather, the perfection of generosity itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of generosity. The perfection of ethical discipline is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of ethical discipline; rather, the perfection of ethical discipline itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of ethical discipline. The perfection of patience is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of patience; rather, the perfection of patience itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of patience.

The perfection of vigor is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of vigor; rather, the perfection of vigor itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of vigor. The perfection of meditation is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of meditation; rather, the perfection of meditation itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of meditation. The perfection of wisdom is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom; rather, the perfection of wisdom itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the perfection of wisdom.

Internal emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of internal emptiness; internal emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is internal emptiness. External emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of external emptiness; external emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is external emptiness. Internal-and-external emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of internal-and-external emptiness; internal-and-external emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is internal-and-external emptiness.

The emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness; emptiness itself is the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness, and the emptiness of the emptiness of emptiness is indeed emptiness. The emptiness of the great emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of the great emptiness; the great emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the great emptiness. The emptiness of the ultimate emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of the ultimate emptiness; the ultimate emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the ultimate emptiness.

Conditioned emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of conditioned emptiness; rather, conditioned emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is conditioned emptiness. Unconditioned emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of unconditioned emptiness; rather, unconditioned emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is unconditioned emptiness. Ultimate emptiness is not empty by means of the emptiness of ultimate emptiness; rather, ultimate emptiness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is ultimate emptiness.

The emptiness of the beginningless and endless is not empty by means of the emptiness of the beginningless and endless; the very emptiness of the beginningless and endless is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of the beginningless and endless. The emptiness of the non-dispersed is not empty by means of the emptiness of the non-dispersed; the very emptiness of the non-dispersed is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of the non-dispersed. The emptiness of intrinsic nature is not empty by means of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the very emptiness of intrinsic nature is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

The emptiness of all phenomena is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of all phenomena; rather, the emptiness of all phenomena is itself emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of all phenomena. The emptiness of specific characteristics is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of specific characteristics; rather, the emptiness of specific characteristics is itself emptiness, and emptiness itself is the emptiness of specific characteristics. The emptiness of non-apprehension is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

The emptiness of non-apprehension is itself emptiness; emptiness itself is the emptiness of non-apprehension. The emptiness of non-existence is not made empty by the emptiness of non-existence; the emptiness of non-existence itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is the emptiness of non-existence. The emptiness of intrinsic nature is not made empty by the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of intrinsic nature itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is the emptiness of intrinsic nature. The emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature is not made empty by the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature itself is emptiness; emptiness itself is the emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature.

The applications of mindfulness are not empty by means of emptiness; the applications of mindfulness are empty, the applications of mindfulness themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the applications of mindfulness. The right efforts are not empty by means of emptiness; the right efforts are empty, the right efforts themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the right efforts. The bases of psychic power are not empty by means of emptiness; the bases of psychic power are empty, the bases of psychic power themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the bases of psychic power.

The sense faculties are not empty by means of emptiness; rather, the sense faculties themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the sense faculties. The powers are not empty by means of emptiness; rather, the powers themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the powers. The factors of enlightenment are not empty by means of emptiness; rather, the factors of enlightenment themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the factors of enlightenment.

The Noble Eightfold Path is not empty because of the emptiness of the Noble Eightfold Path; the Noble Eightfold Path itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is the Noble Eightfold Path. The Noble Truths are not empty because of the emptiness of the Noble Truths; the Noble Truths themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the Noble Truths. The meditative absorptions are not empty because of the emptiness of the meditative absorptions; the meditative absorptions themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the meditative absorptions.

The immeasurables are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the immeasurables; the immeasurables themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the immeasurables. The formless attainments are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the formless attainments; the formless attainments themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the formless attainments. The liberations are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the liberations; the liberations...

Thus, emptiness is indeed the liberations themselves. It is not that the successive meditative attainments are empty by virtue of the emptiness of the successive meditative attainments; rather, the successive meditative attainments are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the successive meditative attainments.

The doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; rather, the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are themselves emptiness, and emptiness itself is the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. The superknowledges are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the superknowledges; rather, the superknowledges themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the superknowledges.

It is not by means of the emptiness of meditative concentrations that meditative concentrations are empty; rather, meditative concentrations themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is meditative concentrations. It is not by means of the emptiness of the gateways of mnemonic formulas that the gateways of mnemonic formulas are empty; rather, the gateways of mnemonic formulas themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the gateways of mnemonic formulas. It is not by means of the emptiness of the powers of a Tathāgata that the powers of a Tathāgata are empty; rather, the powers of a Tathāgata themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the powers of a Tathāgata.

The fearlessnesses are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the fearlessnesses; the fearlessnesses themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the fearlessnesses. The analytical knowledges are not empty by virtue of the emptiness of the analytical knowledges; the analytical knowledges themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the analytical knowledges. Great loving-kindness is not empty by virtue of the emptiness of great loving-kindness; great loving-kindness itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is great loving-kindness.

Great compassion is not empty because of the emptiness of great compassion; great compassion itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is great compassion. The unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are not empty because of the emptiness of the unique qualities of a Buddha; the unique qualities of a Buddha themselves are emptiness, and emptiness itself is the unique qualities of a Buddha. This, Subhūti, is the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Subhūti, this is the skill in means of a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom. Endowed with which skill in means, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this teaching, does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear.

Subhūti said: "Blessed One, who are the spiritual friends of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? By which spiritual friends being taken hold of, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard this teaching on the perfection of wisdom, does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear? The Blessed One replied:

Subhūti, this is the spiritual friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva: one who teaches him the dharma that "form is impermanent," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and who does not dedicate any roots of virtue to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but [dedicates them] only to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). One who teaches him the dharma that "feeling is impermanent," and does so by way of non-apprehension.

And he does not dedicate all his roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). When someone teaches him the Dharma as being "perception is impermanent," he does so by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yogena*). And he does not dedicate all his roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience.

When he teaches him the Dharma that "formations are impermanent," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and when he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather to all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*); and when he teaches him the Dharma that "consciousness is impermanent," and does so by way of non-apprehension;
and when he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather to all-aspect omniscience.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the good friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who...

He teaches the Dharma that "form is suffering," and he does so by way of non-apprehension; furthermore, he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather [dedicates them] to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). He teaches the Dharma that "feeling is suffering," and he does so by way of non-apprehension; furthermore, he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather [dedicates them] to omniscience.

Whoever teaches him the dharma that "perception is suffering," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and whoever dedicates all roots of merit neither to the level of a śrāvaka nor to the level of a pratyekabuddha, but solely to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*); and whoever teaches him the dharma that "formative forces (*saṃskāra*) are suffering," and does so by way of non-apprehension.

And he does not dedicate all roots of goodness to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). When someone teaches him the dharma that "consciousness is suffering," he does so by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yoga*); and he does not dedicate all roots of goodness to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience.

Furthermore, Subhūti, another good friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who teaches him the dharma that "form is non-self," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and they do not dedicate all roots of virtue to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). One who teaches him the dharma that "feeling is non-self," and does so by way of non-apprehension, is also a good friend.

And he does not dedicate all roots of merit to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). When someone teaches him a dharma as being "the self of perception," he does so through the yoga of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*); and he does not dedicate all roots of merit to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience.

Whoever teaches him the dharma that "formations are non-self" by way of non-apprehension, and does not dedicate all roots of virtue to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience; whoever teaches him the dharma that "consciousness is non-self" by way of non-apprehension, and does not dedicate all roots of virtue to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience.

Furthermore, Subhūti, another good friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who teaches him the Dharma that "form is peaceful," and does so by way of non-apprehension; and he does not dedicate all roots of virtue to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). One who teaches him the Dharma that "feeling is peaceful," and does so by way of non-apprehension, is likewise a good friend.

And he does not dedicate all his roots of merit to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). When he teaches the Dharma to him, saying "perception is peace," he does so by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yogena*). And he does not dedicate all his roots of merit to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience.

When he teaches him the Dharma that "formations are peaceful," he does so by way of non-apprehension; and he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience alone. When he teaches him the Dharma that "consciousness is peaceful," he does so by way of non-apprehension; and he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but rather to omniscience alone.

Furthermore, Subhūti, another good friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who teaches him the dharma that "form is empty," and that by way of non-apprehension; and who does not dedicate all roots of virtue to the level of a śrāvaka or the level of a pratyekabuddha, but [dedicates them] only to omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). One who teaches him the dharma that "feeling is empty" [is likewise a good friend].

And that is by way of non-apprehension. He does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but [dedicates them] only to the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). To him, one teaches the Dharma that "perception is empty," and that too is by way of non-apprehension. And he does not dedicate any roots of merit to the level of a Śrāvaka or the level of a Pratyekabuddha, but [dedicates them] only to the knowledge of all aspects.

Subhūti said: "Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, become unskilled in means, fall into the hands of evil friends, and be deprived of virtuous friends—yet, having heard this teaching on the perfection of wisdom, does not tremble, is not terrified, and does not fall into terror?
The Blessed One said: "In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while [practicing] the perfection of wisdom..."

While practicing the perfection of wisdom, being devoid of a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to external emptiness as grasping; yet he perceives that external emptiness, and likewise conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

While practicing the perfection of wisdom, he—possessing mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects—attends to grasping as "empty internally and externally. Yet, he perceives that internal and external emptiness, and likewise conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he attends to the fact that grasping (*upādāna*) is empty of emptiness. And he perceives that emptiness of emptiness; furthermore, he conceives of it as emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that grasping is the great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*). And he perceives that great emptiness; furthermore, he conceives of it as emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects removed, he attends to grasping as being ultimately empty; yet he perceives that ultimate emptiness, and likewise conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that grasping is empty of the conditioned; yet he perceives that emptiness of the conditioned, and he conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he attends to the fact that appropriation (*upādāna*) is absolutely empty; yet he perceives that absolute emptiness, and likewise conceives of it as emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that appropriation is empty of beginning and end (*anavarāgra-śūnya*); yet he perceives that emptiness of beginning and end, and likewise conceives of it as emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, his mental attention being dissociated from all-aspect omniscience, he attends to the fact that grasping is empty of intrinsic nature; yet he perceives that intrinsic emptiness, and likewise conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, possessing mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought, "Existence is internally empty. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought: "An entity is internally empty. And he perceives that internal emptiness; furthermore, he conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension.

He attends to the thought associated with the *pratisaṃyuktamanasikāra* that "existence is empty of emptiness," and he perceives that emptiness of emptiness. Likewise, by means of apprehension, he conceives of it as emptiness.

While practicing the perfection of wisdom, being devoid of the mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he attends to the thought that "existence is the great emptiness," and he perceives that great emptiness. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought: "Existence is empty of ultimate reality. And he perceives that emptiness of ultimate reality; yet he conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought: "Existence is empty of the conditioned. And he perceives that emptiness of the conditioned; yet he conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought that "existence is empty of the unconditioned. Yet he perceives that very emptiness of the unconditioned, and he conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought that "existence is absolutely empty. Yet he perceives that very absolute emptiness, and he conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that "existence is empty of beginninglessness and endlessness" (*anavarāgra-śūnya*). Yet, he perceives that emptiness of beginninglessness and endlessness; and he conceives of it as emptiness through the application of perception.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that "existence is empty of non-dispersal" (*anavakāra-śūnya*). Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought, "Existence is empty by nature. Yet, he perceives that very emptiness of nature; and thus, by means of apprehension, he conceives of it as emptiness.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that "all phenomena are empty of intrinsic existence. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he attends to the thought: "Existence is empty of its own specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇaśūnya*). Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought: "Existence is empty of non-apprehension (*anupalambhaśūnya*). Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought that "birth is internally empty. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, his mental attention being dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to birth as "emptiness of emptiness" (*śūnyatā-śūnyatā*). And he perceives that emptiness of emptiness; furthermore, by means of apprehension, he conceives of it through emptiness.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he attends to the thought that birth is "great emptiness" (*mahāśūnyatā*). And he perceives that great emptiness; furthermore, he conceives of it as empty by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the thought that birth is "emptiness of the ultimate truth" (*paramārthaśūnyatā*). And he perceives that emptiness of the ultimate truth; furthermore, he conceives of it as empty by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that birth is empty of the conditioned; yet he perceives that emptiness of the conditioned, and he conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that birth is empty of the unconditioned; yet he perceives that emptiness of the unconditioned, and he conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that birth is absolutely empty; yet he perceives that absolute emptiness, and likewise conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that birth is empty of beginningless and endlessness; yet he perceives that emptiness of beginningless and endlessness, and likewise conceives of it as emptiness by way of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he attends to birth as "emptiness of non-dispersal" (*anavakāraśūnyatā*). Likewise, [he conceives] the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, and the powers.

the factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the liberations, the serial attainments of successive dwellings, the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the superknowledges, the samādhis, the gateways to the dhāraṇīs, the powers of a Tathāgata, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, great compassion, and the unique qualities of a Buddha.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to old age and death as "internally empty. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to old age and death as being "externally empty. Yet, he perceives that external emptiness; furthermore, he conceives of it through that emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to old age and death as "empty internally and externally. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to aging and death as "the emptiness of emptiness," and he perceives that emptiness of emptiness. Yet, he conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that old age and death are empty by nature; yet he perceives that emptiness of nature through the application of apprehension, and likewise conceives of it as emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to the fact that old age and death—and indeed all phenomena—are empty. He attends to old age and death as being empty of non-existence, and he perceives that emptiness of non-existence; furthermore, he conceives of it through emptiness by means of apprehension.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he attends to aging and death as being empty of the nature of non-existence; yet he perceives that emptiness of the nature of non-existence, and he conceives of it through that emptiness by means of apprehension.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he cultivates the applications of mindfulness with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects; yet he perceives those applications of mindfulness and, by means of the application of perception, he conceives himself as possessing those applications of mindfulness.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects removed, he cultivates the right efforts; yet he perceives those right efforts and conceives himself by means of those right efforts through the application of perception. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects removed, he cultivates the bases of psychic power; yet he perceives those bases of psychic power and conceives himself by means of those bases of psychic power through the application of perception.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects removed, he cultivates the faculties; yet he perceives those faculties and conceives himself by means of those faculties through the application of perception. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement dissociated from the knowledge of all aspects, he cultivates the noble eightfold path; yet he perceives that noble eightfold path and conceives of himself by means of that noble eightfold path through the application of apprehension.

Practicing the perfection of wisdom, he cultivates the noble truths with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects; yet he perceives those noble truths and, by means of that perception, conceives himself in relation to them. Practicing the perfection of wisdom, he cultivates the meditative absorptions with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects; yet he perceives those meditative absorptions and, by means of that perception, conceives himself in relation to them.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he cultivates the immeasurables; yet he perceives those immeasurables and, by means of the apprehension of them, he conceives himself through those immeasurables. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he cultivates the formless attainments; yet he perceives those formless attainments and, by means of the apprehension of them, he conceives himself through those formless attainments.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental engagement associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he cultivates the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and yet he perceives those gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and by means of those gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, he conceives through the application of perception.

Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he cultivates the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*); yet he perceives those supernormal powers and, by means of those supernormal powers, he conceives through the application of apprehension (*upalambha*). Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, he cultivates the powers of a Tathāgata with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects; yet he perceives those powers of a Tathāgata, and through those powers of a Tathāgata, he conceives [of them] by way of apprehension.
