Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he cultivates great compassion; yet he perceives that great compassion and, by means of that perception, conceives himself as possessing it. Practicing in the perfection of wisdom, with a mental attention associated with the knowledge of all aspects, he cultivates the unique qualities of a Buddha; yet he perceives those Buddha-qualities and, by means of that perception, conceives himself as possessing them.

"In this way indeed, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, being unskilled in means, upon hearing this teaching of the perfection of wisdom, becomes afraid, terrified, and falls into terror. He asked: "Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva fall into the hands of a bad friend? By what kind of bad friend being taken hold of does he, upon hearing this teaching of the perfection of wisdom, become afraid, terrified, and fall into terror?"

The Blessed One said: "In this regard, Subhūti, the evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who dissuades and discourages him while he is practicing the perfection of wisdom; who dissuades and discourages him while he is practicing the perfection of meditation; who dissuades and discourages him while he is practicing the perfection of vigor; who dissuades and discourages him while he is practicing the perfection of patience; and who dissuades and discourages him while he is practicing the perfection of ethical discipline."

While he is practicing the perfection of generosity, [the evil friend] causes him to reject it and dissuade him from it, saying: "One should not train in this; this was not spoken by the Tathāgata; this is neither the Dharma nor the Vinaya. These sūtras are of wrong reasoning; they should not be heard, nor taken up, nor retained, nor recited, nor mastered, nor properly attended to, nor taught to others.
Subhūti, this should be known as the evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, another evil friend of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who does not instruct him in the works of Māra, nor point out the faults of Māra. Thus, Māra the Evil One approaches the bodhisattva mahāsattva in the guise of a Buddha and causes him to turn away from and lose interest in the six perfections, saying: "Noble son, what use have you for the perfection of wisdom being spoken? What use have you for the perfection of meditation being spoken?"

"What is the use of speaking of the perfection of vigor? What is the use of speaking of the perfection of patience? What is the use of speaking of the perfection of ethical discipline? What is the use of speaking of the perfection of generosity?"—in this way, one should recognize such a person as a bad friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One approaches a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the form of a Buddha and teaches, explains, analyzes, clarifies, and fully reveals sūtras associated with the śrāvakas—namely, the *geya*, *vyākaraṇa*, *gāthā*, *udāna*, *nidāna*, *ityuktaka*, *jātaka*, *vaipulya*, *adbhutadharma*, *avadāna*, and *upadeśa*.
Subhūti, one should know that whoever does not point out nor awaken [the bodhisattva] to such deeds of Māra is a bad friend to the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One approaches a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the guise of a Buddha and says this: "Son of good family, you have no thought of awakening at all;

nor are you irreversible, nor are you capable of fully awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Subhūti, one who does not point out nor make known such deeds of Māra should be recognized as a bad friend to the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One, having approached a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the guise of a Buddha, speaks thus: "Noble son, the eye is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; the ear is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; the nose is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; the tongue is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; the body is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; the mind is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; and form is empty of self or of what belongs to a self."

Sound is empty of self or what belongs to a self; odor is empty of self or what belongs to a self; taste is empty of self or what belongs to a self; touch is empty of self or what belongs to a self; mental phenomena are empty of self or what belongs to a self. Eye-consciousness is empty of self or what belongs to a self; ear-consciousness is empty of self or what belongs to a self; nose-consciousness is empty of self or what belongs to a self; tongue-consciousness is empty of self or what belongs to a self.

Body-consciousness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; mind-consciousness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self. Eye-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; ear-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; nose-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; tongue-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; body-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; mind-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.

Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; feeling conditioned by ear-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; feeling conditioned by nose-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; feeling conditioned by body-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; feeling conditioned by mind-contact is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.

The earth element is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the water element is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the fire element is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the air element is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the space element is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the consciousness element is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; ignorance is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the formative forces are empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; consciousness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.

Name-and-form is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; the six sense bases are empty of self or of what belongs to a self; contact is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; feeling is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; craving is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; clinging is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; becoming is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; birth is empty of self or of what belongs to a self; and old age and death are empty of self or of what belongs to a self.

The perfection of generosity is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the perfection of ethical discipline is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the perfection of patience is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the perfection of vigor is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the perfection of meditative concentration is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the perfection of wisdom is empty of a self or what belongs to a self.

Internal emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; external emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; internal-external emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the emptiness of emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; great emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; ultimate emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; conditioned emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; unconditioned emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.

Absolute emptiness is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the emptiness of non-dispersal is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self.

Or, all phenomena are empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the emptiness of non-existence is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of a self or what belongs to a self; and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of a self or what belongs to a self.

The foundations of mindfulness are empty of self or what belongs to self; the right efforts are empty of self or what belongs to self; the bases of psychic power are empty of self or what belongs to self; the faculties are empty of self or what belongs to self; the powers are empty of self or what belongs to self; the factors of enlightenment are empty of self or what belongs to self; the noble eightfold path is empty of self or what belongs to self; the noble truths are empty of self or what belongs to self.

The meditative absorptions (dhyānas) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the immeasurables (apramāṇas) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the formless attainments (ārūpya-samāpattis) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the liberations (vimokṣas) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the serial attainments of the meditative dwellings (anupūrva-vihāra-samāpattis) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita-vimokṣamukhas) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the concentrations (samādhis) are empty of self or what belongs to a self; and the gateways of the mnemonic formulas (dhāraṇī-mukhas) are empty of self or what belongs to a self.

The powers of a Tathāgata are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the grounds of self-confidence are empty of self or what belongs to a self; the analytical knowledges are empty of self or what belongs to a self; great compassion is empty of self or what belongs to a self; the unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of self or what belongs to a self. Having fully awakened to such unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, what will you do? Subhūti, one who does not point out nor teach these kinds of works of Māra should be known as a bad friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One, approaching a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the guise of a Buddha, says this to him: "Son of good family, the eastern direction is empty of Buddhas, Blessed Ones, bodhisattvas, and śrāvakas; nor are there any Buddhas, bodhisattvas, or śrāvakas here."

In this way, the southern direction is empty, as are the western, northern, downward, upward, and indeed all ten directions, empty of Buddhas, Blessed Ones, Bodhisattvas, and Śrāvakas. Herein there are no Buddhas, no Bodhisattvas, and no Śrāvakas. One who does not point out nor teach such deeds of Māra as these should be known as a bad friend to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One approaches a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the guise of a śrāvaka and diverts him from mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). He speaks to and instructs him with mental engagements associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. One who neither points out nor teaches such deeds of Māra should be known as a bad friend (*pāpamitra*) to the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One, approaching in the guise of a preceptor or a teacher, diverts the bodhisattva mahāsattva from the conduct of a bodhisattva and diverts him from the mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects. He enjoins him to the applications of mindfulness; he enjoins him to the right efforts; he enjoins him to the bases of psychic power; he enjoins him to the powers; he enjoins him to the factors of enlightenment; and he enjoins him to the noble eightfold path.

He establishes them in the noble truths; he establishes them in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*); he establishes them in the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*); he establishes them in the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*); he establishes them in the liberations (*vimokṣa*); he establishes them in the serial attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*); he establishes them in the gateways to liberation (*vimokṣamukha*)—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. In this way, O son of good family, you [should establish them].

"Having taught the dharmas, realize the stage of a śrāvaka; what will you do with unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening? Subhūti, one who does not point out nor instruct regarding such deeds of Māra should be known as a bad friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra, the Evil One, approaching in the guise of a father or mother, says this to the bodhisattva mahāsattva: "Son of good family, apply yourself to that wherein there is the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the realization of the fruit of once-returning, the realization of the fruit of non-returning, the realization of arhatship, and the realization of pratyekabuddhahood. What is the use to you of awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

For whose sake you will undergo immeasurable and incalculable eons of wandering through saṃsāra, experiencing the severing of hands, feet, and heads—Subhūti, one who does not awaken you to, does not declare, and does not instruct you regarding such deeds of Māra should be known as a bad friend to a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One approaches a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the guise of a monk and, by means of the apprehension of objective referents (*upalambha-yoga*), teaches that "it is selfless," "it is peaceful," "it is empty," "it is signless," "it is wishless," "it is unconditioned," and "it is secluded. He teaches that "feeling is impermanent" by means of the non-apprehension of objective referents; and he teaches that "feeling is suffering," "selfless," "peaceful," "empty," and "signless."
He teaches that it is "wishless," "unconditioned," and "secluded" by way of apprehension; he teaches that "perception is impermanent" by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that perception is suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that formations are impermanent. He teaches by way of apprehension that formations are suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches that consciousness is impermanent by way of apprehension; he teaches that consciousness is suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the eye is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, unknown, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. [He teaches] that the nose is impermanent. Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, one speaks of a 'bodhisattva mahāsattva. What is the meaning of this term? When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable Subhūti:

Subhūti, the term "bodhisattva" is a term for that which has no objective referent (*apadārtha*). Why is that? Because awakening is non-arising, and a sentient being is non-arising. Indeed, Subhūti, there is no footprint in awakening, nor in a sentient being; therefore, the term "bodhisattva" is a term for that which has no objective referent. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint of a bird is found in the sky, even so the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint is found in a dream, [so it is with the term "bodhisattva"].

In the same way, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example, the track of a magical illusion does not exist, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, for example, the track of a mirage does not exist, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example...

The footprint of the moon in water does not exist; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, for example, the footprint of an echo does not exist, even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, the footprint of a reflected image does not exist, even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, the footprint of a reflection does not exist, [even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist].

In the same way, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no track of a Tathāgata’s emanation; in the same way, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no track of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); in the same way, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no track of suchness (*tathatā*); in the same way, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, just as, for example, no locus for "suchness" exists, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example, no locus for "non-other suchness" exists, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example, no locus for "the nature of phenomena" exists, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of the *dharmadhātu* is found; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of the stability of phenomena (*dharmasthititā*) is found; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*) is found; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a foot is found in the form of an illusory person; no trace is found in feeling, no trace is found in perception, no trace is found in mental formations, and no trace is found in consciousness. No trace is found in mental formations, and no trace is found in consciousness.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person there is no trace in the eye, no trace in the ear, no trace in the nose, no trace in the tongue, no trace in the body, and no trace in the mind.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person there is no footing in eye-consciousness, no footing in ear-consciousness, no footing in nose-consciousness, no footing in tongue-consciousness, no footing in body-consciousness, and no footing in mind-consciousness.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person there is no trace found in visual contact, no trace found in auditory contact, no trace found in olfactory contact, no trace found in gustatory contact, no trace found in tactile contact, and no trace found in mental contact.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person there exists no basis for the feeling conditioned by eye-contact, no basis for the feeling conditioned by ear-contact, no basis for the feeling conditioned by nose-contact, and no basis for the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact.
In the feeling conditioned by bodily contact, no footing is found; in the feeling conditioned by mental contact, no footing is found.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person there is no footing in ignorance, no footing in volitional formations, no footing in consciousness, no footing in name-and-form, no footing in the six sense bases, no footing in contact, no footing in feeling, and no footing in craving;
No footprint is found in grasping; no footprint is found in becoming; no footprint is found in birth; no footprint is found in old age and death.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing the perfection of generosity, no referent is found; just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing the perfection of ethical discipline, no referent is found.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there were no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the perfection of patience; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there were no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the perfection of vigor; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there were no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the perfection of meditation; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there were no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the perfection of wisdom.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing internal emptiness, no referent exists; just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing external emptiness, no referent exists; and just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing internal-and-external emptiness—

No real entity exists for one who courses [in these]. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no real entity exists for an illusory person who courses in the emptiness of emptiness; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no real entity exists for an illusory person who courses in great emptiness; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no real entity exists for an illusory person who courses in the emptiness of the ultimate truth.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of the conditioned; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of the unconditioned; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of the ultimate; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of non-dispersal; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of intrinsic nature; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the emptiness of all phenomena.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person who courses in the emptiness of specific characteristics; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person who courses in the emptiness of non-apprehension; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person who courses in the emptiness of non-existence; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person who courses in the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person who courses in the emptiness of the nature of non-existence;
even so, Subhūti, there is no real entity found in a bodhisattva mahāsattva who courses in the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, in the case of a phantom person...

For one who courses in the foundations of mindfulness, no real entity exists. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no real entity exists for an illusory person coursing in the right efforts. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no real entity exists for an illusory person coursing in the bases of psychic power. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no real entity exists for an illusory person coursing in the faculties.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in the powers of an illusory person as they practice; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in the factors of enlightenment of an illusory person as they practice; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no real entity found in the noble eightfold path of an illusory person as they practice.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing the noble truths, no referent exists; just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing the meditative concentrations, no referent exists; and just as, Subhūti, for an illusory person practicing the immeasurables, no referent exists.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no objective referent for a phantom person practicing the formless attainments. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, one might teach a phantom person practicing the eight liberations by means of apprehension, saying: "suffering," "selfless," "peaceful," "empty," "signless," "wishless," "unconditioned," or "secluded."

He teaches by way of apprehension that the tongue is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the body is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. [He teaches] that the mind is impermanent, suffering, selfless, and peaceful...
He teaches by way of apprehension that [all things] are empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that form is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that sound is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches that odor is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. He teaches that taste is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that phenomena are impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that eye-consciousness is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that ear-consciousness is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that olfactory consciousness is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that gustatory consciousness is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches that body-consciousness is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded, by way of apprehension. He teaches that mind-consciousness is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded, by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that eye-contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that ear-contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. [He teaches] that nose-contact is impermanent and suffering...
He teaches by way of apprehension that [the mind] is "selfless," "peaceful," "empty," "signless," "wishless," "unconditioned," and "secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that tongue-contact is "impermanent," "suffering," "selfless," "peaceful," "empty," "signless," "wishless," "unconditioned," and "secluded. He teaches that body-contact is "impermanent," "suffering," "selfless," "peaceful," "empty," and "signless."

He teaches by way of apprehension that [it] is wishless, that it is without volitional formation, and that it is secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that mental contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, without volitional formation, and secluded.

He teaches that what is felt conditioned by eye-contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. He teaches that what is felt conditioned by ear-contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that what is felt conditioned by olfactory contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that what is felt conditioned by gustatory contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that what is felt conditioned by bodily contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that what is felt conditioned by mental contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.
[He teaches that] the earth element is impermanent, suffering, non-self, and peaceful.

He teaches by way of apprehension that [the realm] is empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the water element is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the fire element is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that the wind element is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.
He teaches by way of apprehension that the space element is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the consciousness element is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that ignorance is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the formative forces (*saṃskāra*) are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that consciousness (*vijñāna*) is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that name-and-form is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the six sense-bases are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that contact is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that feeling is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that craving is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that grasping is impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that existence is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that birth is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.
He teaches aging and death as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self, as peaceful, as empty, as signless, as wishless, as unconditioned, and as secluded, by means of the approach of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the perfection of generosity is permanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that the perfection of ethical discipline is permanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches that the perfection of patience is permanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. He teaches that the perfection of vigor is permanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the perfection of meditation is permanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that the perfection of wisdom is permanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that internal emptiness is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that external emptiness is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that internal-external emptiness is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; and that the emptiness of emptiness is impermanent, suffering, and selfless.

He teaches by way of apprehension that [all things] are peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that great emptiness is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches ultimate emptiness as impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded, by means of the mode of apprehension. He teaches conditioned emptiness as impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded, by means of the mode of apprehension.

He teaches unconditioned emptiness as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self, as peaceful, as empty, as signless, as wishless, as without formative activity, and as secluded—by way of apprehension. He teaches absolute emptiness as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self, as peaceful, as empty, as signless, as wishless, as without formative activity, and as secluded—by way of apprehension.

He teaches that the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. He teaches that the emptiness of non-dispersal is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that intrinsic emptiness is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, and unconditioned; and that the emptiness of all phenomena is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, and unconditioned.

He teaches that "secluded" is by way of apprehension. He teaches that the emptiness of specific characteristics is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. He teaches that the emptiness of non-apprehension is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the emptiness of non-existence is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the emptiness of intrinsic nature is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. [He teaches] that the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is impermanent...
He teaches by way of apprehension that [phenomena] are suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches the applications of mindfulness as being impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded, by means of the mode of apprehension. He teaches the right efforts as being impermanent, suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded, by means of the mode of apprehension.

He teaches by means of the mode of apprehension that the bases of psychic power are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; likewise, he teaches that the faculties are impermanent.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the sufferings are selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that the powers are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the factors of enlightenment are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the noble eightfold path is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the noble truths are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; he teaches by way of apprehension that the meditative absorptions are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the immeasurables are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded; and that the formless attainments are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, and signless.

He teaches by way of apprehension that they are wishless, that they are without volitional effort, and that they are secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the liberations are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, without volitional effort, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the successive attainments of meditative dwelling (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*) are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the gateways to liberation (*vimokṣamukha*)—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches that the gateways of dhāraṇī are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. Likewise, he teaches that the powers of a Tathāgata are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded—by way of apprehension. He [teaches] that the grounds of self-confidence are impermanent...

He teaches by way of apprehension that [the aggregates] are suffering, are non-self, are peaceful, are empty, are signless, are wishless, are unconditioned, and are secluded. He teaches by way of apprehension that the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are impermanent, are suffering, are non-self, are peaceful, are empty, are signless, are wishless, are unconditioned, and are secluded.

He teaches great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) by means of the approach of apprehension (*upalambha-yoga*), saying it is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. He teaches great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) by means of the approach of apprehension, saying it is impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded.

He teaches by way of apprehension that the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and secluded. One who does not point out nor teach these uniform deeds of Māra should be known as a bad friend (pāpamitra) to a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Thus, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should recognize bad friends and, having recognized them, avoid them.
The sixth chapter of the Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā.

Now begins the seventh chapter. Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, when it is said 'bodhisattva mahāsattva,' what is the meaning of this term? When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti: "Subhūti, the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva' is a non-meaning. Why is that? Because awakening is non-arising, and a sentient being is non-arising."

For indeed, Subhūti, there is no footprint in awakening, nor in a sentient being; therefore, the meaning of the term "bodhisattva" is a non-meaning. Just as, Subhūti, the footprint of a bird in the sky is not found, even so the meaning of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Just as, for example, a footprint is not found in a dream, even so the meaning of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Just as, Subhūti, the footprint of an illusion is not found—

In the same way, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example, the track of a mirage does not exist, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example, the track of the moon in water does not exist, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, just as, for example, the track of an echo does not exist, even so the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a reflected image is found; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a reflection is found; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a Tathāgata’s emanation is found; even so, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found.
Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a magically created person who practices the noble eightfold path; even so, Subhūti, it is with the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

For one practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the referent of the term "illusory person" does not exist when practicing the noble truths; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the referent of the term "illusory person" does not exist when practicing the meditative concentrations; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the referent of the term "illusory person" does not exist when practicing the immeasurables.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no objective referent for a phantom person practicing the formless attainments; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no objective referent for a phantom person practicing the eight liberations; Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no footing for a phantom person practicing the nine successive meditative attainments.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no objective entity found in a phantom person who courses in the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no objective entity found in a phantom person who courses in the superknowledges. Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no objective entity found in a phantom person who courses in the meditative concentrations. Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, there is no objective entity found in a phantom person who courses in the gateways of the dhāraṇīs.
In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a magically created person practicing the powers of a Tathāgata; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a magically created person practicing the grounds of self-confidence; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a magically created person practicing the analytical knowledges; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a magically created person practicing great loving-kindness.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing great compassion; Subhūti, it is just as, for example, there is no real entity found in a phantom person practicing the unique qualities of a buddha. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, no real entity called a "bodhisattva" is found.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found in form; why is that? Because that form does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "Bodhisattva" cannot be found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found in feeling.

For what reason? Because that feeling does not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no referent exists within the designation of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—for what reason? Because that designation does not exist.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the conditioned formations (saṃskāra) of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha, why is that? Because those conditioned formations do not exist.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent-object of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no trace of a footprint exists in the consciousness of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—why is that? Because that consciousness is non-existent—in the very same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent-object of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint can be found in the eye of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha; and why? Because that eye does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "Bodhisattva" [does not exist].

It does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is found in the ear; why is that? Because that ear does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha could be found in the mind; why is that? Because that mind does not exist.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists in the form of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha—why is that? Because that form does not exist—just so, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found in sound; why is that? Because that sound does not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, no referent for the term "Bodhisattva" exists. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found in smell; why is that? Because that smell does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found in his touch; why is that? Because that touch does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" cannot be found.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found among phenomena; why is that? Because those phenomena do not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is found in visual consciousness. Why is that? Because that visual consciousness does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "Bodhisattva" is not found.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, no trace of a footprint exists in the auditory consciousness of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Why is that? Because that auditory consciousness does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, it is for a Bodhisattva...

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a "footprint" is found in the internal emptiness of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; why is that? Because that internal emptiness does not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, no referential object corresponding to the term "Bodhisattva" exists.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found in external emptiness. Why is that? Because that external emptiness does not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, it is for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

For one practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no referent exists for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha within the emptiness of the internal and external; why is that? Because that emptiness of the internal and external does not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found in the emptiness of emptiness; why is that? Because that emptiness of emptiness does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" is not found.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha can be found within great emptiness. Why is that? Because that great emptiness does not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" cannot be found.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found in ultimate emptiness. Why is that? Because that ultimate emptiness does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the emptiness of specific characteristics of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, so it is because [the bodhisattva] is non-existent.

Of that very emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), Subhūti, in the same way, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), the referent-object of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha, no footprint exists within the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*), why is that? Because that emptiness of non-apprehension is non-existent.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the emptiness of non-existence of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha, why is that? Because that emptiness of non-existence is itself non-existent.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the emptiness of intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, why is that? Because that emptiness of intrinsic nature is non-existent.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent-object of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha—for what reason? Because that emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is itself non-existent.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found in the foundations of mindfulness; why is that? Because those foundations of mindfulness do not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "Bodhisattva" is not found.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is found in the right efforts; why is that? Because those right efforts do not exist. In the very same way...

Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint exists in the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; why is that? Because those bases of psychic power do not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha could be found among the sense faculties; why is that? Because those sense faculties do not exist.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the powers of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha—because those powers are non-existent—in the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is found among the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga). Why is that? Because those factors of enlightenment do not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), the referent-object of the term "Bodhisattva" is not found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is found on the path.

For what reason? Because that path does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent-object "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no trace of a Tathāgata, Arhat, or Samyaksaṃbuddha is found within the noble truths—for what reason? Because those noble truths do not exist—in the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent-object "bodhisattva" [does not exist].

It does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found within the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*). Why is that? Because those meditative absorptions do not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), the referent-object of the term "Bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found within the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*).

For what reason? Because those immeasurables do not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha in the formless attainments, for what reason? Because those formless attainments do not exist.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists within the liberations of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—for what reason? Because those liberations do not exist—just so, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found in the successive meditative attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*); why is that? Because those successive meditative attainments do not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), the referent-object of the term "Bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is found within the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is that? Because those liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness do not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "Bodhisattva" [is not found].

It does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a "Tathāgata, Arhat, perfectly enlightened Buddha" is found within the superknowledges (*abhijñā*); why is that? Because those superknowledges do not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), the referent-object of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no trace of a "Tathāgata, Arhat, perfectly enlightened Buddha" is found within the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*).

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no referent exists for the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, in respect to the four grounds of self-confidence, why is that? Because those grounds of self-confidence do not exist.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, for a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, no referent exists for the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), why is that? Because those analytical knowledges do not exist.
In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" [does not exist].

It does not exist. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no "footprint" of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha exists within his great compassion; why is that? Because that great compassion is non-existent. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent-object of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, no footprint can be found among the unique qualities of a Buddha belonging to a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha; why is that? Because those unique qualities of a Buddha do not exist. In the very same way, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "Bodhisattva" does not exist.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, in the unconditioned realm (asaṃskṛtadhātu), no term for the conditioned realm (saṃskṛtadhātu) is found; and in the conditioned realm, no term for the unconditioned realm is found. In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), no referent for the term "bodhisattva" is found. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, in non-arising (anutpāda), no term is found.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no trace exists in the absence of cessation, even so, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no trace exists in the absence of affliction and designation, even so it is.

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists in that which is unconditioned (*anabhisaṃskāra*), even so, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists in that which is non-manifestation (*aprādurbhāva*), [so it is here].

In the same way, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist. Just as, Subhūti, no footprint exists in that which is unapprehendable, even so, Subhūti, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom, the referent of the term "bodhisattva" does not exist.

He asked: "Blessed One, in the non-arising of what is no track found? In the non-ceasing of what is no track found? In the absence of defilement and purification of what is no track found? In the non-manifestation of what is no track found? In the lack of volitional formation of what is no track found? In the non-apprehension of what is no track found? The Blessed One replied: "Subhūti, in the non-arising of form, no track is found. In the non-ceasing of form, no track is found."

In the non-affliction and non-purification of form, no footing is found; in the non-conditioning of form, no footing is found; in the non-manifestation of form, no footing is found; in the non-apprehension of form, no footing is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of feeling, no footing is found; in the non-ceasing of feeling, no footing is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of feeling, no footing is found; in the non-conditioning of feeling, no footing is found.

In the non-appearance of feeling, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of feeling, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of perception, no track is found; in the non-cessation of perception, no track is found; in the absence of affliction and purification in perception, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation in perception, no track is found; in the non-appearance of perception, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of perception, no track is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), no track is found; in the non-ceasing of conditioned phenomena, no track is found; in the absence of affliction and purification of conditioned phenomena, no track is found; in the lack of volitional construction of conditioned phenomena, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of conditioned phenomena, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of conditioned phenomena, no track is found. [The same applies to] consciousness (*vijñāna*).

Subhūti, in non-arising there is no track; in the non-ceasing of consciousness there is no track; in the non-defilement and non-purification of consciousness there is no track; in the non-conditioning of consciousness there is no track; in the non-manifestation of consciousness there is no track; in the non-apprehension of consciousness there is no track.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of the eye, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of the eye, no track is found; in the absence of affliction and purification of the eye, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation of the eye, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of the eye, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of the eye, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of the ear, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of the ear, no track is found.

There is no footing for the ear in its lack of affliction and lack of purification; there is no footing for the ear in its lack of volitional formation; there is no footing for the ear in its non-appearance; there is no footing for the ear in its non-apprehension. Subhūti, there is no footing for the nose in its non-arising; there is no footing for the nose in its non-cessation; there is no footing for the nose in its lack of affliction and lack of purification; there is no footing for the nose in its lack of volitional formation.

In the non-manifestation of the nose, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of the nose, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of the tongue, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of the tongue, no track is found; in the absence of affliction or purification of the tongue, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation of the tongue, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of the tongue, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of the tongue, no track is found.

Subhūti, regarding the body, no track is found in its non-arising; no track is found in its non-cessation; no track is found in its lack of affliction or purification; no track is found in its lack of volitional formation; no track is found in its non-manifestation; no track is found in its non-apprehension. This is also the case for the mind.

Subhūti, in non-arising there is no track; in the non-ceasing of the mind there is no track; in the absence of affliction and purification of the mind there is no track; in the absence of volitional formation of the mind there is no track; in the absence of manifestation of the mind there is no track; in the non-apprehension of the mind there is no track.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of form, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of form, no track is found; in the non-defilement and non-purification of form, no track is found; in the non-conditioning of form, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of form, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of form, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of sound, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of sound, no track is found.

In sound, there is no foothold for non-affliction or purification; in sound, there is no foothold for lack of volitional formation; in sound, there is no foothold for non-manifestation; in sound, there is no foothold for non-apprehension. Subhūti, in the non-arising of odor, there is no foothold; in the non-ceasing of odor, there is no foothold; in the non-affliction and non-purification of odor, there is no foothold; in the lack of volitional formation of odor, there is no foothold.

In the non-appearance of odor, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of odor, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of taste, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of taste, no track is found; in the absence of affliction or purification of taste, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation of taste, no track is found; in the non-appearance of taste, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of taste, no track is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of contact, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of contact, no track is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of contact, no track is found; in the non-conditioning of contact, no track is found; in the non-appearance of contact, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of contact, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of phenomena (*dharmas*), no track is found.

There is no footing for phenomena in their non-ceasing; there is no footing for phenomena in their lack of affliction or purification; there is no footing for phenomena in their lack of volitional formation; there is no footing for phenomena in their non-manifestation; there is no footing for phenomena in their non-apprehension.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of eye-consciousness, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of eye-consciousness, no track is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of eye-consciousness, no track is found; in the non-conditioning of eye-consciousness, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of eye-consciousness, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of eye-consciousness, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of gustatory consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-cessation of gustatory consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of gustatory consciousness, no footing is found.

In the non-conditioning of tongue-consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-manifestation of tongue-consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-apprehension of tongue-consciousness, no footing is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of body-consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-ceasing of body-consciousness...

No footing is found. In the non-affliction and non-purification of body-consciousness, no footing is found. In the non-conditioning of body-consciousness, no footing is found. In the non-manifestation of body-consciousness, no footing is found. In the non-apprehension of body-consciousness, no footing is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of mind-consciousness, no footing is found. In the non-ceasing of mind-consciousness, no footing is found. In the non-affliction and non-purification of mind-consciousness, no footing is found.

In the non-conditioning of mental consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-manifestation of mental consciousness, no footing is found; in the non-apprehension of mental consciousness, no footing is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of eye-contact, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of eye-contact, no track is found; in the absence of defilement and purification of eye-contact, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation of eye-contact, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of eye-contact, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of eye-contact, no track is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of olfactory contact, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of olfactory contact, no track is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of olfactory contact, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation of olfactory contact, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of olfactory contact, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of olfactory contact, no track is found.

No track is found. It does not exist. When contact does not manifest, a track is not found; when contact is not apprehended, a track is not found. Subhūti, when feeling is unarisen, a track is not found; when feeling is unceasing, a track is not found; when feeling is neither defiled nor purified, a track is not found; when feeling is unconditioned, a track is not found; when feeling does not manifest, a track is not found; when feeling is not apprehended, a track is not found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of grasping, no track is found; in the non-cessation of grasping, no track is found.

In the absence of affliction and purification of grasping (*upādāna*), no footing is found. In the absence of volitional construction (*anabhisaṃskāra*) of grasping, no footing is found. In the absence of manifestation of grasping, no footing is found. In the absence of apprehension of grasping, no footing is found. In the absence of affliction and purification of becoming, no footing is found. In the absence of volitional construction of becoming, no footing is found.

When existence does not manifest, no track is found; when existence is not apprehended, no track is found. Subhūti, when there is the non-arising of birth, no track is found; when there is the non-cessation of birth, no track is found; when there is neither affliction nor purification of birth, no track is found; when there is the lack of volitional formation of birth, no track is found; when there is the non-manifestation of birth, no track is found; when birth is not apprehended, no track is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of aging and death, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of aging and death, no track is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of aging and death, no track is found; in the non-conditioning of aging and death, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of aging and death, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of aging and death, no track is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of the perfection of generosity, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of the perfection of generosity, no track is found; in the non-affliction and non-purification of the perfection of generosity, no track is found; in the non-conditioning of the perfection of generosity, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of the perfection of generosity, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of the perfection of generosity, no track is found. In the non-cessation of the perfection of ethical discipline, no track is found; in the absence of affliction and purification in the perfection of ethical discipline, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation in the perfection of ethical discipline, no track is found; in the non-appearance of the perfection of ethical discipline, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of the perfection of ethical discipline, no track is found. In the perfection of patience, no trace is found of defilement or purification; in the perfection of patience, no trace is found of volitional formation; in the perfection of patience, no trace is found of manifestation; in the perfection of patience, no trace is found of non-apprehension. Subhūti, in the perfection of vigor, no trace is found of arising; in the perfection of vigor, no trace is found of cessation.

In the perfection of vigor, no trace is found of defilement or purification; in the perfection of vigor, no trace is found of volitional formation; in the perfection of vigor, no trace is found of manifestation; in the perfection of vigor, no trace is found of non-apprehension. Subhūti, in the perfection of meditation, no trace is found of non-arising; in the perfection of meditation—

In non-cessation, no track is found; in the absence of affliction and purification, no track of the perfection of meditation is found; in the absence of volitional formation, no track of the perfection of meditation is found; in the absence of manifestation, no track of the perfection of meditation is found; in the absence of apprehension, no track of the perfection of meditation is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of the perfection of wisdom, no track is found; in the non-cessation of the perfection of wisdom, no track is found.

In the perfection of wisdom, no trace of affliction or purification is found; in the perfection of wisdom, no trace of volitional formation is found; in the perfection of wisdom, no trace of manifestation is found; in the perfection of wisdom, no trace of apprehension is found.

Subhūti, in the non-arising of internal emptiness, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of internal emptiness, no track is found; in the absence of defilement or purification in internal emptiness, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation in internal emptiness, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of internal emptiness, no track is found; in the non-apprehension of internal emptiness, no track is found.

In the absence of manifestation, no footing exists. In the non-apprehension of internal and external emptiness, no footing exists. In the absence of affliction and purification in the emptiness of emptiness, no footing exists. In the lack of volitional formation in the emptiness of emptiness, no footing exists. In the absence of manifestation in the emptiness of emptiness, no footing exists.

In the non-apprehension of the emptiness of emptiness, no track is found. Subhūti, in the non-arising of great emptiness, no track is found; in the non-ceasing of great emptiness, no track is found; in the absence of affliction and purification in great emptiness, no track is found; in the lack of volitional formation in great emptiness, no track is found; in the non-manifestation of great emptiness, no track is found; and in the non-apprehension of great emptiness, no track is found.
