Because, O Blessed One, form is empty of form; feeling is empty of feeling; perception is empty of perception; mental formations are empty of mental formations; consciousness is empty of consciousness; and the eye is empty of the eye."

The ear is empty of the ear; the nose is empty of the nose; the tongue is empty of the tongue; the body is empty of the body; the mind is empty of the mind. Form is empty of form; sound is empty of sound; odor is empty of odor; taste is empty of taste; tangibility is empty of tangibility; mental phenomena are empty of mental phenomena. Eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness; ear-consciousness is empty of ear-consciousness.

Olfactory consciousness is empty of olfactory consciousness; gustatory consciousness is empty of gustatory consciousness; tactile consciousness is empty of tactile consciousness; mental consciousness is empty of mental consciousness. Visual contact is empty of visual contact; auditory contact is empty of auditory contact; olfactory contact is empty of olfactory contact; gustatory contact is empty of gustatory contact.

Body-contact is empty of body-contact; mind-contact is empty of mind-contact. Feeling conditioned by eye-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by eye-contact; feeling conditioned by ear-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by ear-contact; feeling conditioned by nose-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by nose-contact.
Feeling conditioned by bodily contact is empty of feeling conditioned by bodily contact; feeling conditioned by mental contact is empty of feeling conditioned by mental contact.

The earth element is empty of the earth element; the water element is empty of the water element; the fire element is empty of the fire element; the wind element is empty of the wind element; the space element is empty of the space element; the consciousness element is empty of the consciousness element. Ignorance is empty of ignorance; the formative forces are empty of the formative forces; consciousness is empty of consciousness; name-and-form is empty of name-and-form.

The six sense bases are empty of the six sense bases; contact is empty of contact; feeling is empty of feeling; craving is empty of craving; grasping is empty of grasping; becoming is empty of becoming; birth is empty of birth; and old age and death are empty of old age and death.

The perfection of generosity is empty of the perfection of generosity; the perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline; the perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience; the perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor; the perfection of meditative concentration is empty of the perfection of meditative concentration; the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom.

Internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness; external emptiness is empty of external emptiness; internal-external emptiness is empty of internal-external emptiness; the emptiness of emptiness is empty of the emptiness of emptiness; great emptiness is empty of great emptiness; ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness; conditioned emptiness is empty of conditioned emptiness.

Unconditioned emptiness is empty of unconditioned emptiness; ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness; emptiness without beginning or end is empty of emptiness without beginning or end; non-dispersal emptiness is empty of non-dispersal emptiness; essential nature emptiness is empty of essential nature emptiness; the emptiness of all phenomena is empty of the emptiness of all phenomena; the emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of the emptiness of specific characteristics;
the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of the emptiness of non-apprehension; the emptiness of non-existence is [empty] of the emptiness of non-existence.

It is empty; intrinsic nature-emptiness is empty of intrinsic nature-emptiness; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

The foundations of mindfulness are empty of the foundations of mindfulness; the right efforts are empty of the right efforts; the bases of psychic power are empty of the bases of psychic power; the faculties are empty of the faculties; the powers are empty of the powers; the factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment; the noble eightfold path is empty of the noble eightfold path; the noble truths are empty of the noble truths; the meditative absorptions are empty of the meditative absorptions; the immeasurables are empty of the immeasurables.

The formless attainments are empty of formless attainments; the liberations are empty of liberations; the serial meditative attainments are empty of serial meditative attainments; the gateways to liberation through emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness are empty of the gateways to liberation through emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the superknowledges are empty of superknowledges; the concentrations are empty of concentrations; and the gateways of dhāraṇī are empty of gateways of dhāraṇī.

The powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the powers of a Tathāgata; the grounds of self-confidence are empty of the grounds of self-confidence; the analytical knowledges are empty of the analytical knowledges; great loving-kindness is empty of great loving-kindness; great compassion is empty of great compassion; the unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha; the bodhisattva is empty of the bodhisattva; and the great armor is empty of the great armor.

"In this manner, Blessed One, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should be known as one who is girded with the armor. The Blessed One said: "It is just so, Subhūti; it is just as you say. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) is uncreated, unmodified, and unconditioned—[it is for the sake of this] that the bodhisattva mahāsattva has girded himself with the great armor.
[Subhūti] asked: "For what reason, Blessed One, is omniscience uncreated, unmodified, and unconditioned?"

"For the sake of whom the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has donned the great armor. The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, based on the non-apprehension of an agent, all-aspect-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) is uncreated, unaltered, and unconditioned. Those beings for whose sake the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has donned the great armor are also uncreated, unaltered, and unconditioned. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, form (*rūpa*) neither acts nor alters."

It does not construct; feeling does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; perception does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; mental formations do not act, do not transform, and do not construct; consciousness does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Subhūti, the eye does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; the ear does not act, does not transform, and does not construct.

Tongue-consciousness does not...

Tongue-contact does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; body-contact does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; mind-contact does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. “Subhūti, the self does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, contact does not act, does not transform, and does not construct.

For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, feeling does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, craving does not transform and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely [non-apprehensible].

It is not apprehended. Subhūti, grasping does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely not apprehended. Subhūti, becoming does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely not apprehended. Subhūti, birth does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely not apprehended.
Subhūti, old age and death do not act, do not transform, and do not construct; why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible.

The perfection of generosity does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is ultimately non-apprehendable. The perfection of ethical discipline does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is ultimately non-apprehendable. The perfection of patience does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is ultimately non-apprehendable.

The perfection of vigor does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. The perfection of meditation does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. The perfection of wisdom does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, internal emptiness does not act, does not transform, and does not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. External emptiness does not act, does not transform, and does not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Internal-external emptiness does not act, does not transform, and does not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible.

The emptiness of emptiness does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. The great emptiness does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. The emptiness of the ultimate truth does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible.

The emptiness of the conditioned does not act, does not transform, and does not bring about formative activity. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. The emptiness of the unconditioned does not act, does not transform, and does not bring about formative activity. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the absolute emptiness does not act, does not transform, and does not bring about formative activity. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the emptiness of non-dispersal does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the emptiness of intrinsic nature does not act, does not transform, and does not construct.
For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the emptiness of all phenomena neither acts nor transforms.

It does not construct [anything]. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the emptiness of self-characteristic does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the emptiness of non-apprehension does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, the emptiness of non-existence does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely unapprehendable. Subhūti, the emptiness of intrinsic nature does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely unapprehendable. Subhūti, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely unapprehendable.

Subhūti, the applications of mindfulness do not act, do not transform, and do not perform volitional formations. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, the right efforts do not act, do not transform, and do not perform volitional formations. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, the bases of psychic power do not act, do not transform, and do not perform volitional formations.

For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the faculties do not act, do not transform, and do not perform formative activity. For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the powers do not act, do not transform, and do not perform formative activity. For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible.

The factors of enlightenment do not act, do not transform, and do not perform conditioned formations. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, as for the noble eightfold path—

It does not act, it does not transform, and it does not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because it does not exist at all. Subhūti, the noble truths do not act, they do not transform, and they do not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because they are not apprehended at all. Subhūti, the meditative absorptions do not act, they do not transform, and they do not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because they are not apprehended at all.

Subhūti, the immeasurables do not act, they do not transform, and they do not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the formless attainments do not act, they do not transform, and they do not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the liberations do not act, they do not transform, and they do not perform formative activity.

For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the attainments of the successive dwellings do not act, do not transform, and do not perform formative activity. For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—do not act, do not transform, and do not perform formative activity. For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, the superknowledges do not act, do not transform, and do not perform conditioned activities. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, all meditative concentrations do not act, do not transform, and do not perform conditioned activities. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehendable. All doors of dhāraṇīs do not act, do not transform, and do not perform conditioned activities.

For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the powers of a Tathāgata do not act, do not transform, and do not perform conditioned formations. For what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, the grounds of self-confidence do not act, do not transform, and do not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, the analytical knowledges do not act, do not transform, and do not perform formative activity. Why is that? Because they are absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, great loving-kindness does not act, does not transform, and does not perform formative activity.

For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, great compassion does not act, does not transform, and does not construct; for what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the unique qualities of a Buddha do not act, do not transform, and do not construct; for what reason? Because they are absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, suchness does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, non-falsity does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, non-otherness does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible.

Subhūti, the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, the stability of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehendable.

Subhūti, the fixed nature of phenomena (dharmmaniyāmatā) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. Why is that? Because it is absolutely non-apprehendable. Subhūti, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct.

For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, the inconceivable realm does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, awakening (*bodhi*) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct.

For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Subhūti, omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) does not act, does not transform, and does not construct. For what reason? Because it is absolutely non-apprehensible. Therefore, Subhūti, by this method it should be understood that omniscience is uncreated, untransformed, and unconstructed; those sentient beings as well are uncreated, untransformed, and unconstructed.

"For the sake of whom the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has donned the great armor—Subhūti, it is for this reason that a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is said to be 'one who has donned the great armor. Subhūti said: "As I understand the meaning of what has been taught by the Blessed One, O Blessed One, form (*rūpa*) is neither bound nor liberated; feeling (*vedanā*) is neither bound nor liberated; perception (*saṃjñā*) is neither bound nor liberated; mental formations (*saṃskāra*) are neither bound nor liberated; and consciousness (*vijñāna*) is neither bound nor liberated."

Then the Venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra said this to the Venerable Subhūti: "Venerable Subhūti, form is neither bound nor liberated; feeling is neither bound nor liberated; perception is neither bound nor liberated; mental formations are neither bound nor liberated; consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. He replied: "It is so, Venerable Pūrṇa, it is so. Form, Venerable Pūrṇa, is neither bound nor liberated; feeling is neither bound nor liberated; perception is neither bound nor liberated; mental formations are neither bound nor liberated; consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Pūrṇa said:

"Venerable Subhūti, what is that which is neither bound nor liberated? What is that feeling which is neither bound nor liberated? What is that perception which is neither bound nor liberated? What are those formations which are neither bound nor liberated? What is that consciousness which is neither bound nor liberated? He replied: "Venerable Pūrṇa, that form which is like a dream is neither bound nor liberated. That feeling which is like a dream is neither bound nor liberated. That perception which is like a dream is neither bound nor liberated."

These conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) which are like a dream are neither bound nor liberated. This consciousness (*vijñāna*) which is like a dream is neither bound nor liberated. This form (*rūpa*) which is like an illusion (*māyā*) is neither bound nor liberated. This feeling (*vedanā*) which is like an illusion is neither bound nor liberated. This perception (*saṃjñā*) which is like an illusion is neither bound nor liberated. These formations (*saṃskāra*) which are like an illusion are neither bound nor liberated. This consciousness (*vijñāna*) which is like an illusion is neither bound nor liberated.

This form, which is like an echo, is neither bound nor liberated. This feeling, which is like an echo, is neither bound nor liberated. This perception, which is like an echo, is neither bound nor liberated. These formations, which are like echoes, are neither bound nor liberated. This consciousness, which is like an echo, is neither bound nor liberated. This form, which is like a reflection, is neither bound nor liberated.

This feeling which is like a reflection is neither bound nor liberated; this perception which is like a reflection is neither bound nor liberated; these formations which are like reflections are unbound and unliberated; this consciousness which is like a reflection is unbound and unliberated; this form which is like a reflected image is unbound and unliberated; this feeling which is like a reflected image is neither bound nor liberated; this perception which is like a reflected image is neither bound nor liberated.

These conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), which are like reflections, are neither bound nor liberated. This consciousness (*vijñāna*), which is like a reflection, is neither bound nor liberated. This form (*rūpa*), which is like a mirage, is neither bound nor liberated. This feeling (*vedanā*), which is like a mirage, is neither bound nor liberated. This...

Perception, which is like a mirage, is neither bound nor liberated. These conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), which are like a mirage, are unbound and unliberated. This consciousness (*vijñāna*), which is like a mirage, is unbound and unliberated. This form (*rūpa*), which is like a magical creation (*nirmita*), is unbound and unliberated. This feeling (*vedanā*), which is like a magical creation, is neither bound nor liberated. This perception (*saṃjñā*), which is like a magical creation, is neither bound nor liberated. These conditioned phenomena, which are like magical creations, are unbound and unliberated. This consciousness, which is like a magical creation, is unbound and unliberated.

"Venerable Pūrṇa, past form is unbound and unliberated; past feeling is unbound and unliberated; past perception is unbound and unliberated; past formations are unbound and unliberated; past consciousness is unbound and unliberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, present form is unbound and unliberated; present feeling is unbound and unliberated; present perception is unbound and unliberated; present formations are unbound and unliberated."

Present consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Why is that? Because, Venerable Pūrṇa, due to its non-existence, form is neither bound nor liberated; due to the non-existence of feeling, feeling is neither bound nor liberated; due to the non-existence of perception, perception is neither bound nor liberated; due to the non-existence of volitional formations, volitional formations are neither bound nor liberated; due to the non-existence of consciousness, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Furthermore, due to the solitude of form, form is neither bound nor liberated.

Because perception is secluded, perception is neither bound nor liberated. Because mental formations are secluded, mental formations are neither bound nor liberated. Because consciousness is secluded, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Because form is unarisen, form is neither bound nor liberated. Because feeling is unarisen, feeling is neither bound nor liberated. Because perception is unarisen, perception is neither bound nor liberated. Because mental formations are unarisen, mental formations are neither bound nor liberated.
Because consciousness is unarisen, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.

“Venerable Pūrṇa, wholesome form is neither bound nor liberated; wholesome feeling is neither bound nor liberated; wholesome perception is neither bound nor liberated; wholesome formations are neither bound nor liberated; wholesome consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, unwholesome form is neither bound nor liberated; unwholesome feeling is neither bound nor liberated; unwholesome perception is neither bound nor liberated; unwholesome formations are neither bound nor liberated; unwholesome consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, indeterminate form is neither bound nor liberated.”

Indeterminate feeling is neither bound nor liberated; indeterminate perception is neither bound nor liberated; indeterminate formations are neither bound nor liberated; indeterminate consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, mundane form is neither bound nor liberated; mundane feeling is neither bound nor liberated; mundane perception is neither bound nor liberated; mundane formations are neither bound nor liberated; mundane consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.

Venerable Pūrṇa, supramundane form is neither bound nor liberated; supramundane feeling is neither bound nor liberated; supramundane perception is neither bound nor liberated; supramundane formations are neither bound nor liberated; supramundane consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, contaminated form is neither bound nor liberated; contaminated feeling is neither bound nor liberated; contaminated perception is neither bound nor liberated; contaminated formations are neither bound nor liberated.

Contaminated consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, uncontaminated form is neither bound nor liberated; uncontaminated feeling is neither bound nor liberated; uncontaminated perception is neither bound nor liberated; uncontaminated volitional formations are neither bound nor liberated; uncontaminated consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Why is that? Because form does not exist, form is neither bound nor liberated; because feeling does not exist, feeling is neither bound nor liberated.

Because perception does not exist, perception is neither bound nor liberated. Because mental formations do not exist, mental formations are neither bound nor liberated. Because consciousness does not exist, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Because form is secluded, form is neither bound nor liberated. Because feeling is secluded, feeling is neither bound nor liberated. Because perception is secluded...

Perception is neither bound nor liberated. Because conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are secluded, conditioned phenomena are neither bound nor liberated. Because consciousness (*vijñāna*) is secluded, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Because form (*rūpa*) is unarisen, form is neither bound nor liberated. Because feeling (*vedanā*) is unarisen, feeling is neither bound nor liberated. Because perception (*saṃjñā*) is unarisen, perception is neither bound nor liberated. Because conditioned phenomena are unarisen, conditioned phenomena are neither bound nor liberated. Because consciousness is unarisen, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated.

"Venerable Pūrṇa, all phenomena (*dharmas*) are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are non-existent, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, they are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, even the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) is neither bound nor liberated; the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) is neither bound nor liberated; the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) is neither bound nor liberated; the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*) is neither bound nor liberated; the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*) is neither bound nor liberated; and the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is neither bound nor liberated."

Because of non-existence, the perfection of generosity is neither bound nor liberated; because of solitude, the perfection of generosity is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, the perfection of generosity is neither bound nor liberated. Because of non-existence, the perfection of ethical discipline is neither bound nor liberated; because of solitude, the perfection of ethical discipline is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, the perfection of ethical discipline is neither bound nor liberated. Because of non-existence, the perfection of patience is neither bound nor liberated; because of solitude, the perfection of patience is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, the perfection of patience is neither bound nor liberated.

Because of its non-existence, the perfection of vigor is neither bound nor liberated; because of its solitude, the perfection of vigor is neither bound nor liberated; because of its non-arising, the perfection of vigor is neither bound nor liberated. Because of its non-existence, the perfection of meditation is neither bound nor liberated; because of its solitude, the perfection of meditation is neither bound nor liberated; because of its non-arising, the perfection of meditation is neither bound nor liberated. Because of its non-existence, the perfection of wisdom is neither bound nor liberated;
because of its solitude, the perfection of wisdom is neither bound nor liberated; because of its non-arising, the perfection of wisdom is neither bound nor liberated.

Internal emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; internal-and-external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; the emptiness of emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; great emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; ultimate emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; conditioned emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; unconditioned emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; absolute emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; and the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is neither bound nor liberated.

Non-dispersal emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; intrinsic nature emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; the emptiness of all phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; the emptiness of specific characteristics is neither bound nor liberated; the emptiness of non-apprehension is neither bound nor liberated; the emptiness of non-existence is neither bound nor liberated; the emptiness of self-nature is neither bound nor liberated; and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence is neither bound nor liberated.

Because of non-existence, internal emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because of seclusion, internal emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, internal emptiness is neither bound nor liberated. Because of non-existence, external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because of seclusion, external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated. Because of non-existence, internal-and-external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because of seclusion, internal-and-external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are unarisen, internal and external emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because they are non-existent, the emptiness of emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the emptiness of emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the emptiness of emptiness is neither bound nor liberated. Because they are non-existent, great emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, great emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, great emptiness is neither bound nor liberated. Because they are non-existent, the emptiness of the ultimate is neither bound nor liberated.

Because it is secluded, ultimate emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, ultimate emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is non-existent, conditioned emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, conditioned emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, conditioned emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is non-existent, unconditioned emptiness is neither bound nor liberated.

Because it is secluded, the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, the emptiness of the unconditioned is neither bound nor liberated; because it is non-existent, absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, absolute emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, absolute emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is non-existent, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is neither bound nor liberated.

Because of non-existence, the emptiness of non-dispersal is neither bound nor liberated; because of solitude, the emptiness of non-dispersal is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, the emptiness of non-dispersal is neither bound nor liberated. Because of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither bound nor liberated; because of solitude, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither bound nor liberated; because of non-arising, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither bound nor liberated. Because of non-existence, the emptiness of all phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; because of solitude, the emptiness of all phenomena is neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are unarisen, all phenomena are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of all phenomena. Because they do not exist, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of self-characteristics. Because they are secluded, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of self-characteristics. Because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of self-characteristics. Because they do not exist, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-apprehension. Because they are secluded, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-apprehension. Because they are unarisen, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-apprehension. Because they do not exist, they are neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-existence.

Because it is secluded, non-existence emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, non-existence emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is non-existent, intrinsic nature emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, intrinsic nature emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, intrinsic nature emptiness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is non-existent, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither bound nor liberated.

"Venerable Pūrṇa, the foundations of mindfulness are unbound and unliberated; the right efforts, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the bases of psychic power, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the faculties, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the powers, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the factors of enlightenment, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; and the noble eightfold path, venerable Pūrṇa, is also unbound and unliberated."

Because they do not exist, the foundations of mindfulness are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the foundations of mindfulness are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the foundations of mindfulness are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, the right efforts are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the right efforts are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the right efforts are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, the bases of psychic power are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are secluded, the bases of psychic power are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the bases of psychic power are neither bound nor liberated; because they are non-existent, the faculties are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the faculties are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the faculties are neither bound nor liberated; because they are non-existent, the powers are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the powers are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the powers are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they do not exist, the factors of enlightenment are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the factors of enlightenment are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the factors of enlightenment are neither bound nor liberated. Because it does not exist, the noble eightfold path is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, the noble eightfold path is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, the noble eightfold path is neither bound nor liberated.

Venerable Pūrṇa, the noble truths, too, are unbound and unliberated; the meditative absorptions, Venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the immeasurables, Venerable Pūrṇa, are unbound and unliberated; the formless attainments, Venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the liberations, Venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the successive dwellings in attainment, Venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, Venerable Pūrṇa—[are likewise].

They are unbound and unliberated, Pūrṇa. Even the superknowledges, venerable Pūrṇa, are unbound and unliberated. All meditative absorptions, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated. All doors of dhāraṇīs, venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated.

For what reason? Venerable Pūrṇa, because they do not exist, the noble truths are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the noble truths are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the noble truths are neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, because they do not exist, the meditative absorptions are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the meditative absorptions are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the meditative absorptions are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the immeasurables are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the immeasurables are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the immeasurables are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the formless attainments are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the formless attainments are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the formless attainments are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the liberations are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are secluded, the liberations are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the liberations are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, O Venerable Pūrṇa, the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are secluded, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are unarisen, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the superknowledges are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are secluded, the superknowledges are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are unarisen, the superknowledges are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the meditative concentrations are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are secluded, the meditative concentrations are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are unarisen, the meditative concentrations are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are secluded, the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are neither bound nor liberated. Because they are unarisen, the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are neither bound nor liberated.

Venerable Pūrṇa, even the powers of a Tathāgata are unbound and unliberated; the grounds of self-confidence, Venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; the analytical knowledges, Venerable Pūrṇa, are also unbound and unliberated; great loving-kindness, Venerable Pūrṇa, is unbound and unliberated; great compassion, Venerable Pūrṇa, is also unbound and unliberated; and even the unique qualities of a Buddha, Venerable Pūrṇa, are unbound and unliberated. For what reason?

Because they do not exist, Venerable Pūrṇa, the powers of a Tathāgata are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the powers of a Tathāgata are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the powers of a Tathāgata are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, the grounds of self-confidence are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the grounds of self-confidence are neither bound nor liberated; because they do not exist, the grounds of self-confidence are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, the analytical knowledges are neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are secluded, the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the analytical knowledges are neither bound nor liberated. Because it is non-existent, great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, great loving-kindness is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, great loving-kindness is neither bound nor liberated. Because it is non-existent, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is neither bound nor liberated; because it is secluded, great compassion is neither bound nor liberated; because it is unarisen, great compassion is neither bound nor liberated.

Because they are non-existent, the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are neither bound nor liberated; because they are secluded, the unique qualities of a Buddha are neither bound nor liberated; because they are unarisen, the unique qualities of a Buddha are neither bound nor liberated. Furthermore, Venerable Pūrṇa, omniscience (sarvajñatā) is neither bound nor liberated; the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is neither bound nor liberated; and the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is also neither bound nor liberated.

Based on non-existence, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; based on solitude, omniscience is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, omniscience is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; based on solitude, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the knowledge of the aspects of the path is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is neither bound nor liberated.

Based on its seclusion, all-aspect omniscience is neither bound nor liberated; based on its non-arising, all-aspect omniscience is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, the bodhisattva also is neither bound nor liberated; the Buddha also is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, the bodhisattva is neither bound nor liberated; based on seclusion, the bodhisattva is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the bodhisattva is neither bound nor liberated.

Based on non-existence, the Buddha is neither bound nor liberated; based on solitude, the Buddha is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the Buddha is neither bound nor liberated. Furthermore, O Venerable Pūrṇa, suchness is neither bound nor liberated; non-falsity is neither bound nor liberated; non-otherness is neither bound nor liberated; the nature of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; the realm of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; and the fixed order of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated.

The limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is also neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, suchness (*tathatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; based on seclusion, suchness is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, suchness is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, non-falsity (*avitathatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; based on seclusion, non-falsity is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, non-falsity is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, non-other-suchness (*ananyatathatā*) is neither bound nor liberated.

Based on its solitude, suchness is neither bound nor liberated; based on its non-arising, suchness is neither bound nor liberated; based on its non-existence, the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is neither bound nor liberated; based on its solitude, the nature of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; based on its non-arising, the nature of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated.

Based on non-existence, the dharma-realm is neither bound nor liberated; based on solitude, the dharma-realm is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the dharma-realm is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, the stability of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; based on solitude, the stability of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the stability of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated. Based on non-existence, the fixed order of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated.

Based on seclusion, the fixed nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the fixed nature of phenomena is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-existence, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is neither bound nor liberated; based on seclusion, the limit of reality is neither bound nor liberated; based on non-arising, the limit of reality is neither bound nor liberated. Furthermore, O Venerable Pūrṇa, the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) is also neither bound nor liberated; based on non-existence, the unconditioned is neither bound nor liberated.

Based on its seclusion, the unconditioned is neither bound nor liberated; based on its non-arising, the unconditioned is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Pūrṇa, this is the gate of the dharma of names for bodhisattva mahāsattvas: neither bound nor liberated.

That which is bound to and released from the perfection of generosity; bound to and released from the perfection of ethical discipline; bound to and released from the perfection of patience; bound to and released from the perfection of diligence; bound to and released from the perfection of meditative concentration; bound to and released from the perfection of wisdom; bound to and released from internal emptiness; bound to and released from external emptiness; bound to and released from internal and external emptiness; bound to and released from the emptiness of emptiness; bound to and released from great emptiness; bound to and released from the emptiness of the ultimate.

It is neither bound nor liberated by conditioned emptiness; neither bound nor liberated by unconditioned emptiness; neither bound nor liberated by absolute emptiness; neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-dispersal; neither bound nor liberated by natural emptiness; neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of all phenomena; neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of specific characteristics;

neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-apprehension; neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of non-existence; neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of intrinsic nature; and neither bound nor liberated by the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

The applications of mindfulness are neither bound nor liberated; the right efforts are neither bound nor liberated; the bases of psychic power are neither bound nor liberated; the faculties are neither bound nor liberated; the powers are neither bound nor liberated; the factors of enlightenment are neither bound nor liberated; the noble eightfold path is neither bound nor liberated; the noble truths are neither bound nor liberated; the meditative absorptions are neither bound nor liberated; the immeasurables are neither bound nor liberated.

The formless attainments are unbound and unliberated; the liberations are unbound and unliberated; the serial attainments of meditative dwelling are unbound and unliberated; the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are unbound and unliberated; the superknowledges are unbound and unliberated; the concentrations are unbound and unliberated; the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are unbound and unliberated; the powers of a Tathāgata are unbound and unliberated; the grounds of self-confidence are unbound and unliberated.

The analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are unbound and unliberated; great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) is unbound and unliberated; great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is unbound and unliberated; the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are unbound and unliberated; awakening (*bodhi*) is unbound and unliberated; omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) is unbound and unliberated; knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is unbound and unliberated; knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is unbound and unliberated; the bodhisattva is unbound and unliberated; the Buddha is unbound and unliberated; suchness (*tathatā*) is unbound and unliberated; non-falsity (*avitathatā*) is unbound and unliberated.

It is neither bound nor liberated by non-dual suchness; it is neither bound nor liberated by the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is neither bound nor liberated; it is neither bound nor liberated by the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*); it is neither bound nor liberated by the fixed order of phenomena (*dharma-niyāmatā*); the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is neither bound nor liberated; it is neither bound nor liberated by unconditionedness (*asaṃskṛtatā*).

Abiding in this generosity-perfection (*dāna-pāramitā*) which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in this ethical discipline-perfection (*śīla-pāramitā*) which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in this patience-perfection (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in this vigor-perfection (*vīrya-pāramitā*) which is neither bound nor liberated; [abiding in this] meditation-perfection (*dhyāna-pāramitā*) which is neither bound nor liberated...

Abiding in the perfection of meditative concentration; abiding in the perfection of wisdom, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in internal emptiness, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in external emptiness, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in internal-and-external emptiness, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of emptiness, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in great emptiness, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in ultimate emptiness, which is neither bound nor liberated.

Abiding in the emptiness of the conditioned, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of the unconditioned, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of the ultimate, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of non-dispersal, which is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, which is neither bound nor liberated; and abiding in the emptiness of all phenomena, which is neither bound nor liberated.

Abiding in the emptiness of specific characteristics that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of non-apprehension that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of non-existence that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of intrinsic nature that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the four applications of mindfulness that are neither bound nor liberated; and abiding in the four right efforts that are neither bound nor liberated.

Abiding in the four bases of psychic power that are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the five faculties that are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the five powers that are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the seven factors of enlightenment that are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the noble eightfold path that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the noble truths that are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the four meditative absorptions that are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the four immeasurables that are neither bound nor liberated.

Abiding in the four formless attainments which are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the eight liberations which are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the nine successive meditative attainments which are neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—which are neither bound nor liberated; [and] in the supernormal powers which are neither bound nor liberated.

Having stood; having stood in meditative absorptions that are neither bound nor liberated; having stood in the gateways of dhāraṇī that are neither bound nor liberated; having stood in the ten powers of a Tathāgata that are neither bound nor liberated; having stood in the four grounds of self-confidence that are neither bound nor liberated; having stood in the four analytical knowledges that are neither bound nor liberated; having stood in great loving-kindness that is neither bound nor liberated; having stood in great compassion that is neither bound nor liberated.

Abiding in the unbound and unliberated unique qualities of a Buddha; abiding in enlightenment that is unbound and unliberated; abiding in omniscience that is unbound and unliberated; abiding in the knowledge of the aspects of the path that is unbound and unliberated; abiding in the knowledge of all aspects that is unbound and unliberated; abiding in suchness that is unbound and unliberated; abiding in non-falsity that is unbound and unliberated; abiding in non-other-suchness that is unbound and unliberated.

Abiding in the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the stability of phenomena (dharma-sthititā) that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the fixed order of phenomena (dharma-niyāmatā) that is neither bound nor liberated; abiding in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) that is neither bound nor liberated; and abiding in the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) that is neither bound nor liberated—he will liberate sentient beings who are neither bound nor liberated.

Being neither bound nor liberated, he will purify a buddha-field that is neither bound nor liberated; being neither bound nor liberated, he will attend upon Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who are neither bound nor liberated; being neither bound nor liberated, he will hear teachings that are neither bound nor liberated; being neither bound nor liberated, he will never be separated from Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who are neither bound nor liberated; and being neither bound nor liberated, he will never be separated from superknowledges (*abhijñā*) that are neither bound nor liberated.

One who is neither bound nor liberated will never be separated from the five eyes that are neither bound nor liberated; one who is neither bound nor liberated will never be separated from the dhāraṇīs that are neither bound nor liberated; one who is neither bound nor liberated will never be separated from the meditative absorptions (*samāpatti*) that are neither bound nor liberated; one who is neither bound nor liberated will produce the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) that is neither bound nor liberated; and one who is neither bound nor liberated will [produce] the omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) that are neither bound nor liberated.

He will attain perfect awakening; being neither bound nor liberated, he will turn the wheel of Dharma that is neither bound nor liberated. Being neither bound nor liberated, he will establish beings—who are neither bound nor liberated—in the three vehicles. In this way indeed, venerable Pūrṇa, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, being neither bound nor liberated, will awaken to all phenomena by means of the six perfections which are neither bound nor liberated, on account of their non-existence, on account of their solitude, and on account of their non-arising.
In this way indeed, venerable Pūrṇa, it should be understood that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is one who is neither bound nor liberated, having donned the great armor of the Mahāyāna.

Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) of the bodhisattva mahāsattva? Blessed One, how many bodhisattva mahāsattvas should be known as having set out upon the Great Vehicle? From where will that vehicle depart? Where will that vehicle abide? Or who will depart by means of that vehicle? When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Subhūti: "Subhūti, as for what you have thus said..."

What is the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva? Subhūti, the six perfections are the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva. Which six? The perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom.

In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives gifts to those in need with mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), namely internal and external things; and having made that common to all sentient beings, he dedicates it toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). This is the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. He said:
“Blessed One, what is the perfection of ethical discipline of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One replied, “In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva...”

With mental states associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), he himself undertakes and abides in the ten paths of wholesome action (*daśakuśalakarmapatha*), and he likewise encourages others, leads them, and establishes them in the ten paths of wholesome action by means of the yoga of non-apprehension (*anupalambhayoga*). This is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s supreme perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*). [Śāriputra] asked: "Blessed One, what is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*)? The Blessed One said:

"In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), is himself endowed with patience and encourages others toward patience by means of the yoga of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). This is the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. [Subhūti] asked: "Blessed One, what is the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One said:

In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through mental engagements associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), personally does not cast off the yoke regarding the five perfections (*pañcapāramitā*) and likewise establishes others in the five perfections by means of the yoga of non-apprehension (*anupalambhayoga*). This is the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. [Subhūti] asked: "Blessed One, what is the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One said:

In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva enters the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) through skillful means (*upāyakauśala*) by means of mental attentions associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). He also encourages others to enter the meditative concentrations by way of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-yoga*). This is the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Subhūti asked: "Blessed One, what is the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) of a bodhisattva mahāsattva? The Blessed One replied:

In this regard, Subhūti, through mental states associated with the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not himself adhere to any phenomena (*dharma*), and he contemplates the intrinsic nature (*prakṛti*) of all phenomena by means of non-apprehension (*anupalambha*). Not adhering to any phenomena, he dwells in the contemplation of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

He encourages, settles, and establishes sentient beings through the yoga of non-apprehension. This, Subhūti, is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva; this, Subhūti, is the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattva is as follows: namely, internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, and unconditioned emptiness.

extreme emptiness, emptiness without beginning or end, emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of non-apprehension, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of self-nature, and emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence.

In that regard, what is internal emptiness? Internal phenomena are said to be: the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Therein, the eye is empty of the eye, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because such is its intrinsic nature (*prakṛti*). The ear is empty of the ear, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because such is its intrinsic nature. The nose is empty of the nose, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor indestructible.

For what reason? This is its very nature: the tongue is empty of the tongue, by virtue of being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. The body is empty of the body, by virtue of being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. The mind is empty of the mind, by virtue of being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. This is called internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*).

In that regard, what is external emptiness (*bahirdhā-śūnyatā*)? External phenomena (*bāhya-dharma*) are said to be form, sound, odor, taste, tangibles, and mental objects (*dharma*). Among these, form is empty of form, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? Because this is its very nature (*prakṛti*). Sound is empty of sound, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor indestructible.

On account of this. For what reason? Because such is its intrinsic nature (*prakṛti*). Odor is empty of odor, on account of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? Because such is its intrinsic nature. Taste is empty of taste, on account of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? Because such is its intrinsic nature. Tangible object is empty of tangible object, on account of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? Because such is its intrinsic nature.
Phenomena are empty of phenomena, by virtue of being neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their very nature. This is called external emptiness.

In that regard, what is internal-external emptiness? The six internal sense bases—these are called internal-external phenomena (*adhyātmika-bāhyadharmāḥ*). Among them, internal phenomena are empty of external phenomena, by virtue of being neither immutable nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their very nature (*prakṛti*). These external phenomena are empty of internal phenomena, by virtue of being neither immutable nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their very nature.

This is called internal-external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of emptiness (*śūnyatāśūnyatā*)? That which is the emptiness of all phenomena is empty by means of that very emptiness, on account of the immutability and indestructibility of emptiness. For what reason? Because this is its very nature (*prakṛti*). This is called the emptiness of emptiness. In that regard, what is great emptiness (*mahāśūnyatā*)? The eastern direction is empty of the eastern direction; the southern direction is empty of the southern direction; the western direction is empty of the western direction.

The northern direction is empty of the northern direction; the downward direction is empty of the downward direction; the upward direction is empty of the upward direction. Likewise, the intermediate directions are empty of the intermediate directions, on account of their being neither immutable nor subject to destruction. For what reason? This is their intrinsic nature (*prakṛti*). This is called "great emptiness" (*mahāśūnyatā*). In that regard, what is "emptiness of the ultimate" (*paramārthaśūnyatā*)? The ultimate is said to be those things that enter *nirvāṇa*.
And that *nirvāṇa* is empty of *nirvāṇa*, on account of its being neither immutable nor subject to destruction. For what reason? This is their intrinsic nature.

This is called the emptiness of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta-śūnyatā*)? "The conditioned" refers to the realm of desire (*kāmadhātu*), the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*). Therein, the realm of desire is empty of the realm of desire; the realm of form is empty of the realm of form; and the formless realm is empty of the formless realm, by virtue of being neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their very nature (*prakṛti*). This is called the emptiness of the conditioned. In that regard, what is the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*)?

That which has no arising, no cessation, and no alteration of its duration is called the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). That which is conditioned is called the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*). And that unconditioned is empty of the unconditioned, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. This is called the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of the ultimate (*atyanta-śūnyatā*)? That for which no end is perceived is the ultimate. The ultimate is empty of the ultimate, by virtue of its being neither immutable nor subject to destruction.

For what reason? This is its very nature. This is called "emptiness of the ultimate" (*atyanta-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the "emptiness of that which is without beginning or end" (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*)? That for which no beginning (*avara*) is perceived, and no end (*agra*)—for it neither comes nor goes—is without beginning or end. It is empty of being without beginning or end by virtue of its being neither immutable nor subject to destruction. For what reason? This is its very nature. This is called "emptiness of that which is without beginning or end. In that regard, what is the "emptiness of the non-dispersed" (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*)?

Wherein there is no discarding of any dharma, it is non-rejection, empty by way of non-rejection, on account of its being neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. This is called the emptiness of non-rejection (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*).

In that regard, what is the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*)? It is the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, whether conditioned or unconditioned; it is not made by Śrāvakas, nor by Pratyekabuddhas, nor by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, nor by Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas. This intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature because it is based on being immutable and indestructible. Why is that? Because this is its very nature. This is called the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
In that regard, what is the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*)?

"All phenomena" (sarvadharma) are said to be: form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness; the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; form, sound, odor, taste, tangible objects, and mental objects; eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness; and eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact.

Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact, feeling born of body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact; material phenomena, immaterial phenomena; conditioned phenomena and unconditioned phenomena—these are called all phenomena (*sarvadharma*). All phenomena are empty of all phenomena, by virtue of their being neither immutable nor indestructible.

For what reason? This is their very nature; this is called the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*)? Form has the characteristic of form, yet it is non-apprehensible and thus without characteristic. Feeling has the characteristic of feeling. Perception has the characteristic of grasping. Volitional formations have the characteristic of conditioned activity. Consciousness has the characteristic of consciousness. The aggregates have the characteristic of suffering. The elements have the characteristic of venomous serpents. The sense bases have the characteristic of gates of calamity. [The totality] has the characteristic of a collection.

Dependent origination: the perfection of generosity has the characteristic of relinquishment; the perfection of ethical discipline has the characteristic of non-agitation; the perfection of patience has the characteristic of non-irritability; the perfection of vigor has the characteristic of indefatigability; the perfection of meditative concentration has the characteristic of gathering; the perfection of wisdom has the characteristic of non-attachment. The four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments have the characteristic of non-irritability.

The thirty-seven factors of enlightenment have the characteristic of leading to liberation; the gate of liberation of emptiness has the characteristic of seclusion; the gate of liberation of signlessness has the characteristic of peace; the gate of liberation of wishlessness has the characteristic of being neither suffering nor delusion; the liberations have the characteristic of releasing; the powers have the characteristic of being well-determined; the grounds of self-confidence have the characteristic of being well-established; [the unshared qualities] have the characteristic of being indestructible.

The analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*); great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) characterized by the bringing about of welfare; great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) characterized by the sense of smelling; great sympathetic joy (*mahāmuditā*) characterized by gladness; great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) characterized by non-confusion; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) characterized by being unassailable; the knowledge of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatājñāna*) characterized by direct perception; and that which is the characteristic of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*) and that which is the characteristic of unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛtadharma*).

All these phenomena are empty by their respective characteristics, on account of their being neither immutable nor indestructible. Why is that? Because this is their very nature. This is called the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*)? It is that wherein the past is not apprehended, the future is not apprehended, and the stability of the present is not apprehended. Non-apprehension is empty of non-apprehension, on account of its being neither immutable nor indestructible.

For what reason? This is its very nature. This is called the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*)? There is no composite intrinsic nature because all phenomena (*dharma*) are dependently originated. A combination is empty of combination, by virtue of being neither immutable nor indestructible. For what reason? This is its very nature. This is called the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Furthermore, Subhūti, existence is empty of existence.

Non-existence is empty of non-existence; intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature; other-nature is empty of other-nature. In this regard, what is non-existence? Existence is said to be the five aggregates. The five aggregates are empty of the five aggregates; thus, existence is empty of existence. What is non-existence that is empty of intrinsic nature? Non-existence is said to be the unconditioned. And that unconditioned is empty of the unconditioned; thus, non-existence is empty of non-existence.
Intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature; extrinsic nature is empty of extrinsic nature. "Intrinsic nature" refers to the fundamental nature that is non-erroneous; therein lies emptiness.

It is not produced by knowledge, nor by vision; this is called the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*). In that regard, what is the emptiness of other-nature (*parabhāva-śūnyatā*)? That which remains as the stability of phenomena (*dharma-sthititā*), the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), the fixed order of phenomena (*dharmaniyāmatā*), suchness (*tathatā*), non-falsity (*avitathatā*), non-other-suchness (*ananyatathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), whether Tathāgatas arise or do not arise—this is the emptiness of those phenomena by way of another; this is called the emptiness of other-nature. Subhūti, this is the Great Vehicle of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the Mahāyāna of a bodhisattva mahāsattva consists of these: namely, the samādhi called Śūraṅgama; the samādhi called Ratnamudrā; the samādhi called Siṃhavikrīḍita; the samādhi called Sucandra; the samādhi called Candradhvajaketu; the samādhi called Sarvadharmodgata; the samādhi called Adhivacanasaṃpraveśa; and the samādhi called Vilokitamūrdha.

The concentration named "fixed in the realm of phenomena" (*dharmadhātuniyata*); the concentration named "banner of fixed victory" (*niyatadhvajaketu*); the concentration named "vajra"; the concentration named "seal of entry into all phenomena" (*sarvadharmapraveśamudrā*); the concentration named "well-established king of concentrations" (*samādhirājasupratiṣṭhita*); the concentration named "emitted rays of light" (*raśmipramukta*); the concentration named "array of powers" (*balavyūha*); the concentration named "arisen" (*samudgata*); the concentration named "entry into the fixed etymological explanations" (*niruktāniyatapraveśa*); and the concentration named "thorough entry into designations" (*adhivacanasaṃpraveśa*).

The concentration named Surveying the Directions; the concentration named Seal of the Foundation; the concentration named Non-Forgetfulness; the concentration named Ocean-Saṃudra of the Convergence of All Dharmas; the concentration named Pervading Space; the concentration named Vajra-Maṇḍala; the concentration named Armlet on the Top of the Banner; the concentration named Indra’s Banner; the concentration named Following the Stream; the concentration named Lion’s Yawn; the concentration named Dispersion.
The concentration named Abandoning Strife; the concentration named Vairocana; the concentration named Immaculate.

The concentration named "dwelling without a home"; the concentration named "thoughtless"; the concentration named "stainless lamp"; the concentration named "infinite radiance"; the concentration named "light-maker"; the concentration named "universal illumination"; the concentration named "pure essence"; the concentration named "stainless light"; the concentration named "joy-maker"; the concentration named "lamp of lightning"; the concentration named "inexhaustible"; the concentration named "invincible."

The concentration named Tejovatī; the concentration named Kṣayāpagata; the concentration named Aniñja; the concentration named Avivarta; the concentration named Sūryapradīpa; the concentration named Candravimala; the concentration named Prajñāpradīpa; the concentration named Śuddhapratibhāsa; the concentration named Ālokakara; the concentration named Kārākāra; the concentration named Jñānaketu; and the concentration named Vajropama.

The concentration called "abiding of the mind"; the concentration called "universal illumination"; the concentration called "well-established"; the concentration called "jewel-peak"; the concentration called "seal of the sublime Dharma"; the concentration called "equality of all phenomena"; the concentration called "renouncing delight"; the concentration called "Dharma-arisen"; the concentration called "dispersing"; the concentration called "differentiation of the words of all phenomena"; the concentration called "entry into equal syllables."
