Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of the right efforts would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. And Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of the bases of psychic power would desire the departure of those that are without marks. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of the faculties would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks.

Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of signless phenomena would desire the departure of the powers; Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of signless phenomena would desire the departure of the factors of enlightenment; Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of signless phenomena would desire the departure of the noble eightfold path. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, that which is the intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness does not depart from the triple world.

One does not abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) does not depart from the triple world (*traidhātuka*), nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of the faculties (*indriya*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of the powers (*bala*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience.

One does not abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) does not depart from the triple world (*traidhātuka*), nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of the path (*mārga*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience.

He abides in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*). Why is that? Because the intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness; the intrinsic nature of the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the right efforts; the intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power; the intrinsic nature of the faculties (*indriya*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the faculties; the intrinsic nature of the powers (*bala*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the powers; the intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment; and the intrinsic nature of the path (*mārga*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the path.

Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the noble truths would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the meditative absorptions would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the immeasurables would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the formless attainments would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks.

Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from the liberations (vimokṣa) would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks (alakṣaṇa). Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti) would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from emptiness (śūnyatā) would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from the signless (ānimitta) would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks.

Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of signless phenomena would desire the departure of the wishless. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the noble truths does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). The intrinsic nature of the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. The intrinsic nature of the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. [The same applies to] the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*).

That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the eight liberations does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature of the nine successive meditative attainments does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects. That which is the intrinsic nature of emptiness does not emerge from the triple world.

One does not abide in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of immeasurable benefit does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the noble truths is empty of the intrinsic nature of the noble truths; the intrinsic nature of the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the meditative absorptions; the intrinsic nature of the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the immeasurables.

The intrinsic nature of the formless attainments is empty of the intrinsic nature of the formless attainments; the intrinsic nature of the liberations is empty of the intrinsic nature of the liberations; the intrinsic nature of the nine successive dwellings is empty of the intrinsic nature of the nine successive dwellings; the intrinsic nature of emptiness is empty of the intrinsic nature of emptiness; the intrinsic nature of the signless is empty of the intrinsic nature of the signless; the intrinsic nature of the wishless is empty of the intrinsic nature of the wishless.

Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the superknowledges (abhijñā) would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks (alakṣaṇa). Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the meditative concentrations (samādhi) would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the gateways of mnemonic formulas (dhāraṇīmukha) would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is the intrinsic nature (svabhāva) of the superknowledges does not depart from the triple world (traidhātuka).

One does not abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) does not emerge from the triple world (*traidhātuka*), nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*) does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges; the intrinsic nature of the meditative concentrations is empty of the intrinsic nature of the meditative concentrations; the intrinsic nature of the gateways of mnemonic formulas is empty of the intrinsic nature of the gateways of mnemonic formulas.

Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the ten powers of a Tathāgata should desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the four grounds of self-confidence should desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the four analytical knowledges should desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks.

Subhūti, one who would desire the departure of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Why is that? For, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Tathāgata does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). The intrinsic nature of the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*) does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience.

That which is the intrinsic nature of the four analytical knowledges does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects. That which is the intrinsic nature of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata is empty of the intrinsic nature of the powers of a Tathāgata; the intrinsic nature of the grounds of self-confidence is empty of the intrinsic nature of the grounds of self-confidence.
The nature of the analytical knowledges is empty of the nature of the analytical knowledges; the nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha is empty of the nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha.
Subhūti, one who would desire the arising of an Arhat whose outflows are exhausted would desire the arising of dharmas that are without marks.

Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the dharmas that are without marks would desire the departure of a pratyekabuddha; Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the dharmas that are without marks would desire the departure of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; Subhūti, he who would desire the departure of the dharmas that are without marks would desire the departure of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature of a Pratyekabuddha does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience.

That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of an Arhat is empty of the intrinsic nature of an Arhat; the intrinsic nature of a Pratyekabuddha is empty of the intrinsic nature of a Pratyekabuddha; the intrinsic nature of a Bodhisattva is empty of the intrinsic nature of a Bodhisattva; and the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata is empty of the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata.

Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from the fruit of stream-entry would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from the fruit of once-returning would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from the fruit of non-returning would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure from arhatship would desire the departure from phenomena that are without marks.

Subhūti, he who would desire the departure from the dharma-s that are without marks would desire the departure from pratyekabodhi; Subhūti, he who would desire the departure from the dharma-s that are without marks would desire the departure from the knowledge of the aspects of the path; [he would desire the departure] from the knowledge of all aspects.

Subhūti, one who desires the departure of phenomena that are without marks desires the departure of what is unconditioned. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. The intrinsic nature of the fruit of once-returning does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. The intrinsic nature of the fruit of non-returning does not depart from the triple world.

One does not abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of arhatship does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of solitary awakening (*pratyekabodhi*) does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience.

That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) does not emerge from the three realms, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry; the intrinsic nature of the fruit of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of once-returning; the intrinsic nature of the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of non-returning; and the intrinsic nature of arhatship (*arhattva*) is empty of the intrinsic nature of arhatship.

The intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is empty of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path; the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of all aspects is empty of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of all aspects.

Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of phenomena that are without characteristics would desire the departure of sound. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of phenomena that are without characteristics would desire the departure of signs. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of phenomena that are without characteristics would desire the departure of conventional designations. Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of phenomena that are without characteristics would desire the departure of worldly discourse. [Whoever would desire the departure of phenomena that are without characteristics would desire the departure] of conceptual construction.

Subhūti, one who would desire the departure of phenomena that are without marks would desire the departure of what is not. Why is that? Because emptiness of name is empty of the intrinsic nature of emptiness of name; emptiness of signs is empty of the intrinsic nature of emptiness of signs; emptiness of convention is empty of the intrinsic nature of emptiness of convention; emptiness of purification is empty of the intrinsic nature of emptiness of purification; emptiness of designation is empty of the intrinsic nature of emptiness of designation.

Subhūti, one who would desire the departure of non-arising would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, one who would desire the departure of non-cessation would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, one who would desire the departure of affliction would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks. Subhūti, one who would desire the departure of purification would desire the departure of dharmas that are without marks.

Subhūti, whoever would desire the departure of signless phenomena would desire the departure of the unconditioned (*anabhisaṃskāra*). Why is that? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of non-arising does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature of non-cessation does not depart from the triple world, nor does it abide in the knowledge of all aspects. That which is the intrinsic nature of affliction (*saṃkleśa*) does not depart from the triple world.

One does not abide in omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). That which is the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of purification does not emerge from the triple world (*traidhātuka*), nor does it abide in omniscience. That which is the intrinsic nature of non-conditioning (*anabhisaṃskāra*) does not emerge from the triple world, nor does it abide in omniscience. Why is that? Because, in this way: the intrinsic nature of non-arising is empty of the intrinsic nature of non-arising; the intrinsic nature of cessation is empty of the intrinsic nature of cessation.

The nature of affliction is empty of the nature of affliction; the nature of purification is empty of the nature of purification; the nature of non-conditioning is empty of the nature of non-conditioning.

Therefore, Subhūti, by this method as well, it should be understood in this way: the Great Vehicle departs from the triple world; it will go toward that which is all-aspect-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), for that state is immovable. Furthermore, Subhūti, as to what you asked—"Where will that vehicle abide?"—that vehicle will not abide anywhere. Why is that? Because all phenomena (*dharma*) are non-abiding, due to the non-apprehension of any foundation.

Moreover, Subhūti, that vehicle will abide by way of the yoga of non-abiding. Just as, Subhūti, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) neither abides nor does not abide, even so, Subhūti, that vehicle neither abides nor does not abide. Just as, Subhūti, suchness (tathatā) neither abides nor does not abide, even so, Subhūti, that vehicle neither abides nor does not abide. Just as, Subhūti, the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) neither abides nor does not abide, [even so, Subhūti, that vehicle neither abides nor does not abide].

In the same way, that vehicle is neither situated nor not situated. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the inconceivable realm is neither situated nor not situated; in the same way, that vehicle is neither situated nor not situated. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm is neither situated nor not situated; the intrinsic nature of suchness is neither situated nor not situated; the intrinsic nature of the limit of reality is neither situated nor not situated.

The nature of the inconceivable realm is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the nature of the dharma-realm is empty of the nature of the dharma-realm; the nature of suchness is empty of the nature of suchness; the nature of the limit of reality is empty of the nature of the limit of reality; and the nature of the inconceivable realm is empty of the nature of the inconceivable realm. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the realm of space is neither established nor unestablished.

In the same way, Subhūti, that vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Just as, Subhūti, the realm of the destruction of passion is neither situated nor non-situated, so too, Subhūti, that vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Just as, Subhūti, the realm of abandonment is neither situated nor non-situated, so too, Subhūti...

That vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the element of dispassion (*virāga-dhātu*) is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the element of cessation (*nirodha-dhātu*) is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the element of space (*ākāśa-dhātu*) is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

It does not abide, nor does it not abide, in the intrinsic nature of the realm of the destruction of passion; it does not abide, nor does it not abide, in the intrinsic nature of the realm of abandonment; it does not abide, nor does it not abide, in the intrinsic nature of the realm of dispassion; it does not abide, nor does it not abide, in the intrinsic nature of the realm of cessation. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the realm of space is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realm of space; the intrinsic nature of the realm of the destruction of passion is empty of the intrinsic nature of the realm of the destruction of passion.

The nature of the element of abandonment is empty of the nature of the element of abandonment; the nature of the element of dispassion is empty of the nature of the element of dispassion; the nature of the element of cessation is empty of the nature of the element of cessation.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of form is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of feeling is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of perception is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of formative forces (*saṃskāra*) is neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of consciousness (*vijñāna*) is neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of form is neither established nor non-established; the intrinsic nature of feeling (*vedanā*) is not established... [and so on].

It is neither established nor unestablished. The intrinsic nature of perception is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of mental formations is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of consciousness is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because form is empty of form; feeling is empty of feeling; perception is empty of perception; mental formations are empty of mental formations; and consciousness is empty of consciousness.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the eye is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the ear is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the nose is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the tongue is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the body is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the mind is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the eye is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the ear is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the nose is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the tongue is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the body is neither established nor unestablished; and the intrinsic nature of the mind is neither established nor unestablished. For what reason? Because the eye is empty of the eye, and the ear is empty of the ear.
The nose is empty of the nose; the tongue is empty of the tongue; the body is empty of the body; the mind is empty of the mind.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of form is neither established nor unestablished; in the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of sound is neither established nor unestablished; in the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of odor is neither established nor unestablished; in the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of taste is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of contact is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of phenomena is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of form is neither stable nor unstable; the intrinsic nature of sound is neither stable nor unstable; the intrinsic nature of odor is neither stable nor unstable; the intrinsic nature of taste is neither stable nor unstable; the intrinsic nature of tangibility is neither stable nor unstable; the intrinsic nature of phenomena is neither stable nor unstable. For what reason? Because form is empty of form; sound is empty of sound.
Odor is empty of odor; taste is empty of taste; touch is empty of touch; phenomena are empty of phenomena.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of eye-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of ear-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of nose-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti...

That Mahāyāna is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of tongue-consciousness is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Mahāyāna is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of body-consciousness is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Mahāyāna is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of mind-consciousness is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of eye-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; the intrinsic nature of ear-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; the intrinsic nature of nose-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; the intrinsic nature of tongue-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed; the intrinsic nature of body-consciousness is neither stationed nor unstationed.

Is the nature of mental consciousness established or unestablished? For what reason? Because visual consciousness is empty of visual consciousness; auditory consciousness is empty of auditory consciousness; olfactory consciousness is empty of olfactory consciousness; gustatory consciousness is empty of gustatory consciousness; tactile consciousness is empty of tactile consciousness; and mental consciousness is empty of mental consciousness.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of eye-contact is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of ear-contact is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of nose-contact is neither established nor unestablished.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Just as, Subhūti, the emptiness of tongue-contact is neither situated nor non-situated, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is not situated.

It is not non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of body-contact is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of mind-contact is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because the intrinsic nature of eye-contact is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

The intrinsic nature of nose-contact does not abide, nor does it not abide; the intrinsic nature of tongue-contact does not abide, nor does it not abide; the intrinsic nature of body-contact does not abide, nor does it not abide; the intrinsic nature of mind-contact does not abide, nor does it not abide. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, eye-contact is empty of eye-contact; ear-contact is empty of ear-contact.
Olfactory contact is empty of olfactory contact; gustatory contact is empty of gustatory contact; tactile contact is empty of tactile contact; mental contact is empty of mental contact.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is neither fixed nor unfixed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither fixed nor unfixed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the feeling conditioned by ear-contact is neither fixed nor unfixed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither fixed nor unfixed.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the feeling conditioned by olfactory contact is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the feeling conditioned by gustatory contact is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the feeling conditioned by bodily contact is neither situated nor not situated; in the very same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor not situated.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by visual contact is neither stationed nor unstationed; the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by auditory contact is neither stationed nor unstationed.

The nature of feeling conditioned by nose-contact is neither stationary nor non-stationary; the nature of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is neither stationary nor non-stationary; the nature of feeling conditioned by body-contact is neither stationary nor non-stationary; the nature of feeling conditioned by mind-contact is neither stationary nor non-stationary. Why is that? Because the feeling conditioned by eye-contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by eye-contact.

Feeling conditioned by ear-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by ear-contact; feeling conditioned by nose-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by nose-contact; feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; feeling conditioned by body-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by body-contact; feeling conditioned by mind-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a dream is neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, an illusion is neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a mirage is neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, an echo is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a reflection is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, an emanation of a Tathāgata is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because the nature of a dream is neither abiding nor non-abiding; the nature of an illusion is neither abiding nor non-abiding; the nature of a mirage is neither abiding nor non-abiding; the nature of an echo is neither abiding nor non-abiding; and the nature of a reflection is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

The nature of a Tathāgata’s emanation is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because a dream is empty of a dream; an illusion is empty of an illusion; a mirage is empty of a mirage; an echo is empty of an echo; a reflection is empty of a reflection; and a Tathāgata’s emanation is empty of a Tathāgata’s emanation.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the perfection of generosity is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the perfection of ethical discipline is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the perfection of patience is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the perfection of vigor is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the perfection of meditation is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the perfection of wisdom is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed.
For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of generosity is neither established nor unestablished. Not...

The intrinsic nature of the perfection of ethical discipline neither stands nor does not stand; the intrinsic nature of the perfection of patience neither stands nor does not stand; the intrinsic nature of the perfection of vigor neither stands nor does not stand; the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditative concentration neither stands nor does not stand; the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom neither stands nor does not stand. Why is that? Because the perfection of generosity is empty of the perfection of generosity; the perfection of ethical discipline is empty of the perfection of ethical discipline.

The perfection of patience is empty of the perfection of patience; the perfection of vigor is empty of the perfection of vigor; the perfection of meditation is empty of the perfection of meditation; the perfection of wisdom is empty of the perfection of wisdom.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, internal emptiness is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, external emptiness is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, internal-external emptiness is neither established nor unestablished.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor not situated. Just as, Subhūti, the emptiness of emptiness is neither situated nor not situated, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor not situated. Just as, Subhūti, the great emptiness is neither situated nor not situated, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor not situated. Just as, Subhūti, the emptiness of the ultimate truth is neither situated nor not situated, [even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor not situated].

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, the emptiness of the conditioned is neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, the emptiness of the unconditioned is neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti...

That Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, absolute emptiness is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of non-dispersal is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, intrinsic emptiness is neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, the emptiness of all phenomena is neither stationed nor unstationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of self-characteristic is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of non-apprehension is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of non-existence is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of internal emptiness is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of external emptiness is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of internal-and-external emptiness is neither established nor unestablished; nor is the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of emptiness [established or unestablished].

Whether abiding or not abiding, the intrinsic nature of great emptiness is neither abiding nor not abiding. The intrinsic nature of ultimate emptiness is neither abiding nor not abiding. The intrinsic nature of conditioned emptiness is neither abiding nor not abiding. The intrinsic nature of unconditioned emptiness is neither abiding nor not abiding. The intrinsic nature of absolute emptiness is neither abiding nor not abiding. The intrinsic nature of emptiness without beginning or end is neither abiding nor not abiding.

The intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-dispersal is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of essential nature is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of all phenomena is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of specific characteristics is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the non-apprehendable is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of non-existence is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither established nor unestablished;
and the intrinsic nature of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither established nor unestablished.

For what reason? Because internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness; external emptiness is empty of external emptiness; internal-and-external emptiness is empty of internal-and-external emptiness; the emptiness of emptiness is empty of the emptiness of emptiness; great emptiness is empty of great emptiness; the emptiness of the ultimate is empty of the emptiness of the ultimate; and the emptiness of the conditioned is empty of the emptiness of the conditioned.

Unconditioned emptiness is empty of unconditioned emptiness; ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness; emptiness without beginning or end is empty of emptiness without beginning or end; non-dispersal emptiness is empty of non-dispersal emptiness; essential nature emptiness is empty of essential nature emptiness; the emptiness of all phenomena is empty of the emptiness of all phenomena; the emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of the emptiness of specific characteristics; and the emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of the emptiness of non-apprehension.

It is empty. The emptiness of non-existence is empty of the emptiness of non-existence; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of the emptiness of intrinsic nature; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the foundations of mindfulness are neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the right efforts are neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the bases of psychic power are neither established nor non-established; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor non-established.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the sense faculties are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the powers are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the factors of enlightenment are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the noble eightfold path is neither situated nor non-situated; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the applications of mindfulness is neither situated nor non-situated; the intrinsic nature of the right efforts is neither situated nor non-situated; the intrinsic nature of the bases of psychic power is neither situated nor non-situated; and the intrinsic nature of the faculties is neither situated nor non-situated.

It does not abide, nor does it not abide, as having the intrinsic nature of the powers; it does not abide, nor does it not abide, as having the intrinsic nature of the factors of enlightenment; it does not abide, nor does it not abide, as having the intrinsic nature of the noble eightfold path. Why is that? Because the applications of mindfulness are empty of the applications of mindfulness; the right efforts are empty of the right efforts; the bases of psychic power are empty of the bases of psychic power;
the faculties are empty of the faculties; the powers are empty of the powers; the factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment; and the path is empty of the path.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the noble truths are neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the meditative concentrations are neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the immeasurables are neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the formless attainments are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the eight liberations are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the serial meditative attainments are neither established nor unestablished.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, the superknowledges are neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, meditative absorptions (samādhi) are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the gateways of mnemonic formulas (dhāraṇīmukha) are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature (svabhāva) of the noble truths is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the meditative concentrations (dhyāna) is neither established nor unestablished; nor is the intrinsic nature of the immeasurables (apramāṇa).

Whether abiding or not abiding, it does not have the nature of the formless attainments; whether abiding or not abiding, it does not have the nature of the eight liberations; whether abiding or not abiding, it does not have the nature of the serial attainments; whether abiding or not abiding, it does not have the nature of the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; whether abiding or not abiding, it does not have the nature of the superknowledges; whether abiding or not abiding, it does not have the nature of meditative concentrations.

The nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because the noble truths are empty of the noble truths; the meditative concentrations are empty of the meditative concentrations; the immeasurables are empty of the immeasurables; the formless attainments are empty of the formless attainments; the liberations are empty of the liberations; and the serial attainments of meditative dwelling are empty of the serial attainments of meditative dwelling.

The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. The superknowledges are empty of the superknowledges. The meditative concentrations are empty of the meditative concentrations. The gateways to the dhāraṇīs are empty of the gateways to the dhāraṇīs.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the ten powers of a Tathāgata are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the four grounds of self-confidence are neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the four analytical knowledges are neither established nor unestablished.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Just as, Subhūti, great compassion is neither situated nor non-situated, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Just as, Subhūti, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are neither situated nor non-situated, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Tathāgata is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the [four] fearlessnesses is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the [four] analytical knowledges is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of great compassion is neither established nor unestablished; and the intrinsic nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha is neither established nor unestablished. For what reason? Because, in this way, the ten powers of a Tathāgata are empty of powers.

The four fearlessnesses are empty of the fearlessnesses; the four analytical knowledges are empty of the intrinsic nature of the analytical knowledges; great compassion is empty of great compassion; and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, an Arhat whose bases are exhausted is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a Pratyekabuddha is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of an Arhat whose outflows are exhausted is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

The nature of a pratyekabuddha is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because the nature of an arhat is empty of the nature of an arhat; the nature of a pratyekabuddha is empty of the nature of a pratyekabuddha.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a bodhisattva is neither stationed nor not stationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor not stationed. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha is neither stationed nor not stationed; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor not stationed. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva is neither stationed nor not stationed.

The intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because the intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva is empty of the intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva; the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata is empty of the intrinsic nature of a Tathāgata.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the fruit of stream-entry is neither situated nor non-situated; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the fruit of once-returning is neither situated nor non-situated; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither situated nor non-situated. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the fruit of non-returning is neither situated nor non-situated.

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, arhatship is neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed. Just as, Subhūti, solitary enlightenment is neither stationed nor unstationed, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither stationed nor unstationed.

For what reason? Subhūti, it is because the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the fruit of once-returning is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of the fruit of non-returning is neither established nor unestablished; the intrinsic nature of arhatship is neither established nor unestablished; and the intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is neither established nor unestablished. For what reason? Because the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of stream-entry.

The intrinsic nature of the fruit of once-returning is empty of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of once-returning; the intrinsic nature of the fruit of non-returning is empty of the intrinsic nature of the fruit of non-returning; the intrinsic nature of arhatship is empty of the intrinsic nature of arhatship; the intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is empty of the intrinsic nature of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature (svabhāva) of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is neither abiding nor non-abiding, nor is the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of all aspects.

Whether abiding or not abiding—why is that? Because the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is empty of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of the aspects of the path; the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of all aspects is empty of the intrinsic nature of the knowledge of all aspects.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a name does not abide and does not not abide; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle does not abide and does not not abide. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a sign does not abide and does not not abide; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle does not abide and does not not abide. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a conventional designation does not abide and does not not abide; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle does not abide and does not not abide.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, conventional usage is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, a designation is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, a name has no intrinsic nature that is either established or unestablished; nor does a name have the intrinsic nature of a sign that is either established or unestablished.

The nature of convention neither abides nor does not abide; the nature of worldly usage neither abides nor does not abide; the nature of designation neither abides nor does not abide. Why is that? For indeed, the so-called "nature" is empty of the nature of a nature; the nature of signs is empty of the nature of signs; the nature of convention is empty of the nature of convention; the nature of worldly usage is empty of the nature of worldly usage; the nature of designation is empty of the nature of designation.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, non-arising is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither established nor unestablished. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, non-cessation is neither established nor unestablished; even so, Subhūti, is that Great Vehicle.

It is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, just as non-affliction is neither abiding nor non-abiding, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Subhūti, just as purification is neither abiding nor non-abiding, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of non-arising is neither abiding nor non-abiding.

The nature of cessation is neither established nor unestablished; the nature of non-affliction is neither established nor unestablished; the nature of non-purification is neither established nor unestablished. Why is that? Because the nature of non-arising is empty of the nature of non-arising; the nature of non-cessation is empty of the nature of non-cessation; the nature of non-affliction is empty of the nature of non-affliction; the nature of non-purification is empty of the nature of non-purification.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, non-conditioning is neither abiding nor non-abiding; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of non-conditioning is neither abiding nor non-abiding. Why is that? Because the intrinsic nature of non-conditioning is empty of the intrinsic nature of non-conditioning. By this method, that vehicle will not abide anywhere, by way of the application of non-abiding abiding.

Furthermore, as for what Subhūti said: "Who will set out by means of that vehicle?"—no one will set out by means of that vehicle; no one sets out by means of that vehicle. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, in every respect, those phenomena—the vehicle itself, the one who would set out, that by which one would set out, and that from which one would set out—do not exist and are not apprehended.

Since all phenomena (*dharmas*) are thus non-existent and unapprehendable, what phenomenon will emerge by means of what phenomenon? For what reason? Because, Subhūti, an absolutely such self (*ātman*) is not apprehended; a sentient being (*sattva*) is not apprehended; a living soul (*jīva*) is not apprehended; a creature (*jantu*) is not apprehended.

A nourisher is not apprehended; a person is not apprehended; a soul is not apprehended; a human being is not apprehended; a youth is not apprehended; an agent is not apprehended; an experiencer is not apprehended; a knower is not apprehended; a seer is not apprehended—by virtue of absolute purity, by virtue of the absolute purity of the self, by virtue of the absolute purity of a sentient being, and by virtue of the absolute purity of a life-principle.

Based on the absolute purity of the sentient being; based on the absolute purity of the nourisher; based on the absolute purity of the person; based on the absolute purity of the individual; based on the absolute purity of the human; based on the absolute purity of the youth; based on the absolute purity of the agent; based on the absolute purity of the experiencer; based on the absolute purity of the knower.

Based on its absolute purity, the seer is not apprehended; based on its absolute purity, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is not apprehended; based on its absolute purity, suchness (*tathatā*) is not apprehended; based on its absolute purity, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is not apprehended; based on its absolute purity, the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) is not apprehended; and based on its absolute purity, the aggregates (*skandha*) are not apprehended.

The elements are not apprehended, by virtue of their absolute purity; the sense bases are not apprehended, by virtue of their absolute purity; dependent origination is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the perfection of generosity is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the perfection of ethical discipline is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the perfection of patience is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity.

The perfection of vigor is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the perfection of meditation is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the perfection of wisdom is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity.

Internal emptiness is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; external emptiness is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; internal-external emptiness is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; great emptiness is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity.

Ultimate emptiness is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; conditioned emptiness is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; unconditioned emptiness is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; infinite emptiness is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; and emptiness without beginning or end is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity.

Non-dispersal emptiness is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; natural emptiness is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the emptiness of all phenomena is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the emptiness of specific characteristics is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the emptiness of non-apprehension is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity.

The emptiness of non-existence is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not apprehended, by virtue of its absolute purity.

The foundations of mindfulness are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the right efforts are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the bases of psychic power are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the faculties are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the powers are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the factors of enlightenment are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity.
The noble eightfold path is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; [so too are] the noble truths.

They are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*) are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; and the successive attainments of the stages of dwelling (*anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*) are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity.

The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not apprehended, on account of their absolute purity. The superknowledges are not apprehended, on account of their absolute purity. The meditative concentrations are not apprehended, on account of their absolute purity. The gateways of the dhāraṇīs are not apprehended, on account of their absolute purity. The powers of a Tathāgata are not apprehended, on account of their absolute purity.

The grounds of self-confidence are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the analytical knowledges are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; great compassion is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the unique qualities of a Buddha are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the stream-enterers are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity; the once-returners are not apprehended, by reason of their absolute purity.

Non-returners are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; arhats are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; pratyekabuddhas are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; bodhisattvas are not apprehended on account of their absolute purity; and the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, is not apprehended on account of his absolute purity.

The fruit of stream-entry is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; the fruit of once-returning is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; the fruit of non-returning is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity; arhatship is not apprehended on account of its absolute purity.

Based on ultimate purity, individual enlightenment (*pratyekabodhi*) is not apprehended; based on ultimate purity, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*) is not apprehended; based on ultimate purity, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is not apprehended; based on ultimate purity, non-arising (*anutpāda*) is not apprehended; based on ultimate purity, non-cessation (*anirodha*) is not apprehended; based on ultimate purity, non-defilement (*asaṃkleśa*) is not apprehended.

Non-purification is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; non-conditioning is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the prior limit is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the subsequent limit is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; the present is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity; and that which is to come is not apprehended, by reason of its absolute purity.

Going is not apprehended on account of ultimate purity; staying is not apprehended on account of ultimate purity; passing away is not apprehended on account of ultimate purity; rebirth is not apprehended on account of ultimate purity; decrease is not apprehended on account of ultimate purity; increase is not apprehended on account of ultimate purity. Through the non-apprehension of what is everything not apprehended?

Through the non-apprehension of the *dharmadhātu*, the *dharmadhātu* is not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the *dharmadhātu* is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of *tathatā*, [the *dharmadhātu*] is not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of *tathatā* is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

The limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is not apprehended because the limit of reality is non-apprehensible. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the limit of reality is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) is not apprehended because the inconceivable realm is non-apprehensible. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the inconceivable realm is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The aggregates, elements, and sense-bases (*skandha-dhātu-āyatana*) are not apprehended because the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are non-apprehensible. Why is that? It is because...

Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of dependent origination, dependent origination is not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of dependent origination is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the perfection of generosity, the perfection of generosity is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the perfection of generosity is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of ethical discipline is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the perfection of ethical discipline is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the perfection of patience, the perfection of patience is not apprehended.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the perfection of patience is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended; by means of the non-apprehension of the perfection of vigor, the perfection of vigor is not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the perfection of vigor is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended; by means of the non-apprehension of the perfection of meditation, the perfection of meditation is not apprehended.

For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the perfection of meditation is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended; by means of the non-apprehension of the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of wisdom is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the perfection of wisdom is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of internal emptiness, internal emptiness is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of internal emptiness is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of external emptiness, external emptiness is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of external emptiness is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Internal-external emptiness is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of internal-external emptiness. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, there is no such thing as the non-apprehension of internal-external emptiness.

It is apprehended, yet it is not apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of emptiness is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of great emptiness, great emptiness is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of great emptiness is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the ultimate is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the ultimate is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the conditioned is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the conditioned is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the unconditioned is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the unconditioned is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*), absolute emptiness is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of absolute emptiness is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the non-dispersed (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of the non-dispersed is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the non-dispersed is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of all phenomena is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of all phenomena is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the emptiness of specific characteristics is not apprehended. Why is that?

For, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of self-characteristics is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. By means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-apprehension is not apprehended. Why is that? For, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-apprehension is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. By means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of non-existence is not apprehended.

For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of non-existence is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. By means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. By means of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is not apprehended.
For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Because the applications of mindfulness are not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the applications of mindfulness, the applications of mindfulness are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the applications of mindfulness is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because the right efforts are not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the right efforts, the right efforts are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the right efforts is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because the bases of psychic power are not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the bases of psychic power, the bases of psychic power are not apprehended.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Due to the non-apprehension of the faculties (*indriya*), the faculties are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the faculties is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Due to the non-apprehension of the powers (*bala*), the powers are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the powers is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Because the factors of enlightenment are not apprehended, the factors of enlightenment are not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the factors of enlightenment is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because the path is not apprehended, the path is not apprehended. Why is that? It is because...

Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the path is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because the noble truths are not apprehended, the noble truths themselves are not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the noble truths is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because the meditative absorptions (dhyānas) are not apprehended, the meditative absorptions themselves are not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the meditative absorptions is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

The immeasurables are not apprehended because of the non-apprehension of the immeasurables. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the immeasurables is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The formless attainments are not apprehended because of the non-apprehension of the formless attainments. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the formless attainments is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The liberations are not apprehended because of the non-apprehension of the liberations.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the liberations is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Due to the non-apprehension of the serial attainments of meditative dwelling, the serial attainments of meditative dwelling are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the serial attainments of meditative dwelling is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the superknowledges, the superknowledges are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the superknowledges is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), meditative concentrations are not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of meditative concentration is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*), the gateways of mnemonic formulas are not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the gateways of mnemonic formulas is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the powers of a Tathāgata (*tathāgatabala*), [the powers] are not apprehended.

The powers of a Tathāgata. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the powers of a Tathāgata is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the grounds of self-confidence, the grounds of self-confidence are not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the grounds of self-confidence is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the analytical knowledges, the analytical knowledges are not apprehended.

For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is not apprehended through its own non-apprehension, great compassion is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of great compassion is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are not apprehended through their own non-apprehension, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of the stream-enterer, the stream-enterer is not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the stream-enterer is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the once-returner, the once-returner is not apprehended. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the once-returner is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the non-returner, the non-returner is not apprehended.

For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of a non-returner is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because of the non-apprehension of arhatship, an arhat is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of arhatship is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because of the non-apprehension of a pratyekabuddha, a pratyekabuddha is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of a pratyekabuddha is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.
