Through the non-apprehension of a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of a bodhisattva is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of a Tathāgata, a Tathāgata is not apprehended. Why is that? Because indeed...

Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the Tathāgata is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the fruit of stream-entry is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning is not apprehended.

For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the fruit of a once-returner is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because of the non-apprehension of the fruit of a non-returner, the fruit of a non-returner is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the fruit of a non-returner is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because of the non-apprehension of arhatship, arhatship is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of arhatship is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of individual enlightenment (*pratyekabodhi*), individual enlightenment is not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of individual enlightenment is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), the knowledge of the aspects of the path is not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the knowledge of the aspects of the path is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), the knowledge of all aspects is not apprehended.

For what reason? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of non-arising, non-arising is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of non-arising is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of non-cessation, non-cessation is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of non-cessation is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Non-affliction is not apprehended because non-affliction is unapprehendable. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the unapprehensibility of non-affliction is neither apprehended nor unapprehended. Purity is not apprehended because purity is unapprehendable. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the unapprehensibility of purity...

It is perceived, yet it is not perceived. Through the non-perception of the unconditioned (*anabhisaṃskāra*), the unconditioned is not perceived. Why is that? Subhūti, the non-perception of the unconditioned is neither perceived nor is it not perceived. Through the non-perception of the prior limit (*pūrvānta*), the prior limit is not perceived. Why is that? Subhūti, the non-perception of the prior limit is neither perceived nor is it not perceived. Through the non-perception of the posterior limit (*aparānta*), the posterior limit is not perceived.

For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the future is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because of the non-apprehension of the present, the present is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the present is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Because of the non-apprehension of coming, coming is not apprehended. For what reason? Subhūti, the non-apprehension of coming is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

Through the non-apprehension of going, going is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of going is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of staying, staying is not apprehended. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of staying is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of passing away, passing away is not apprehended.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of death is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of birth, birth is not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of birth is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. Through the non-apprehension of decline, decline is not apprehended. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of decline is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.
Increase is not apprehended because increase is unapprehendable. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the unapprehensibility of increase is neither apprehended nor unapprehended.

The first stage is not apprehended because the stage is unapprehendable. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the unapprehensibility of the first stage is neither apprehended nor unapprehended. [The same applies to] the second...

The second stage is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the stage. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the second stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The third stage is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the stage. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the third stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The fourth stage is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the stage.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the fourth stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The fifth stage is not apprehended by means of the non-apprehension of the stages. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the fifth stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The sixth stage is not apprehended by means of the non-apprehension of the stages. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the sixth stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

The seventh stage is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the stage. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the seventh stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The eighth stage is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the stage. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the non-apprehension of the eighth stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The ninth stage is not apprehended through the non-apprehension of the stage.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the ninth stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended. The tenth stage is not apprehended because of the non-apprehension of the stages. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the non-apprehension of the tenth stage is neither apprehended nor non-apprehended.

What is the first stage? What is the second stage? What is the third stage? What is the fourth stage? What is the fifth stage? What is the sixth stage? What is the seventh stage? What is the eighth stage? What is the ninth stage? What is the tenth stage? Namely: the stage of bright insight (*śuklavidarśanā-bhūmi*), the stage of the spiritual lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), the stage of the eighth person (*aṣṭamaka-bhūmi*), the stage of seeing (*darśana-bhūmi*), the stage of refinement (*tanu-bhūmi*), the stage of freedom from passion (*vītarāga-bhūmi*), the stage of one who has completed what was to be done (*kṛtāvi-bhūmi*), the stage of the solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddha-bhūmi*), the stage of the bodhisattva (*bodhisattva-bhūmi*), and the stage of the buddha (*buddha-bhūmi*).

The first stage of internal emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of external emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of internal and external emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of great emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of the emptiness of the ultimate is not apprehended.

The first stage of conditioned emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of unconditioned emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of absolute emptiness is not apprehended; the first stage of emptiness without beginning or end is not apprehended; the first stage of emptiness of non-dispersal is not apprehended; the first stage of natural emptiness is not apprehended.

Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, it is called the 'Great Vehicle, the Great Vehicle' because it will set forth having surpassed the world with its gods, asuras, and humans; therefore it is called the Great Vehicle. Blessed One, that Great Vehicle is equal to space. Just as there is room in space for immeasurable and incalculable beings, even so, Blessed One, in this Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable and incalculable beings."

In this manner, O Blessed One, this Great Vehicle belongs to the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas. Yet, of this Great Vehicle, neither arrival nor departure nor abiding is perceived; nor is its prior limit, nor its subsequent limit, nor its middle perceived. Just as, O Blessed One, of space neither arrival is perceived nor departure is perceived, nor is any abiding perceived.

In the same way, Blessed One, of this Mahāyāna neither a coming is perceived, nor a going is perceived, nor a staying is perceived. Just as, Blessed One, of space neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a posterior limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived—on account of the equality of the three times—just so, Blessed One, of this Mahāyāna neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a posterior limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the non-existence of internal and external emptiness is not a [substantial] existence, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the non-existence of the emptiness of emptiness were an existence and not a non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the emptiness of emptiness is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle transcends and emerges from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the great emptiness were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and emerge from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the great emptiness is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle transcends and emerges from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the non-existence of ultimate emptiness were not itself non-existent, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the non-existence of ultimate emptiness [is itself non-existent], [it does so].

Therefore, because it is not an entity, the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if conditioned emptiness were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, emptiness is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if the non-existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned were not its non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the emptiness of the unconditioned is a non-existence and not an existence, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the non-existence of absolute emptiness were not its non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because absolute emptiness is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and goes forth. If, Subhūti, beginningless and endless emptiness were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not surpass the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and go forth. But since, Subhūti, beginningless and endless emptiness is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and goes forth.

Subhūti, if the non-existence of the emptiness of non-dispersal were not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not have emerged, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the emptiness of non-dispersal is non-existence and not existence, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the non-existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature were not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not have emerged, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because intrinsic emptiness is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the emptiness of all phenomena were an entity...

If non-existence were not to exist, this Mahāyāna would not have emerged, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the emptiness of all phenomena is neither existence nor non-existence, therefore the Mahāyāna emerges, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the emptiness of specific characteristics were to be a non-existence rather than an absence of being, this Mahāyāna would not have emerged, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is neither a non-entity nor an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the emptiness of non-apprehension were a non-entity and not an entity, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the emptiness of non-apprehension is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the emptiness of non-existence were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the emptiness of non-existence is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if the non-existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature were itself an existence and not a non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is a non-existence and not an existence, therefore the Great Vehicle transcends and departs from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence were itself an existent and not a non-existent, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is a non-existent and not an existent, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the four foundations of mindfulness were themselves existents and not non-existents, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because...

Subhūti, because the foundations of mindfulness are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle surpasses and emerges from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the right efforts were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not surpass and emerge from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the right efforts are non-existence and not existence, therefore the Great Vehicle surpasses and emerges from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not have gone forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the bases of psychic power are a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle goes forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the faculties (*indriya*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not have gone forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the faculties are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the powers were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not proceed having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the powers are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the factors of enlightenment were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the factors of enlightenment are a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the path were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the path is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the noble truths were entities and not non-entities, this Great Vehicle would not surpass the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

It would have departed having surpassed the world. But since, Subhūti, the noble truths are non-existence and not existence, therefore the Mahāyāna departs having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the meditative absorptions were existence and not non-existence, this Mahāyāna would not have departed having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the immeasurables are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if the formless attainments were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not go forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the formless attainments are a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle goes forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the liberations were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not go forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the liberations are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle goes forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the serial attainments of meditative dwelling were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not go forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—[are non-existence...]

Non-existence is not existence; therefore, the Mahāyāna emerges having transcended the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the superknowledges were existence and not non-existence, this Mahāyāna would not emerge having transcended the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the superknowledges are non-existence and not existence, the Mahāyāna emerges having transcended the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if meditative concentrations were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, meditative concentrations are a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle transcends and departs from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the gateways of dhāraṇī were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the powers of a Tathāgata were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not proceed having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the powers of a Tathāgata are non-existence and not existence, therefore the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the grounds of self-confidence were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not depart having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the grounds of self-confidence are a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle departs having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the analytical knowledges were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not depart having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle goes forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, there were great compassion...

If existence were not non-existence, this Mahāyāna would not have emerged, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the non-existence of great compassion is not an existence, therefore the Mahāyāna emerges, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha were existence and not non-existence, this Mahāyāna would not have emerged, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
Therefore, Subhūti, because the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and goes forth.

If, Subhūti, the qualities of the stage of the spiritual lineage were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not have surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and gone forth. But since, Subhūti, the qualities of the stage of the spiritual lineage are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and goes forth.

Subhūti, if the state of an eighth-rank person (*aṣṭamaka*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not have emerged, transcending the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the state of an eighth-rank person is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges, transcending the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the state of one who has entered [the path] (*āpanna*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not have emerged, transcending the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the state of one who has attained the fruit of once-returning is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the state of one who has attained the fruit of once-returning were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the state of one who has attained the fruit of once-returning is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if the dharmas of a non-returner were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the dharmas of a non-returner are a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle transcends and departs from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the dharmas of an arhat were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the dharmas of an Arhat are non-existence and not existence, the Mahāyāna goes forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the dharmas of a Pratyekabuddha were existence and not non-existence, this Mahāyāna would not go forth, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the dharmas of a Pratyekabuddha are non-existence and not existence, the Mahāyāna goes forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the dharmas of a Bodhisattva were existence and not non-existence, this Mahāyāna would not go forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the qualities of a bodhisattva are non-existence and not existence, the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the qualities of a Buddha were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not proceed having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the qualities of a Buddha are non-existence and not existence, therefore the Great Vehicle proceeds having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the spiritual lineage (*gotrabhū*) were an existent thing and not a non-existent thing, this Great Vehicle would not have emerged, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the spiritual lineage is a non-existent thing and not an existent thing, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the eighth stage (*aṣṭamaka*) were an existent thing and not a non-existent thing, this Great Vehicle would not have emerged, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the eighth person is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the stream-enterer were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the stream-enterer is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the once-returner were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not depart having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the once-returner is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle departs having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the non-returner were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not depart having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the non-returner is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle goes forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the arhat were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not go forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, the arhat is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle goes forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, existence were not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, non-existence is not existence, therefore the Great Vehicle transcends and departs from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, a Pratyekabuddha were existence and not non-existence, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because a Pratyekabuddha is a non-entity and not an entity, the Mahāyāna goes forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the Bodhisattva were an entity and not a non-entity, this Mahāyāna would not go forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the Bodhisattva is a non-entity and not an entity, the Mahāyāna goes forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

If, Subhūti, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha were an existent entity and not a non-entity, this Mahāyāna would not have emerged, transcending the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is a non-entity and not an existent entity, therefore the Mahāyāna emerges, transcending the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the dharmadhātu were an existent entity and not a non-entity, this Mahāyāna would not have emerged, transcending the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, suchness (*tathatā*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not proceed forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But since, Subhūti, suchness is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle proceeds forth, surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. But because, Subhūti, the limit of reality is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle transcends and departs from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. Subhūti, if the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not transcend and depart from the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the inconceivable realm is a non-entity and not an entity, the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras. If, Subhūti, the world with its gods, humans, and asuras were an entity and not a non-entity, this Great Vehicle would not emerge having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
But since, Subhūti, the world with its gods, humans, and asuras is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the Great Vehicle emerges having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Subhūti, if for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first production of the thought of awakening until reaching the seat of awakening, all those productions of thought in this interval were entities, [then...]

"It is not the case that this Mahāyāna will set forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras by being a non-entity. For this reason, Subhūti, because all those productions of the thought of awakening—from the first production of the thought of a bodhisattva mahāsattva until reaching the seat of awakening—are neither non-entities nor entities, therefore the Mahāyāna sets forth having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras."

Subhūti, if the diamond-like gnosis of a bodhisattva mahāsattva were an entity and not a non-entity, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, having understood that all afflictions along with their residual impressions and continuities are not entities, would not attain the knowledge of all aspects; he would not emerge, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

Because, Subhūti, the diamond-like gnosis of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is a non-entity and not an entity, therefore the bodhisattva mahāsattva, having realized that all afflictions along with their latencies and continuities are non-entities, attains the knowledge of all aspects. Having surpassed the world of gods, humans, and asuras, he goes forth.

Subhūti, if the thirty-two marks of a great man belonging to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, were an existent and not a non-existent, then this Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, would not have outshone the world with its gods, humans, and asuras by means of his splendor and majesty, nor would he have shone, blazed, and radiated.

Therefore, Subhūti, the thirty-two marks of a great man belonging to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, are non-existence, not existence; therefore, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, shines, blazes, and radiates with splendor and glory.

Subhūti, if the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One were an existent and not a non-existent, then the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One would not have pervaded world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā. But because, Subhūti, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One is a non-existent and not an existent, therefore the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One [pervades] world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.

It radiates from the navel of the world-system. Subhūti, if the voice of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, were something existent and not non-existent, then the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One would not have made himself known by his voice throughout immeasurable and incalculable world-systems in the ten directions.

Therefore, Subhūti, because the voice of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, endowed with sixty qualities, is neither a non-entity nor an entity, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, makes himself heard by his voice throughout immeasurable and incalculable world-systems in the ten directions.

Subhūti, if the wheel of Dharma of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, were an existent thing and not a non-existent thing, then this wheel of Dharma would not have been turned by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; it could not be turned by anyone in the world in accordance with the Dharma—whether by a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a deva, a Māra, a Brahmā, or anyone else.

Because, Subhūti, the wheel of Dharma of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, is neither a non-entity nor an entity, therefore the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, turns the wheel of Dharma which cannot be turned back by any ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, or anyone else in the world in accordance with the Dharma.

Subhūti, if beings were non-existent as non-existence, for whose sake would the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, have turned the wheel of Dharma? Those beings would not have been led to final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder. But because, Subhūti, beings are neither non-existence nor existence—for whose sake the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has turned the wheel of Dharma—therefore those beings have entered final nirvāṇa, are entering final nirvāṇa, and will enter final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder.

Furthermore, as for what Subhūti said: "That vehicle is equal to space. It is so, Subhūti; it is so. That vehicle is equal to space. Just as, Subhūti, for space no eastern direction is discerned, nor a southern, nor a western, nor a northern, nor an upward, nor a downward, nor intermediate directions are discerned; even so, Subhūti, for that Great Vehicle no eastern direction is discerned, nor a southern, nor a western, nor a northern, nor intermediate directions are discerned. Therefore, it is called "that vehicle is equal to space."

Subhūti, just as space is neither blue, nor yellow, nor red, nor white, nor crimson, nor the color of crystal or silver, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither blue, nor yellow, nor red, nor white, nor crimson, nor the color of crystal or silver; therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, just as space is neither past, nor future, nor present, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither past, nor future, nor present; therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as space has no decrease, no increase, and no diminution, even so that Great Vehicle has no decrease, no increase, and no diminution; therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, just as space has neither defilement nor purification, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle has neither defilement nor purification; therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as in space no arising, no cessation, no staying, no persisting, and no alteration of staying is perceived.

In the same way, Subhūti, of that Great Vehicle (mahāyāna), neither arising, nor cessation, nor staying, nor remaining, nor alteration of staying is perceived. Therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Just as, Subhūti, space is neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor indeterminate, even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor indeterminate; therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.
Subhūti, just as space is not seen, not heard, not thought, and not cognized, even so, Subhūti, is that Great Vehicle.

That vehicle has not been seen, nor heard, nor thought, nor cognized; therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as space is not to be known, not to be unknown, not to be cognized, not to be fully understood, not to be realized, not to be abandoned, and not to be cultivated—exactly so, Subhūti, this Great Vehicle is not to be known, not to be unknown, not to be cognized, not to be fully understood, not to be realized, not to be abandoned, and not to be cultivated.

Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as space is neither a karmic maturation nor subject to the nature of maturation, even so, Subhūti, this Great Vehicle is neither a karmic maturation nor subject to the nature of maturation; therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, it is just as if space were not included within the realm of desire, not included within the realm of form, and not included within the formless realm; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is not included within the realm of desire, not included within the realm of form, and not included within the formless realm. Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, space is neither with passion nor free from passion, neither with hatred nor free from hatred, neither with delusion nor free from delusion; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither with passion nor free from passion, neither with hatred nor free from hatred, neither with delusion nor free from delusion. Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, in space there is no first production of the thought of awakening, nor a second, nor a third, nor a fourth, nor a fifth, nor a sixth, nor a seventh, nor an eighth, nor a ninth, nor a tenth production of the thought of awakening; even so, Subhūti, in that Great Vehicle there is no first production of the thought of awakening, nor a second, nor a third, nor a fourth, nor a fifth, nor a sixth, nor a seventh, nor an eighth, nor a ninth, nor a tenth production of the thought of awakening.

Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as in space there is no stage of bright insight (*śuklavidarśanā-bhūmi*), no stage of the lineage (*gotra-bhūmi*), no stage of the eighth person (*aṣṭamaka-bhūmi*), no stage of seeing (*darśana-bhūmi*), no stage of refinement (*tanu-bhūmi*), no stage of freedom from passion (*vītarāga-bhūmi*), and no stage of one who has completed what was to be done (*kṛtāvi-bhūmi*); even so, Subhūti, in that Great Vehicle there is no stage of bright insight, no stage of the lineage, no stage of the eighth person, no stage of seeing, no stage of refinement, and no stage of one who has completed what was to be done. Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, just as in space there is no fruit of stream-entry, no fruit of once-returning, no fruit of non-returning, and no state of arhatship, even so, Subhūti, in that Great Vehicle there is no fruit of stream-entry, no fruit of once-returning, and no fruit of non-returning; therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, just as in space there is no stage of a śrāvaka, no stage of a pratyekabuddha, no stage of a bodhisattva, and no stage of a perfectly awakened buddha, even so, Subhūti, in that Great Vehicle there is no stage of a śrāvaka, no stage of a pratyekabuddha, no stage of a bodhisattva, and no stage of a perfectly awakened buddha; therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, space is neither material nor non-material, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant, neither joined nor disjoined; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither material nor non-material, neither visible nor invisible, neither resistant nor non-resistant, neither joined nor disjoined. Therefore, that vehicle is said to be equal to space.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, space is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, and neither pure nor impure; even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasure nor suffering, neither self nor non-self, and neither pure nor impure. Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space.

Subhūti, it is just as, for example, space is neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither wishless nor non-wishless; even so, that Great Vehicle is neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither wishless nor non-wishless. Therefore, that vehicle is said to be equal to space. Subhūti, it is just as, for example, space is neither peaceful nor unpeaceful, neither secluded nor unsecluded;
even so, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither peaceful nor unpeaceful, neither secluded nor unsecluded.

Therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as space is neither light nor darkness, even so, Subhūti, this Great Vehicle is neither light nor darkness; therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as space is not apprehended, even so this Great Vehicle is not apprehended; therefore, it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. Subhūti, just as space is neither expressible nor inexpressible, [so too is this Great Vehicle].

In the same way, Subhūti, that Great Vehicle is neither an expression nor a non-expression. Therefore it is said that this vehicle is equal to space. By this method, Subhūti, that vehicle which is the Great Vehicle is equal to space.

As for what Subhūti has said: "Just as there is room in space for immeasurable and incalculable beings, even so there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings"—it is so, Subhūti, it is so. Just as there is room in space for immeasurable and incalculable beings, even so there is room in this Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Subhūti, by the non-existence of sentient beings, the non-existence of space should be understood; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle should be understood. By this method as well, there is room within that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable realities. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, those who are sentient beings, that which is space, and that which is the Great Vehicle—all these are not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by reason of the immeasurability of sentient beings, the immeasurability of space should be known; by reason of the immeasurability of space, the immeasurability of the Mahāyāna should be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room within that Mahāyāna for immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, those who are sentient beings, that which is space, and that which is the Mahāyāna—all that is not apprehended. Furthermore, Subhūti, by reason of the boundlessness of sentient beings, the boundlessness of space [should be known].

It should be known that because space is immeasurable, the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna) is immeasurable. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, both that which is space and that which is the Great Vehicle—all this is non-apprehendable. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of sentient beings, the non-existence of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) should be known.

Through the non-existence of the *dharmadhātu*, the non-existence of space is to be understood; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be understood; through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable (*aprameya*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is to be understood; and through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the limitless (*aparimāṇa*) is to be understood. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Mahāyāna for immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings.

For what reason? It is because, Subhūti, those beings who exist, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), space, the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), the immeasurable, the incalculable, and the infinite—all these are non-apprehendable. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of beings, the non-existence of suchness (*tathatā*) is to be known; by the non-existence of suchness, the non-existence of space is to be known; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle is to be known; and by the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known; through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the limitless is to be known; and through the non-existence of all phenomena, the non-existence of all things is to be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? It is because, Subhūti, those beings, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), space, the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), the immeasurable, the incalculable, and the limitless—all these are non-apprehendible. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of beings, the non-existence of suchness (*tathatā*) is to be known; by the non-existence of suchness, the non-existence of space is to be known; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle is to be known; by the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be known; and by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known.

It should be understood that through the non-existence of the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*), the non-existence of the immeasurable (*aparimāṇa*) is to be understood; and through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) is to be understood. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

Why is that? Because, Subhūti, those who are beings, that which is suchness (*tathatā*), that which is space (*ākāśa*), that which is the Great Vehicle, that which is the immeasurable, that which is the incalculable, that which is the immeasurable, and all phenomena—all of this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by means of the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by means of the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a man is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person (*mānava*), the non-existence of the agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler (*vedaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower (*jñaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the limit of reality, the non-existence of space (*ākāśa*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is to be understood; and through the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable (*aprameya*) is to be understood.

By the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known; by the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the limitless is to be known; by the non-existence of the limitless, the non-existence of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) is to be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, that which is called a self, that which is called a being, that which is called a life-soul, that which is called a creature, that which is called a nourisher, that which is called a person, and that which is called an individual—[all these are non-existent].

Whoever is a human being and whoever is a person; whoever is an agent and whoever is a non-agent; whoever is a knower and whoever is a seer; and whatever is the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), and whatever is space, and whatever is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), and whatever is immeasurable, and whatever is incalculable, and whatever is boundless, and whatever are all phenomena (*sarvadharma*)—all this is not apprehended. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self (*ātman*), the non-existence of a sentient being (*sattva*) is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul (*jīva*) is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature (*jantu*) is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher (*poṣa*) is to be known.

Through the non-existence of a nourisher (*poṣa*), the non-existence of a person (*puruṣa*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of a soul (*pudgala*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a soul, the non-existence of a human being (*manuja*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a human being, the non-existence of a youth (*mānava*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a youth, the non-existence of an agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of an agent, the non-existence of an experiencer (*vedaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of an experiencer, the non-existence of a knower (*jñaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a knower, the non-existence of a seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; and through the non-existence of a seer, the non-existence of the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*) is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the inconceivable realm, the non-existence of form should be understood; through the non-existence of form, the non-existence of feeling should be understood; through the non-existence of feeling, the non-existence of perception should be understood; through the non-existence of perception, the non-existence of mental formations should be understood; through the non-existence of mental formations, the non-existence of consciousness should be understood; through the non-existence of consciousness, the non-existence of space should be understood; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle should be understood; and through the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be understood.

Through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known; through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the limitless is to be known; through the non-existence of the limitless, the non-existence of all phenomena is to be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a sentient being, that which is a living soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, that which is a seer, as well as the inconceivable realm, and that which is form, and that which is feeling, and that which is perception—[all these are non-existent].

Whatever are the formative forces (*saṃskāra*), whatever is consciousness (*vijñāna*), whatever is space (*ākāśa*), whatever is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), whatever is immeasurable (*aprameya*), whatever is incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*), whatever is infinite (*aparimāṇa*), and whatever are all phenomena (*sarvadharma*)—all this is not apprehended. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self (*ātman*), the non-existence of a sentient being (*sattva*) is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul (*jīva*) is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature (*jantu*) is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person (*poṣa*) is to be known.

Through the non-existence of a nourisher (*poṣa*), the non-existence of a person (*puruṣa*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of a soul (*pudgala*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a soul, the non-existence of a human (*manuja*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a youth (*mānava*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a youth, the non-existence of an agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of an agent, the non-existence of an experiencer (*vedaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of an experiencer, the non-existence of a knower (*jñaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a knower, the non-existence of a seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of a seer, the non-existence of the eye (*cakṣus*) is to be understood.

By the non-existence of the eye, the non-existence of the ear is to be known; by the non-existence of the ear, the non-existence of the nose is to be known; by the non-existence of the nose, the non-existence of the tongue is to be known; by the non-existence of the tongue, the non-existence of the body is to be known; by the non-existence of the body, the non-existence of the mind is to be known; by the non-existence of the mind, the non-existence of space is to be known; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be known; by the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be known; by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be known; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena should be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, and that which is a sentient being, and that which is a living soul, and that which is a creature, and that which is a nourisher, and that which is a person, and that which is an individual, and that which is a human, and that which is a youth, and that which is an agent, and that which is an experiencer, and that which is a knower, and that which is a seer; and that which is the eye, and that which is the ear, and that which is the nose, and that which is the tongue, and that which is the body, and that which is the mind.
That which is space, that which is the Mahāyāna, that which is immeasurable, that which is incalculable, that which is infinite, and all dharmas—all that is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a youth is to be known.

By the non-existence of the person, the non-existence of the agent is to be understood; by the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler is to be understood; by the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; by the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer is to be understood; by the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of form is to be understood; by the non-existence of form, the non-existence of sound is to be understood; by the non-existence of sound, the non-existence of odor is to be understood; by the non-existence of odor, the non-existence of taste is to be understood; by the non-existence of taste, the non-existence of tangibles is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of contact, the non-existence of phenomena (*dharma*) is to be known; through the non-existence of phenomena, the non-existence of space (*ākāśa*) is to be known; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be known; through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable (*aprameya*) is to be known; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is to be known; through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the limitless (*aparimāṇa*) is to be known; and through the non-existence of the limitless, the non-existence of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) is to be known.

By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the self and the being and the life-soul and the creature and the nourisher and the person and the individual and the human and the man and the agent and the feeler and the knower and the seer, and form and sound and smell and taste and touch and mental phenomena, and space and—
That which is the Mahāyāna—whether it be immeasurable, incalculable, or infinite—and all dharmas: all of this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a descendant of Manu is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person (*mānava*), the non-existence of the agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler (*vedaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower (*jānaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of eye-consciousness (*cakṣurvijñāna*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of eye-consciousness, the non-existence of ear-consciousness (*śrotravijñāna*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of ear-consciousness, the non-existence of nose-consciousness (*ghrāṇavijñāna*) is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of olfactory consciousness, the non-existence of gustatory consciousness is to be known; through the non-existence of gustatory consciousness, the non-existence of tactile consciousness is to be known; through the non-existence of tactile consciousness, the non-existence of mental consciousness is to be known; through the non-existence of mental consciousness, the non-existence of space is to be known; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be known; through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be known; and through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known.

The non-existence of the immeasurable should be understood through the non-existence of the incalculable; the non-existence of all phenomena should be understood through the non-existence of the immeasurable. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in the Mahāyāna for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

Why is that? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a being, that which is a soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, and that which is a seer [are all non-existent].

That which is eye-consciousness, that which is ear-consciousness, that which is nose-consciousness, that which is tongue-consciousness, that which is body-consciousness, that which is mind-consciousness, that which is space, that which is the Great Vehicle, that which is immeasurable, that which is incalculable, that which is infinite, and all dharmas—all this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher is to be known; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a descendant of Manu is to be known.

By the non-existence of the person (*mānava*), the non-existence of the agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler (*vedaka*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower (*jñaka*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of visual contact (*cakṣuḥ-saṃsparśa*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of visual contact, the non-existence of auditory contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of auditory contact, the non-existence of olfactory contact (*ghrāṇa-saṃsparśa*) is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of olfactory contact, the non-existence of gustatory contact should be known; through the non-existence of gustatory contact, the non-existence of tactile contact should be known; through the non-existence of tactile contact, the non-existence of mental contact should be known; through the non-existence of mental contact, the non-existence of space should be known; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle should be known; through the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be known; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable should be known.

By the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be understood; by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) should be understood. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings. For what reason? Because that which is a self, that which is a being, and that which is...

And what is the living soul (*jīva*), and what is the creature (*jantu*), and what is the nourished being (*poṣa*), and what is the person (*puruṣa*), and what is the individual (*pudgala*), and what is the human (*manuja*), and what is the descendant of Manu (*mānava*), and what is the agent (*kāraka*), and what is the experiencer (*vedaka*), and what is the knower (*jñātṛ*), and what is the seer (*paśyaka*), and what is visual contact (*cakṣuḥ-saṃsparśa*), and what is auditory contact (*śrotra-saṃsparśa*), and what is olfactory contact (*ghrāṇa-saṃsparśa*), and what is gustatory contact (*jihvā-saṃsparśa*), and what is tactile contact (*kāya-saṃsparśa*), and what is mental contact (*manaḥ-saṃsparśa*), and what is space (*ākāśa*), and what is the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), and what is the immeasurable (*aprameya*), and what is the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*)... [and so forth].

And that which is immeasurable, and all dharmas—all this is not apprehended. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human being is to be known; by the non-existence of a human being, the non-existence of a descendant of Manu is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person, the non-existence of the agent is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler is to be understood; through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of sensation born of eye-contact is to be understood; and through the non-existence of sensation born of eye-contact, the non-existence of sensation born of ear-contact is to be understood.

By means of the non-existence of feeling born of ear-contact, the non-existence of feeling born of nose-contact is to be understood; by means of the non-existence of feeling born of nose-contact, the non-existence of feeling born of tongue-contact is to be understood; by means of the non-existence of feeling born of tongue-contact, the non-existence of feeling born of body-contact is to be understood; by means of the non-existence of feeling born of body-contact, the non-existence of feeling born of mind-contact is to be understood; and by means of the non-existence of feeling born of mind-contact, the non-existence of space is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be understood; through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be understood; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be understood; through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the infinite is to be understood; and through the non-existence of the infinite, the non-existence of all phenomena is to be understood. Subhūti, by this very method, there is room in that Mahāyāna for immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a sentient being, that which is a living soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, that which is a seer, and furthermore, whatever feeling born of eye-contact, whatever feeling born of ear-contact, whatever feeling born of nose-contact, and whatever feeling born of tongue-contact—[all these are non-existent].

The feeling born of body-contact and the feeling born of mind-contact, as well as space, the Great Vehicle, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the boundless, and all phenomena—all this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher is to be known; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a youth is to be known.

Through the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of the agent is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler is to be understood; through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the earth element is to be understood; through the non-existence of the earth element, the non-existence of the water element is to be understood; through the non-existence of the water element, the non-existence of the fire element is to be understood; through the non-existence of the fire element, the non-existence of the wind element is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the wind element, the non-existence of the space element is to be known; through the non-existence of the space element, the non-existence of the consciousness element is to be known; through the non-existence of the consciousness element, the non-existence of space is to be known; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be known; through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna...

The non-existence of the immeasurable should be understood; by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable should be understood; by the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the infinite should be understood; and by the non-existence of the infinite, the non-existence of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) should be understood. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a sentient being, that which is a living soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, that which is a seer; and that which is the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, and the consciousness element; and that which is space, and that which is the Great Vehicle—[all these are non-dual].
That which is immeasurable, that which is incalculable, that which is limitless, and all phenomena—all this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher is to be known; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a descendant of Manu is to be known.

By the non-existence of the person, the non-existence of the agent is to be understood; by the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler is to be understood; by the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; by the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer is to be understood; by the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of ignorance is to be understood; by the non-existence of ignorance, the non-existence of formative forces is to be understood; by the non-existence of formative forces, the non-existence of consciousness is to be understood; by the non-existence of consciousness, the non-existence of name-and-form is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of name-and-form, the non-existence of the six sense bases is to be understood; through the non-existence of the six sense bases, the non-existence of contact is to be understood; through the non-existence of contact, the non-existence of feeling is to be understood; through the non-existence of feeling...

The non-existence of craving is to be understood; by the non-existence of craving, the non-existence of grasping is to be understood; by the non-existence of grasping, the non-existence of becoming is to be understood; by the non-existence of becoming, the non-existence of birth is to be understood; by the non-existence of birth, the non-existence of old age and death is to be understood; by the non-existence of old age and death, the non-existence of space is to be understood; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle is to be understood; by the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be understood; by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be understood; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) is to be understood. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a being, that which is a soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, and that which is an agent—[all these are non-existent].

The one who feels, the one who knows, and the one who sees; ignorance, the formative forces, consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, sensation, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death; space, the Great Vehicle, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the infinite, and all phenomena—all this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher is to be known; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a youth is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person, the non-existence of the agent is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler is to be understood; through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower—
