The non-existence of the seer is to be understood; by the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the perfection of generosity is to be understood; by the non-existence of the perfection of generosity, the non-existence of the perfection of ethical discipline is to be understood; by the non-existence of the perfection of ethical discipline, the non-existence of the perfection of patience is to be understood; by the non-existence of the perfection of patience, the non-existence of the perfection of vigor is to be understood; by the non-existence of the perfection of vigor, the non-existence of the perfection of meditative concentration is to be understood; by the non-existence of the perfection of meditative concentration, the non-existence of the perfection of wisdom is to be understood.

By the non-existence of the perfection of wisdom, the non-existence of space should be known; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna should be known; by the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be known; by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable should be known; by the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the infinite should be known; by the non-existence of the infinite, the non-existence of all phenomena should be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Mahāyāna for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because that which is the self, that which is the sentient being, that which is the life-principle, that which is the creature, that which is the nourisher, that which is the person, that which is the individual, that which is the human, that which is the youth, that which is the agent, that which is the feeler, that which is the knower, that which is the seer, and that which is the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of wisdom, and that which is space—[all these are non-dual].

That which is the Mahāyāna—whether it be immeasurable, incalculable, or infinite—and all dharmas: all this is not apprehended. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher is to be known; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual...

The non-existence of a human being is to be understood; by the non-existence of a human being, the non-existence of a youth is to be understood; by the non-existence of a youth, the non-existence of an agent is to be understood; by the non-existence of an agent, the non-existence of an experiencer is to be understood; by the non-existence of an experiencer, the non-existence of a knower is to be understood; by the non-existence of a knower, the non-existence of a seer is to be understood; by the non-existence of a seer, the non-existence of internal emptiness is to be understood; by the non-existence of internal emptiness, the non-existence of external emptiness is to be understood.

By the non-existence of external emptiness, the non-existence of internal-external emptiness is to be known; by the non-existence of internal-external emptiness, the non-existence of the emptiness of emptiness is to be known; by the non-existence of the emptiness of emptiness, the non-existence of great emptiness is to be known; by the non-existence of great emptiness, the non-existence of ultimate emptiness is to be known; by the non-existence of ultimate emptiness, the non-existence of conditioned emptiness is to be known; by the non-existence of conditioned emptiness, the non-existence of unconditioned emptiness is to be known.

By the existence of the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*), the existence of absolute emptiness (*atyanta-śūnyatā*) is to be known; by the existence of absolute emptiness, the existence of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end (*anavarāgra-śūnyatā*) is to be known; by the existence of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, the existence of the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) is to be known; by the existence of the emptiness of non-dispersal, the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*) is to be known; by the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the existence of the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) is to be known; and by the existence of the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) is to be known.

By the existence of the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*), the existence of the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*) is to be known. By the existence of the emptiness of non-apprehension, the existence of the emptiness of non-existence (*abhāva-śūnyatā*) is to be known. By the existence of the emptiness of non-existence, the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnyatā*) is to be known. By the existence of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the existence of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā*) is to be known. By the existence of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, the non-existence of space (*ākāśa*) is to be known. By the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be known; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the infinite should be known; and through the non-existence of the infinite, the non-existence of all phenomena should be known.

By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, and that which is a being, and that which is a soul, and that which is a creature, and that which is a nourisher, and that which is a person, and that which is an individual, and that which is a human, and that which is a youth, and that which is an agent, and that which is an experiencer, and that which is a knower, and that which is a seer, as well as internal emptiness and external emptiness—[all these are non-existent].

And internal-external emptiness, and the emptiness of emptiness, and great emptiness, and the emptiness of the ultimate, and the emptiness of the conditioned, and the emptiness of the unconditioned, and absolute emptiness, and the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, and the emptiness of non-dispersal, and the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of all phenomena, and the emptiness of specific characteristics, and the emptiness of non-apprehension, and the emptiness of non-existence, and the emptiness of self-nature.

The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, that which is space, that which is the Great Vehicle, that which is immeasurable, that which is incalculable, that which is infinite, and all phenomena—all of this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher is to be known; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a descendant of Manu is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person (*mānava*), the non-existence of the agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the feeler (*vedaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower (*jñaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the foundations of mindfulness, the non-existence of the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the right efforts, the non-existence of the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the bases of psychic power, the non-existence of the faculties (*indriya*) [is to be understood].

It should be understood that because the faculties (*indriya*) are non-existent, the powers (*bala*) are non-existent; because the powers are non-existent, the factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) are non-existent; because the factors of enlightenment are non-existent, the noble eightfold path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*) is non-existent; because the noble eightfold path is non-existent, space (*ākāśa*) is non-existent; because space is non-existent, the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is non-existent; because the Great Vehicle is non-existent, the immeasurable (*aprameya*) is non-existent; and because the immeasurable is non-existent, the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is non-existent.

Through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be known; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena is to be known. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because that which is the self, that which is the sentient being, that which is the living soul, that which is the creature, that which is the nourisher, that which is the person, that which is the individual, that which is the human, that which is the youth, that which is the agent, that which is the feeler, that which is the knower, that which is the seer; and those which are the foundations of mindfulness, those which are the right efforts, those which are the bases of psychic power, those which are the faculties, those which are the powers, those which are the factors of enlightenment, that which is the noble eightfold path, that which is space, and that which is the Great Vehicle—[all these are non-dual].
That which is immeasurable, that which is incalculable, that which is limitless, and all dharmas—all this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by means of the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by means of the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by means of the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a man is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person, the non-existence of the agent is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the experiencer is to be understood; through the non-existence of the experiencer, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the noble truths is to be understood.

Due to the non-existence of the noble truths, the non-existence of the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) is to be understood; due to the non-existence of the meditative absorptions, the non-existence of the immeasurables (apramāṇa) is to be understood; due to the non-existence of the immeasurables, the non-existence of the formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) is to be understood; due to the non-existence of the formless attainments, the non-existence of the liberations (vimokṣa) is to be understood; due to the non-existence of the liberations, the non-existence of the successive dwellings and attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti) is to be understood; and due to the non-existence of the successive dwellings and attainments, the non-existence of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—the non-existence of the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) is to be understood. Through the non-existence of the superknowledges, the non-existence of meditative concentrations (*samādhi*) is to be understood. Through the non-existence of meditative concentrations, the non-existence of the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*) is to be understood. Through the non-existence of the gateways of mnemonic formulas, the non-existence of space is to be understood. Through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) is to be understood. Through the non-existence of the Great Vehicle, the non-existence of the immeasurable (*aprameya*) is to be understood. Through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be understood; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena should be understood. By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a sentient being, that which is a living soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, that which is a seer; and those which are the noble truths, those which are the immeasurables, those which are the formless attainments, those which are the liberations, those which are the serial attainments of meditative dwelling, and those which are the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—[are all non-existent].

And the superknowledges, and the meditative concentrations, and the gateways of the dhāraṇīs, and space, and the Great Vehicle, and that which is immeasurable, and that which is incalculable, and that which is limitless, and all phenomena—all this is not apprehended. Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, [the non-existence of a life-force is to be known].

The non-existence of a living being (*jīva*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of a living being, the non-existence of a creature (*jantu*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a nourisher (*poṣa*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of a nourisher, the non-existence of a person (*puruṣa*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual (*pudgala*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human (*manuja*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a youth (*mānava*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of a youth, the non-existence of an agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; and by the non-existence of an agent, the non-existence of an experiencer (*vedaka*) is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the feeler, the non-existence of the knower is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata is to be understood; through the non-existence of the powers of a Tathāgata, the non-existence of the grounds of self-confidence is to be understood; through the non-existence of the grounds of self-confidence, the non-existence of the analytical knowledges is to be understood; through the non-existence of the analytical knowledges, the non-existence of great compassion is to be understood; through the non-existence of great compassion, the non-existence of the unique qualities of a Buddha is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the unique qualities of a Buddha, the non-existence of space is to be known; through the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be known; through the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be known; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable is to be known; through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the limitless is to be known; and through the non-existence of the limitless, the non-existence of all phenomena is to be known.

By this method also, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a being, that which is a soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, that which is a seer, as well as the powers of a Tathāgata, the grounds of self-confidence, and those... [which are]... (are all non-existent).

The analytical knowledges, great compassion, the unique qualities of a Buddha, space, the Great Vehicle, the immeasurable, the incalculable, the limitless, and all phenomena—all this is not apprehended.

Furthermore, Subhūti, by the non-existence of a self, the non-existence of a sentient being is to be known; by the non-existence of a sentient being, the non-existence of a living soul is to be known; by the non-existence of a living soul, the non-existence of a creature is to be known; by the non-existence of a creature, the non-existence of a person is to be known; by the non-existence of a person, the non-existence of an individual is to be known; by the non-existence of an individual, the non-existence of a human is to be known; by the non-existence of a human, the non-existence of a youth is to be known.

Through the non-existence of the person (*mānava*), the non-existence of the agent (*kāraka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the agent, the non-existence of the experiencer (*vedaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the experiencer, the non-existence of the knower (*jñaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the knower, the non-existence of the seer (*paśyaka*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the seer, the non-existence of the factors of the stage of the lineage (*gotrabhū-dharma*) is to be understood; through the non-existence of the factors of the stage of the lineage, the non-existence of the factors of the eighth stage (*aṣṭamaka-dharma*) is to be understood; and through the non-existence of the factors of the eighth stage, the non-existence of the stage of vision (*darśanabhūmi*) is to be understood.

By the non-existence of the stage of vision (*darśanabhūmi*), the non-existence of the stage of refinement (*tanubhūmi*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the stage of refinement, the non-existence of the stage free from passion (*vītarāgabhūmi*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the stage free from passion, the non-existence of the stage of one who has accomplished what was to be done (*kṛtāvibhūmi*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of the stage of one who has accomplished what was to be done, the non-existence of space (*ākāśa*) is to be understood; by the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the Mahāyāna is to be understood; by the non-existence of the Mahāyāna, the non-existence of the immeasurable (*aprameya*) is to be understood; and by the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) is to be understood.

Through the non-existence of the incalculable, the non-existence of the immeasurable should be understood; through the non-existence of the immeasurable, the non-existence of all phenomena should be understood. By this method as well, Subhūti, there is room in that Great Vehicle for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, that which is a self, that which is a sentient being, that which is a living soul, that which is a creature, that which is a nourisher, that which is a person, that which is an individual, that which is a human, that which is a youth, that which is an agent, that which is an experiencer, that which is a knower, that which is a seer, as well as the dharmas of the lineage-stage, the dharmas of the eighth-rank stage, the dharmas of the stage of vision, the dharmas of the stage of refinement, the dharmas of the stage free from passion, and the dharmas of one who has done what was to be done—[all these are non-existent].
That which is space, that which is the Great Vehicle, that which is immeasurable, that which is incalculable, that which is infinite, and all phenomena—all of this is not apprehended.

The suchness of the superknowledges does not come from anywhere, does not go anywhere, and does not abide anywhere. The self-nature of the superknowledges does not come from anywhere, does not go anywhere, and does not abide anywhere.

The characteristic of the superknowledges does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The meditative concentrations do not come from anywhere, they do not go anywhere, and they do not abide anywhere. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the meditative concentrations does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The suchness of the meditative concentrations does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Nor does the self-nature of the meditative concentrations [come from anywhere, go anywhere, or abide anywhere].

It comes from nowhere; it goes nowhere; it abides nowhere. The characteristic of the meditative absorptions (*samādhi*) does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere; it abides nowhere. The gateways of the mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇīmukha*) do not come from anywhere; they go nowhere; they abide nowhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature (*prakṛti*) of the gateways of the mnemonic formulas does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere; it abides nowhere.

The suchness of the gateways of dhāraṇī does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. The intrinsic nature of the gateways of dhāraṇī does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. The characteristic of the gateways of dhāraṇī does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. The ten powers of a Tathāgata do not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the nature of the ten powers of a Tathāgata does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The suchness of the ten powers of a Tathāgata does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The intrinsic nature of the ten powers of a Tathāgata does not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The characteristic of the ten powers of a Tathāgata does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The four fearlessnesses do not come from anywhere; they go nowhere and stay nowhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses does not come from anywhere, nor does it go anywhere, nor does it stay anywhere.

The suchness of the fearlessnesses does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The intrinsic nature of the fearlessnesses does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The characteristic of the fearlessnesses does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not...

It abides nowhere; the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) do not come from anywhere, they do not go anywhere, and they do not abide anywhere. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature (*prakṛti*) of the four analytical knowledges does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The suchness (*tathatā*) of the four analytical knowledges does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere.

The intrinsic nature of the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The characteristic of the four analytical knowledges does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of great compassion does not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The suchness of great compassion does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The intrinsic nature of great compassion does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The characteristic of great compassion does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere.

The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha do not come from anywhere, they do not go anywhere, and they do not abide anywhere. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the intrinsic nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha does not come from anywhere, does not go anywhere, and does not abide anywhere. Furthermore, the suchness of the unique qualities of a Buddha does not come from anywhere, does not go anywhere, and does not abide anywhere.

The intrinsic nature of the unique qualities of a Buddha does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. The characteristic of the unique qualities of a Buddha does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. Subhūti, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not [abide anywhere].

In some places it remains. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the nature of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not remain anywhere. The suchness (tathatā) of the dharma-realm does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not remain anywhere. The intrinsic nature (svabhāva) of the dharma-realm does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not remain anywhere.

The characteristic of the dharma-realm does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Subhūti, suchness does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the nature of suchness does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Nor does the suchness of suchness come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of suchness (*tathatā*) does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*) of suchness does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the nature of the limit of reality does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The suchness of the limit of reality does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The intrinsic nature of the limit of reality does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The characteristic of the limit of reality does not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Subhūti, the inconceivable realm does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the nature of the inconceivable realm does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The suchness of the inconceivable realm does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere.

The intrinsic nature of the inconceivable realm does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. The characteristic of the inconceivable realm does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. Subhūti, awakening does not come from anywhere; it does not go anywhere; it does not abide anywhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the nature of awakening does not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The suchness of awakening does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The intrinsic nature of awakening does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The characteristic of awakening does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Subhūti, the Buddha does not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the nature (*prakṛti*) of a Buddha does not come from anywhere, nor does it go anywhere, nor does it stay anywhere. The suchness (*tathatā*) of a Buddha does not come from anywhere, nor does it go anywhere, nor does it stay anywhere. The intrinsic being (*svabhāva*) of a Buddha does not come from anywhere, nor does it go anywhere, nor does it stay anywhere.

The characteristic of a Buddha does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Subhūti, the conditioned does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the conditioned does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere. The suchness of the conditioned does not come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the conditioned does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*) of the conditioned does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Furthermore, Subhūti, the unconditioned does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the nature of the unconditioned does not come from anywhere, it does not go anywhere, and it does not abide anywhere; nor does the suchness of the unconditioned come from anywhere.

It goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. The characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*) of the unconditioned does not come from anywhere; it goes nowhere and stays nowhere. Thus, of that Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*), neither coming nor going is perceived, nor is staying perceived.

As for what Subhūti has said: "Neither a beginning of this vehicle is perceived, nor an end is perceived, nor a middle is perceived; because of the equality of the time-periods, this vehicle is the Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna). Therefore, it is called the 'Great Vehicle'. It is so, Subhūti, it is so. Neither a beginning of this vehicle is perceived, nor an end is perceived, nor a middle is perceived.

This vehicle is the equality of the three times; therefore, it is called the Mahāyāna. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, the past time is empty of the past; the future time is empty of the future; the present time is empty of the present. The equality of the three times is empty of the equality of the three times. The Mahāyāna is empty of the Mahāyāna. The Bodhisattva is empty of the Bodhisattva.

Subhūti, emptiness is not one, nor two, nor three, nor four, nor five, nor six, nor seven, nor eight, nor nine, nor ten, nor is it distinct; therefore, this is the equality of the three times for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Herein, neither equality nor inequality is apprehended. Neither passion is apprehended nor the absence of passion; neither hatred is apprehended nor the absence of hatred; neither delusion is apprehended nor the absence of delusion; neither name is apprehended nor the absence of name.

The conditioned is not apprehended, nor is the unconditioned; the wholesome is not apprehended, nor is the unwholesome; the faulty is not apprehended, nor is the faultless; the tainted is not apprehended, nor is the untainted; the defiled is not apprehended, nor is the undefiled; the mundane is not apprehended, nor is the supramundane; arising is not apprehended, nor is cessation; affliction is not apprehended, nor is purification; indeed, nothing permanent is apprehended herein.

Neither impermanence nor permanence is perceived; neither pleasure nor suffering is perceived; neither self nor non-self is perceived; neither peace nor non-peace is perceived. Neither the desire realm is perceived nor the transcendence of the desire realm; neither the form realm is perceived nor the transcendence of the form realm; neither the formless realm is perceived nor the transcendence of the formless realm. Neither saṃsāra is perceived nor nirvāṇa. Why is that? Because its intrinsic nature is not perceived.

Subhūti, past form is empty of past form. Why is that? Because within emptiness, past form is not apprehended. Since even emptiness itself is empty and is not apprehended by way of emptiness, how much less could past form be apprehended within emptiness? Past feeling is empty of past feeling. Why is that? Because within emptiness, past feeling is not apprehended.

First of all, emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of being empty or non-empty; how much less, then, can past feeling be apprehended within emptiness? Past perception is empty of past perception. Why is that? Because past perception is not apprehended within emptiness. First of all, emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of being empty or non-empty; how much less, then, can past perception be apprehended within emptiness?

Past conditioned phenomena are empty of past conditioned phenomena. Why is that? Subhūti, it is because past conditioned phenomena are not apprehended within emptiness. Emptiness itself is empty; since emptiness is not apprehended by means of emptiness, how much less could past conditioned phenomena be apprehended within emptiness? Past consciousness is empty of past consciousness. Why is that? It is because past consciousness is not apprehended within emptiness.
First of all, emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of being empty or non-empty. How much less, then, can past consciousness be apprehended within emptiness?

Subhūti, future form is empty of future form. For what reason? Because future form is not apprehended within emptiness. First of all, emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of being empty or non-empty.

Furthermore, how could future form be apprehended within emptiness? Future feeling is empty of future feeling. For what reason? Because future feeling is not apprehended within emptiness. Indeed, even emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of emptiness; so how could future feeling be apprehended within emptiness? Future perception is empty of future perception.

For what reason? Subhūti, for future perception is not apprehended. Since emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of the emptiness of emptiness, how much less can future perception be apprehended within emptiness? Future conditioned phenomena are empty of future conditioned phenomena. For what reason? Subhūti, for future conditioned phenomena are not apprehended within emptiness. Since emptiness itself is not apprehended by way of the emptiness of emptiness, [how much less so are future phenomena].

Furthermore, how could future conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) be apprehended within emptiness? Future consciousness is not empty of consciousness within the future. Why is that? Subhūti, future consciousness is not apprehended within emptiness; for emptiness itself is not apprehended by means of emptiness. How then could future consciousness be apprehended within emptiness?

Subhūti, present form is empty of present form. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, in emptiness present form is not apprehended. Indeed, emptiness itself is empty and is not apprehended by way of emptiness; how much less, then, can present form be apprehended in emptiness? Present feeling is empty of present feeling.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, present feeling is not apprehended in emptiness. Indeed, emptiness itself is not apprehended by means of emptiness; how much less, then, can present feeling be apprehended in emptiness? Present perception is empty of present perception. For what reason? Because present perception is not apprehended in emptiness. Emptiness itself...

To that extent, emptiness is not apprehended by means of the emptiness of emptiness. How much less, then, can present perception be apprehended within emptiness? Present conditioned phenomena are empty of present conditioned phenomena. For what reason? Subhūti, it is because present conditioned phenomena are not apprehended within emptiness. To begin with, even emptiness itself is not apprehended by means of the emptiness of emptiness. How much less, then, can present conditioned phenomena be apprehended within emptiness?

Present consciousness is empty of present consciousness. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, in emptiness present consciousness is not apprehended; indeed, even emptiness itself is not apprehended as empty by means of emptiness. How much less, then, could present consciousness be apprehended within emptiness?

Subhūti, the perfection of generosity is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; the perfection of generosity is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the perfection of generosity is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the perfection of generosity is not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; within equality, the future time is not apprehended; within equality, the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, how could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended? And how could the present time be apprehended? The perfection of ethical discipline is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the perfection of ethical discipline is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the perfection of ethical discipline is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the perfection of ethical discipline is not apprehended.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, in equality the past time is not apprehended; in equality the future time is not apprehended; in equality the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, can the past time be apprehended in equality? How can the future time be apprehended? How can the present time be apprehended? From the perspective of the prior limit, the perfection of patience is not apprehended.

The perfection of patience is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; the perfection of patience is not apprehended from the perspective of the present; the perfection of patience is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. For what reason? Because, Subhūti, within equality the past time is not apprehended; within equality the future time is not apprehended; within equality the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, how could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended? How could the present time be apprehended? The perfection of vigor is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the perfection of vigor is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the perfection of vigor is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the perfection of vigor is not apprehended.

For what reason? Because, Subhūti, in equality the past time is not apprehended; in equality the future time is not apprehended; in equality the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time be apprehended? How could the present time be apprehended? From the perspective of the prior limit, the perfection of meditation is not apprehended.

The perfection of meditation is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the perfection of meditation is not apprehended from the perspective of the present; the perfection of meditation is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, in equality the past time is not apprehended; in equality the future time is not apprehended; in equality the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, how could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended? How could the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the perfection of wisdom is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the perfection of wisdom is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the perfection of wisdom is not apprehended. Why is that?

For this reason, Subhūti, within equality the past time is not apprehended; within equality the future time is not apprehended; within equality the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, can the past time be apprehended within equality? How can the future time be apprehended? How can the present time be apprehended?

Subhūti, internal emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; internal emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; internal emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, internal emptiness is not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, how could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended? How could the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, external emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; external emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; external emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, external emptiness is not apprehended.

Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; the present time is not apprehended. Furthermore, how could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended? How could the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit (*pūrvānta*), internal and external emptiness (*adhyātmabahirdhā-śūnyatā*) is not apprehended; from the perspective of the posterior limit (*aparānta*), internal and external emptiness is not apprehended.

Internal-external emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Internal-external emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, equality itself [is not apprehended] within equality.

It is not apprehended. How, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended? How could the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the emptiness of emptiness is not apprehended.

Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How then could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, great emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; great emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit.

Great emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Great emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended within equality?

Subhūti, ultimate emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; ultimate emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; ultimate emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Ultimate emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within that equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, from where could a past time be apprehended within equality? From where could a future time or a present time be apprehended? Subhūti, conditioned emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; conditioned emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; conditioned emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Conditioned emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. It is not so, Subhūti.

In equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, can the past time be apprehended in equality? How can the future time or the present time be apprehended in equality? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit (*pūrvānta*), the emptiness of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta-śūnyatā*) is not apprehended; from the perspective of the posterior limit (*aparānta*), the emptiness of the unconditioned is not apprehended.

Unconditioned emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Unconditioned emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended within equality?

Subhūti, absolute emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; absolute emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; absolute emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Absolute emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within that equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, from where could the past time be apprehended within equality? From where could the future time be apprehended, and from where could the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, beginningless and endless emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; beginningless and endless emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; beginningless and endless emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, beginningless and endless emptiness is not apprehended. Subhūti, the past time is not apprehended within equality.

Neither the future time nor the present time is perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less could the past time be perceived within equality? How could the future time be perceived, or the present time be perceived? Subhūti, non-dispersal emptiness is not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit; non-dispersal emptiness [is not perceived] from the perspective of the posterior limit.

It is not apprehended. Non-dispersal emptiness (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Non-dispersal emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; neither the future time nor the present time is apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended within equality?

Subhūti, intrinsic emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; intrinsic emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; intrinsic emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. In the equality of the three times, intrinsic emptiness is not apprehended. Subhūti, within that equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, from where could a past time be apprehended within equality? From where could a future time be apprehended, and from where could a present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the emptiness of all phenomena is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the emptiness of all phenomena is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the emptiness of all phenomena is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the emptiness of all phenomena is not apprehended.

Subhūti, in equality the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How the future time, or how the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit (*pūrvānta*), the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) is not apprehended; from the perspective of the posterior limit (*aparānta*), the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is not apprehended.

From the perspective of the present, the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is not apprehended; within the equality of the three times, the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics is not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended, nor is the future time, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality; how much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality?

From where is the future time [derived], and from where is the present time apprehended? Subhūti, non-apprehension-emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; non-apprehension-emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; non-apprehension-emptiness is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Non-apprehension-emptiness is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended.

Neither the future time nor the present time is perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less can the past time be perceived within equality? How can the future time be perceived, and how can the present time be perceived? Subhūti, non-existence emptiness is not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit; non-existence emptiness is not perceived from the perspective of the posterior limit; non-existence emptiness is not perceived from the perspective of the present.

In the equality of the three times, the emptiness of non-existence is not apprehended. Subhūti, in equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended.

Inferior-limit emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended; present-limit emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended; in the equality of the three times, emptiness of intrinsic nature is not apprehended. Subhūti, in that equality, the past time is not apprehended, nor is the future time, nor is the present time apprehended.

Even equality itself is not apprehended within equality; how much less, then, can the past time be apprehended within equality? How can the future time be apprehended, and how can the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not apprehended from the perspective of the present.

In the equality of the three times, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence is not apprehended. Subhūti, in equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended in equality?

Subhūti, the foundations of mindfulness are not apprehended from the perspective of the past; the foundations of mindfulness are not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the foundations of mindfulness are not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the foundations of mindfulness are not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, how could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time be apprehended, and how could the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*) are not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the right efforts are not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the right efforts are not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the right efforts are not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended.

Neither the future time nor the present time is perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less can the past time be perceived within equality? How can the future time be perceived, and how can the present time be perceived? Subhūti, the bases of psychic power (ṛddhipāda) are not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit; the bases of psychic power are not perceived from the perspective of the posterior limit; the bases of psychic power are not perceived from the perspective of the present.

In the equality of the three times, the bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*) are not apprehended. Subhūti, in equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended in equality? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit (*pūrvānta*), the faculties (*indriya*) are not apprehended.

The faculties are not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the faculties are not apprehended from the perspective of the present; [they are likewise not apprehended] in the equality of the three times.

The sense faculties are not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; and the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How then could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the powers are not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the powers are not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit.

The powers are not apprehended from the perspective of the present; the powers are not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended within equality?

Subhūti, the factors of enlightenment (bodhyaṅga) are not apprehended from the perspective of the past; the factors of enlightenment are not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the factors of enlightenment are not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the factors of enlightenment are not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended, nor is the future time, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, from where could the past time be apprehended within equality? From where could the future time be apprehended, or from where the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the Noble Eightfold Path is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the Noble Eightfold Path is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; the Noble Eightfold Path is not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the Noble Eightfold Path is not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended.

Neither the future time nor the present time is perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less could the past time be perceived within equality? How could the future time or the present time be perceived? Subhūti, the noble truths are not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit; the noble truths are not perceived from the perspective of the subsequent limit.

The noble truths are not apprehended in the present; the noble truths are not apprehended in the equality of the three times. Subhūti, in equality the past time is not apprehended, nor is the future time, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended in equality?

Subhūti, meditative absorptions (dhyāna) are not apprehended from the perspective of the past; meditative absorptions are not apprehended from the perspective of the future; meditative absorptions are not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Meditative absorptions are not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality?

From where is the future time [obtained], and from where is the present time perceived? Subhūti, from the perspective of the past limit (*pūrvānta*), immeasurable things are not perceived; from the perspective of the future limit (*aparānta*), immeasurable things are not perceived; from the perspective of the present, immeasurable things are not perceived; and within the equality of the three times (*tryadhvasamatā*), immeasurable things are not perceived. Subhūti, within that equality, the past time is not perceived, nor is the future time, nor is the present time perceived.

Even equality itself is not apprehended within equality; how much less, then, can the past time be apprehended within equality? How can the future time be apprehended, and how can the present time be apprehended? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit, the formless attainments are not apprehended; from the perspective of the subsequent limit, the formless attainments are not apprehended; from the perspective of the present, the formless attainments are not apprehended. Within the equality of the three times, the formless attainments are not apprehended.

Subhūti, in equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended?

Subhūti, the eight liberations are not apprehended from the perspective of the past; the eight liberations are not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the eight liberations are not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the eight liberations are not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality.

Furthermore, from where could a past time be apprehended within equality? From where could a future time be apprehended, or from where could a present time be apprehended? Subhūti, the nine successive attainments of meditative abiding are not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; the nine successive attainments of meditative abiding are not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; and the nine successive attainments of meditative abiding are not apprehended from the perspective of the present.

Within the equality of the three times, the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling are not apprehended. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended within equality?

Subhūti, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not apprehended from the perspective of the past. The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not apprehended from the perspective of the future. The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not apprehended from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are not apprehended. Subhūti, within that equality, the past time is not apprehended.

Neither the future time nor the present time is perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less can the past time be perceived within equality? How can the future time be perceived, and how can the present time be perceived? Subhūti, supernormal knowledge (*abhijñā*) is not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit (*pūrvānta*); supernormal knowledge is not perceived from the perspective of the posterior limit (*aparānta*); supernormal knowledge is not perceived from the perspective of the present. Supernormal knowledge is not perceived within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, the past is not [perceived] within equality.

The past time is not perceived; the future time is not perceived; the present time is not perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality. How, then, could the past time be perceived within equality? How could the future time be perceived? How could the present time be perceived? Subhūti, meditative absorptions (samādhis) are not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit; meditative absorptions are not perceived from the perspective of the posterior limit; meditative absorptions are not perceived from the perspective of the present.

In the equality of the three times, concentrations are not apprehended. Subhūti, in equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended; the present time is not apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, can the past time be apprehended in equality? How can the future time or the present time be apprehended in equality? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit, the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are not apprehended.

The gateways of dhāraṇī are not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the gateways of dhāraṇī are not apprehended from the perspective of the present; the gateways of dhāraṇī are not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality?

From where is the future time obtained, and from where is the present time obtained? Subhūti, the ten powers of a Tathāgata are not obtained from the past limit; the ten powers of a Tathāgata are not obtained from the future limit; the ten powers of a Tathāgata are not obtained from the present. The ten powers of a Tathāgata are not obtained within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not obtained.

Neither the future time nor the present time is perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less can the past time be perceived within equality? How can the future time be perceived, and how can the present time be perceived? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit, the four grounds of self-confidence are not perceived.

The four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*) are not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; the four grounds of self-confidence are not apprehended from the perspective of the present; and the four grounds of self-confidence are not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How much less, then, could the past time be apprehended within equality?

From where is the future time [derived], and from where is the present time perceived? Subhūti, the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are not perceived from the perspective of the past limit; the four analytical knowledges are not perceived from the perspective of the future limit; the four analytical knowledges are not perceived from the perspective of the present. Within the equality of the three times, the four analytical knowledges are not perceived. Subhūti, within that equality, the past time is not perceived.

The future time is not perceived, nor is the present time perceived. Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less can the past time be perceived within equality? How can the future time be perceived, and how can the present time be perceived? Subhūti, great compassion is not perceived from the perspective of the prior limit; great compassion is not perceived from the perspective of the posterior limit; great compassion is not perceived from the perspective of the present.

In the equality of the three times, great compassion is not apprehended. Subhūti, in equality, the past time is not apprehended; the future time is not apprehended, nor is the present time apprehended. Indeed, even equality itself is not apprehended within equality. How, then, could the past time be apprehended in equality? How could the future time or the present time be apprehended in equality? Subhūti, from the perspective of the prior limit, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) are not apprehended.

The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not apprehended from the perspective of the present; and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Subhūti, within equality, the past time is not apprehended, nor is the future time, nor is the present time apprehended.
Even equality itself is not perceived within equality; how much less can the past time be perceived within equality? How can the future time be perceived, or the present time be perceived?

Furthermore, Subhūti, an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*) is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; an ordinary person is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; an ordinary person is not apprehended from the perspective of the present; and an ordinary person is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Why is that? Because of the non-apprehensibility of sentient beings (*sattva*). Furthermore, Subhūti, a disciple (*śrāvaka*) is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; a disciple is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

From the perspective of the present, a śrāvaka is not apprehended; within the equality of the three times, a śrāvaka is not apprehended. Why is that? Because of the non-apprehension of sentient beings. Furthermore, Subhūti, from the perspective of the past limit, a pratyekabuddha is not apprehended; from the perspective of the future limit, a pratyekabuddha is not apprehended; from the perspective of the present, a pratyekabuddha is not apprehended; within the equality of the three times, a pratyekabuddha is not apprehended.

For what reason? Because of the non-apprehension of sentient beings. Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the present; and a bodhisattva is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. For what reason? Because of the non-apprehension of sentient beings. Furthermore, Subhūti, a Tathāgata is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

The Tathāgata is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; the Tathāgata is not apprehended from the perspective of the present; the Tathāgata is not apprehended within the equality of the three times. Why is that? Because of the non-apprehension of sentient beings. Thus, indeed, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, abiding in the perfection of wisdom and training in the three times, should fulfill the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Subhūti, this is the Mahāyāna of the bodhisattva mahāsattva called "the equality of the three times."

Abiding in this, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, having surpassed the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, goes forth toward the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*). Then, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! How well has this Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*) of the equality of the three times for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas been spoken by the Blessed One! Having trained in this Great Vehicle, Blessed One, even the bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the past attained the knowledge of all aspects."

"Blessed One, even those bodhisattva mahāsattvas of the future, having trained in this very Mahāyāna, will attain all-aspect omniscience. Blessed One, those immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattva mahāsattvas who currently exist in the infinite world-systems throughout the ten directions—they too, having trained in this Mahāyāna, attain all-aspect omniscience."

"Therefore, Blessed One, this Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is called 'the equality of the three times. When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti: 'So it is, Subhūti, so it is. Having trained in this Great Vehicle, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas of the past, future, and present have attained, will attain, and are attaining omniscience.'"
The eleventh chapter of the Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā.

Then the twelfth chapter. Then indeed, Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this Elder Subhūti has been requested by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, for the sake of the *prajñāpāramitā*; yet he thinks that the Mahāyāna should be taught. Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "May it not be, O Blessed One, that I teach the Mahāyāna by overstepping the *prajñāpāramitā*. The Blessed One said:

"It is not so, Subhūti. Subhūti, you are teaching the Mahāyāna in accordance with the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, whatever wholesome dharmas there are—whether they be the dharmas of a śrāvaka, the dharmas of a pratyekabuddha, the dharmas of a bodhisattva, or the dharmas of a Buddha—all of them are included within and converge upon the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti said:

"Blessed One, which are the wholesome dharmas that are the factors of enlightenment? And what are the dharmas of the Pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the Bodhisattvas, and the dharmas of the Buddhas that enter into and converge within the Perfection of Wisdom? The Blessed One said: "They are as follows: the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, and the seven factors of enlightenment."

The noble eightfold path; the four noble truths; the gateways to liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; the four meditative absorptions (dhyānas); the four immeasurables; the four formless attainments; the six superknowledges (abhijñās); the perfection of generosity; the perfection of ethical discipline; the perfection of patience; the perfection of vigor; the perfection of meditation; the perfection of wisdom; internal emptiness; external emptiness; internal and external emptiness; the emptiness of emptiness.

Great emptiness; emptiness of the ultimate truth; emptiness of the conditioned; emptiness of the unconditioned; absolute emptiness; emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; emptiness of non-dispersal; emptiness of intrinsic nature; emptiness of all phenomena; emptiness of specific characteristics; emptiness of non-apprehension; emptiness of non-existence; emptiness of self-nature; emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence; all meditative concentrations; all gateways of dhāraṇī; the ten powers of a Tathāgata.

The four grounds of self-confidence; the four analytical knowledges; great loving-kindness; great compassion; great sympathetic joy; great equanimity; the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the state of immeasurable qualities; and dwelling in great equanimity—these, Subhūti, are the wholesome qualities that are factors conducive to enlightenment.

The dharmas of the śrāvakas, the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the bodhisattvas, and the dharmas of the buddhas—all these go toward inclusion and convergence within the perfection of wisdom. And, Subhūti, that which is the Mahāyāna and that which is the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity—[all these are one].

Whatever form, whatever feeling, whatever perception, whatever mental formations, and whatever consciousness; whatever eye, whatever form, and whatever eye-consciousness; whatever eye-contact and whatever feeling conditioned by eye-contact; whatever ear, whatever sound, and whatever ear-consciousness; whatever ear-contact and whatever feeling conditioned by ear-contact.

That which is the nose, that which is odor, that which is nose-consciousness, that which is nose-contact, and that which is the feeling conditioned by nose-contact; that which is the tongue, that which is taste, that which is tongue-consciousness, that which is tongue-contact, and that which is the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; that which is the body, that which is tangibility, that which is body-consciousness, that which is body-contact, and that which is the feeling conditioned by body-contact.

That which is the mind, those which are mental phenomena, that which is mental consciousness, that which is mental contact, and that which is feeling conditioned by mental contact; and that which is ignorance, those which are volitional formations, and that which is consciousness...

Name-and-form, the six sense bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and old age and death; as well as the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom.
