That which is internal emptiness, that which is external emptiness, that which is internal-external emptiness, that which is the emptiness of emptiness, that which is great emptiness, that which is the emptiness of the ultimate truth, that which is the emptiness of the conditioned, that which is the emptiness of the unconditioned, that which is absolute emptiness, that which is the emptiness of the beginningless and endless, that which is the emptiness of non-dispersal, that which is the emptiness of intrinsic nature, that which is the emptiness of all phenomena, that which is the emptiness of specific characteristics, and that which is the emptiness of non-apprehension—

And there is the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence; and those which are the applications of mindfulness, the right exertions, the bases of miraculous power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the noble eightfold path; and those which are the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, and the six supernormal knowledges; and those which are the eight bases of mastery.

The ten bases of totality (*kṛtsnāyatana*), the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*), the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling (*anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*), suffering (*duḥkha*), its origin (*samudaya*), its cessation (*nirodha*), and the path (*mārga*); the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (*śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*); the various concentrations (*samādhi*), the gateways of mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇī-mukha*), the ten powers of a Tathāgata (*tathāgata-bala*), and the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*).

And the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*); and the realm of desire (*kāmadhātu*), and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), and wholesome phenomena (*kuśaladharma*), and contaminated phenomena (*sāśravadharma*), and uncontaminated phenomena (*anāśravadharma*), and mundane phenomena (*laukikadharma*).

Those dharmas which are supramundane, those which are conditioned, and those which are unconditioned; that which is the dharma of the Tathāgata; that Dharma-Vinaya entered by the Tathāgata; and that which is the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), suchness (tathatā), the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), the inconceivable realm (acintyadhātu), and the realm of nirvāṇa—in all these cases, these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined. They are formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and possess a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics.

By this method, Subhūti, I teach the Mahāyāna as being in conformity with the perfection of wisdom. Why is that? Because, Subhūti, the Mahāyāna is not one thing and the perfection of wisdom another; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual and cannot be divided. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the perfection of meditation another; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual and cannot be divided.

The Mahāyāna is not other than the perfection of vigor; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the perfection of vigor are non-dual, this being an indivisibility. The Mahāyāna is not other than the perfection of patience; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the perfection of patience are non-dual, this being an indivisibility. The Mahāyāna is not other than the perfection of ethical discipline; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the perfection of ethical discipline are non-dual, this being an indivisibility. The Mahāyāna is not other than the perfection of generosity.

Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the perfection of giving are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated state. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and internal emptiness another; thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and internal emptiness are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated state. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and external emptiness another; thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and external emptiness are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated state. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and internal-and-external emptiness another.

Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and internal-external emptiness are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and emptiness another. Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of emptiness are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing [and emptiness another].

The Great Emptiness is not other [than the Mahāyāna]. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the Great Emptiness are non-dual; they are not divided into two. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the Ultimate Emptiness another. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the Ultimate Emptiness are non-dual; they are not divided into two. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the Conditioned Emptiness another. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the Conditioned Emptiness are non-dual; they are not divided into two. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the Unconditioned Emptiness another.

Thus, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of the unconditioned are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the absolute emptiness another. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the absolute emptiness are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end another. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of non-dispersal another.

Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*) are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*) another. Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of all phenomena (*sarvadharma-śūnyatā*) another. Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of all phenomena are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*) another.

Thus, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of specific characteristics (svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā) are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of non-apprehension (anupalambha-śūnyatā) another. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of non-apprehension are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of non-existence (abhāva-śūnyatā) another. Thus, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of non-existence are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the emptiness of intrinsic nature (svabhāva-śūnyatā) another.

Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of intrinsic nature are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. There is no Mahāyāna other than the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. There is no Mahāyāna other than the applications of mindfulness. Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and...

The foundations of mindfulness are non-dual and indivisible; the Great Vehicle is not one thing and the right efforts another—for indeed, the Great Vehicle and the right efforts are non-dual and indivisible. The Great Vehicle is not one thing and the bases of psychic power another—for indeed, the Great Vehicle and the bases of psychic power are non-dual and indivisible. The Great Vehicle is not one thing and the faculties another—for indeed, the Great Vehicle and the faculties are non-dual and indivisible.

The Mahāyāna is not other than the powers; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the powers are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not other than the factors of enlightenment; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the factors of enlightenment are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not other than the noble eightfold path; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the noble eightfold path are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not other than the noble truths.

Thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the Noble Truths are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*) another; thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the meditative absorptions are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*) another; thus, indeed, the Mahāyāna and the immeasurables are non-dual; this is an undifferentiated unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*) another.

For thus, the Mahāyāna and the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*) are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*) another; for thus, the Mahāyāna and the liberations are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity. The Mahāyāna is not one thing and the nine successive meditative attainments (*anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti*) another; for thus, the Mahāyāna and the successive meditative attainments are non-dual; this is an indivisible unity.

The Mahāyāna is not other than the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-dual and cannot be divided. The Mahāyāna is not other than the supernormal knowledges (abhijñā); for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the supernormal knowledges are non-dual.

There is no duality; the Mahāyāna is not one thing and the samādhis another. For indeed, the Mahāyāna and the samādhis are non-dual; this is their non-duality. There is no duality; the Mahāyāna is not one thing and the doors of dhāraṇī another. For indeed, the Mahāyāna and the doors of dhāraṇī are non-dual; this is their non-duality. There is no duality; the Mahāyāna is not one thing and the ten powers of a Tathāgata another. For indeed, the Mahāyāna and the powers of a Tathāgata are non-dual; this is their non-duality.

The Mahāyāna is not other than the fearlessnesses; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the fearlessnesses are non-dual, they are not divided into two. The Mahāyāna is not other than the four analytical knowledges; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the analytical knowledges are non-dual, they are not divided into two. The Mahāyāna is not other than great compassion; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and great compassion are non-dual, they are not divided into two.
The Mahāyāna is not other than the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; for indeed, the Mahāyāna and the unique qualities of a Buddha are non-dual and indivisible.

"Subhūti, by this method, when the Mahāyāna is taught, the Perfection of Wisdom is taught; and when the Perfection of Wisdom is taught, the Mahāyāna is taught. Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One: "Furthermore, Blessed One, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; nor is a bodhisattva apprehended even from the perspective of the middle."

Through the boundlessness of form, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be known; through the boundlessness of feeling, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be known; through the boundlessness of perception, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be known; through the boundlessness of mental formations, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be known; through the boundlessness of consciousness, the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be known. Even "form is the bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended; even "feeling is the bodhisattva" [does not exist and is not apprehended].

It does not exist and is not apprehended. Even as "a bodhisattva is perception," it does not exist and is not apprehended. Even as "a bodhisattva is volitional formations," it does not exist and is not apprehended. Even as "a bodhisattva is consciousness," it does not exist and is not apprehended.

Thus, O Blessed One, not perceiving and not apprehending a bodhisattva in any way whatsoever, which bodhisattva shall I instruct and admonish in which perfection of wisdom? Indeed, I do not perceive and do not apprehend even the entirety of a "bodhisattva" itself; so which bodhisattva shall I instruct and admonish in which perfection of wisdom?

"Blessed One, that which is called a 'bodhisattva mahāsattva' is merely a name. Just as, Blessed One, that which is called 'self' is a self that is absolutely unproduced (*atyantānabhinirvṛtta*), even so, Blessed One, that which is called a 'bodhisattva mahāsattva' is a bodhisattva who is absolutely unproduced. Thus, among phenomena whose intrinsic nature is non-existence (*abhāvasvabhāva*), what is that form which is unproduced? What is that feeling which is unproduced?"

What is that perception which is unproduced? What are those formations which are unproduced? What is that consciousness which is unproduced? And, Blessed One, that which is unproduced is not form; that which is unproduced is not feeling; that which is unproduced is not perception; those which are unproduced are not formations; and that which is unproduced is not consciousness.

Therefore, how could I instruct or admonish that which is unproduced within the unproduced perfection of wisdom? Furthermore, apart from non-production, no bodhisattva mahāsattva is apprehended who would course toward awakening. If, when this is being taught, the mind of the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not sink, does not become despondent, does not feel regret, and his mind does not tremble, is not terrified, and does not fall into terror, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom.

Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to the venerable Subhūti: "For what reason, venerable Subhūti, does a bodhisattva not come from the past limit? Why does a bodhisattva not come from the future limit? Why does a bodhisattva not come from the middle? For what reason, venerable Subhūti, should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of form? Should the boundlessness of the bodhisattva be understood through the boundlessness of feeling?"

The boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood through the boundlessness of perception; the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood through the boundlessness of mental formations; the boundlessness of the bodhisattva is to be understood through the boundlessness of consciousness. For what reason, Venerable Subhūti, is it that even "form is a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended? Even "feeling is a bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended.

The designation "bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended even in this way; "consciousness is the bodhisattva" does not exist and is not apprehended even in this way. For what reason, Venerable Subhūti, do you speak thus? Since I do not perceive and do not apprehend a bodhisattva at all—in every respect, in every way, and in every manner—what bodhisattva shall I instruct and admonish in which perfection of wisdom?

"For what reason, Venerable Subhūti, do you say this: 'I do not perceive, nor do I apprehend, even a Bodhisattva as a whole; which Bodhisattva shall I instruct and admonish in which perfection of wisdom? For what reason, Venerable Subhūti, do you say, 'O Blessed One, one is called a "Bodhisattva, a Bodhisattva"?'—it is merely a name."

"For what reason, Venerable Subhūti, do you say this: 'Just as that which is called "self" is absolutely unproduced, even so, Blessed One, that which is called "bodhisattva mahāsattva" is an absolutely unproduced bodhisattva'? And since all dharmas have non-existence as their intrinsic nature (*abhāvasvabhāva*), what is that form (*rūpa*) which is unproduced? What is that feeling (*vedanā*)?"

That which is unproduced—what is that perception (saṃjñā) which is unproduced? What are those formations (saṃskāra) which are unproduced? What is that consciousness (vijñāna) which is unproduced? That which is unproduced is not form (rūpa); that which is unproduced is not feeling (vedanā); that which is unproduced is not perception; those which are unproduced are not formations; that which is unproduced is not consciousness.

For what reason, Subhūti, do you say this: "How shall I instruct and admonish that which is unproduced within the unproduced perfection of wisdom"? For what reason, Subhūti, is it that no bodhisattva who courses toward awakening is perceived apart from these unproduced things?

"For what reason, Subhūti, do you say this: 'If, when it is taught in this way, the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not sink, does not become despondent, does not feel regret, and his mind does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear, then this bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom'? When this was said, the venerable Subhūti spoke thus to the venerable Śāradvatīputra:

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the non-existence of a sentient being, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By virtue of the solitude of a sentient being, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of a sentient being, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By virtue of the non-existence of a sentient being, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future. By virtue of the emptiness of a sentient being, the solitude of a sentient being, and the lack of intrinsic nature of a sentient being, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the non-existence of a sentient being, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the middle. By way of the emptiness of a sentient being, by way of the solitude of a sentient being, and by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of a sentient being, one does not approach a bodhisattva from the middle. Why is that? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the emptiness of a sentient being, in the solitude of a sentient being, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of a sentient being, neither a prior limit nor a subsequent limit nor a middle is apprehended;
nor is the non-existence of a sentient being one thing, the emptiness of a sentient being another, the solitude of a sentient being another, and [the lack of intrinsic nature] another.

"Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is not that the absence of intrinsic nature in sentient beings is one thing, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another. For indeed, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of sentient beings, that which is the emptiness of sentient beings, that which is the solitude of sentient beings, and that which is the absence of intrinsic nature in sentient beings; and that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by virtue of the non-existence of form, a bodhisattva does not approach [existence] from the prior limit."

By way of the emptiness of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit; by way of the seclusion of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the past limit. By way of the non-existence of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the future limit; by way of the emptiness of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the future limit; by way of the seclusion of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of form, one does not apprehend a bodhisattva from the future limit.

By way of the non-existence of form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the emptiness of form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the solitude of form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of form, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of form, the emptiness of form, the seclusion of form, and the lack of intrinsic nature of form are not apprehended in the past limit, nor are they apprehended in the future limit, nor are they apprehended in the middle. Furthermore, the non-existence of form is not one thing, the emptiness of form another, the seclusion of form another, the lack of intrinsic nature of form another, the bodhisattva another, the past limit another, the future limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, the non-existence of form, the emptiness of form, the solitude of form, the lack of intrinsic nature of form, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.
By virtue of the non-existence of feeling, venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva does not approach [it] from the prior limit.

By way of the emptiness of feeling (*vedanā*), a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit; by way of the solitude of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit; by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the past limit. By way of the non-existence of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit; by way of the emptiness of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit; by way of the solitude of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit; by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach from the future limit.

By way of the existence of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle; by way of the emptiness of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle; by way of the solitude of feeling, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that? For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the existence of feeling, in the emptiness of feeling, in the solitude of feeling, and in the intrinsic nature of feeling, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of feeling is not one thing, the emptiness of feeling another, the solitude of feeling another, the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another.

For indeed, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of feeling, that which is the emptiness of feeling, that which is the solitude of feeling, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling, that which is the Bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the posterior limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit by way of the existence of perception; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit by way of the emptiness of perception; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit by way of the isolation of perception; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit by way of the intrinsic nature of perception. A bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the subsequent limit by way of the existence of perception; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the subsequent limit by way of the emptiness of perception; a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the subsequent limit by way of the isolation of perception; [a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the subsequent limit] by way of the intrinsic nature of perception.

A bodhisattva does not approach [them]. By way of the existence of perception, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. By way of the emptiness of perception, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. By way of the solitude of perception, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. By way of the intrinsic nature of perception, a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither a prior limit, nor a posterior limit, nor a middle is perceived in the existence of perception, in the emptiness of perception, in the isolation of perception, or in the intrinsic nature of perception. Furthermore, the existence of perception is not one thing, the emptiness of perception another, the isolation of perception another, and the intrinsic nature of perception another; nor is the bodhisattva one thing, the prior limit another, the posterior limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of perception, that which is the emptiness of perception, that which is the solitude of perception, and that which is the intrinsic nature of perception; and that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the prior limit, that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by reason of the non-existence of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by reason of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by reason of the isolation of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by reason of the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit. By reason of the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; by reason of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.

By virtue of the isolation of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit. By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the future limit. By virtue of the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle. By virtue of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle. By virtue of the isolation of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle. By virtue of the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena, a bodhisattva does not approach them from the perspective of the middle.
Why is that? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of conditioned phenomena and in the emptiness of conditioned phenomena...

In the state of the isolation of formative forces (*saṃskāra*) and in the absence of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of formative forces, neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived. Furthermore, the non-existence of formative forces is not one thing, their emptiness another, their isolation another, their absence of intrinsic nature another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another. Thus it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra.

That which is the non-existence of conditioned phenomena, that which is the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, that which is the solitude of conditioned phenomena, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of conditioned phenomena, the bodhisattva, the past limit, the future limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and cannot be divided into two.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the emptiness of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the solitude of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit. By way of the non-existence of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of consciousness, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit.

By way of the isolation of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit. By way of the non-existence of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the emptiness of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the isolation of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of consciousness, in the emptiness of consciousness, in the isolation of consciousness, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness, no prior limit is apprehended; no subsequent limit is apprehended; and no middle is apprehended. Nor is the non-existence of consciousness one thing, the emptiness of consciousness another, and the isolation of consciousness yet another.

Consciousness is not of one nature, the bodhisattva is another, the prior limit is another, the posterior limit is another, and the middle is another. For in this way, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of consciousness, that which is the emptiness of consciousness, that which is the solitude of consciousness, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of consciousness—along with the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the eye, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the emptiness of the eye, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of the eye, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By way of the non-existence of the eye, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; by way of the emptiness of the eye, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the isolation of the eye, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the non-existence of the eye, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the emptiness of the eye, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the isolation of the eye, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of the eye, the emptiness of the eye, the solitude of the eye, and the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye, neither a prior limit is perceived, nor a subsequent limit is perceived, nor a middle is perceived. Furthermore, the non-existence of the eye is not one thing, the emptiness of the eye another, the solitude of the eye another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the eye, that which is the emptiness of the eye, that which is the solitude of the eye, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the eye, and that which is the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the ear, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the emptiness of the ear, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of the ear, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the ear, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By way of the non-existence of the ear, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; by way of the emptiness of the ear, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the seclusion of the ear, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the ear, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the non-existence of the ear, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the emptiness of the ear, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the seclusion of the ear, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the ear, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the ear, in the emptiness of the ear, in the solitude of the ear, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the ear, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of the ear is not one thing, the emptiness of the ear another, the solitude of the ear another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the ear another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of the ear, that which is the emptiness of the ear, that which is the solitude of the ear, that which is the intrinsic nature of the ear, and that which is the bodhisattva, as well as the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the nose, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the emptiness of the nose, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the solitude of the nose, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the nose, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past limit. By way of the non-existence of the nose, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the emptiness of the nose, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the solitude of the nose, [a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future limit...]

A bodhisattva does not approach [them]. Due to the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of the nose, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit (*aparānta*). Due to the non-existence (*asattā*) of the nose, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. Due to the emptiness (*śūnyatā*) of the nose, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. Due to the solitude (*viviktatā*) of the nose, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. Due to the lack of intrinsic nature of the nose, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the nose, in the emptiness of the nose, in the solitude of the nose, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of the nose, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the non-existence of the nose is not one thing, the emptiness of the nose another, the solitude of the nose another, the lack of intrinsic nature of the nose another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-attachment of the nose, that which is the emptiness of the nose, that which is the solitude of the nose, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of the nose, and that which is the bodhisattva, as well as the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the tongue, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past; by way of the emptiness of the tongue, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past; by way of the solitude of the tongue, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past; by way of the intrinsic nature of the tongue, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the past. By way of the non-existence of the tongue, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the future; by way of the emptiness of the tongue, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the future.

Through the isolation of the tongue, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; through the intrinsic nature of the tongue, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; through the non-existence of the tongue, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; through the emptiness of the tongue, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; through the isolation of the tongue, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; through the intrinsic nature of the tongue, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. Why is that? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of the tongue...

In the emptiness of the tongue, in the seclusion of the tongue, and in the intrinsic nature of the tongue, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended. Furthermore, the existence of the tongue is not other than the emptiness of the tongue, the seclusion of the tongue, and the intrinsic nature of the tongue; nor is the bodhisattva other, nor the prior limit other, nor the subsequent limit other, nor the middle other.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of the tongue, that which is the emptiness of the tongue, that which is the solitude of the tongue, that which is the intrinsic nature of the tongue, and that which is the bodhisattva, as well as the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of the body, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the emptiness of the body, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of the body, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of the body, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past. By way of the non-existence of the body, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future; by way of the emptiness of the body, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the body’s seclusion, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit; by way of the body’s lack of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit. By way of the body’s non-existence, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the body’s emptiness, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the body’s seclusion, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle; by way of the body’s lack of intrinsic nature, a bodhisattva does not approach the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of eye-contact, the emptiness of eye-contact, the seclusion of eye-contact, and the lack of intrinsic nature of eye-contact, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of eye-contact is not one thing, the emptiness of eye-contact another, the seclusion of eye-contact another, the lack of intrinsic nature of eye-contact another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of eye-contact, that which is the emptiness of eye-contact, that which is the solitude of eye-contact, and that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of eye-contact—along with the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the non-existence of ear-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; by way of the emptiness of ear-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; by way of the solitude of ear-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of ear-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit. By way of the non-existence of ear-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the posterior limit; by way of the emptiness of ear-contact, [a bodhisattva is not apprehended] from the perspective of the posterior limit...

A bodhisattva does not approach [them]. Because of the seclusion of ear-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit. Because of the lack of intrinsic nature of ear-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the future limit. Because of the non-existence of ear-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the middle. Because of the emptiness of ear-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the middle. Because of the seclusion of ear-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach from the perspective of the middle.

By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of auditory contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that? Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because in the non-existence of auditory contact, in the emptiness of auditory contact, in the solitude of auditory contact, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of auditory contact, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of ear-contact is not one thing, the emptiness of ear-contact another, the solitude of ear-contact another, the lack of intrinsic nature of ear-contact another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of ear-contact, that which is the emptiness of ear-contact, that which is the solitude of ear-contact, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of ear-contact, and that which is the bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit, and that which is the subsequent limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of olfactory contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; because of the emptiness of olfactory contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; because of the isolation of olfactory contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; because of the lack of intrinsic nature of olfactory contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the prior limit; because of the non-existence of olfactory contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the subsequent limit.

By way of the emptiness of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the seclusion of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the non-existence of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; by way of the emptiness of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; by way of the seclusion of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle; by way of the lack of intrinsic nature of nose-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.

For what reason? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, in the non-existence of nose-contact, in the emptiness of nose-contact, in the seclusion of nose-contact, and in the lack of intrinsic nature of nose-contact, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of nose-contact is not one thing, the emptiness of nose-contact another, the seclusion of nose-contact another, the lack of intrinsic nature of nose-contact another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, or the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of olfactory contact, that which is the emptiness of olfactory contact, that which is the solitude of olfactory contact, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of olfactory contact, and that which is the bodhisattva, and that which is the prior limit, and that which is the later limit, and that which is the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the emptiness of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the solitude of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the lack of intrinsic nature of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the non-existence of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the emptiness of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the seclusion of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the non-existence of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the emptiness of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the seclusion of tongue-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of tongue-contact...

A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that? Because, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the non-existence of tongue-contact, the emptiness of tongue-contact, the solitude of tongue-contact, and the lack of intrinsic nature of tongue-contact, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the non-existence of tongue-contact is not other than the emptiness of tongue-contact, the solitude of tongue-contact, the lack of intrinsic nature of tongue-contact; nor is the bodhisattva other, nor the prior limit other, nor the subsequent limit other, nor the middle other.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the non-existence of tongue-contact, that which is the emptiness of tongue-contact, that which is the solitude of tongue-contact, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of tongue-contact, and that which is the bodhisattva, as well as the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, because of the non-existence of body-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the emptiness of body-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the solitude of body-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; because of the lack of intrinsic nature of body-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; and because of the non-existence of body-contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the future.

By way of the emptiness of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the seclusion of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the lack of intrinsic nature of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the future limit. By way of the non-existence of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the emptiness of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle. By way of the seclusion of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the perspective of the middle.

By way of the lack of intrinsic nature (*asvabhāvatā*) of body-contact, a bodhisattva does not approach it from the middle. Why is that? For, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, neither a prior limit, nor a subsequent limit, nor a middle is apprehended in the existence of feeling conditioned by body-contact, nor in the emptiness of feeling conditioned by body-contact, nor in the seclusion of feeling conditioned by body-contact, nor in the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by body-contact.

Furthermore, the existence of feeling conditioned by bodily contact is not one thing, the emptiness of feeling conditioned by bodily contact another, the seclusion of feeling conditioned by bodily contact another, the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by bodily contact another, the Bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of feeling conditioned by bodily contact, that which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by bodily contact, that which is the solitude of feeling conditioned by bodily contact, that which is the lack of intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by bodily contact, the bodhisattva, the prior limit, the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and indivisible.

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, by way of the existence of feeling conditioned by mental contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; by way of the solitude of feeling conditioned by mental contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past; and by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact, a bodhisattva is not apprehended from the perspective of the past.

A bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the existence of feeling conditioned by mental contact; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the solitude of feeling conditioned by mental contact; a bodhisattva does not approach the future limit by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact; a bodhisattva does not approach the middle limit by way of the existence of feeling conditioned by mental contact.

A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact; a bodhisattva does not approach from the middle by way of the seclusion of feeling conditioned by mental contact; [a bodhisattva does not approach] by way of the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact.

A bodhisattva does not approach from the middle. Why is that? For, venerable Śāradvatīputra, within the existence of feeling conditioned by mental contact, within the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact, within the solitude of feeling conditioned by mental contact, and within the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact, neither a prior limit is apprehended, nor a subsequent limit is apprehended, nor a middle is apprehended.

Furthermore, the existence of feeling conditioned by mental contact is not one thing, the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact another, the isolation of feeling conditioned by mental contact another, the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact another, the bodhisattva another, the prior limit another, the subsequent limit another, and the middle another.

Thus, venerable Śāradvatīputra, that which is the existence of feeling conditioned by mental contact, that which is the emptiness of feeling conditioned by mental contact, that which is the solitude of feeling conditioned by mental contact, and that which is the intrinsic nature of feeling conditioned by mental contact; and the bodhisattva, and the prior limit, and the subsequent limit, and the middle—all this is non-dual and not divided into two.
This is the twelfth chapter of the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
Thus ends the first section.
